Salesforce Certification Pass Mark, Exam Fee & Prerequisites Guide

Every card above shows the same four figures, taken from the official exam pages. Here is what each one means when you are choosing a Salesforce certification to sit.

The percentage needed to pass. Each exam sets its own pass mark; it is not curved. For example, a 65% pass mark means you need 65% of the scored questions. Pass marks appear in official exam guides, so check yours before booking.

Exam fee and retake fee

The exam fee is the first-attempt price in USD, before local taxes. Retakes usually cost half the exam fee; $75 entry-level exams have free retakes. Fees can change, so confirm the current price on the official page linked from each card.

Most Salesforce certifications have no formal prerequisite, though experience may be recommended. Some require another credential first; two are awarded after you pass a set of component exams. The cards show which applies.

Choose a certification that fits the work you want to do. Compare the role categories above with your experience and interests, such as administration, development, consulting, architecture, marketing, or analytics. A role category does not set prerequisites. Check the credential page and current exam guide for prerequisites, recommended experience, format, fees, and availability.

Build a study plan from the exam objectives

Start with the current official exam guide and use its objectives as a checklist. Mark each topic as familiar, partly familiar, or new, then spend more time on areas you have not used in Salesforce. The linked study resources and practice questions can help you review and check your understanding. Use practice scores to find gaps; they cannot guarantee a result or replace hands-on work and the official guide.

Use hands-on practice and verify changing details

When possible, practise in a Salesforce Developer Edition, Trailhead Playground, or another suitable environment. Admins can configure a feature and check its effect on records and users; developers can build and test a component or automation. Consultants and architects can practise explaining why a solution meets the stated requirements. Note your mistakes and record the documentation that helped you confirm the answer.

chunks.title: ADM-201 vs App Builder: Compare Salesforce Exam Paths
chunks.content:
Which should you take first?

Take Salesforce Administrator if:

You are new to Salesforce

Your work involves users, data, security, or reports

You want a credential commonly requested for admin roles

You want a foundation for other Salesforce certifications

Take Platform App Builder if:

You already have the Administrator certification

You regularly build Lightning pages, flows, or custom apps

You want a second certification that builds on your current knowledge

You are working toward the Architect certification path

Our Recommendation: Start with Salesforce Administrator

Take Administrator first to build your knowledge of Salesforce setup, security, automation, and data. App Builder uses many of the same platform concepts, so this foundation can make the next exam easier to prepare for.

Side-by-Side Comparison

Which One Should You Take First?

Start with ADM-201 if you are new to Salesforce or want an admin-focused role.

Take DEV-402 next if you want to build custom apps using declarative tools.

A common sequence is ADM-201, then DEV-402, followed by an Advanced Administrator or Consultant path.

Career Outcome & Salary Differences

ADM-201 covers day-to-day Salesforce administration, including user setup, access controls, automation, data quality, and reporting. App Builder focuses on designing and creating custom apps with declarative tools.

ADM-201 (Administrator)

Salesforce Admin: $70–95k

Senior Admin: $90–125k

Most job postings require this cert first

Faster path to employment

DEV-402 (App Builder), added to ADM-201

Solution Designer / Functional Consultant: $95–130k

Opens Consultant & Architect certification paths

Valued for custom app delivery roles

App Builder alone (without Admin) is less common

If you are aiming for a Salesforce operations role, ADM-201 may be the more relevant first credential. Adding DEV-402 can show that you also know how to design and build custom apps, and it supports Consultant-track options.

Start Here: Which Cert Based on Your Goal

Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201)

ADM-201 is the foundation of the admin track and the most widely held Salesforce credential. It covers core admin work, including security, Flow Builder, data management, reports, dashboards, and sales and service setup. Many Salesforce admin roles require it, making it a common starting point for this career path.

Salesforce Platform App Builder (DEV-402)

App Builder tests your ability to design and build Salesforce apps with declarative tools. It builds on ADM-201 and adds data modelling, app design, and Lightning app configuration. Some admin roles ask for both ADM-201 and App Builder to show a broader set of declarative skills.

Salesforce Advanced Administrator

Advanced Administrator builds on ADM-201 with more complex automation, such as advanced Flow patterns and approval processes with conditional logic; advanced security, including delegated administration and custom sharing rules; and advanced reporting, such as joined reports and custom report types. Consider it for senior admin roles or before pursuing consultant certifications.

Salesforce Sales Cloud Consultant or Service Cloud Consultant

After ADM-201 and App Builder, consultant certifications let you focus on a business area. Sales Cloud Consultant covers CRM implementation, the lead-to-close process, forecasting, and territory management. Service Cloud Consultant covers case management, Omni-Channel, entitlements, and Knowledge. Choose the one that fits your current client work or target role.

chunks.title: Administrator vs Advanced Administrator: Which Next?
chunks.content:
Which should you take first?

Take Salesforce Administrator if:

You do not yet hold any Salesforce certification

You are new to the platform or have less than 1 year of hands-on experience

You want the most widely required credential across all Salesforce roles

You are starting any Salesforce career path

Take Advanced Administrator if:

You already hold the Administrator certification

You have 2+ years of hands-on Salesforce admin experience

You work with advanced automation, territory management, or Salesforce Connect

You are targeting senior admin or platform manager roles

Our Recommendation: Start with Salesforce Administrator

Administrator is the first step. Advanced Administrator builds on the admin concepts covered by ADM-201, so learn those topics before taking the advanced exam.

Side-by-Side Comparison

What Advanced Administrator Tests That ADM-201 Doesn’t

Complex automation: Multi-step Flows with decisions, fault paths, loops, and scheduled triggers. ADM-201 covers basic Flow creation; Advanced Administrator covers how to design Flows for complex business processes.

Advanced sharing and security: Sharing rules, manual sharing, team access, territory management, and field-level security at scale. ADM-201 covers OWD, while Advanced Administrator tests more complex sharing scenarios.

Change sets and deployment: Move metadata between sandboxes and production with change sets. Understand dependencies and validate a deployment before it goes live.

Advanced analytics: Build reports with cross-object formulas, joined reports, and exceptions, and work with CRM Analytics (Einstein) dashboards beyond the basic report builder.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do you need ADM-201 before taking Advanced Administrator?

Yes. You must pass Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201) before taking the Advanced Administrator exam.

Is the Advanced Administrator exam harder than ADM-201?

Yes. Advanced Administrator is widely considered harder. It assumes ADM-201 knowledge and tests more advanced configuration, including multi-step Flows, scheduled triggers, sharing and security, change sets, deployments, and reports with cross-object formulas. Many candidates recommend 1–2 years of hands-on admin experience before taking it.

How long should I wait between ADM-201 and Advanced Administrator?

Salesforce recommends at least 1–2 years of admin experience before taking Advanced Administrator. Avoid rushing to it right after ADM-201; the exam tests practical knowledge gained from managing a real Salesforce org, not study alone.

chunks.title: Administrator vs Advanced Administrator: Which Next?
chunks.content:
Which certification is worth more: Administrator or Advanced Administrator?

Both can be useful. Advanced Administrator may support applications for senior admin roles and is associated with higher salaries. In 2026, holding both certifications, or ADM-201 plus a specialist certification such as Sales Cloud or Service Cloud Consultant, may make you more competitive than ADM-201 alone.

chunks.title: Salesforce Architect Certification Roadmap & Career Guide
chunks.content:
Download as PNGSave or share this roadmap.

The Architect Pyramid

Application Architect Path (Recommended Order)

Begin with the platform foundation, then work through the four component exams. The suggested sequence starts with the more familiar credentials.

Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201): Foundation

ADM-201 is not a component exam. It provides platform knowledge used across the architect components, including security, object relationships, and declarative automation.

Platform App Builder (DEV-402): Component 1

Study data modeling, Flow automation, Lightning App Builder, and the security model. The passing score is 73%, and many candidates prepare for 4-6 weeks.

Platform Developer I (PD1): Component 2

Review Apex fundamentals, SOQL/DML, governor limits, triggers, and LWC. The passing score is 68%; prepare with hands-on Apex coding practice.

Data Architect: Component 3

This exam covers data modeling at scale, large data volumes, master data management, and migration strategy. The passing score is 58%, and real LDV project experience is useful.

Sharing & Visibility Architect: Component 4

Study OWD design, sharing rule strategy, performance implications, and Apex managed sharing. The passing score is 58%; this component has the highest retry rate of the four.

System Architect Path (Recommended Order)

Platform Developer I (PD1)

PD1 is the only exam shared with Application Architect, so you have already completed it if you hold that credential. It covers Apex, triggers, LWC, and governor limits.

Integration Architect

Study API selection, integration patterns, middleware architecture, OAuth flows, and Platform Events. The passing score is 67%.

Identity & Access Management (IAM) Architect

This exam covers SSO, OAuth, SAML, Connected Apps, and identity federation. The passing score is 65%; real SSO/OAuth implementation experience is useful.

Dev Lifecycle & Deployment Architect

Review environment strategy, sandbox hierarchy, release management, SFDX, and CI/CD pipelines. The passing score is 65%.

System Architect credential granted

There is no additional exam. Salesforce adds System Architect to your profile when you hold the four credentials listed above.

Compare Certifications

→ How to become a Salesforce Architect, step-by-step guide

→ System Architect vs Application Architect comparison

After Both Architect Credentials: The CTA Path

At the CTA Review Board, present a solution to a panel of current CTAs. Preparation takes months and calls for broad architecture knowledge.

Less than 1% of Salesforce professionals hold the CTA credential, the top level in the certification hierarchy.

chunks.title: B2B vs B2C Solution Architect (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 9 November 2026

These architect credentials focus on different commerce models. Compare the business needs, products, and client work each covers to find the closer fit.

Which should you take first?

Take B2B Solution Architect if:

Your enterprise clients use Sales, Service, or Revenue Cloud

You design solutions for business-to-business sales

Your projects include CRM, CPQ, or partner portals

You want a credential focused on B2B architecture

Take B2C Solution Architect if:

Your clients sell to consumers through Commerce, Marketing, or Service Cloud

Your projects involve consumer ecommerce, loyalty, or marketing automation

You integrate Salesforce Commerce Cloud and Marketing Cloud

You design systems for high-volume consumer activity

Our Recommendation: Start with B2B Solution Architect

Choose the credential that matches your client base. B2B Solution Architect fits enterprise sales and partner commerce work; B2C Solution Architect fits consumer storefronts and marketing. Your project experience is the clearest guide to which exam to take first.

B2B Solution Architect

Focus: Enterprise sales, commerce & revenue

Industries: Manufacturing, distribution, wholesale, technology

Experience Cloud (partner)

B2C Solution Architect

Focus: Consumer commerce & marketing

Industries: Retail, consumer goods, fashion, hospitality

B2C Commerce (Commerce Cloud)

Marketing Cloud Engagement

Marketing Cloud Personalisation

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between B2B and B2C Solution Architect certifications?

B2B Solution Architect covers enterprise sales and commerce systems, including B2B Commerce, Sales Cloud, CPQ, Revenue Cloud, and partner portals. B2C Solution Architect focuses on consumer commerce through B2C Commerce (Salesforce Commerce Cloud), Marketing Cloud personalization, and omnichannel engagement. The first fits enterprise, manufacturing, and distribution work; the second fits retail and consumer goods.

Which should I take: B2B or B2C Solution Architect?

Choose based on the projects you know. If you work on enterprise sales cycles involving CPQ, Revenue Cloud, partner communities, or B2B Commerce, choose B2B Solution Architect. If you work on consumer ecommerce, retail, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Marketing Cloud personalization, or loyalty, choose B2C Solution Architect. The credentials serve different industries.

What prerequisites are required for B2B Solution Architect?

chunks.title: B2B vs B2C Solution Architect (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
No formal prerequisites are listed. Salesforce recommends Sales Cloud Consultant, Service Cloud Consultant, and either CPQ Administrator or Experience Cloud Consultant as relevant foundation credentials. The scenario-based exam covers several parts of the Salesforce B2B stack. Many candidates have 4–6 years of Salesforce implementation experience.

What prerequisites are required for B2C Solution Architect?

No formal prerequisites are listed. Salesforce recommends Marketing Cloud Email Specialist, B2C Commerce Developer, and Experience Cloud Consultant as useful foundation credentials. The exam covers integrations across Commerce Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Service Cloud, and Einstein personalization. Hands-on experience with B2C Commerce and Marketing Cloud is important.

Are B2B and B2C Solution Architect exams similar in format?

Both exams are scenario-based and test multi-cloud architecture decisions. Each has 60 questions, 120 minutes, an approximately 68% passing score, and a $400 fee. The product scope differs: B2B Commerce, CPQ, and Revenue Cloud for B2B; B2C Commerce, Marketing Cloud, and personalization for B2C.

What This CTA Roadmap Is For

The Salesforce Certified Technical Architect path involves more than a single exam. It moves through platform fundamentals, development, domain architect credentials, solution design, and the CTA evaluation and review board. Use this roadmap to see where each certification fits.

If you are early in your career, use the first phases to build a foundation. If you already lead implementations, review the architect phases to find gaps in identity, integration, data, sharing, deployment, or application design. Plan each step around your experience instead of collecting certifications without a clear purpose.

Before moving to the next credential, try to apply its skills on a real project. CTA reviewers assess how you weigh trade-offs. Strong candidates can explain why they chose a sharing model, integration pattern, identity flow, data strategy, or deployment approach for a particular business need.

Choose a next credential that builds a skill you need, then pair study with implementation practice. Admins may want more development and data-model experience; developers may need to deepen sharing, identity, and stakeholder communication; consultants may benefit from architecture concepts and better discovery of non-functional needs.

Start here – Foundations

Build core platform and CRM knowledge. No prior Salesforce experience needed.

Administrator & App Builder

chunks.title: Business Analyst vs Strategy Designer: Which Cert?
chunks.content:
Which should you take first?

Take Business Analyst if:

You gather requirements, write user stories, or manage stakeholders

You work in a non-technical Salesforce role and want a credential to match

You are transitioning from a BA or project management background

You want a cert that pairs well with a functional consultant credential

Take Strategy Designer if:

You lead design thinking workshops or UX research sessions

You translate business needs into Salesforce solutions visually

You work closely with UX teams or run journey mapping exercises

You want to differentiate as a consultant who can lead human-centred design

Our Recommendation: Start with Business Analyst

Business Analyst has broader employer recognition and pairs naturally with any functional consultant cert. Strategy Designer is a strong differentiator but is best taken after BA, it extends the skillset rather than replacing it.

Side-by-Side Comparison

Which Certification Should You Take?

Choose Business Analyst if you gather requirements, write user stories, run workshops, or manage UAT on Salesforce projects.

Choose Strategy Designer if you set experience strategy, run design workshops, map customer journeys, or define what a Salesforce solution should do for users.

Business Analyst has a higher passing score (72%) than most Salesforce certifications. Allow extra study time for scenario questions about requirements and stakeholder communication.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between Salesforce Business Analyst and Strategy Designer?

The Business Analyst certification covers requirements gathering, process mapping, user stories, Agile collaboration, and turning business needs into Salesforce solutions. Strategy Designer focuses on human-centred design, including stakeholder research, journey mapping, ideation, prototyping, and experience design. Business Analysts capture and communicate requirements; Strategy Designers shape the user experience and direction of an implementation.

Which should I take first: Business Analyst or Strategy Designer?

Neither certification has prerequisites. Employers more often request Business Analyst for analyst and consultant roles. Strategy Designer is more specialized and may suit design-led consultancies and roles that combine product design with Salesforce delivery. Choose Business Analyst if you focus on requirements and Agile delivery. Choose Strategy Designer if you work on customer experience strategy, design workshops, or experience design.

chunks.title: Business Analyst vs Strategy Designer: Which Cert?
chunks.content:
Is the Strategy Designer exam harder than Business Analyst?

Strategy Designer may feel harder because design methods can be abstract and unfamiliar to Salesforce professionals. Business Analyst covers requirements, user stories, and process flows, which may be closer to a consultant's daily work. Strategy Designer also requires knowledge of design research, facilitation, and design sprints.

Can you take both Business Analyst and Strategy Designer?

Yes. The certifications complement each other. Together, they show skills in stakeholder engagement and requirements analysis as well as experience design and customer experience strategy. This combination may be useful on large transformation programmes where user experience matters alongside technical delivery.

How do I find the current Salesforce certification catalog?

Which Salesforce certification should I explore first?

How much does a Salesforce certification cost?

Fees vary by credential, location, taxes, and promotions. Before booking, confirm the current price and retake terms in the issuer’s exam guide and registration portal. Our fee guide is for reference, not a price quote.

How long should I spend preparing?

The Platform Administrator exam covers several areas, including setup, security, automation, data, and reports. You need to choose the right feature for a task; you do not need to write code.

60 multiple-choice questions in 105 minutes, or about one minute and 45 seconds per scored question.

Use timed practice tests to find the topics you need to revisit. An 80%+ practice target can give you room above the listed passing score, but it does not guarantee an exam result.

Salesforce Platform Administrator Exam Format Explained

You can take the proctored Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) exam online via Pearson OnVUE or in-person at a Pearson VUE testing center, registered through Trailhead Academy. Here is the listed format:

60 scored questions, plus up to 5 unscored questions

68% (41 of 60 scored questions)

Multiple-choice & multiple-select

How Many Questions Are Scenario-Based?

Some questions describe a business need and ask you to select a Salesforce feature or action. Others check your knowledge of setup and platform features. Salesforce does not publish an exact scenario-question percentage.

Practise in a free Salesforce Developer Edition org. Setting up features yourself helps you explain when to use them and why they fit a requirement.

Is ADM-201 Harder Than Platform App Builder?

Administrator covers a broad range of setup and administration topics. Platform App Builder focuses more on designing custom apps, data models, and business logic. Your experience will affect which exam feels harder. You can compare these topics before choosing the Platform App Builder exam.

Want a focused strategy? Jump to the scenario decision rules and the 6-week study plan below, or read the detailed ADM-201 vs App Builder comparison before booking your exam.

Platform Administrator Exam Traps and Readiness Checklist

On a scenario question, several features may look useful. Read the requirement carefully and choose the one that meets its specific conditions.

Common traps to avoid

Profiles vs permission sets vs roles

Profiles and permission sets control object/field/app permissions. Roles affect record visibility through hierarchy, not what a user can do.

OWD, sharing rules, and manual sharing

Start with the private/public baseline, then add access through role hierarchy, sharing rules, teams, queues, or manual sharing.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Choosing old automation tools

For new automation, consider Flow. Review older Workflow Rules and Process Builder so you can recognize them in existing orgs.

Dashboard running user mistakes

Check the dashboard’s running user. A dynamic dashboard can show data based on the person viewing it.

Signs you may be ready to book

You can score at least 80% on three timed practice tests without using notes.

You can explain why each answer fits or does not fit, especially for security and automation.

You have practised setting up users, permissions, sharing, reports, dashboards, and flows in a development org.

You can finish a 60-question practice test within 105 minutes and leave time to review.

3 concepts that fail most ADM-201 candidates

OWD vs. profiles vs. roles (three layers, one wrong answer): Organization-wide defaults (OWD) set the baseline record-access floor. Profiles and permission sets control object and field permissions, what a user can see or edit at the object/field level. Role hierarchy opens record-level access upward above the OWD floor, roles can never restrict access below OWD, and profiles cannot override OWD unless View All / Modify All is granted.

Flow vs. legacy automation (end of support for Workflow Rules & Process Builder): Workflow Rules and Process Builder reached end of support on December 31, 2025. For new declarative automation, choose a before-save record-triggered Flow for same-record field updates, an after-save record-triggered Flow for related records or email alerts, a screen Flow for guided input, an approval process for multi-step human sign-off with record locking, and the Migrate to Flow tool to convert legacy automation.

Reports vs. dashboards (cross filters, joined reports & filter limits): Custom report types support up to 4 related objects. A cross filter filters a primary object by the presence or absence of related records (e.g. Accounts without Opportunities) without a custom report type. Bucket fields categorize values on the fly without a formula field. Reporting snapshots schedule report results into a custom object to track trends over time. Dashboard filters only support exact field equality, not contains or starts with.

Why the Salesforce Platform Administrator Certification Matters

The Admin cert is the gateway to most Salesforce roles.

It is often required for Consultant and Developer paths.

2Know the difference between Process Builder, Flow, and Workflow (and when to use each).

3Security is always tested: roles, profiles, permission sets, sharing rules, OWD.

4Practice building reports (summary, matrix, joined) and dashboards from scratch.

5Review standard objects: Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, Case, and their relationships.

•No prerequisite certification is required

•Recommended preparation: Salesforce Certified Platform Foundations

•6+ months Salesforce Admin experience

•Platform Fundamentals or equivalent knowledge

•Data and Analytics Management

•Configuration and Setup

•Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

•Sales and Marketing Applications

Spend roughly 60% of your study time mastering Data and Analytics Management, Configuration and Setup, Object Manager and Lightning App Builder, and Automation, the four domains that together make up 62% of the exam.

Use a Developer Edition org to practice.

Take full-length practice exams under time pressure.

Salesforce Platform Administrator: Key Concepts for the Exam

Objects, Fields & Data Model

Standard objects such as Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, and Case store common business records. Custom objects store data specific to your organization. Review field types and relationships, including lookup and master-detail. A roll-up summary can count or summarize detail records, and a junction object connects two objects in a many-to-many relationship.

Security Model: Profiles, Permission Sets, Roles & Sharing

Org-wide defaults set the baseline for record access. Roles, sharing rules, and manual sharing can grant additional access where applicable. Profiles and permission sets control object and field permissions separately. Practise diagnosing whether a user needs permission to the object, field, or particular record.

Automation: Flows, Approval Processes & Email Alerts

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Record-triggered flows respond to record changes. A before-save flow can update the triggering record; an after-save flow can also work with related records. Scheduled flows run at specified times. Approval processes route work to people for a decision, and email alerts send messages from templates. Practise selecting a tool for each requirement.

Reports, Dashboards & List Views

A report type determines the records and fields available for a report. Tabular reports list rows; summary reports group them; matrix reports group rows and columns; and joined reports combine blocks. Dashboards display report data as charts or other components. Check the running user to understand which data a dashboard displays. List views provide filtered record lists, while report subscriptions can deliver results by email.

Sales & Service Cloud Fundamentals

Lead conversion creates or links an account and contact, and can also create an opportunity. Opportunity stages and probability support forecasting. Service teams track requests as cases, which can arrive through channels such as email or web forms. Review queues, assignment rules, escalation rules, entitlements, and milestones for routing and managing service work.

Official Exam Objectives: Additional Coverage by Domain

Configuration and Setup (15%)

Freezing vs. deactivating users: Users can never be deleted in Salesforce. Use Freeze to immediately block a departing employee from logging in while you reassign their records, queues, and dashboard running-user dependencies; use Deactivate once cleanup is complete to free up their user license.

Permission set groups & muting permission sets: Salesforce recommends minimum-access profiles paired with reusable permission sets bundled into persona-based permission set groups. A muting permission set inside a group removes specific permissions for that group without modifying the underlying permission sets.

Troubleshooting record & field access: Check in order: (1) login history / freeze / login hours / IP ranges, (2) object CRUD via User Access Summary on the user record, (3) record visibility via the Sharing Hierarchy button on the record, and (4) field visibility via field-level security, page layout, and Lightning App Builder Dynamic Forms visibility rules.

Productivity and Collaboration (10%)

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Shared Activities: Enabling Shared Activities allows users to relate up to 50 contacts (alongside 1 primary contact and 1 Related To / WhatId record) to a single task or event.

Sandbox email deliverability: Newly refreshed sandboxes default to System email only, which blocks outbound Flow and workflow test emails. Set Setup → Deliverability → Access Level to All email when testing email notifications in a sandbox.

AppExchange & AgentExchange: Managed packages are upgradable, IP-protected, namespace-prefixed, and count toward fewer org limits; unmanaged packages are editable templates that are not upgradable. AgentExchange offers pre-built prompts, flows, and agent actions you can install.

Agentforce Builder architecture: An agent consists of a role/description, topics (also called subagents, defining the category of job to be done and classification instructions), and actions (Flows, Apex, Prompt Builder templates, or standard actions).

Testing & maintenance: Admins refine topic instructions and action descriptions when an agent selects the wrong action, adjust tone or grounding in Prompt Builder, and validate changes using Conversation Preview in Agentforce Builder for interactive testing and the Testing Center for batch evaluation before activating.

Agent security & the Einstein Trust Layer: Employee agents run in the context of the logged-in user's permissions, while service agents run under a dedicated Agent User whose permission sets govern object, field, and action access. The Einstein Trust Layer enforces data masking, toxicity detection, audit logging, and zero data retention with external LLMs.

Salesforce runs a fixed sequence every time a record is saved. Validation and before-save logic run first, the record is written to the database, then after-save automation (assignment rules, workflow, Flow, escalation) fires, with post-commit actions like emails and async Apex running only after the transaction succeeds.

Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Sections: Topics and Weightings

The four sections weighted at 15% or more make up 62% of the outline. Use the weightings to prioritize your study, and cover all eight sections.

Data and Analytics Management (17%)

Review Data Import Wizard and Data Loader, duplicate management, report formats, and dashboards. Practise importing supported objects, building reports, and checking which records a dashboard viewer can see.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Configuration and Setup (15%)

Set up users and review login restrictions, profiles, permission sets, and permission set groups. Separate object and field permissions from record access, then practise choosing org-wide defaults, roles, and sharing rules.

Object Manager and Lightning App Builder (15%)

Build a custom object and compare formula, roll-up summary, lookup, and master-detail fields. Review validation rules, record types, page layouts, and Lightning pages for apps, records, and the home screen.

Compare screen flows with record-triggered and scheduled flows. Review when a flow runs, when code may be needed, and how approval processes use entry criteria, steps, and final actions.

Sales and Marketing Applications (10%)

Follow a lead from qualification through conversion, and review how its fields map to accounts, contacts, and opportunities. Study opportunity stages, forecasts, products, price books, campaigns, and activities.

Service and Support Applications (10%)

Practise routing and responding to cases using queues, assignment rules, escalation rules, and auto-response rules. Review Knowledge visibility, entitlements, milestones, and the Service Console.

Productivity and Collaboration (10%)

Review Chatter groups and files, tasks, events, email templates, and mobile navigation. Try using compact layouts to show useful record details on mobile.

Learn the basics of Agent Builder, topics, and actions. Compare an agent with a Flow or Apex solution, and review the permissions needed to build and deploy an agent.

6-Week Salesforce Platform Administrator Study Plan (Plat-Admn-201)

Use this six-week plan as a starting point and adjust it to your experience and available time. Pair reading with practice in a free Developer Edition org.

Week 1 — Configuration and Setup (15%): Org setup, user management, profiles, permission sets, OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rules, and field-level security. Practice: create a user, review object permissions, and use field-level security to restrict a field.

Week 2 — Object Manager and Lightning App Builder (15%): Build a custom object and review its fields, record types, layouts, and validation rules. Practise creating a master-detail relationship and roll-up summary, then assign layouts to record types.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Week 3 — Data and Analytics Management (17%, the heaviest section): Compare Data Import Wizard and Data Loader, then review duplicate management, reports, and dashboards. Build a matrix report for opportunity stage and owner and use it in a dashboard.

Week 4 — Automation (15%): Review record-triggered and screen flows, approval processes, and execution order. Build a flow that creates a follow-up task when an opportunity closes, then configure an approval process.

Week 5 — Sales, Service, Productivity, and Agentforce (38% combined): Follow lead conversion and review products and price books. Practise case routing, review Knowledge and entitlements, and explore Chatter, mobile settings, and Agent Builder basics.

Week 6 — Mocks and weak areas: Take a timed 60-question practice test with a 105-minute limit and no notes. Use the results to revisit weak topics; an 80% practice target can provide a margin above the listed passing score.

Decision Rules for Platform Administrator Scenario Questions

When a question describes a business need, identify the required result and any limits before choosing a feature.

Security questions: first decide whether the requirement is about object access (profiles and permission sets) or record visibility (OWD, sharing rules, role hierarchy). Review field permissions separately as well.

Automation questions: compare a record-triggered Flow for record changes, a Screen Flow for guided input, and an Approval Process for sign-off. Review each requirement before choosing.

Data management questions: compare the supported objects and operation size for Data Import Wizard and Data Loader. Data Loader can also support scheduled operations.

Relationship field questions: compare parent requirements, access behavior, and deletion settings. A standard roll-up summary field requires a master-detail relationship.

Top 10 Topics to Review the Day Before

Org-wide defaults: compare Private, Public Read Only, Public Read/Write, and Controlled by Parent

Role hierarchy: review how roles can open record access

Profiles, permission sets, and permission set groups: compare how they grant permissions

Order of execution: review validation and record-triggered flow timing

Record-triggered flows: compare before-save and after-save uses

Data Import Wizard and Data Loader: compare supported operations and limits

Master-detail and lookup: compare parent requirements, roll-ups, and deletion behavior

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide

Approval processes: review entry criteria, submission actions, steps, and final actions

Lead conversion: review field mapping and the records created or linked

Report formats: compare tabular, summary, matrix, and joined reports

Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator Practice Questions (With Explanations)

Test your knowledge with these 20 sample questions. Select the requested number of answers, then check your selection.

Answered: 0 / 20Correct: 0

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Configuration and Setup

Question 1: Which separate system permission is built for transferring multiple records in bulk?

Correct answer: B. Transfer Records

Transfer Records. It lets a user hand off records they don't own to someone else.

View All just grants read access, it doesn't let anyone move ownership.

Modify All is broad and can touch ownership too, but Transfer Records is the dedicated permission built for bulk transfers.

Edit lets you change records you can already reach. It doesn't give you rights over records you don't own.

Question 2: An admin assigns a Sales Operations Permission Set Group to 15 users. Three of them should keep every permission in the group except Delete on Opportunity. How should the admin set this up without touching other groups that reuse the same underlying permission sets?

ACreate a Muting Permission Set inside the Sales Operations Permission Set Group and mute Delete on Opportunity

BClone the underlying permission sets, strip out Delete on Opportunity, and assign those clones individually

CChange the Organization-Wide Default (OWD) for Opportunity to Public Read Only

DRemove the Delete permission from the users' baseline Profile

Correct answer: A. Create a Muting Permission Set inside the Sales Operations Permission Set Group and mute Delete on Opportunity

A Muting Permission Set, added inside that Permission Set Group. It strips out just the one permission for that group, and leaves the underlying permission sets untouched for everyone else reusing them.

Cloning permission sets for a small exception just creates duplicate maintenance work, which defeats the point of a reusable Permission Set Group.

OWD controls record visibility, not object-level permissions like Delete.

Permissions stack across Profile and Permission Sets. If the group already grants Delete, pulling it from the Profile won't take it away.

Question 3: A regional sales director is leaving right now. The admin needs to block their login immediately, but the director is the running user on several executive dashboards and gets active workflow email alerts. What should the admin do first?

AFreeze the user, reassign the dashboards and automation references, then deactivate

BDelete the user record from Setup

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
CDeactivate the user right away and ignore the dependency warnings

DMove the user's Role to an inactive branch of the hierarchy

Correct answer: A. Freeze the user, reassign the dashboards and automation references, then deactivate

Freeze them first. That blocks login instantly without breaking the dashboards or email alerts that depend on them. Once those dependencies are reassigned, deactivate to free up the license.

You can't delete a user record in Salesforce, full stop. Freeze or deactivate are the only options.

Salesforce won't let you deactivate someone who's the sole recipient of active workflow emails or tied to critical automation, and the dashboards would break too.

Moving a Role affects what gets shared up the hierarchy. It doesn't stop anyone from logging in.

Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

Question 4: Which feature lets an admin change the components shown on a Home page?

CLightning App Builder for Home

Correct answer: C. Lightning App Builder for Home

Lightning App Builder. Use it to add and arrange components on a Home page.

Validation rules check what gets entered into a record, they have nothing to do with Home page layout.

Record types control which picklist values and layouts a record gets. They don't touch the Home page.

Profiles control access and settings, not what shows up on Home. That's Lightning App Builder's job.

Question 5: An admin wants a component on a Lightning record page to show up only when the Opportunity's Stage is Closed Won. What should they configure in Lightning App Builder?

AComponent visibility filters

CRecord-triggered Flow

Correct answer: A. Component visibility filters

Component visibility filters, set right on the component in Lightning App Builder. The filter criteria decide when it shows up.

Dynamic Forms is about arranging fields and sections, not about showing or hiding a component based on a condition.

A record-triggered Flow reacts to record changes, it doesn't control whether a page component is visible.

Page activation decides who sees the page at all. It's the visibility filter that decides when one component on it appears.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Question 6: What's the max number of master-detail relationships a custom object can have?

Two. A custom object can carry up to two master-detail relationship fields.

One is allowed, but the real cap is higher than that.

Three is over the actual limit.

It's not unlimited. Salesforce caps this to keep sharing and cascade-delete behavior sane.

Sales and Marketing Applications

Question 7: What can sales managers learn from a Campaign Influence report?

AEmail open rates only

BCampaign spending only

CLead source counts only

DCampaigns that influenced opportunities and closed revenue

Correct answer: D. Campaigns that influenced opportunities and closed revenue

It shows which campaigns actually influenced opportunities, and how much of that closed revenue they can take credit for.

Email open rates are a separate marketing metric, not what Campaign Influence reports on in Sales Cloud.

Campaign Influence ties campaigns to revenue, it isn't limited to spend.

Lead source counts won't tell you which campaigns moved opportunities forward.

Question 8: Which records provide the product catalog and pricing that can be added to an opportunity?

DProduct and Price Book

Correct answer: D. Product and Price Book

Products define what the company sells. Price books and their entries set the prices you can actually use on an opportunity.

Leads matter earlier in the sales process, but they don't carry product or price book data.

Campaigns track marketing activity. You don't need one to add products and pricing to an opportunity.

Opportunities are where products and price books get used, but they aren't the source of the product data itself.

Service and Support Applications

Question 9: Which criteria options can a Case assignment rule use?

BFormula criteria only

CBoth rule criteria and formula criteria

DManual assignment only

Correct answer: C. Both rule criteria and formula criteria

Both. You can build criteria from fields or from formulas.

Assignment rules support formulas too, not just field-based criteria.

They support field-based criteria too, not just formulas.

Manual assignment isn't a criteria type at all, it's just what happens when no rule catches the case.

Question 10: Why assign cases to a queue?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
BSend email notifications only

CGive a team a shared list of cases to claim or work

DDelete cases automatically

Correct answer: C. Give a team a shared list of cases to claim or work

So a team has one shared pool of work to pull from. Assignment rules or other routing can feed cases into that queue.

Queues route and share work. Reporting is a separate feature.

A queue might send a notification, but its real job is giving a team a shared list to work.

Queues organize work, they don't delete anything.

Productivity and Collaboration

Question 11: After a Full Sandbox refresh, an admin tests a record-triggered Flow that's supposed to email external customers. The Flow logs show no errors, but no emails arrive. What should the admin check first?

ASetup → Deliverability → Access to Send Email is set to System email only

BThe Organization-Wide Default on Contact is Private

CThe admin's own user record is missing the Marketing User checkbox

DField History Tracking is off for the Email field

Correct answer: A. Setup → Deliverability → Access to Send Email is set to System email only

Check Email Deliverability first. Every sandbox refresh resets it to System email only, so only password resets and system notices go out, nothing to real customers. Flip it to All email to let Flow and alert emails through again.

OWD is about record visibility. It won't silently swallow an email action that already ran clean.

Marketing User just controls Campaign creation. It has nothing to do with sandbox email settings.

Field History Tracking logs field changes. It can't block an outbound email.

Question 12: Account execs keep hosting kickoff meetings with up to 12 client stakeholders from the same Account, and want one Event logged that shows up on every attendee's timeline. What should the admin turn on?

AShared Activities in Activity Settings

BEinstein Activity Capture

CA custom Junction Object between Event and Contact

DOpportunity Contact Roles

Correct answer: A. Shared Activities in Activity Settings

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Shared Activities. Turn on 'Allow Users to Relate Multiple Contacts to Tasks and Events' and reps can tie up to 50 Contacts to one Event or Task.

Einstein Activity Capture syncs email and calendar from Google or Microsoft. Relating multiple Contacts to a native Event still needs Shared Activities.

You can't build a custom master-detail or junction object on Event or Task, Salesforce doesn't allow that.

Opportunity Contact Roles link Contacts to an Opportunity, not to a Task or Event.

Data and Analytics Management

Question 13: A sales manager wants to know which reps logged the most calls this month. Which report type should they use?

BActivities with Accounts

CAccounts with Activities

Correct answer: A. Tasks and Events

Use Tasks and Events. It pulls calls, meetings, and tasks for everyone in the org, so the manager can see call counts by rep.

Activities with Accounts and Accounts with Activities are about account-level activity, not calls per rep.

Activity History is just a list on a record page. It isn't a report type you can build this report from.

Question 14: With standard field history tracking, how many fields can an administrator track per object?

Correct answer: B. 20 fields

20. That's the cap, on every standard or custom object.

20 is the real number, so 10, 15, and 25 are all wrong.

Question 15: Which report format groups data by both rows and columns, with subtotals where they meet?

Correct answer: A. Matrix

Matrix. It groups by rows and columns and totals up where they cross.

Tabular is just a flat list, no grouped subtotals at all.

Joined puts multiple report types side by side, it doesn't build the row-and-column grid a Matrix report does.

Summary groups rows and subtotals them, but not at row-and-column intersections like Matrix does.

Question 16: The VP of Sales wants a weekly report of active Accounts with zero open or closed Opportunities, and doesn't want the admin to build a new Custom Report Type for it. What feature fits?

AA standard Accounts report with a Cross Filter set to Accounts without Opportunities

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
BA Bucket Field on the Opportunity Stage column

CA Reporting Snapshot that runs every Monday

DA Row-Level Formula on an Opportunities report

Correct answer: A. A standard Accounts report with a Cross Filter set to Accounts without Opportunities

A Cross Filter, right inside a standard Accounts report. It can filter by whether related Opportunities (or Cases, or Activities) exist or don't, with sub-filters on top, no custom report type needed.

Bucket Fields just group values that are already in the report. An Opportunities report only ever shows Accounts that already have Opportunities.

A Reporting Snapshot saves report results into a custom object over time, it's for trend tracking, not for finding parents missing a child record.

A Row-Level Formula works on rows that are already in the report. It can't surface Accounts that are missing from an Opportunities report in the first place.

Question 17: Which record-triggered flow option runs before a record is saved?

Correct answer: D. Before Save

Before Save. It runs before the record hits the database, so it can update or check fields on the way in.

A Platform Event flow kicks off from an event message, that's a different trigger entirely, not a before-save timing option.

After Save runs once the record is already saved, too late to change fields before that save.

After Delete fires once a record is gone. It has nothing to do with saving a record.

Question 18: A flow needs to branch depending on whether an opportunity is Closed Won, then do different things for each case. Which element handles that?

Correct answer: A. Decision

A Decision element. It checks the condition and sends the flow down the matching path.

Assignment just sets variable values, it doesn't route the flow between paths.

Loop walks through a collection, that's not how you branch on a condition.

Get Records just fetches data. It doesn't evaluate anything to decide a path.

Question 19: A company wants an AI agent to answer common customer questions from approved company info, and hand off anything complicated to a person. What should the administrator configure?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (Plat-Admn-201 / ADM-201) Exam Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
AAgentforce with an appropriate topic and actions

BA scheduled Flow that runs once each day

CA dashboard with a filtered report

DA validation rule on the Case object

Correct answer: A. Agentforce with an appropriate topic and actions

Agentforce, set up with the right topic and actions. Give it proper guardrails and a handoff path for anything it can't safely answer.

A scheduled Flow just runs at a set time. It can't hold a conversation with a customer.

A dashboard shows report data. It doesn't respond to anyone.

A validation rule only checks data on save, it can't answer questions or route a conversation.

Question 20: An admin updates a customer-facing Agentforce Service Agent and adds a Flow action that reads a custom Warranty_Status__c field on Asset. In testing, the agent picks the right action but says it can't read the warranty status. What should the admin fix, and how should they confirm it before going live?

AGrant Read on Asset and Warranty_Status__c to the Agent User's Permission Set, then verify with Conversation Preview in Agentforce Builder

BSet Asset's Organization-Wide Default to Public Read/Write and tweak the tone in Prompt Builder

CTurn off the Einstein Trust Layer so the agent can read custom fields without masking

DRebuild the Flow action as a legacy Workflow Rule

Correct answer: A. Grant Read on Asset and Warranty_Status__c to the Agent User's Permission Set, then verify with Conversation Preview in Agentforce Builder

Customer-facing Service Agents run as a dedicated Agent User, kept on a tight leash by design. No object or field access on Warranty_Status__c for that user means the action fails. Grant the access, then confirm it actually works with Conversation Preview before activating.

OWD is about record sharing, not field-level security, and Prompt Builder just manages prompt wording, not permissions.

The Trust Layer masks sensitive data going to the LLM and doesn't retain it. It's not what's blocking an internal Flow from reading a field, and turning off a security control isn't the fix anyway.

Best Way to Pass on Your First Attempt

Review security: Compare delegated administration, sharing rules, Apex-managed sharing, and territory management.

Practise advanced flows: Review subflows, fault paths, scheduled paths, and execution order when several automations run on a record.

Study approval processes: Review field updates, parallel approvals, recall actions, and routing decisions.

Review change management: Compare sandbox types, change sets, and deployment approaches.

Advanced Administrator: Key Concepts

The Salesforce Security Model (Layered Access)

Org-wide defaults set the baseline for record access. The role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing can grant more access. Profiles and permission sets control object and field permissions separately. Practise choosing the right access layer for a requirement.

Advanced Automation: Flow vs Approval Process

Flows can carry out multi-step logic, decisions, loops, and scheduled work. Approval processes route records to people for sign-off and define actions for approval or rejection. Compare both tools when a requirement needs human review or automatic processing.

Delegated Administration and Permission Set Groups

Delegated administration gives selected users limited administration duties without full admin access. Permission Set Groups bundle permissions for assignment; a muting permission set can suppress selected permissions within a group. Practise choosing the right feature for each need.

Data Management: Duplicate Rules, External IDs, and Custom Metadata

Matching rules identify potential duplicates; duplicate rules decide what happens when a match is found. External ID fields help match records during an upsert. Custom Metadata Type records can be deployed as metadata. Review how configuration data moves between environments.

Advanced Reporting: Joined Reports and Cross Filters

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator II (Plat-Admn-301 / ADM-211) Practice & Study Guide
chunks.content:
A joined report combines up to five blocks, which can use different report types. A cross filter selects records based on related records, such as accounts without open opportunities. Also review report types, subscriptions, and bucket fields.

Implicit access comes automatically from ownership and role hierarchy, no admin config needed. Explicit access is deliberately granted: sharing rules, manual shares, and permission set groups layered on top of Organization-Wide Defaults.

How to Pass the Salesforce Advanced Administrator Exam

This exam asks you to choose the right feature for a more complex requirement. Practise explaining why your choice fits and why the alternatives do not.

Advanced Automation: Flows with Custom Metadata

Practise using Custom Metadata Types and Custom Settings to supply values to flows. Review collections, loops, and decisions for multi-step automation.

Change Sets & Deployment

Review what change sets can deploy, their dependencies, and the difference between outbound and inbound sets. Understand how sandboxes support the deployment process.

Advanced Reporting: Joined Reports & Buckets

Use joined reports to bring related views together. Review how buckets group report values and how cross filters select records based on related records.

Complex Security: Delegated Administration

Review what delegated admins can manage. Practise diagnosing access by checking field permissions, page layouts, and record sharing separately.

Review territory hierarchies and assignment rules. Practise explaining how territory assignments affect account access and forecasting.

Question 1: A company wants records to be shared automatically based on set conditions. Which feature should it use?

Correct answer: C. Sharing Rules

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator II (Plat-Admn-301 / ADM-211) Practice & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Sharing Rules automatically share records with users or groups based on record ownership or specified criteria.

Question 2: What relationship must exist before you can add a roll-up summary field to a custom object?

AA lookup relationship to the parent object

BA master-detail relationship where the custom object is the master

CAn external ID field

Correct answer: B. A master-detail relationship where the custom object is the master

A roll-up summary field can be added to the master object in a master-detail relationship.

Question 3: Which feature shows administrators changes made to Salesforce setup?

CField History Tracking

Correct answer: B. Setup Audit Trail

Setup Audit Trail shows setup changes made by administrators during the past 180 days.

Question 4: A company wants to stop users from creating duplicate leads. Which features should it use?

AMatching Rules and Duplicate Rules

Correct answer: A. Matching Rules and Duplicate Rules

Matching Rules identify possible duplicates, and Duplicate Rules can alert users or block duplicate records.

Question 5: Why would an admin create a Permission Set Group?

AAssign multiple profiles to one user

BSet up a permission hierarchy

CRestrict access to objects

DGroup permission sets for easier assignment

Correct answer: D. Group permission sets for easier assignment

A Permission Set Group bundles several permission sets so an admin can assign them together.

Question 6: How do Salesforce record access settings work together?

ASharing Rules set the baseline, and profiles add more access

BProfiles set the access limit, and OWD cannot go beyond it

COWD sets baseline record access; the role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing can expand it, but not reduce it

DOWD and profiles are checked together, and the more restrictive setting applies

Correct answer: C. OWD sets baseline record access; the role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing can expand it, but not reduce it

Organization-Wide Defaults (OWD) set the baseline record access. The role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing can open access further, but do not reduce access below that baseline. Profiles and permission sets control object and field permissions separately.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator II (Plat-Admn-301 / ADM-211) Practice & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Question 7: How do Custom Metadata Types differ from Custom Settings?

ACustom Settings support more field types than Custom Metadata Types

BCustom Metadata Types and their records can be packaged and deployed with Change Sets; Custom Settings records cannot

CCustom Metadata Types belong to one org and cannot be moved to another

DThere is no practical difference

Correct answer: B. Custom Metadata Types and their records can be packaged and deployed with Change Sets; Custom Settings records cannot

Custom Metadata Types and their records can be deployed in packages and Change Sets. Custom Setting records are not packaged and must be recreated in each target org, so Custom Metadata Types suit portable configuration.

Question 8: An admin wants an HR manager to create and deactivate some users without giving them full System Administrator access. What should the admin set up?

ASet up Delegated Administration and give the HR manager a defined scope for managing users

BGive the HR manager the Manage Users system permission through a permission set

CAssign the HR manager the System Administrator profile

DAdd the HR manager to a Public Group with user-management access

Correct answer: A. Set up Delegated Administration and give the HR manager a defined scope for managing users

Delegated Administration lets designated non-admin users perform limited tasks, such as creating or deactivating users within specified profiles and roles.

Question 9: What does Territory Management let a Salesforce admin do?

ASet geographic boundaries for Experience Cloud sites

BSet account OWD based on postal code

CAssign accounts and opportunities to multiple sales territories by rules, for flexible coverage across teams or regions

DLimit lead assignment to regions with assignment rules

Correct answer: C. Assign accounts and opportunities to multiple sales territories by rules, for flexible coverage across teams or regions

Enterprise Territory Management lets admins define territory types and hierarchies, then assign accounts and opportunities to multiple territories for flexible sales coverage.

Question 10: Which report type can show up to five report blocks from different report types in one view?

Correct answer: D. Joined

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator II (Plat-Admn-301 / ADM-211) Practice & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Joined Reports can place up to five report blocks, each based on a different report type, in one view. They are useful for side-by-side comparisons, such as opportunities and cases for the same accounts.

Question 11: A company wants discounts over 30% approved by two managers, one after the other. Which feature should it use?

AAn Approval Process with entry criteria and multiple approval steps in sequence

BA Validation Rule that blocks saving when the discount exceeds 30%

CA Workflow Rule that emails the managers

DA Flow with a Pause element and a record update

Correct answer: A. An Approval Process with entry criteria and multiple approval steps in sequence

Approval Processes support multiple sequential steps, each with its own approver, criteria, and actions. They are designed for workflows such as multi-level discount approval.

Question 12: What does a Muting Permission Set do inside a Permission Set Group?

ASilence Chatter notifications for everyone in a permission set group

BHide custom objects from a permission set group

CRestrict field access to sensitive fields for a group of users

DRemove selected permissions from a Permission Set Group without removing the permission set

Correct answer: D. Remove selected permissions from a Permission Set Group without removing the permission set

A Muting Permission Set suppresses selected permissions from the permission sets in a group without removing those permission sets.

Question 13: Data Loader imports are creating duplicate Account records. Which features can help prevent this?

AValidation Rules on Account

BA unique constraint on the Account Name field

CMatching Rules and Duplicate Rules on Account

DA Process Builder process that checks for existing records before inserting

Correct answer: C. Matching Rules and Duplicate Rules on Account

Matching Rules identify possible duplicates by comparing fields such as name, email, or phone. Duplicate Rules decide whether to block, alert on, or log a possible match.

Question 14: A company needs to import 200,000 records and later match updates using an external system’s unique ID. What field should it add before importing?

CText field with a unique constraint

DFormula field that returns the record ID

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator II (Plat-Admn-301 / ADM-211) Practice & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Correct answer: B. External ID field

An External ID stores an identifier from another system. Data Loader and the API can use it to upsert records, updating matches or inserting new records without the Salesforce record ID.

Question 15: Which feature adds permissions for a user without changing their profile?

Correct answer: A. Permission Set

Permission Sets add access without changing a user’s profile. Each user has one profile and can have multiple permission sets.

Question 16: A regional administrator should reset passwords for one group of users. Which feature grants that scope?

ADelegated administration

BA territory assignment rule

CA public group membership

DA criteria-based sharing rule

Correct answer: A. Delegated administration

A delegated administration group can grant specific user management tasks for selected roles and subordinate roles.

Territory rules group records and support territory assignment.

A public group alone grants no user administration privileges.

A sharing rule governs access to records.

Question 17: A sales leader needs account access assigned by product line and geography rather than by reporting hierarchy. What should the team evaluate?

AA new Salesforce role hierarchy

BEnterprise Territory Management

CAn Account field-level security rule

DA permission set for the sales app

Correct answer: B. Enterprise Territory Management

A territory model can assign accounts and users along sales coverage lines that differ from the reporting hierarchy.

The reporting hierarchy may not match overlapping coverage rules.

Field-level security cannot assign accounts to a coverage group.

An app permission does not determine territory-level record access.

Question 18: A new stage should be set before an Opportunity is saved. The automation changes only that Opportunity. What should the admin use?

AAn auto-launched Flow run daily

BAn after-save Flow with a record update

CA before-save record-triggered Flow

DA screen Flow from a custom action

Correct answer: C. A before-save record-triggered Flow

A before-save flow can update fields on the triggering record in the original save.

A daily flow would set the stage later.

An after-save update adds a write for a change that can happen before save.

A screen flow requires a user interaction.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator II (Plat-Admn-301 / ADM-211) Practice & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Question 19: A release manager wants to validate a change set in production ahead of the scheduled release. What should the manager do?

AActivate the new components in production first

BRefresh the source sandbox after uploading it

CDeploy it during a peak production window

DRun the target validation before deployment

Correct answer: D. Run the target validation before deployment

Validation checks metadata and applicable tests in the target without deploying the change set.

Activation would change production without a validation pass.

A sandbox refresh does not validate metadata against production.

A production deployment applies changes rather than performing a validation-only run.

Question 20: Sales managers need one dashboard that shows each manager their own team’s opportunities according to their record access. What should the admin use?

AA single dashboard subscription

BA dashboard folder with public access

CA dynamic dashboard running as the viewer

DA static dashboard running as the system admin

Correct answer: C. A dynamic dashboard running as the viewer

A dynamic dashboard shows each viewer the records they are allowed to see, which can include team opportunities shared through the role hierarchy.

A subscription schedules delivery without choosing record visibility.

Folder access determines who can open the dashboard, not which rows should appear.

A static administrator context can show records outside a manager’s access.

chunks.content:
A scheduling policy combines work rules and service objectives. Work rules define constraints, such as required skills, territory, or availability. Service objectives rank the resources that meet those constraints, for example by travel time or arrival window. Optimization can improve schedules across appointments. Global optimization can plan a broader set of upcoming appointments, in-day optimization can respond to changes during the day, and resource schedule optimization can improve an individual technician’s schedule. Choose the mode that matches the scope and timing of the problem.

Work Orders, Work Types, and Appointments

A work order describes the service job. A work type can provide a reusable configuration such as duration, required skills, or whether an appointment is created. The service appointment is the scheduled visit. Dependencies can order multiple appointments, while multi-day work supports jobs that span several days. A service crew or multiple assigned resources can support work that requires more than one person.

Assets and Maintenance Plans

Assets represent products installed at customer locations. A maintenance plan can generate work orders on a recurring schedule for one or more assets. Plan settings can control the generation horizon and grouping. Asset history helps teams review prior visits and parts used. Warranty and entitlement information can help determine which service is covered.

Locations can represent warehouses, depots, or technician vehicles. Product items track stock at a location. Product requests ask for parts, transfers move them between locations, and product consumed records parts used on a job. Where configuration supports it, required parts on a work type can help scheduling account for technician inventory.

Mobile Work and Offline Access

The Field Service mobile app lets technicians review assignments, update work orders, capture signatures, and record time or parts. Offline work depends on downloading the required data to the device ahead of time, then syncing changes when connectivity returns. Administrators control what is primed. Mobile flows can add guided steps such as checklists, and status updates help dispatchers see current field progress.
