chunks.content:
Answered: 0 / 15Correct: 0

Question 1: A technician without the required certification keeps appearing in suggestions for electrical jobs. What should you change?

AIncrease the job duration

BAdd a service objective to prefer the account’s technician

CRequired work type skill and skill rule

DTurn off optimization

Correct answer: C. Required work type skill and skill rule

Work Rules act as filters. A skill work rule removes technicians who do not have the required skill.

Job duration does not affect technician skills.

Objectives rank candidates but do not exclude them.

Turning off optimization does not filter out unqualified technicians.

Question 2: The business wants to reduce driving time while still following all scheduling rules. What should be adjusted?

AMinimize Travel objective weight

BThe number of work types

DThe serial numbers on the assets

Correct answer: A. Minimize Travel objective weight

Service Objectives rank schedule options. A higher weight for Minimize Travel tells the scheduler to prefer shorter trips.

The number of work types does not control travel time.

Page layouts do not affect scheduling.

Asset serial numbers do not affect travel time.

Question 3: Several technicians called in sick, leaving gaps and conflicts in today’s schedule. Which optimization should you use?

AResource schedule optimization for one technician

BNo optimization; wait for the schedule to fix itself

CGlobal optimization for the next two weeks

Correct answer: D. In-Day Optimization

In-Day Optimization repairs today’s schedule after changes such as absences or emergencies.

Optimizing one technician will not fix the wider schedule.

Waiting does not fill the gaps or resolve conflicts.

Global optimization plans further ahead and often runs overnight.

Question 4: A job requires two technicians to work together at the same time. How should you schedule it?

ADouble the job duration

BCreate one appointment and expect two people to arrive

CService crew or multiple resources

DSchedule two appointments on different days

Correct answer: C. Service crew or multiple resources

Service crews and multiple-resource scheduling let more than one person work on one appointment at the same time.

A longer job still has only one assigned person.

chunks.title: Advanced Field Service Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
An appointment must be assigned to the needed resources.

Appointments on different days do not let the technicians work together.

Question 5: Installing a pump must finish before an electrical connection job can start. How should you set this up?

AAdd a note to the description

BCreate one very long appointment

CAppointment dependency

DCreate two unrelated appointments

Correct answer: C. Appointment dependency

Appointment dependencies tell the scheduler that one job must finish before another can start.

A note does not affect scheduling.

One long appointment cannot represent two jobs that need different skills.

Unrelated appointments may be scheduled in the wrong order.

Question 6: A building’s lifts need an inspection every three months. How should the work orders be created?

ACreate each work order by hand every quarter

BMaintenance Plan for lift assets

CEmail the team a report

DCreate a Case for each inspection

Correct answer: B. Maintenance Plan for lift assets

Maintenance Plans create work orders on a schedule for the assets they cover.

Manual creation is easy to forget.

A report does not create work orders.

Cases track issues, and each inspection would still need to be created by hand.

Question 7: A technician uses a spare part on a job. How should they record it so inventory stays accurate?

ARecord it as a Product Consumed item on the work order

BDelete the product item

CAdd the part to the work type’s required products

DCreate a Product Request

Correct answer: A. Record it as a Product Consumed item on the work order

A Product Consumed record tracks the part used and reduces the stock at the technician’s location.

Deleting the product item removes its inventory records.

Required Products say what a job needs; they do not record what was used.

A Product Request asks for more stock; it does not record usage.

Question 8: A technician’s van is low on a part. How should they request more?

AAdd the part as a required product on the work type

BRecord a Product Consumed item with a negative quantity

CTransfer the part back to the warehouse

DCreate a Product Request

chunks.title: Advanced Field Service Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Correct answer: D. Create a Product Request

Technicians use Product Requests to ask for parts to be sent to their location.

Required Products say what a job needs; they do not order stock.

Product Consumed records parts used, not parts needed.

A transfer moves stock that has already been approved. Request the stock first.

Question 9: Technicians often work in basements without a signal. What should be set up so the mobile app can still work?

AOffline data priming for the records they need

BMove the jobs to a different service territory

CCreate a mobile flow that saves data to a custom object

DShorten the appointment durations

Correct answer: A. Offline data priming for the records they need

The app downloads needed records before a technician goes offline, then syncs changes after the connection returns.

Changing a territory does not put data on the device.

A flow still needs the required data on the device, so prime the data first.

Appointment duration does not affect connectivity.

Question 10: Technicians must complete a safety checklist in the mobile app before each job. What should you add?

BA new scheduling policy

CMobile Flow on work order

DA new service territory

Correct answer: C. Mobile Flow on work order

Mobile Flows guide users through steps such as a checklist in the mobile app.

Dashboards show data; they do not guide job steps.

Scheduling policies choose technicians; they do not provide checklist steps.

Service territories group work by area; they do not provide task steps.

Question 11: A contractor should receive up to 40 hours of work each week, without fixed appointment times. How should they be set up?

BAs a capacity-based resource

CAs a regular resource with a fixed shift

Correct answer: B. As a capacity-based resource

Capacity-based resources are scheduled by hours or job count within a period, which suits this contractor arrangement.

A location is a place, not a person or contractor.

Regular resources are scheduled into specific time slots.

Assets are equipment at customer sites.

Question 12: A scheduling policy includes Work Rules and Service Objectives. How do they differ?

chunks.title: Advanced Field Service Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
AObjectives remove candidates, then Work Rules rank those left

BRules filter; Objectives rank

CBoth apply only to mobile users

DThey do the same thing

Correct answer: B. Rules filter; Objectives rank

Work Rules are pass-or-fail filters. Service Objectives score the options that remain.

This reverses the roles of Work Rules and Objectives.

Both can apply to scheduling, not only to mobile users.

They have different roles in a scheduling policy.

Question 13: Customers keep booking appointment slots that technicians cannot reach in time. What should you check?

ATravel time settings, such as street-level routing

BThe work order priority

CThe appointment slot length only

DThe scheduling policy’s preferred-resource objective

Correct answer: A. Travel time settings, such as street-level routing

Accurate travel times depend on routing settings and territories. Poor travel estimates can lead to impossible appointment slots.

Priority changes the order of work, not travel time.

Changing slot length does not correct inaccurate travel estimates.

Preferring a technician does not make travel estimates more accurate.

Question 14: A new hire should get only simple jobs during their first month. How can you do this?

ADo not assign them to a territory

BAssign suitable skills and levels

CTurn off their user account

DPut them in a separate org

Correct answer: B. Assign suitable skills and levels

Skills and skill levels help the scheduler match each technician only to suitable jobs.

Without a territory, the technician will not get jobs.

A disabled user cannot do any work.

A separate org would cut the hire off from the rest of the team.

Question 15: A manager wants to know how often technicians solve an issue on the first visit. Which measure should they use?

BOn-time arrival rate

CResource utilization

Correct answer: D. First-time fix rate

First-time fix rate shows how often a job is completed without a return visit. It is a key measure of service quality.

Travel time measures driving, not whether the issue was fixed.

On-time arrival measures punctuality, not whether another visit was needed.

Utilization shows how busy technicians are, not whether they fixed the issue on the first visit.

Before booking, practice setting up accounts and territories, an engagement plan, and a compliant HCP interaction without hesitation.

Agentforce Life Sciences Consultant exam format

The proctored exam has multiple-choice and multiple-select questions. You can take it online or at a test center.

Multiple-choice & multiple-select

How Many Questions Are Scenario-Based?

Many questions describe a life sciences field or medical affairs team and ask how to set up territories, engagement plans, or Agentforce interactions.

Best Way to Pass on Your First Attempt

Learn accounts and territories: Understand how HCOs and HCPs are organized and how territories determine field coverage.

Study engagement plans: Learn how plans and templates support repeatable interactions.

Understand Data 360: Know how it combines customer data and makes that data available to Agentforce.

Follow compliance rules: Know which choices support compliant HCP and HCO interactions.

Agentforce Life Sciences Consultant: Key Concepts

Account and Territory Management

Life Sciences for Customer Engagement organizes healthcare organizations (HCOs) and healthcare professionals (HCPs) under territories. This helps reps see who they can contact and where. Set territories and account hierarchies to match the client’s sales and medical affairs teams.

Engagement Planning and Execution

Engagement plans define a repeatable series of interactions, such as product launch visits or calls and sample drops. Templates provide the reusable steps. Set templates to match approved interaction types, then track each plan as it is carried out.

Data 360 for Life Sciences

Data 360 combines HCP/HCO data, interaction history, and consent in one customer profile. Agentforce can use this profile to personalize interactions. Make sure users only see data they are allowed to access.

Agentforce for Life Sciences

Compliance and HCP/HCO Interactions

Life sciences teams must follow rules about what they can say, to whom, and how they record it. For example, decide whether a rep may edit a completed interaction based on compliance needs as well as general Salesforce security.

How to pass the Agentforce Life Sciences Consultant exam

Questions often describe a field or medical affairs team. Choose a setup that works for the team and follows compliance rules.

Separate 'what the rep sees' from 'what the rep can do'

A rep may be allowed to view an interaction but not change its final record. Check what the user can see separately from what they can edit.

Match the template to the interaction type

Choose an engagement plan template that matches the interaction, such as a sample drop or a medical information request.

Trace data back to Data 360

When a question asks what Agentforce knows about an HCP, check what Data 360 has unified and whether consent allows its use.

Watch for territory and hierarchy traps

If a rep needs access outside their territory, check the territory setup. Do not assume the role hierarchy controls this access.

Don't assume general Health Cloud knowledge transfers directly

This product is designed for life sciences work. Some ideas overlap with Health Cloud, but territory and engagement-plan features are specific to this product.

The rep should review a compliance-sensitive summary before submitting it.

Question 15: What should guide how long a life sciences client keeps interaction records?

AMinimize storage cost alone

CFollow regulatory and audit rules

DFollow the rep’s preference

Question 16: A pharma company wants each rep capped at a fixed number of product samples per month, with no way to exceed that cap. What should the consultant configure?

ASample Limits and Allocations for the rep

BA Territory record with no limit field

BGxP standards appropriate to the region

COnly the rep's personal judgment

DA general data retention policy with no regional variation

Correct answer: B. GxP standards appropriate to the region

Sampling workflows must apply GxP (Good x Practice) standards aligned with regional regulatory requirements for sample distribution.

Sample distribution in life sciences is heavily regulated, not unregulated.

Personal judgment alone doesn't satisfy documented regulatory compliance requirements.

A generic retention policy doesn't address region-specific handling and reporting standards for samples.

A Case record tracks issues, it isn't designed for sample chain-of-custody tracking.

A Content Workspace organizes CMS content, unrelated to physical sample tracking.

An Opportunity tracks a potential sale, not physical sample movement.

Question 19: A compliance team wants periodic verification that recorded sample stock matches what's physically on hand, with discrepancies flagged for correction. What should the consultant set up?

AA one-time manual email reminder sent to the compliance team

Correct answer: D. Inventory Counting, Adjustment, and Audits

A one-time email reminder isn't a repeatable, systematic audit process.

Territory reassignment manages coverage, not inventory reconciliation.

An Engagement Plan template structures visit activities, not sample stock audits.

Question 20: Leadership wants ongoing visibility into total sample stock levels, usage trends, and potential shortages across the whole sales organization. What should the consultant provide?

AA single static spreadsheet emailed out once a year

BVerbal updates shared only in meetings, with nothing written down

CNo reporting at all, since samples can't be reported on

DSample Reports and Dashboards monitoring the full stock lifecycle

Correct answer: D. Sample Reports and Dashboards monitoring the full stock lifecycle

Sample Reports and Dashboards are built specifically to monitor the full lifecycle of sample stock on an ongoing basis.

A once-a-year static spreadsheet can't provide ongoing visibility into trends and shortages.

Verbal-only updates aren't a repeatable, auditable reporting mechanism.

Sample stock is explicitly reportable through configured dashboards, not excluded from reporting.

Agentforce Specialist: concepts to understand

Official credential and exam details

The Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist Exam Guide lists 60 multiple-choice questions, up to five unscored questions, 105 minutes, a 72% passing score, and no prerequisite. Platform Administrator and Platform App Builder are recommended credentials, not requirements. The Salesforce credential page describes the credential as managing and optimizing Agentforce. Check Salesforce certification pricing before registering.

Topics and actions are core parts of agent configuration in the official exam outline. Review how standard and custom topics describe the work an agent handles, and how actions let it perform specific tasks. Consider the agent security context and select an architecture that fits the business need.

Instructions and Guardrails

Instructions guide the agent’s role, tone, and scope. Guardrails set boundaries on what it should not do. In a scenario, identify whether the requirement is asking for behavior guidance or a restriction, then configure the appropriate control.

The Einstein Trust Layer provides security and privacy services for Agentforce, but do not assume every form of data masking is enabled for every agent. Salesforce documents that pattern-based and field-based LLM masking is disabled for agents. Salesforce also documents zero data retention for information sent to third-party LLM providers; audit and feedback handling depends on the supported service and configuration. See Salesforce Help: Trust and Agentforce, Data Masking Limitations in Agentforce, and Agentforce (Default) Considerations.

Data Grounding and Permissions

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist (AI-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Agentforce can use Salesforce CRM data according to the permissions and security context that apply to the agent. Data 360 and Agentforce Data Libraries offer additional grounding options for configured sources, such as knowledge articles, fields, uploaded files, or web sources. These options are not required for every agent data access path. Choose a source that contains the information needed and confirm access is configured. See Salesforce Help: The Building Blocks of Agents and Ground Agentforce in Data.

Channels and Human Escalation

Agentforce can be deployed through supported channels such as Experience Cloud, web chat, Slack, and messaging. The Escalate to Agent standard action can hand a conversation to Omni-Channel for human routing. Learn which setup applies to the channel and when a handoff is appropriate.

User messages enter through a channel; the agent routes to a Topic, runs Actions (Flow, Apex, APIs, prompts). Outbound model calls pass through the Einstein Trust Layer. Data 360 optionally grounds responses in a unified profile. Compare to merge-field grounding from core CRM when you study.

Agentforce Specialist (AI-201) Exam Sections: Topics and Weightings

AI Agents alone is 35% of the outline, and with Prompt Engineering and Data 360 Fundamentals it reaches 75%. Start there, then cover the three smaller sections.

How an agent is built from Agent Script, including Canvas View and Script View; managing deterministic behavior with filters, variables, and template expressions; configuring standard and custom topics and actions; connecting agents to channels such as digital experience, email, voice, and Slack; and understanding the security context an agent runs in.

Week 2 — AI Agents (35%), design: Study the agent types (Service Agent, SDR Agent, custom), use case selection, topic scope planning, and action selection (Flow vs Apex vs Prompt Template). Practice: design a multi-topic agent for a customer service scenario on paper before building it.

Weeks 3 and 4 — AI Agents (35%), build: Build at least two complete agents with multiple topics and action types. For each one, write topic instructions, add a Flow action and a Prompt Template action, configure input and output variables, and set guardrails.

Week 5 — Testing, Deployment, and Maintenance (10%), Governance and Observability (10%), and Multi-Agent Orchestration (5%): Practice the Conversation Preview workflow and Testing Center. Decision Rules for Agentforce Specialist Scenario Questions

Most questions describe a business need or an agent that misbehaves. Identify which part of the agent the scenario is about before choosing an answer.

Action type questions: for data retrieval or updates with no custom code, choose a Flow action. For complex logic, callouts with custom error handling, or limit-sensitive operations, choose an Apex action. For generating a natural-language response from record data, such as summarizing a case, choose a Prompt Template action.

Topic instruction questions: good instructions are specific and bounded. When a scenario describes an agent responding out of scope, the fix is usually to revise the topic instructions with explicit constraints, not to create a new agent or action.

Trust Layer questions: capabilities vary by feature and configuration. Salesforce documents that pattern-based and field-based data masking is disabled for agents, so do not assume all PII is automatically masked, and check the documented retention terms for the specific service.

Access questions: if a user cannot reach an agent feature, check permission sets and feature licensing before org-wide defaults.

Debugging questions: work top down. First check topic routing (is the right topic selected?), then action invocation (are the inputs populated correctly?), then the action itself (does the Flow or Apex return the expected output?).

Three Agentforce Concepts to Distinguish

Use the current Salesforce guide and product documentation to check terminology and configuration details.

1. Topics vs. Actions vs. Instructions: What Goes Where

Topics define an agent's scope, instructions guide its behavior within that scope, and actions are the configured capabilities it can invoke, such as a Flow, Apex, or Prompt Template action. Data sources depend on configuration and access controls.

2. Apex Actions vs. Flow Actions: When to Use Each

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist (AI-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Apex @InvocableMethod actions suit complex data processing, callouts, or operations not possible in Flow. Auto-launched flows suit standard business logic, data manipulation, and multi-step orchestration. If the requirement is achievable declaratively, use a Flow action.

3. Data 360 Grounding vs. Standard Object Data Access

Agents reach Salesforce object data through the access granted to the agent's security context. Data 360 grounding needs explicit setup; it is not automatic, and it is not a prerequisite for every agent data path.

How to prepare for the Agentforce Specialist exam

Expect questions that describe a business need or an agent setup and ask you to choose a suitable configuration. Learn how the parts work together so you can explain why a design fits the scenario.

Route requests to a topic and action

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist (AI-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
A topic describes the kinds of requests an agent should handle; its description helps guide classification. Actions perform work associated with a topic, such as invoking a flow, Apex, a prompt template, or a supported standard action. Choose the action based on the task the scenario requires.

Apply Trust Layer controls carefully

Do not assume the Trust Layer masks personal information in every agent request. Salesforce documents that pattern-based and field-based masking are disabled for agents. Salesforce describes zero data retention for information sent to third-party LLM providers, while audit and feedback handling depends on service and configuration. These services support security and privacy but do not guarantee a generated answer is correct. Review Agentforce masking limitations and Trust and Agentforce.

Choose an appropriate grounding source

Prompt templates can use Salesforce record data through supported merge fields and grounding features. Data 360 can support broader grounding when the needed information comes from configured sources. Identify what data the response needs, where that data lives, and whether the agent has permission to use it.

Plan channels and handoffs

When a scenario requires a human to take over, identify the supported escalation action and routing setup for that deployment. Check channel-specific configuration rather than assuming the same steps apply to every channel.

Question 2: What is a Topic in Agentforce?

AA report category that groups agent dashboards by team, region, and service channel

BAn area that tells an agent which requests to handle and what actions it can use

CA Flow element that runs each time a customer record is created or later updated

DA permission set group that decides which internal users may open Agent Builder

Correct answer: B. An area that tells an agent which requests to handle and what actions it can use

A Topic defines the kinds of requests an agent handles. It includes instructions and the actions the agent can use.

Reports and dashboards are not part of Topic setup.

A record-triggered Flow is a different automation feature.

Permission set groups control access, not which customer requests the agent handles.

Question 3: What is an Agent Action?

AA page layout that arranges the fields and related lists shown in the Agent Console

BAn email alert sent to a supervisor queue each time a Case is escalated by a customer

CA task an agent can perform, such as running a Flow, Apex, API, or Prompt Template

DA Lightning Web Component that displays the conversation in the customer chat window

Correct answer: C. A task an agent can perform, such as running a Flow, Apex, API, or Prompt Template

Agent Actions are tasks an agent can perform. They can use Flows, Apex, external services, Prompt Templates, and standard Salesforce actions.

A page layout changes the user interface; it is not an action an agent performs.

An email sent on escalation is not an Agent Action.

A Lightning Web Component changes the interface; it is not a task the agent performs.

Question 4: Which Salesforce capability gives Agentforce unified customer data?

AMarketing Cloud Journeys

BCommerce Cloud product catalog

Correct answer: D. Data 360

Data 360 provides unified customer profiles that Agentforce can use to add current customer context to responses.

Marketing Cloud Journeys manages marketing automation.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist (AI-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
The Commerce Cloud catalog contains product data, not a unified customer profile.

Slack channels are for communication, not unified customer data.

Question 5: What does the Einstein Trust Layer do for Agentforce?

AProtects customer data, applies privacy controls, and logs AI activity

BReports on agent performance and suggests new Topics for common requests

CRequires a human supervisor to approve every agent response as it is sent

DRuns a custom Flow that rewrites each agent output into the brand's tone

Correct answer: A. Protects customer data, applies privacy controls, and logs AI activity

The Einstein Trust Layer applies privacy controls such as zero data retention at supported external model providers. Pattern-based and field-based PII masking is disabled for Agentforce agents. The available audit records depend on the service and configuration.

Performance reports do not provide privacy and security controls.

Human approval for every answer is not what the Trust Layer does.

A custom Flow can post-process outputs, but it is separate from the Trust Layer.

Question 6: What are Guardrails in an Agentforce agent?

ASharing rules that open record access to a role

BInstructions for what the agent must not do

CLimits on how many messages a channel accepts

DRules for testing different agent versions

Correct answer: B. Instructions for what the agent must not do

Guardrails tell the agent what not to do. They can help prevent off-topic replies, unauthorized promises, and harmful content.

Sharing rules control which records a user can see.

Message limits control system traffic, not agent behavior.

A/B testing compares agent versions; it does not set behavior limits.

Question 7: Where can you deploy Agentforce agents for customer self-service?

AThe internal Service Console, where only signed-in support staff can reach the agent

BReport subscriptions, which email the agent's answers to customers on a schedule

CExperience Cloud, web chat, and messaging channels such as SMS or WhatsApp

DSalesforce mobile push notifications, which customers answer from the lock screen

Correct answer: C. Experience Cloud, web chat, and messaging channels such as SMS or WhatsApp

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist (AI-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Agents can be deployed on Experience Cloud sites, web chat, and messaging channels so customers can get help without first reaching a person.

The internal Service Console alone does not provide customer self-service.

Report subscriptions deliver report results; they are not an agent channel.

Push notifications are not a conversational self-service channel for agents.

Question 8: What is Prompt Builder used for in Agentforce?

ABuilding Lightning record pages that show agent conversations next to the open Case details

BSetting the Omni-Channel routing rules that decide which queue receives an escalation

CWriting Apex test classes that cover the custom actions an agent is allowed to invoke

DCreating reusable prompt templates that combine instructions with CRM or Data 360 data

Correct answer: D. Creating reusable prompt templates that combine instructions with CRM or Data 360 data

Prompt Builder lets admins create prompt templates that combine instructions with live CRM data. These templates can support field generation, record summaries, sales emails, and agent actions.

Lightning Record Pages are built with Lightning App Builder.

Omni-Channel routing is a Service Cloud feature.

Apex tests are written by developers; Prompt Builder is a declarative tool.

Question 9: How does an Agentforce agent choose a Topic for a customer message?

AIt uses a large language model to match the message to a Topic description and scope

BIt matches the Case category picklist value to a record type assigned to each Topic

CIt asks the customer to pick a Topic from a menu before the conversation is allowed to start

DIt selects a Topic at random and escalates to a person after two turns

Correct answer: A. It uses a large language model to match the message to a Topic description and scope

The reasoning engine uses a large language model to identify the customer’s intent and choose a Topic based on its description and scope.

Matching a Case category to a record type is a rule-based approach, not the described intent matching.

Customers do not have to choose a Topic from a menu.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist (AI-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Topic selection is based on the request, not a random choice or fixed two-turn rule.

Question 10: An agent gives incorrect or off-topic replies. What should the specialist do?

ADelete the agent and rebuild it from a template before looking at what went wrong

BReview Topic instructions, Guardrails, and prompt grounding, then test different conversations

CAdd several more Agent Actions so the agent has additional ways to respond to each customer request

DRaise the model temperature so the agent produces more varied wording in its replies

Correct answer: B. Review Topic instructions, Guardrails, and prompt grounding, then test different conversations

Improve the Topic instructions, Guardrails, and prompt templates, then test a range of real conversation examples to find gaps.

Rebuilding discards the setup before you know what needs to change.

More actions do not fix unclear instructions or incorrect grounding.

A higher temperature adds variation and may make answers less reliable.

Question 11: How can an Agentforce agent hand a conversation to a human service agent?

AUse an Agent Escalation Flow that copies the transcript into a new Case comment for the team

BUse a Workflow Rule to create a high-priority Case whenever customer sentiment turns negative

CUse the standard Escalate to Agent action to send the conversation and context to Omni-Channel

DEmail the full transcript to the service team’s shared inbox and close the messaging session

Correct answer: C. Use the standard Escalate to Agent action to send the conversation and context to Omni-Channel

The standard escalation action transfers the conversation and its context to a human agent through Omni-Channel.

The built-in action is called Escalate to Agent.

A Workflow Rule may create a Case, but it does not hand over a live conversation.

An email alert does not transfer the live conversation and its context.

Question 12: What does the Agentforce Specialist exam mainly test?

ADeveloping Apex classes and Lightning Web Components that extend the standard agent interface

BDesigning Data 360 ingestion architecture, including data streams, mappings, and identity rules

CSetting up Service Cloud routing, Case classification, entitlements, and milestone tracking

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist (AI-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
DConfiguring agents, including Topics, actions, prompts, Guardrails, channels, and Data 360

Correct answer: D. Configuring agents, including Topics, actions, prompts, Guardrails, channels, and Data 360

The exam tests how to configure agents: define Topics and actions, create prompt templates, use Guardrails, choose channels, and ground responses with Data 360.

Apex and Lightning Web Components are development topics, not the main focus of this exam.

Data 360 ingestion architecture is a separate architecture skill.

Omni-Channel routing and Case classification are Service Cloud topics.

Question 13: What is the purpose of Agentforce Guardrails?

ASet limits on what the agent can do or say

BMake the agent's replies more creative

CRaise the temperature of the language model

DConnect more data sources for grounding

Correct answer: A. Set limits on what the agent can do or say

Guardrails set limits on the agent’s actions and responses.

Guardrails do not control how creative responses are.

Model temperature is a separate setting.

Guardrails do not add data sources.

Question 14: Which action type can an Agentforce agent use to run a Flow?

DPrompt Template action

Correct answer: B. Flow action

A Flow is one of the standard action types an agent can use to perform tasks.

An Apex action invokes Apex code, not a Flow.

An API action calls an external service; it is a separate action type.

A Prompt Template action generates text from a template; it does not run a Flow.

Question 15: When should you use Data 360 grounding for an Agentforce agent?

AWhen the agent only needs fields from the record the user is already viewing

BOnly for agents on external channels, since internal agents cannot use grounding

CWhen the agent needs unified customer profiles and CRM data for its responses

DOnly while testing in a sandbox, since grounding is switched off in production orgs

Correct answer: C. When the agent needs unified customer profiles and CRM data for its responses

Data 360 grounding gives the agent access to unified customer data so it can provide responses based on that information.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist (AI-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Record data can be reached through standard access and merge fields; that alone does not call for Data 360 grounding.

Grounding is not limited to external channels.

Grounding can be used in production, not only in tests.

Question 16: Before activating an agent for real users, how should a specialist confirm it behaves correctly across a range of scenarios?

ADeploy straight to production and watch for customer complaints

BAsk the agent to describe its own instructions

CSkip testing if the agent was built with a template

DRun it through Testing Center and review the evaluations

Correct answer: D. Run it through Testing Center and review the evaluations

Testing Center runs an agent against defined test cases and scores its responses, so a specialist can catch problems before real users see them.

Deploying untested and waiting for complaints skips the verification step the exam expects.

Asking an agent to describe its own instructions doesn't verify its actual behavior across scenarios.

Templates still need testing, they aren't pre-verified for a specific org's data and configuration.

Question 17: What's the difference between an Employee agent and a Service agent in Agentforce?

AThere is no difference; Salesforce uses the two names for the same agent type in different editions

BAn Employee agent can only use Flow actions, while a Service agent can only use Apex actions

CAn Employee agent runs as the logged-in internal user; a Service agent runs as a dedicated Agent User

DAn Employee agent can be tested in Testing Center, but a Service agent has to be tested in production

Correct answer: C. An Employee agent runs as the logged-in internal user; a Service agent runs as a dedicated Agent User

Employee agents act with the permissions of the internal user who's using them. Service agents, typically customer-facing, run under a separate Agent User whose permission sets define exactly what the agent can access.

They run under different security contexts, which is why the exam tests telling them apart.

Both agent types can use Flow, Apex, and other action types, the distinction isn't about which actions are available.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist (AI-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Testing Center works with both Employee and Service agents.

Question 18: A company wants two specialized agents, one for billing and one for technical support, to collaborate on a single complex customer request. Which concept addresses this?

AA single Topic with far more detailed instructions covering both billing and technical support

BA stricter set of Guardrails that blocks the agent from answering outside either subject

CA longer prompt template that lists every billing and support article the company has published

DMulti-Agent architecture, using open protocols such as MCP or A2A to orchestrate between agents

Correct answer: D. Multi-Agent architecture, using open protocols such as MCP or A2A to orchestrate between agents

When a use case needs more scalability and control than one agent configuration can offer, Multi-Agent Orchestration lets separate agents work together, coordinated through protocols like Model Context Protocol (MCP) or Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication.

Adding instructions to one Topic doesn't give you two specialized, independently-governed agents working together.

Guardrails constrain what a single agent can say or do, they don't coordinate multiple agents.

A longer prompt template doesn't solve a multi-agent coordination problem.

Question 19: An agent was built and tested in a sandbox. What should the specialist account for when moving it to production?

ADependencies such as data sources, Agent User permission sets, and environment-specific settings

BNothing, because an agent built in a sandbox deploys identically to every other environment

COnly the agent's API name, which must be changed to match the production naming convention in use

DWhether production supports Agentforce at all, since agents can only run in sandbox orgs

Correct answer: A. Dependencies such as data sources, Agent User permission sets, and environment-specific settings

Moving an agent from sandbox to production means checking that its grounding data sources, the Agent User's access, and any environment-specific settings all exist and are correctly configured in the target org.

Environments differ in data, access, and configuration, so deployment isn't a simple no-op copy.

A name change alone doesn't address the real dependencies a deployment needs to carry over.

Production is a normal, supported environment for Agentforce agents.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist (AI-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Question 20: A company wants to prevent a specific large language model from being used by any agent in their org, for compliance reasons. Where is that controlled?

AIn the instructions written for each agent Topic

BThrough model access management in the Trust Layer

CBy removing the Prompt Builder app from the org

DNowhere, since every model is always available

Correct answer: B. Through model access management in the Trust Layer

The Trust Layer includes model access management, letting admins allow or block specific models from being used across the org's agents and prompt templates.

Topic instructions shape agent behavior, they don't govern which underlying models are available org-wide.

Deleting Prompt Builder would break prompt template functionality entirely, it isn't a targeted model restriction.

Model access is specifically a governable setting through the Trust Layer, not an all-or-nothing default.

Salesforce AI Associate: Key Concepts

Predictive AI vs Generative AI

Predictive AI uses past data to estimate outcomes. Opportunity Scoring and Lead Scoring are examples. Generative AI creates content from prompts, such as a sales email or case summary. Practice choosing the right type for each use case.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified AI Associate (AI-101): Historical AI Learning Notes & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
The Einstein Trust Layer provides safeguards for AI use, including data masking, secure retrieval, and audit features. Learn how these safeguards help protect customer data, and check the settings and terms that apply to your implementation.

Salesforce's Trusted AI Principles

Salesforce describes five trusted AI principles: Responsible, Accountable, Transparent, Empowering, and Inclusive. Learn how each applies to real decisions, such as protecting data, explaining predictions, and keeping people involved.

Grounding and Hallucinations

Grounding adds relevant CRM data to a prompt so a response can use real customer context. Generative AI can still produce incorrect information, so review its output even when it is grounded.

Data Quality and AI Bias

Duplicate, missing, or outdated data can lead to inaccurate predictions. Biased training data can also affect results. Review the data, test for unfair outcomes, and monitor the model after deployment.

A user prompt is grounded with real CRM data, then sensitive fields are masked before the request ever leaves Salesforce. The external LLM sees only masked data, has zero data retention, and the response is demasked and checked for toxicity before the user sees it. Every step is logged to an audit trail.

Salesforce Certified AI Associate Practice Questions (With Explanations)

Test your knowledge with these 15 sample questions.

Answered: 0 / 15Correct: 0

Question 1: Who can benefit from the AI Associate credential?

BPeople with AI knowledge, whether new to the subject or experienced

Correct answer: B. People with AI knowledge, whether new to the subject or experienced

AI Associate is for people at different levels of AI knowledge, from beginners to experienced users.

The credential is open to people in different roles and does not focus on coding.

You do not need to be an architect to study this material.

The concepts apply to many roles, not just marketing.

Question 2: What knowledge does the AI Associate certification check?

BBasic skills for using data ethically and responsibly with AI in CRM

CReporting skills alone

DIntegration skills alone

Correct answer: B. Basic skills for using data ethically and responsibly with AI in CRM

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified AI Associate (AI-101): Historical AI Learning Notes & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
It checks basic knowledge of responsible and ethical data use for AI in CRM.

The certification focused on concepts rather than programming.

Reporting is a separate skill; this question asks about AI and responsible data use.

Integration skills are outside the main focus of this credential.

Question 3: What does the Einstein Trust Layer do in Salesforce?

AShows AI model performance on a reporting dashboard

BProvides built-in safeguards for customer data and AI prompts and responses

CSecures payment processing for Salesforce transactions

DAuthenticates external AI model providers

Correct answer: B. Provides built-in safeguards for customer data and AI prompts and responses

The Einstein Trust Layer provides data masking, secure data retrieval, toxicity detection, and audit trails to ensure AI outputs are safe, private, and traceable within the Salesforce platform.

A dashboard displays metrics; it does not provide the Trust Layer safeguards.

The Trust Layer addresses AI privacy and safety, not payment processing.

The Trust Layer is not a login protocol for model providers.

Question 4: How do predictive AI and generative AI differ?

APredictive AI uses only numbers; generative AI uses only text

BPredictive AI estimates outcomes from past patterns; generative AI creates content from prompts

CThey work the same way in CRM

DGenerative AI always needs more historical data than predictive AI

Correct answer: B. Predictive AI estimates outcomes from past patterns; generative AI creates content from prompts

Predictive AI (e.g., Einstein Opportunity Scoring) uses historical data to forecast future outcomes. Generative AI (e.g., Einstein Copilot) generates new content from prompts and context.

Both types can use different kinds of data. The key difference here is prediction versus content generation.

The two types serve different purposes in CRM.

The difference is how the systems use data, not a universal rule about data volume.

Question 5: Which of Salesforce's trusted AI principles states that AI models should explain their outputs?

Correct answer: B. Transparency

Transparency means AI systems should be understandable, users and administrators should be able to see why the AI made a recommendation or generated a response.

Accountability concerns responsibility for outcomes; transparency concerns understandable results.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified AI Associate (AI-101): Historical AI Learning Notes & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Fairness concerns equitable treatment, rather than explaining a result.

Safety concerns preventing harm, rather than explaining a result.

Question 6: What does AI bias mean in CRM and machine learning?

AA deliberate choice to make AI favor certain customers

BUnfair patterns in AI results, which can arise from unrepresentative training data

CA difference in response speed between AI and people

DAn optional setting that changes model sensitivity

Correct answer: B. Unfair patterns in AI results, which can arise from unrepresentative training data

Bias can arise when training data does not represent the people affected, causing results that systematically disadvantage some groups. Teams need to monitor and reduce bias.

Bias can arise unintentionally from data or design choices.

Response speed is a performance measure, not the bias described here.

Bias is a potential problem to monitor and reduce, not a feature setting.

Question 7: Why does data quality matter for Salesforce AI results?

AIt matters for dashboards but not AI models

BPoor data can lead to inaccurate predictions, biased results, and unreliable recommendations

CA large amount of data automatically makes up for poor quality

DIt affects processing speed but not accuracy

Correct answer: B. Poor data can lead to inaccurate predictions, biased results, and unreliable recommendations

AI models are only as good as the data they train on. Duplicate records, missing values, and inaccurate data produce unreliable AI outputs. Data governance and hygiene are prerequisites for trustworthy AI.

Poor data can affect AI results as well as reports.

More data does not automatically fix poor data quality.

Data quality can affect whether results are accurate and reliable.

Question 8: What does grounding mean for generative AI on Salesforce?

ASetting a word limit on AI responses

BGiving the model relevant CRM data so its response uses customer context

CConnecting the model to live internet sources

DBlocking the model from accessing Salesforce metadata

Correct answer: B. Giving the model relevant CRM data so its response uses customer context

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified AI Associate (AI-101): Historical AI Learning Notes & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Grounding adds relevant CRM data, such as accounts, cases, or opportunities, to a prompt. This gives the response customer context, although it does not guarantee accuracy.

A word limit changes response length; it does not add CRM context.

This Salesforce example grounds the prompt in relevant CRM data.

Grounding supplies relevant context rather than blocking metadata.

Question 9: Which Salesforce AI principle says people remain responsible for AI decisions?

Correct answer: C. Accountability

Accountability means assigning responsibility for AI outcomes and keeping people involved in oversight, especially for high-stakes decisions.

Transparency concerns understandable outputs; accountability concerns responsibility.

Fairness concerns equitable treatment, not who is responsible for a decision.

Inclusivity concerns the people affected by AI, not who is accountable.

Question 10: What is a generative AI hallucination?

AAn intentionally creative piece of marketing copy

BA plausible response that contains incorrect or made-up information

CA visual error on the Salesforce AI dashboard

DA model deliberately hiding information from users

Correct answer: B. A plausible response that contains incorrect or made-up information

A hallucination is plausible-sounding content that is inaccurate or invented. Grounding, careful prompts, and human review can help reduce these errors.

A creative response is not necessarily a factual error.

A hallucination concerns the content, not a display error.

A hallucination makes up information; it is not deliberate withholding.

Question 11: Which Einstein feature predicts how likely an opportunity is to close?

BEinstein Opportunity Scoring

Correct answer: B. Einstein Opportunity Scoring

Einstein Opportunity Scoring uses past win and loss patterns to score opportunities, helping sales reps decide where to focus.

Einstein Discovery provides broader analytics; Opportunity Scoring scores opportunities.

Einstein Copilot is an AI assistant, not the scoring feature described.

Einstein Vision handles image recognition, not opportunity scoring.

Question 12: How does a prompt template help with Salesforce generative AI?

AIt is a Flow that automatically updates records

BIt combines reusable instructions with CRM data to guide AI responses

CIt is an email template using Contact merge fields

DIt is a permission set for access to Einstein features

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified AI Associate (AI-101): Historical AI Learning Notes & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Correct answer: B. It combines reusable instructions with CRM data to guide AI responses

Prompt templates combine business instructions with CRM data, such as account names or case history, to help produce responses with relevant context.

A prompt template provides instructions for AI; it is not a record-update Flow.

A prompt template can include CRM context, but it is not a Contact email template.

A permission set controls access; a prompt template supplies instructions.

Question 13: What does the Salesforce AI Associate exam mainly cover?

AWriting Python scripts to build custom Salesforce AI models

BBasic AI concepts, responsible AI, and AI uses in Salesforce CRM

CManaging Einstein Analytics dashboards and CRM Analytics datasets

DSetting up MuleSoft connectors for external AI services

Correct answer: B. Basic AI concepts, responsible AI, and AI uses in Salesforce CRM

The AI Associate focuses on foundational AI concepts, predictive vs generative AI, the Einstein Trust Layer, responsible AI principles, data quality, and how AI is applied across the Salesforce platform. No coding required.

The credential focuses on AI concepts rather than writing Python.

Managing analytics dashboards is a separate skill.

MuleSoft integration setup is outside the main focus of this credential.

Question 14: A company wants to protect customer data when it sends prompts to an external large language model. Which Salesforce feature helps?

AEinstein Activity Capture, which stores AI interactions locally

BEinstein Trust Layer, which can mask personal data in prompts and supports zero data retention with model providers

CAn Apex trigger that filters records before every AI request

DField-Level Security, which blocks AI from reading sensitive fields

Correct answer: B. Einstein Trust Layer, which can mask personal data in prompts and supports zero data retention with model providers

The Einstein Trust Layer automatically masks PII in prompts sent to external LLMs and enforces a zero data retention agreement with model providers, ensuring customer data is not stored or used for training.

Einstein Activity Capture records activities such as emails and events; it does not provide this masking feature.

A custom trigger is not the built-in AI safeguard described in the question.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified AI Associate (AI-101): Historical AI Learning Notes & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Field-Level Security controls field access; the Trust Layer provides safeguards for AI prompts.

Question 15: Which Salesforce AI feature uses past data to predict an opportunity’s chance of closing?

BEinstein Opportunity Scoring (predictive AI)

Correct answer: B. Einstein Opportunity Scoring (predictive AI)

Einstein Opportunity Scoring uses historical data to estimate outcomes such as the chance of a win.

Einstein Copilot is an AI assistant, not the scoring feature described.

Prompt Builder creates prompt templates; it does not score opportunities.

Data Cloud provides a data platform; a scoring model is needed to predict a win.

Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder

Platform App Builder tests whether you can design, build and deploy custom Salesforce applications with declarative tools: the data model, Flow and business logic, Lightning App Builder, and deployment. Review Agentforce capabilities and licensing, AgentExchange alongside AppExchange, and Flow Approval Processes. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 73% pass mark, weighted towards Business Logic and Process Automation (32%) and Data Modeling and Management (20%).

Platform App Builder: Key Concepts for the Exam

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder (Plat-Admn-202 / DEV-402) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Data Modeling: Objects, Fields, and Relationships

Custom objects store business-specific data. Master-detail creates a dependent relationship: the detail record inherits sharing from its master, and the master can have roll-up summary fields. A lookup is more flexible, and the related record can exist independently. Junction Objects implement many-to-many relationships using two master-detail relationships. Schema Builder provides a visual data model canvas. Exam scenarios ask you to choose a relationship and object design for a business need. Compare master-detail and lookup based on record dependency, sharing, deletion behavior, and roll-up summaries.

Business Logic and Process Automation

Flow is Salesforce’s recommended tool for new automation. Record-triggered flows respond to record changes; screen flows guide users through a process; scheduled flows run at a set time. Approval Processes manage formal human approvals with defined approvers and criteria. Be able to select the tool that fits a scenario, and recognize Workflow Rules and Process Builder as legacy automation.

User Interface: Lightning App Builder and Page Layouts

Lightning App Builder lets admins arrange standard and custom components on Record Pages, Home Pages, and App Pages. Dynamic Forms place supported fields on a Record Page and allow field visibility rules. Path guides users through stages, and Dynamic Actions can control when actions appear. List Views filter and display records. Know how page layouts differ from Lightning Record Pages and Dynamic Forms.

Mobile Design: Compact Layouts and Navigation

Compact Layouts choose the fields shown in record highlights and other compact record displays; field order matters. Mobile Navigation controls which items appear in the Salesforce mobile navigation menu. Quick Actions provide shortcuts to common tasks. Know which setting controls each part of the mobile experience.

Analytics: Reports, Dashboards, and AppExchange

Report Types determine which objects and relationships are available in a report. Tabular reports list records; Summary reports add grouping and subtotals; Matrix reports group by rows and columns; Joined reports combine up to five report blocks. Dashboards show charts, tables, and other components based on report data. AppExchange offers apps, components, and flows. Review permissions and test a package in a sandbox before installing it in production.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder (Plat-Admn-202 / DEV-402) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
App Builder exam scenarios almost always reduce to one question: can this be built declaratively? Default to Flow, it's faster to build, easier to maintain, and requires no code deployment. Reach for Apex only when the requirement genuinely exceeds what Flow can do.

Platform App Builder (Plat-Admn-202 / DEV-402) Exam Sections: Topics and Weightings

Business Logic and Process Automation, Data Modeling and Management, and Salesforce Fundamentals together make up 70% of the outline. Master those three first.

Business Logic and Process Automation (32%)

Flow Builder is the dominant topic here. A before-save record-triggered flow updates fields on the triggering record without DML, faster and more efficient. An after-save flow is needed when you must query or update related records after insert. Screen flows collect user input through screens and can launch from a button on a record page. Approval processes define entry criteria, submission actions, one or more approval steps, and final actions. Validation rules evaluate before triggers fire. The Summer ’26 outline also asks you to describe the capabilities and use cases for Flow Approval processes, and for using Agentforce to automate business processes.

Data Modeling and Management (20%)

Master-detail requires a parent, cascades delete, and is the only relationship type eligible for roll-up summary fields. Lookup has an optional parent and no cascade delete. A many-to-many relationship needs a junction object with two master-detail relationships. Formula fields are read-only calculated fields. Compare the Import Wizard (up to 50,000 records, no CLI) with Data Loader (bulk operations on any object, command-line capable, schedulable). Know the capabilities of external data sources: Salesforce Connect exposes outside data as external objects, whose API names end in __x, without copying it into Salesforce.

Salesforce Fundamentals (18%)

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder (Plat-Admn-202 / DEV-402) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Prefer declarative tools (Flow, validation rules, formula fields) unless a requirement cannot be met declaratively; the exam rewards the least-code answer. Org-wide defaults set the baseline record access, roles grant upward visibility, sharing rules open access horizontally, and manual sharing allows one-off exceptions. Profiles control object access and app access; permission sets grant additional permissions without changing the profile; permission set groups bundle several permission sets. The outline also covers common scenarios for extending an org through AgentExchange, and reports, report types, and dashboards.

Lightning App Builder has three page types: Home pages, Record pages, and App pages. Component visibility rules hide or show components based on field values or user attributes, with no code needed. Compact layouts control the fields shown in the highlights panel and on mobile cards. Record types control page layout, picklist values, and business process assignment, not field visibility. For mobile, know the difference between global actions, which are not tied to a record, and object-specific actions, which act on or create records related to the one being viewed.

Change sets move metadata, such as objects, fields, and flows, between related orgs, like sandbox to production, but cannot delete components; that needs the Metadata API or a destructive-changes manifest. Sandbox types differ in storage and refresh interval: Developer, Developer Pro, Partial Copy, and Full. Unmanaged packages are fully editable by the installer; managed packages are locked and upgradable by the publisher, as on AppExchange.

4-Week Platform App Builder Study Plan (DEV-402)

Use this four-week plan as a starting point and adjust it to your experience. Pair reading with hands-on practice in a free Developer Edition org.

chunks.content:
Week 1 — Business Logic and Process Automation (32%, the heaviest section): Flow Builder in depth: record-triggered flows (before and after save), screen flows, scheduled flows, approval processes, validation rules, and order of execution. Practice: build a record-triggered flow that creates a follow-up task on Opportunity close, and a screen flow for new case intake.

Week 2 — Data Modeling and Management (20%): Custom objects, field types (formula, roll-up summary, lookup, master-detail), schema design, and Import Wizard versus Data Loader. Practice: design a data model for a custom app with the right relationship types.

Week 3 — Salesforce Fundamentals (18%) and User Interface (17%): Org-wide defaults, role hierarchy, sharing rules, profiles versus permission sets, Lightning App Builder page types, component visibility rules, compact layouts, and record types.

Week 4 — App Deployment (13%) and mocks: Change sets, sandbox types, package types, and deployment order. Take full timed mock exams (60 questions, 105 minutes) and target 85%+ before booking, 10 points above the 73% pass mark.

Decision Rules for Platform App Builder Scenario Questions

Most questions present a business requirement and ask which declarative feature best meets it. Identify the constraint in each scenario before choosing an answer.

Automation questions: the default answer is Flow. If the scenario can be solved by either a record-triggered flow or an Apex trigger, the exam's correct answer is Flow, the “declarative-first” principle. Choose an approval process only when a multi-step human approval with rejection paths is described.

Relationship questions: use master-detail when the child record cannot exist without the parent, when access should cascade from the parent's org-wide default, or when the scenario mentions roll-up summary fields. Use lookup when the child can exist independently. A junction object (two master-detail relationships) solves a many-to-many relationship.

Deployment questions: change sets move metadata between related orgs, such as sandbox to production in the same organization. If the question asks about deleting a component, change sets cannot do it; that needs the Metadata API.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder (Plat-Admn-202 / DEV-402) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Watch for key phrases: “without code” points to a declarative answer, “most efficient” favors a native feature over a custom build, and “only show this component to managers” points to a component visibility rule, not a separate page layout.

3 Concepts That Fail Most Platform App Builder Candidates

These are not the hardest topics; they are the ones where candidates are most confidently wrong. Learn the distinction early.

1. Declarative-First: The Exam Prefers Flow Over Apex

When a scenario could be solved by either a record-triggered flow or an Apex trigger, the exam's answer is Flow. Candidates with real-world Apex experience often choose the code solution; the exam penalizes this. Only choose Apex when the scenario explicitly states something Flow cannot do.

2. Master-Detail vs. Lookup: The Sharing and Roll-Up Difference

Master-detail relationships support roll-up summary fields from child to parent; lookup relationships do not. Master-detail access also follows the parent's org-wide default: if the master record is Private, child records follow that access level regardless of the child object's own setting. A lookup child record does not inherit access this way.

3. Component Visibility Rules vs. Profile-Based Page Layout Assignment

Component visibility rules in Lightning App Builder control whether a component renders on a page, based on field values, user permissions, or device type; they do not control which page layout a profile sees. Page layout assignment is a separate, profile-based setting. If a scenario says “only show this component to managers,” the answer is a visibility rule, not a separate layout.

How to Pass the Platform App Builder Exam (DEV-402)

The DEV-402 exam uses business scenarios to test how you choose and configure Salesforce features. Focus on when each declarative tool fits a requirement.

Data Modelling Scenarios

Use master-detail when the detail record depends on its master. Deleting a master deletes its detail records, and roll-up summary fields require a master-detail relationship. Use lookup when the related record can exist independently; lookup deletion behavior can be configured. A junction object uses two master-detail relationships to model a many-to-many relationship.

Automation Decision Tree

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder (Plat-Admn-202 / DEV-402) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
For new automation, Salesforce recommends Flow. Record-triggered flows can update fields, create records, and automate work across related records. Approval Processes manage structured human approvals. Workflow Rules and Process Builder are legacy tools; know their capabilities, but use Flow for new automation unless the question gives a specific constraint.

Security and Visibility Layering

Understand the difference between record access and field access. Organization-Wide Defaults set baseline record access; role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing can open record access further. Profiles and permission sets control object and field permissions. Page layouts affect how fields appear, not whether a user has permission to access them. Record Types can provide different business processes, picklist values, and page layouts.

App Design and Lightning App Builder

Know the difference between App Pages, Record Pages, and Home Pages in Lightning App Builder. Dynamic Forms let admins place supported fields on a Record Page and set visibility rules. Standard apps, tabs, and navigation items can be configured without code.

Look for constraints such as “without code,” which points to declarative tools. Compare standard Salesforce features with custom solutions, and distinguish field permissions from record sharing when a scenario limits access. The current listed passing score is 73%. Question 1: By default, which relationship type deletes detail records when its master is deleted?

BMaster-Detail Relationship

DHierarchical Relationship

Correct answer: B. Master-Detail Relationship

Deleting a master record also deletes its related detail records. Lookup relationships normally clear the lookup value or block deletion, though some custom lookup fields can be configured for cascade deletion.

A lookup usually clears its value or prevents the parent from being deleted. Cascade deletion is an optional setting for eligible custom lookups, not the standard behavior.

External Lookup links to data outside Salesforce and has no cascade delete behavior on internal records.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder (Plat-Admn-202 / DEV-402) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Hierarchical Relationship is a special lookup limited to the User object; it does not cascade delete.

Question 2: What is the default limit of roll-up summary fields on an object?

Correct answer: B. 25

The default limit is 25 per object. Salesforce Support can increase it to a maximum of 40.

The default limit is 25, not 10.

40 is the maximum after an approved increase, not the default.

There is a limit: the default is 25 and the maximum after an increase is 40.

Question 3: A user wants to display different page layouts based on the record type. What should be configured?

BPage Layout Assignment

CRecord Type Assignment

Correct answer: B. Page Layout Assignment

Page Layout Assignment allows you to assign different page layouts to different record types and profiles.

Profile Assignment alone controls object/field access, not which page layout displays per record type.

Record Type Assignment controls which record types a profile can use, but the layout itself is set via Page Layout Assignment.

Permission Set grants additional access, it doesn’t control which page layout is shown for a record type.

Question 4: Which tool is recommended for a new field update when a record is created or edited?

Correct answer: B. Flow

Flow (Record-Triggered Flow) is the recommended tool for automating field updates when records are created or edited.

Workflow Rules can update fields, but Salesforce recommends Flow for new automation.

Approval Process routes records for approval, it isn’t designed for straightforward criteria-based field updates.

"All of the above" is wrong because Salesforce’s current guidance is to build new field-update automation in Flow, not treat all three as equally recommended.

Question 5: Why would you create a Junction Object?

ACreate a one-to-many relationship

BCreate a many-to-many relationship

CStore historical data

DConnect external systems

Correct answer: B. Create a many-to-many relationship

A Junction Object uses two master-detail relationships to connect records in a many-to-many relationship.

A single master-detail or lookup relationship already handles a one-to-many relationship, no junction object is needed for that.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder (Plat-Admn-202 / DEV-402) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Storing historical data is a different concept (e.g., field history tracking), unrelated to junction objects.

Linking external systems is handled by external objects/integration tools, not a junction object, which connects two internal Salesforce objects.

Question 6: How many master-detail relationships can a custom object have at most?

A custom object can have up to two master-detail relationships.

A single master-detail relationship is allowed, but the actual platform maximum is higher than 1.

3 exceeds the actual platform limit for master-detail relationships on a custom object.

The limit is not unlimited: Salesforce caps master-detail relationships specifically to preserve sharing and cascade-delete integrity.

Question 7: Which Lightning App Builder component displays all related lists on a record page?

Correct answer: A. Related Lists

The Related Lists component displays the related lists included on the record page. For example, it can show Contacts or Opportunities on an Account page.

Related Record shows a single linked record's fields, not a list of multiple related child records.

Record Detail displays the current record's own fields, not related child records.

List View shows a filtered list of records on a tab or app page, not related records embedded within a specific record page.

Question 8: A developer needs a read-only field that calculates a value from other fields. Which type should they choose?

Correct answer: A. Formula

Formula fields automatically calculate values based on other fields, expressions, or functions. They are read-only and recalculate whenever referenced fields change.

Auto Number generates a sequential unique value on record creation, it doesn’t calculate values from other fields.

A plain Text field stores manually entered or set text; it has no built-in calculation capability.

A plain Number field stores a value directly; it can’t automatically derive that value from other fields.

Question 9: Besides page layout assignment, what can Record Types control on the same object?

AField-level security settings

BDifferent business processes and picklist values

CRecord-level access to records

DAutomatic record creation

Correct answer: B. Different business processes and picklist values

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder (Plat-Admn-202 / DEV-402) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Record Types can provide different business processes and picklist values for the same object. Page layouts can also be assigned by record type and profile.

Field-level security is controlled with profiles and permission sets, not Record Types.

Record-level access is controlled with organization-wide defaults, roles, and sharing, not Record Types.

Automating record creation is handled by Flow or other automation tools, not Record Types.

Question 10: Which tool does Salesforce recommend for new automation that creates related records?

Correct answer: C. Flow

Flow (Record-Triggered Flow) is the recommended tool for creating records in related objects. Process Builder can create related records, but Salesforce recommends Flow for new automation.

Workflow Rule cannot create records at all, it's limited to field updates, email alerts, tasks, and outbound messages.

Process Builder can create related records, but Salesforce no longer supports it and recommends Flow for new automation.

"All of the above" is wrong because Workflow Rule specifically cannot create records, it doesn't belong in this group.

Question 11: An admin needs to limit which fields users can view or edit. Which feature should they use?

AField-Level Security

Correct answer: A. Field-Level Security

Field-Level Security (FLS) controls whether users can view or edit specific fields, regardless of record-level access.

Sharing Rules control record-level access (which records users can see), not field-level visibility.

Record Types control business process and picklist variation, not field visibility by profile.

Page Layouts control which fields are displayed and their arrangement, but they don't enforce security, a field can still be exposed via API even if hidden from a layout.

Question 12: Which feature is supported by a master-detail relationship but not a standard lookup relationship?

ALookup supports roll-up summaries, but master-detail does not

BMaster-detail supports roll-up summary fields; lookup does not

CThere is no difference

DLookup is only for standard objects

Correct answer: B. Master-detail supports roll-up summary fields; lookup does not

A master-detail relationship supports roll-up summary fields on the master. A standard lookup relationship does not.

This reverses the roll-up summary behavior of these relationship types.

There is a real, meaningful difference between the two relationship types, this option denies it entirely.

Lookup relationships can be used on both standard and custom objects, they aren't restricted to standard objects only.

Question 13: Which Lightning App Builder component displays fields from one related record?

Correct answer: B. Related Record

The Related Record component displays a single related record and allows navigation to that record's detail page.

Related List–Single displays child records rather than fields from one related record.

Record Detail shows the current record's own fields, not a related record to navigate to.

'Navigation Menu' isn't a Lightning App Builder record-page component, it's a separate Experience Cloud/app-level navigation feature.

Question 14: A company wants to detect and block duplicate records. Which features work together to do this?

Correct answer: D. Both B and C

Duplicate Rules work with Matching Rules to prevent or alert users about duplicate records. Matching Rules define what constitutes a duplicate, and Duplicate Rules define what action to take.

Validation Rules alone don't detect duplicates, they enforce data-quality logic on individual field values, not cross-record matching.

Duplicate Rules alone need Matching Rules to define what counts as a duplicate, one without the other is incomplete.

Matching Rules alone only identify potential duplicates; they need Duplicate Rules to define the action (block, alert, report) taken when a match is found.

Question 15: Which Lightning App Builder component lets an admin filter a related list on a record page?

ARelated List Quick Links

CDynamic Related List–Single

Correct answer: C. Dynamic Related List–Single

Dynamic Related List–Single lets an admin add filters to a related list in Lightning App Builder.

Related List Quick Links provides links to related lists, not configured list filters.

Related Record displays a related record, not a filtered list.

Record Detail displays fields on the current record, not a filtered related list.

Question 16: An admin builds and tests a new app in a sandbox. Which tool should they use to move that work into production?

Correct answer: A. A change set
