A change set moves metadata, like objects, fields, and flows, from one org to a related org, such as sandbox to production.

A validation rule checks data on save, it isn't a deployment tool.

A dashboard displays report data, it has nothing to do with moving metadata between orgs.

A permission set grants access, it doesn't deploy configuration changes.

Question 17: A team wants to remove a field that was deployed by mistake. Can an inbound change set do that?

ANo, change sets can't delete components, that needs the Metadata API or a destructive-changes package

BYes, change sets can delete any component

COnly an admin with the System Administrator profile can delete it this way

DYes, but only on the first deployment

Correct answer: A. No, change sets can't delete components, that needs the Metadata API or a destructive-changes package

Change sets only add or update components. Removing something already deployed needs the Metadata API or Change Set Deployments with a destructive-changes manifest.

Change sets are an additive tool, deletion isn't one of their capabilities.

Profile has nothing to do with what a change set itself is capable of.

The limitation isn't about which deployment attempt it is, change sets simply don't delete.

Question 18: A sales manager should see every Opportunity owned by their direct reports, but reps shouldn't see each other's records. What combination controls this?

AOrganization-wide defaults set to Private, with the role hierarchy giving managers visibility upward

BA single validation rule on Opportunity

CA custom report type

DA Lightning page component visibility rule

Correct answer: A. Organization-wide defaults set to Private, with the role hierarchy giving managers visibility upward

Setting the OWD to Private creates the baseline (reps only see their own), and the role hierarchy then opens visibility upward to managers over their reports, without opening it sideways between reps.

A validation rule checks data on save, it doesn't control record visibility.

A custom report type determines what fields and objects a report can use, it doesn't grant record access.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder (Plat-Admn-202 / DEV-402) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Component visibility rules control what's shown on a Lightning page, not which records a user can see.

Question 19: A team needs to import 200,000 Account records from a CSV file using a repeatable, schedulable process. Which tool fits?

Correct answer: A. Data Loader

Data Loader handles bulk operations on any object, has no 50,000-record cap, and can run from the command line, which supports scheduling.

Import Wizard supports standard objects and some custom objects but caps out at 50,000 records and has no command-line or scheduling option.

Report Builder creates and filters reports, it doesn't import data.

Schema Builder visualizes and edits the data model, it isn't a data-loading tool.

Question 20: A discount request over $10,000 needs sign-off from a manager, then a director, before the Opportunity can proceed. Which feature fits this requirement?

BA Record-Triggered Flow

DComponent visibility rules

Correct answer: A. An Approval Process

An Approval Process defines entry criteria, a sequence of approval steps, and the actions to take on approval or rejection, exactly the multi-step human sign-off described here.

A Record-Triggered Flow automates logic without a human approval step built in, it's not designed for sequential sign-off.

A validation rule blocks a save based on a condition, it doesn't route a record for approval.

Component visibility rules control what's shown on a page, they have nothing to do with approval routing.

What is covered on the Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder (DEV-402) exam?

The Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder (DEV-402) exam (formerly Salesforce Certified App Builder) has 5 sections. What is the difference between Platform Administrator and Platform App Builder certifications?

Platform Administrator focuses on day-to-day administration, security, and user management. Platform App Builder focuses on declarative development, building custom applications using clicks, not code. App Builder is ideal for those who want to build custom apps without programming.

What is the DEV-402 exam fee and passing score in Summer '26?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Application Architect Credential Path & Domain Readiness Guide
chunks.content:
A common order is Platform App Builder, Platform Developer I, Data Architect, then Sharing and Visibility Architect. Study for each exam separately and use that exam’s practice questions.

How the Application Architect credential works

You do not book an Application Architect exam. You earn the credential by passing four separate exams:

How Many Questions Are Scenario-Based?

The two architect exams often use scenarios. They may describe a business need and ask you to choose a data model, access design, or build approach.

Best Way to Pass on Your First Attempt

Start with Platform App Builder: Study declarative tools, data modeling, and automation basics.

Then take Platform Developer I: Study Apex, SOQL, triggers, and tests. This exam also counts toward System Architect.

Then take Data Architect: Study data modeling, large data volumes, master data management, and migration.

Finish with Sharing and Visibility Architect: Study org-wide defaults, role hierarchy, sharing rules, and external access.

Application Architect: Key Concepts

Data Modelling and Large Data Volumes

From the Data Architect exam: choose relationships based on how the records should work. With a Lookup, each record can exist on its own. With Master-Detail, the child depends on the parent, inherits its sharing, and can use roll-up summary fields. Deleting a parent also deletes its children. External Objects show data that stays in another system. Big Objects store very large amounts of history that is rarely changed. For large tables, keep queries selective by filtering on indexed fields. Watch for data skew, such as one parent with too many children, and plan when to archive old data.

Choosing Between Configuration and Code

Salesforce recommends using configuration when it can meet the need. Flow handles most automation, including record updates, guided screens, and scheduled work. Use code when logic is complex, you need to process very large volumes, or configuration cannot do the task. Configuration is usually easier to maintain and can adapt to upgrades. Code requires tests and careful deployment, and someone must maintain it. When an answer offers a standard feature and custom code, consider the standard feature first.

Designing Record Access

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Application Architect Credential Path & Domain Readiness Guide
chunks.content:
From the Sharing and Visibility exam: record access has layers, and each layer can grant more access. Org-Wide Defaults set the starting level; begin with the most restricted level the business needs. The Role Hierarchy can give managers access to their team’s records. Sharing Rules grant access by record owner or field values. Teams and Manual Sharing grant access to specific records. Apex Managed Sharing handles rules that configuration cannot express. For Experience Cloud customers, Sharing Sets can grant access. Profiles and Permission Sets control object and field permissions before record sharing is applied.

Integration Patterns for Applications

Use the integration pattern that fits the need. Use a synchronous callout when a user needs the answer before continuing. Use Platform Events or Change Data Capture when another system only needs to know that something changed. Use the Bulk API for large scheduled data loads. Use Salesforce Connect when data should remain in its source system. Store secrets in Named Credentials, not in code. Remember the limits of 100 callouts per transaction and 120 seconds total. Move slow work to asynchronous Apex so users do not have to wait.

Build Quality: Testing, Deployment and Governance

The four exams all expect good development practices. Apex needs at least 75% test coverage for production, and tests should create their own data and check real results. Use sandboxes to build and test changes before production. Larger teams may use source control, Salesforce CLI, or DevOps Center. Design Apex for bulk processing so it works with 200 records, not just one. Track org limits and technical debt. Record why you chose a data model or access design so others can understand it later.

This is not a single exam: Salesforce auto-awards the credential once all four component certifications below are passed, in any order.

How to earn Application Architect

Prepare for the four component exams one at a time. These ideas appear across the exam set.

Data Modelling Choices

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Application Architect Credential Path & Domain Readiness Guide
chunks.content:
Use Master-Detail when a child depends on its parent, needs roll-up summaries, or should inherit access. Use Lookup when records stand on their own. Use External Objects when data should stay in another system.

Start with the most restricted org-wide default needed. Grant more access with the role hierarchy and sharing rules. Use Apex sharing only when configuration cannot express the rule.

Configuration Before Code

Consider Flow first. Use code when the logic is complex, the volume is large, or Flow cannot meet the need. Be ready to explain the choice.

If a user needs the response before continuing, use a synchronous callout. Use events to notify other systems. Use Bulk API for large scheduled loads. Use Salesforce Connect when data should stay in its source.

Keep large queries selective, avoid skewed record ownership, and plan to archive data before tables grow too large.

Salesforce Certified Application Architect Practice Questions (With Explanations)

Test your knowledge with these 20 sample questions.

Answered: 0 / 20Correct: 0

Question 1: An object will have 40 million records, and users need to filter by account. What should the architect plan?

AUse selective filters with indexed fields

BCopy records into nightly summary objects

CStore older records in a separate Salesforce org

DBlock reports on the object

Correct answer: A. Use selective filters with indexed fields

Large-volume queries need selective filters on indexed fields to avoid timeouts.

Summary copies help reporting but do not make the base object queryable.

Splitting across orgs fragments the data and complicates every query.

Blocking reporting avoids the symptom rather than solving it.

Question 2: What is a skinny table used for?

ARecord audit history

BArchive records from the main object

CValidate a very large number of records

DFaster reads across commonly queried fields

Correct answer: D. Faster reads across commonly queried fields

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Application Architect Credential Path & Domain Readiness Guide
chunks.content:
A skinny table stores a small set of frequently used fields so Salesforce can read them without joining standard and custom field tables.

Field history tracking records changes.

Archiving is a separate data lifecycle concern.

Validation is unrelated to read performance.

Question 3: Users need read access to records they do not own based on a field value. What should the architect use?

AManual sharing for every record

BCriteria-based Sharing Rules

CMake the object public with OWD

DPut all users under one role

Correct answer: B. Criteria-based Sharing Rules

Criteria-based Sharing Rules grant access automatically when records match field values.

Manual sharing does not scale and depends on owners remembering.

Making the object public grants far more access than required.

Flattening the hierarchy breaks the management visibility it provides.

Question 4: When designing an object’s record-access model, what does the org-wide default establish before the other sharing mechanisms are applied?

AThe total number of records allowed

BWhich profiles can create records

CStarting record access before sharing

DWhich fields appear on the page layout

Correct answer: C. Starting record access before sharing

OWD is the baseline record-access level in the model. The hierarchy and sharing rules can grant additional access, while field visibility is controlled separately.

There is no record cap set by the default.

Object create permission comes from the profile or permission set.

Field visibility is governed by field-level security and layouts.

Question 5: A requirement could use Flow or Apex. What should decide which one to use?

AHow many Flows and Apex classes already exist

BWhich approach the team prefers

CWhether configuration can meet the requirement

DWhether a business or technical user requested it

Correct answer: C. Whether configuration can meet the requirement

Use configuration when it can meet the need. Use Apex when configuration cannot or when the requirement calls for code.

Existing counts say nothing about what suits this requirement.

Team preference is not an architectural criterion.

Who asked for it does not determine how it should be built.

Question 6: What is one cost of choosing Apex when configuration could do the job?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Application Architect Credential Path & Domain Readiness Guide
chunks.content:
BMore maintenance and testing

CHigher Salesforce license fees

Correct answer: B. More maintenance and testing

Apex needs tests, review, careful deployment, and ongoing maintenance.

Storage is unaffected by implementation choice.

Licensing does not change because logic is coded.

Reporting continues to work normally.

Question 7: An integration must notify an outside system when an order is approved without making the user wait. What pattern fits?

ACall the system synchronously during approval

BExport approved orders in a nightly batch

CPublish an event asynchronously

DAsk an admin to export each order

Correct answer: C. Publish an event asynchronously

An event can notify another system asynchronously, keeping it separate from the user’s transaction.

A synchronous callout makes the user wait on an external system's availability.

A nightly batch delays the notification by up to a day.

Manual export is neither timely nor reliable.

Question 8: When should an architect choose a synchronous integration?

AWhen call volume will be very high

BWhen the outside system is slow

CWhen the receiving system is often unavailable

DWhen the user needs the response to continue

Correct answer: D. When the user needs the response to continue

Use a synchronous call when the user cannot continue without a response, such as a credit check or real-time price.

High volume favours asynchronous handling.

A slow system is an argument against making the user wait.

Poor availability is a reason not to couple synchronously.

Question 9: A manager needs access to records owned by their whole team. What is the simplest fit?

ARole hierarchy with access to subordinate records

BManual sharing by each team member

CA separate Sharing Rule for each manager

DView All permission on the object

Correct answer: A. Role hierarchy with access to subordinate records

The Role Hierarchy can give managers access to records owned by people below them.

Manual sharing depends on individuals remembering every time.

Per-manager rules multiply and go stale as the organisation changes.

View All grants access to every record, far beyond the team.

Question 10: What should an architect learn before designing record access?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Application Architect Credential Path & Domain Readiness Guide
chunks.content:
AWho must see each record and what must stay private

BThe number of permission sets in the org

CThe number of profiles from the last implementation

DWhich reporting tool the client will use

Correct answer: A. Who must see each record and what must stay private

Start access design with the business rules for who should see which records and what must remain private.

Existing counts describe the present rather than the requirement.

Legacy profile counts rarely reflect what is actually needed.

Reporting tooling is downstream of the access model.

Question 11: Why should an architect care about test coverage beyond the platform minimum?

AIt controls how many deployments can run each month

BIt controls whether reports can run

CIt increases storage

DTests help make future changes safer

Correct answer: D. Tests help make future changes safer

Good tests help teams change the system later without breaking existing behavior.

Deployment frequency is not governed by coverage.

Reporting is unaffected.

Storage is unrelated to test coverage.

Question 12: What does a Master-Detail relationship require?

AIndependent sharing for both objects

BCascade delete and inherited record access

CReparenting at any time

DOnly one Master-Detail relationship per object

Correct answer: B. Cascade delete and inherited record access

In Master-Detail, the child depends on the parent, inherits its record access, and can be deleted with the parent.

The detail object inherits the master's sharing rather than having its own.

Reparenting is restricted unless explicitly allowed.

An object may have more than one master-detail relationship.

Question 13: When is a Lookup relationship better than Master-Detail?

AWhen the child must inherit access from the parent

BWhen the child must exist without the parent

CWhen the parent needs standard roll-up summaries

DWhen deleting the parent must delete its children

Correct answer: B. When the child must exist without the parent

Lookup is a better fit when the child record must be able to exist independently.

Inherited access is a master-detail behaviour.

Standard roll-up summaries require master-detail.

Cascade delete is a master-detail behaviour.

Question 14: Why use a deployment pipeline with separate environments?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Application Architect Credential Path & Domain Readiness Guide
chunks.content:
ATo let more admins edit production at once

BTo check changes before they reach production

CTo increase the org’s API limit

DTo remove the need for tests

Correct answer: B. To check changes before they reach production

Separate environments let a team build, test, and review a change before it reaches production.

Concurrent production editing is the risk a pipeline reduces.

API limits are unrelated to deployment process.

Tests remain necessary and are part of what the pipeline runs.

Question 15: How do you earn the Application Architect credential?

AHold the four required certifications

BPass one scenario-based exam

CComplete Trailhead superbadges and projects

DPresent a design to an architect panel

Correct answer: A. Hold the four required certifications

You earn Application Architect by holding Platform App Builder, Platform Developer I, Data Architect, and Sharing and Visibility Architect. There is no separate exam.

There is no examination for this credential itself.

Superbadges are not what earns it.

Panel defence is part of the CTA review board, not this credential.

Question 16: A detail record must inherit its parent’s record access and be deleted when the parent is deleted. Which relationship fits?

Correct answer: D. Master-detail

Master-detail makes the child dependent on the parent, with inherited access and cascade delete.

Lookup records have independent sharing.

External lookup connects to an external object.

Indirect lookup maps external data to Salesforce records.

Question 17: A team needs to restrict field visibility for a group of users without changing their record access. Which control should it use?

BOrganization-Wide Defaults

CField-level security

Correct answer: C. Field-level security

Field-level security controls access to fields independently of record sharing.

Sharing rules grant record access.

OWD sets baseline record-level access.

Role hierarchy affects record access.

Question 18: An Apex trigger processes many records at once. Which design choice helps avoid governor-limit failures?

AQuery and update records in collections outside loops

BRun one SOQL query for each record

CPerform a DML statement inside each loop iteration

DUse a synchronous callout for every record

Correct answer: A. Query and update records in collections outside loops

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Application Architect Credential Path & Domain Readiness Guide
chunks.content:
Bulk processing uses collection-based queries and DML outside loops to reduce limit consumption.

Per-record queries can exceed SOQL limits.

Per-record DML can exceed DML limits.

Per-record callouts add latency and do not solve bulk limit usage.

Question 19: A business process needs declarative record updates and a guided user interaction. Which platform tool should the architect assess first?

BVisualforce controller

Correct answer: D. Flow

Flow supports declarative record automation and guided screen experiences.

Apex is code and may be unnecessary when Flow meets the need.

Visualforce controllers are not the default declarative option.

Middleware is unnecessary for an in-org user flow.

Question 20: A custom object has very large data volumes and reports time out on broad queries. What should the architect evaluate first?

AA master-detail relationship for every related object

CSelective filters and appropriate indexed fields

DA dashboard refresh schedule

Correct answer: C. Selective filters and appropriate indexed fields

Selective filters and indexes can help queries target smaller result sets at scale.

Relationship type alone does not solve query selectivity.

Page layouts do not affect query performance.

Refresh scheduling does not address the underlying query design.

B2B Commerce Admin AP: Key Concepts

Store Setup & Storefront Configuration

A B2B store is created in the Commerce app and runs on an Experience Cloud site. Use Experience Builder to design the site. Store settings include currency, language, buyer access, and checkout. Link the store to its catalogs and buyer groups. You can let guests browse products before logging in, but a buyer account is still needed to place an order. Test changes in a sandbox or test store first.

Product Catalog & Pricing

chunks.title: Salesforce Accredited B2B Commerce Administrator Professional Exam Guide & Practice
chunks.content:
Products are organized in a catalog and categories. A product can be simple or have variations, such as size and color. Set up a variation parent and variation attributes so buyers can select an option. Prices come from price books assigned to buyer groups. If a buyer cannot see a price, check the price book linked to their group. After you change products, categories, or searchable fields, rebuild the search index so the store shows the changes.

Buyer Account & Contact Management

A business customer is an Account enabled as a buyer account. Its Contacts can be set up as buyer users, who are external users that sign in to the store. Add buyer accounts to buyer groups. Groups link to entitlement policies, which control which products buyers can see and buy, and to price books, which set prices. To change access for many customers, update the buyer group rather than each account.

Order Management & Checkout

Checkout takes a buyer from cart to order. It can check inventory, calculate price, shipping, and tax, and take payment. These steps may connect to outside systems. After an order is placed, it is stored as an Order in Salesforce. With Salesforce Order Management, an Order Summary tracks fulfillment, changes, and returns. Buyers can reorder from their order history. Admins can also set approval steps or purchase limits.

Integration with Salesforce CRM

The store runs in Salesforce, so sales and service teams can use the same Accounts, Contacts, Orders, and Cases. Reps can see what customers ordered online, and service agents can handle order questions in Cases. Reports and dashboards can include online orders. An ERP system may provide prices, stock levels, and order status through an integration.

B2B Commerce Developer AP: Key Concepts

LWC Commerce Components & Override Pattern

B2B stores use Lightning Web Components in Experience Builder. Add your own LWCs to store pages, or replace a standard component when it does not meet the need. To show a component in Experience Builder, expose it with the right targets in its metadata file and add any properties admins need. Commerce modules and wire adapters provide context such as the current product, cart, and buyer account. Use that context so the component shows data for the signed-in buyer. Keep components small and reuse standard features when possible.

chunks.title: Salesforce Accredited B2B Commerce Developer Professional Exam Guide & Practice
chunks.content:
Commerce APIs & Storefront REST APIs

The Commerce Connect REST APIs let code and external apps work with products, carts, checkout, wishlists, and orders. Apex also has ConnectApi classes for server-side code. Use these APIs instead of directly reading or changing commerce records. They apply the buyer’s entitlements and prices. Headless and mobile apps can use the same APIs to support shopping outside the website.

Checkout Integrations & Tax/Payment

Checkout can call external systems for inventory, pricing, shipping, and tax. Build an Apex class that implements the right integration interface or extension, then register it with the store. A payment gateway adapter connects to the payment provider so card details do not need to be stored in Salesforce. Handle slow and failed responses clearly, and test realistic carts as well as error cases.

Search Configuration & Merchandising

Store search uses an index built from products, categories, and selected fields. Admins choose which fields are searchable and which can be used as filters. Developers can add product fields and mark them as searchable. After changing search settings or loading many products, rebuild the index. Rebuild large catalogs outside busy hours. Product data from integrations must include the fields used by search.

Testing, Deployment & Performance

Apex code needs tests and at least 75% coverage for production deployment. Mock outside calls so tests do not depend on live systems. Store setup includes both metadata and records, so plan how to move catalogs, buyer groups, and settings between orgs. For performance, avoid heavy work in components loaded on every page, cache data that changes rarely, and keep integration calls fast. Slow pricing or tax calls make checkout slower.

Correct answer: D. Register an Apex tax integration with the store

Checkout supports a tax integration. A registered Apex class can call the service and return tax amounts.

Reports show information after checkout.

A validation rule checks data; it does not calculate tax.

A formula field cannot call an outside service.

Question 5: Card payments must use a payment provider without storing card numbers in Salesforce. What should be used?

AA payment gateway adapter for the provider

BA custom encrypted field for card numbers on the Order

CEmail card details to finance

DA long text field on the Order

Correct answer: A. A payment gateway adapter for the provider

A payment gateway adapter connects checkout to the provider, which handles the card information and returns a result.

Storing card numbers in Salesforce fields creates a security risk.

Email is not a safe way to send card details.

A long text field still stores sensitive card details.

Question 6: A custom product field must be searchable in the store. The developer created the field. What else is needed?

ACopy the value into the product name

BMark it searchable in search settings, then rebuild the index

CAdd the field to the buyer’s profile

DNothing; every custom field is searched automatically once created

Correct answer: B. Mark it searchable in search settings, then rebuild the index

chunks.title: Salesforce Accredited B2B Commerce Developer Professional Exam Guide & Practice
chunks.content:
Choose the field in search settings and rebuild the index so it includes the field.

Changing product names is a workaround that can harm data quality.

Profiles do not control store search.

Only selected fields are indexed.

Question 7: A pricing integration can take 20 seconds and slows checkout. What should the developer do first?

ARemove pricing from checkout and show buyers the final amount later by email, once the ERP has responded

BRetry the call ten times

CSet a timeout and clear fallback message, then work with the ERP team to improve response time

Correct answer: C. Set a timeout and clear fallback message, then work with the ERP team to improve response time

Use a timeout and a clear fallback message, and work with the ERP team to improve the slow service.

Removing pricing prevents buyers from placing correct orders.

Repeated retries can make checkout take even longer.

Asking buyers to wait can lead them to abandon the cart.

Question 8: A mobile app must let buyers browse products and manage a cart using the website’s rules. What should it use?

ATake screenshots of the website

BRun SOQL directly from the app

CUse a nightly CSV file

DUse the B2B Commerce REST APIs

Correct answer: D. Use the B2B Commerce REST APIs

Commerce REST APIs give the app access to the store’s products, prices, and cart logic.

Screen scraping is fragile and breaks when the website changes.

Mobile apps should not query Salesforce directly with SOQL; that can also bypass Commerce rules.

A nightly CSV cannot manage a live cart.

Question 9: Tests for a shipping integration fail when the provider is unavailable. What should the developer change?

AUse HttpCalloutMock so tests do not call the live service

BLower the coverage target so the failing tests no longer block it

CRun tests only at night

Correct answer: A. Use HttpCalloutMock so tests do not call the live service

Mock callouts let tests run the integration code without depending on the outside service.

Coverage requirements do not change because the provider is down.

chunks.title: Salesforce Accredited B2B Commerce Developer Professional Exam Guide & Practice
chunks.content:
The provider could also be unavailable at night.

Removing tests can prevent Apex from being deployed to production.

Question 10: A product comparison feature is not available as a standard component. What should the developer do?

AUse a Visualforce page in the store

BBuild a custom LWC and add it to product pages in Experience Builder

CEdit the source of Salesforce’s standard component and redeploy it to the store

DAsk buyers to open two browser tabs

Correct answer: B. Build a custom LWC and add it to product pages in Experience Builder

Custom LWCs are a supported way to add features to store pages.

Visualforce is not the preferred way to extend modern store pages.

Salesforce’s standard component source cannot be edited.

Opening two tabs does not provide a comparison feature.

Question 11: 10,000 products load from the ERP each night, but new items take days to appear in search. What should the team do?

ALoad each product one at a time throughout the night

CRebuild the search index after each nightly load

DShorten product names

Correct answer: C. Rebuild the search index after each nightly load

Rebuild the search index after the nightly load so new products appear in search.

Loading one at a time does not update the search index.

Turning off search would make products harder to find.

Product name length is not the cause.

Question 12: An order must reach the ERP after checkout without slowing the buyer down. What approach fits?

AAsk sales reps to re-enter the order

BMake a synchronous call to the ERP before saving the order, and wait

CExport orders manually each night

DPublish an event or start asynchronous Apex after order creation

Correct answer: D. Publish an event or start asynchronous Apex after order creation

Asynchronous processing sends the order in the background so the buyer does not have to wait.

Re-entering orders is slow and can cause errors.

A synchronous call makes checkout wait and can fail if the ERP is down.

A nightly export delays order processing.

Solution Architecture Fundamentals

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2B Solution Architect (Retiring Feb 1, 2027) Archived Study Guide
chunks.content:
Start with the business process and its problems, then choose the products and systems that support each step. A common B2B flow uses Sales Cloud for leads and opportunities, CPQ or Revenue Cloud for quotes, Order Management or an ERP for orders, an ERP for invoicing, and Service Cloud for support. Experience Cloud or B2B Commerce can give customers and partners self-service access. Prefer standard features and configuration when they meet the need; custom code adds work to maintain and upgrade.

Multi-Cloud Data Architecture

Each important record should have a clear source of truth. For example, Salesforce may own customer accounts while an ERP owns products and prices, with those details synchronized into Salesforce for quoting. Orders may begin in Salesforce and continue in the ERP. Use external IDs to match records across systems and keep the shared Account and Contact model clear. Plan for large order and asset volumes, including archiving. Data Cloud can combine customer information from several sources into unified profiles without copying every record into core CRM objects.

Integration Architecture Patterns

Most B2B designs connect Salesforce to an ERP. Use a real-time API request when someone is waiting for an answer, such as a stock or credit check during quoting. Use Platform Events or Change Data Capture to notify other systems that something changed. Use a batch process and Bulk API for large scheduled transfers, such as nightly price updates. When several systems need connections, middleware such as MuleSoft can organize and reuse those integrations.

Security & Compliance Design

Customers and partners may use an Experience Cloud site to access Salesforce. Set sharing so each company sees only its own accounts, orders, and cases; account relationships and sharing sets can support external access. Consider data residency, consent, and privacy rules such as GDPR when personal data moves between countries or systems. Single sign-on can simplify access for employees and partners. Regulated businesses may also need Shield encryption or Event Monitoring.

Governance, Change Management & Scalability

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2B Solution Architect (Retiring Feb 1, 2027) Archived Study Guide
chunks.content:
Large B2B projects involve many groups, so agree on how design decisions are made. A design authority, shared naming and coding standards, and a release plan help teams stay aligned. Run business discovery before settling on a solution. Plan training and adoption early so people can use the new system. Design with expected growth in users, orders, and markets in mind.

A buyer account created in Sales Cloud feeds pricing/catalog into B2B Commerce; orders placed there flow to Order Management for fulfillment, the architect designs identity and data consistency across all three.

Salesforce Certified B2B Solution Architect Practice Questions (With Explanations)

Test your knowledge with these 15 sample questions.

Answered: 0 / 15Correct: 0

Question 1: Sales reps wait two days for quotes because finance keeps pricing rules in spreadsheets. What should the architect recommend?

ABuild a custom component that reads the spreadsheet for every quote

BMove pricing and discount rules into CPQ with approval steps

CHire more finance staff to answer quote requests

DSend the spreadsheet to sales reps each week

Correct answer: B. Move pricing and discount rules into CPQ with approval steps

Putting prices, discounts, and approval rules in CPQ lets reps create quotes with current rules and route exceptions for review.

Reading spreadsheets from custom code on every quote adds fragile work and leaves the pricing process unchanged.

More staff may reduce a queue but does not give reps a managed quoting process.

Weekly spreadsheets can become stale and do not enforce approvals in the quote flow.

Question 2: The ERP owns product and price data, but sales reps create quotes in Salesforce. How should the architect handle that data?

ALet reps edit Salesforce prices and copy changes back to the ERP

BKeep the ERP as the source of truth and sync the data into Salesforce

CRequire reps to check each price in the ERP while quoting

DKeep two price lists and let reps decide which one to use

Correct answer: B. Keep the ERP as the source of truth and sync the data into Salesforce

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2B Solution Architect (Retiring Feb 1, 2027) Archived Study Guide
chunks.content:
The ERP owns these records, so Salesforce should receive synchronized data for quoting rather than becoming a second owner.

Allowing edits in both systems creates conflicting values and unclear ownership.

Manual lookups slow quoting and can still lead to entry errors.

Two lists create uncertainty about which price is valid.

Question 3: While preparing a quote, a rep must check current ERP stock before promising a delivery date. Which integration pattern fits?

AReal-time ERP stock check

BPublish a Platform Event after the quote is saved

CUse the previous night’s stock batch

DSend a weekly stock export to Salesforce

Correct answer: A. Real-time ERP stock check

The rep needs current stock before making a commitment, so a synchronous request and response fits the decision.

An event after saving the quote does not return stock while the rep is making the decision.

Nightly data may be too old for a live availability check.

A weekly export is even less current and cannot answer the immediate question.

Question 4: The ERP, billing platform, warehouse, and data lake all need to know when Salesforce places an order. What should the architect use?

ASend each system a nightly CSV file

BAdd four separate callouts to the order trigger

CPublish an event when the order is placed

DHave each system poll Salesforce every minute

Correct answer: C. Publish an event when the order is placed

One order event can notify multiple subscribers. New systems can listen without adding another direct call to the order transaction.

A nightly file delays notification and may not meet downstream needs.

Four synchronous callouts couple the order transaction to every receiver.

Frequent polling adds load and makes every receiving system manage its own checks.

Question 5: Partner companies use Experience Cloud to view their orders. What is the key security design requirement?

ARestrict each partner to its own account’s records

BLimit how many reports partners can run

CUse the internal users’ page layout for every partner

DChoose a different color scheme for each company

Correct answer: A. Restrict each partner to its own account’s records

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2B Solution Architect (Retiring Feb 1, 2027) Archived Study Guide
chunks.content:
External sharing must keep each partner’s accounts and orders private from other companies.

Report limits do not define which records a partner can access.

Page layouts control fields and presentation, not record-level access.

Brand colors do not enforce data separation.

Question 6: Customer details are spread across Salesforce, an ERP, a marketing system, and support software. The core org should not hold all source records. What can provide a unified customer view?

AAsk staff to update all four systems by hand

BUse Data Cloud to unify customer profiles from the sources

CDelete all but one of the source systems

DCopy every source record into custom CRM objects

Correct answer: B. Use Data Cloud to unify customer profiles from the sources

Data Cloud can bring data from multiple sources together into unified profiles without requiring every record to be stored in core CRM objects.

Manual updates are costly and can leave the systems inconsistent.

Removing systems does not address the need to use their business functions and data.

Copying all source data into custom objects would add the storage burden the company wants to avoid.

Question 7: Where should an architect begin when planning a new B2B solution?

AMap the process and pain points

BDesign the page layouts

CWrite the integration code

DChoose Salesforce licenses

Correct answer: A. Map the process and pain points

Understanding the process and its problems helps determine which capabilities and systems are needed.

Page layouts come after the user and process needs are understood.

Integration code depends on decisions about the process and systems.

Licensing should follow the solution requirements, not drive discovery.

Question 8: Salesforce captures an order, the ERP fulfills it, and billing creates the invoice. What design principle helps keep the process clear?

ARe-enter the order by hand in each system

BKeep order information only in Salesforce

CGive each step a clear owning system

DLet every system edit every order field

Correct answer: C. Give each step a clear owning system

Clear ownership for each step reduces conflicting updates and makes the order easier to trace across systems.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2B Solution Architect (Retiring Feb 1, 2027) Archived Study Guide
chunks.content:
Manual re-entry increases delay and data entry errors.

The ERP and billing system also need the order data to complete their work.

Allowing all systems to change every field creates conflicts over which value is correct.

Question 9: A global B2B company handles personal data for customers in the EU. What must the architect include in the design?

AWebsite performance alone

BThe number of user licenses alone

CThe interface language only

DPrivacy requirements such as GDPR

Correct answer: D. Privacy requirements such as GDPR

The solution must account for privacy obligations, including consent, data access requests, and where personal data is stored and processed.

Performance alone does not address legal handling of personal data.

License counts do not determine privacy controls.

Language settings do not satisfy privacy requirements.

Question 10: Six delivery teams are making conflicting architecture choices. What governance step should the architect recommend?

AAllow each team to set its own standards

BSet up a design authority and shared standards

CStop all but one team from working

DCombine all work into one annual release

Correct answer: B. Set up a design authority and shared standards

A design authority and shared standards help teams make consistent decisions while continuing work in parallel.

Independent standards can increase inconsistency across teams.

Stopping all but one team unnecessarily blocks parallel delivery.

One annual release can delay value and does not resolve design decisions during delivery.

Question 11: Customers call support to ask about order status and download invoices. What solution could reduce these calls?

AEmail each customer a spreadsheet every week

BHire more support agents

CClose the support phone line

DProvide a self-service portal for orders and invoices

Correct answer: D. Provide a self-service portal for orders and invoices

A portal through Experience Cloud or B2B Commerce lets customers find order and invoice information themselves.

Weekly spreadsheets become outdated and make customers depend on staff.

More agents address call volume without letting customers self-serve.

Closing the support line removes help instead of solving the information need.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2B Solution Architect (Retiring Feb 1, 2027) Archived Study Guide
chunks.content:
Question 12: A sponsor requests a custom quoting engine, but standard CPQ meets 90% of the requirements. What should the architect recommend?

AUse standard CPQ and extend it for remaining needs

BDelay the project for a year in case new features arrive

CRun two quoting tools side by side

DBuild a separate custom quoting engine

Correct answer: A. Use standard CPQ and extend it for remaining needs

Standard CPQ covers most of the need. A limited extension or process adjustment is usually simpler to maintain than a separate engine.

Waiting does not address the remaining requirement or provide a current solution.

Two tools create duplicate processes and make quote management harder.

A separate engine adds cost and ongoing maintenance for needs mostly covered by CPQ.

Question 13: The ERP sends a nightly price update for 200,000 products. Which approach is suitable?

AMake one real-time callout per product

BPublish a Platform Event for every product

CUse a batch load with Bulk API

DAsk the product team to enter every price manually

Correct answer: C. Use a batch load with Bulk API

Bulk API is designed to move large data volumes efficiently in scheduled loads.

A separate real-time call for every item adds avoidable overhead.

An event for each product is not the best fit for a large nightly bulk transfer.

Manual entry is too slow and error-prone at this scale.

Question 14: A solution launched six months ago, but few sales reps use it. What was likely missing?

AAdd more custom code to the solution

BAdd more page fields for the sales reps

CIncrease the sandbox capacity for the project

DPlan training and adoption

Correct answer: D. Plan training and adoption

Users need preparation and support to adopt a new process. Adoption planning should begin during delivery.

More code does not address whether users understand or accept the process.

Adding fields can make the experience more complex without helping adoption.

A larger sandbox does not improve user readiness.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2B Solution Architect (Retiring Feb 1, 2027) Archived Study Guide
chunks.content:
Question 15: The same customer exists in Salesforce and the ERP, but each system uses a different record ID. How should integrations match the records?

AMatch them by customer name during nightly processing

BAsk users to connect the records manually

CStore the ERP key in Salesforce as an external ID

DKeep the records unrelated

Correct answer: C. Store the ERP key in Salesforce as an external ID

An external ID stores the other system’s key so integrations can reliably match and upsert the same customer.

Names can change or be shared by different customers, so they are not a reliable key.

Manual linking does not scale and can lead to mismatches.

Leaving records unrelated makes synchronization and reporting harder.

Architecture Patterns & Scalability

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Commerce Architect (Arch-303 – Retiring Feb 1, 2027) Archived Guide
chunks.content:
A B2C Commerce realm contains environments such as developer sandboxes, Development, Staging, and Production. Teams prepare and test code and data in Staging, then replicate them to Production. One realm can host multiple sites. Those sites may share code while using different catalogs, prices, and settings. For several brands or countries, a common design uses one master catalog for the product set, a storefront catalog for the assortment shown on each site, and price books for market or currency prices. The platform supports scale, but efficient code still matters: avoid costly work on every page request and use jobs for bulk processing.

Storefront Architecture & Headless Commerce

SFRA (Storefront Reference Architecture) renders pages on the server and provides standard storefront features. Extend it with your own cartridges instead of editing its base code. Composable Storefront (PWA Kit with Managed Runtime) is the headless choice: a React front end that uses B2C Commerce APIs. It gives the team more front-end control, but the team must build and operate more pieces. SFRA often suits projects that value a faster launch and built-in commerce features. Headless can fit a highly custom experience or a shared front end for several back ends.

Integration Architecture: OCAPI, SCAPI & Connectors

SCAPI (Salesforce Commerce API), including the Shopper APIs, is the modern API set and a common starting point for new headless storefronts. OCAPI (Open Commerce API) remains in use on many established sites. SLAS provides shopper sign-in and tokens for headless storefronts. For external services, configure calls through the Business Manager service framework to set timeouts, logging, and circuit breakers. Use scheduled jobs to import large product or inventory files, often in XML or CSV. Payment, tax, and address integrations may use certified LINK cartridges.

Performance, Caching & CDN Strategy

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Commerce Architect (Arch-303 – Retiring Feb 1, 2027) Archived Guide
chunks.content:
Page caching is one of the main tools for improving response time. Cache full pages or suitable page sections with the iscache tag. Keep personal content, such as a shopper’s mini cart, in a small uncached section that loads separately. Choose cache times carefully and clear cached content when product or site content changes. The eCDN serves images and other static files from locations closer to shoppers. Watch platform quotas, which limit resources such as objects or API calls in a request, and fix quota violations before a busy season. Test with traffic patterns that resemble real promotions.

Security, Compliance & Site Operations

Do not store unprotected card numbers in B2C Commerce. Send card data to a payment provider through its cartridge and keep a token on the commerce side; this can reduce PCI scope. Use Business Manager roles to give each team only the access it needs. Follow privacy, consent, and cookie requirements in each market. For operations, move code through Staging before replication, schedule large jobs away from busy periods, and monitor logs with alerts. Prepare for peak events such as Black Friday, including a deployment freeze when appropriate.

Requests hit a CDN first (static assets, cached pages), then an application cache layer; and only reach the origin server for truly dynamic content, this layering is what lets a storefront handle Black Friday-scale traffic.

Custom attributes bypass the normal price book model and make price maintenance harder.

AIn site preferences in Business Manager

BIn a custom cartridge placed before the base cartridge

CIn a cartridge placed after the base cartridge

DDirectly in app_storefront_base

Correct answer: B. In a custom cartridge placed before the base cartridge

A custom cartridge earlier in the path can override or extend base behavior while keeping the base cartridge unchanged.

Site preferences do not replace checkout implementation code.

A later cartridge does not take precedence over the base cartridge.

Changing the base cartridge makes future upgrades harder and is not the recommended extension pattern.

Question 3: A retailer wants a highly customized, app-like storefront built by its React team. Which approach is the best fit?

ACall OCAPI from ISML templates

BExtend SFRA with a custom theme

CUse Composable Storefront with the Commerce APIs

DUse only Business Manager content slots

Correct answer: C. Use Composable Storefront with the Commerce APIs

Composable Storefront uses a React front end with Commerce APIs, giving the team control over a custom storefront experience.

OCAPI calls in server-rendered ISML templates do not provide the requested React headless storefront.

SFRA can be customized, but it remains a server-rendered storefront rather than the headless approach requested.

Content slots help manage content but do not create a complete React storefront.

Question 4: Category pages slow down during peak traffic. Each page also renders the shopper’s mini cart. What should the architect recommend?

ARun the entire category page as a job

BDisable page caching so the cart stays current

CAdd more product images

DCache shared pages; load the mini cart separately

Correct answer: D. Cache shared pages; load the mini cart separately

Cache the reusable category page and load the shopper-specific cart separately. This protects page speed while keeping cart details current.

chunks.content:
A page displayed to shoppers cannot be replaced by a background job.

Turning off page caching removes a useful performance benefit for shared category content.

More images would add work and would not address the cart’s effect on caching.

Question 5: A new headless storefront needs shopper sign-in and tokens for calls to the Shopper APIs. Which service should it use?

AShopper Login and API Access Service (SLAS)

BBusiness Manager employee accounts

CA shared API key stored in the front end

DBasic authentication on every shopper request

Correct answer: A. Shopper Login and API Access Service (SLAS)

SLAS handles shopper login and token access for headless B2C Commerce storefronts.

Business Manager accounts are for administrators and staff, not shopper authentication.

A secret embedded in front-end code can be exposed and is not a shopper login solution.

Basic authentication on each request is not the intended shopper token flow.

Question 6: A retailer wants to reduce PCI scope and avoid keeping card numbers in B2C Commerce. What design should it use?

AUse a tokenizing provider LINK cartridge

BEncrypt card numbers in a custom object

CEmail card details to the finance team

DKeep the card number only in session data

Correct answer: A. Use a tokenizing provider LINK cartridge

A provider can receive payment details and return a token, so the commerce site does not need to retain the raw card number.

Encryption does not remove the risk and scope created by storing card numbers in the platform.

Email is not a secure payment data flow and leaves card details exposed.

Session storage still puts card data on the commerce platform.

Question 7: A warehouse sends inventory updates for 500,000 products every hour. How should the team load the feed?

AMake one OCAPI request for each product every hour

BUpdate inventory during every shopper page view

CEnter each update manually in Business Manager

DRun a scheduled inventory import job

Correct answer: D. Run a scheduled inventory import job

chunks.content:
Hundreds of thousands of individual calls create avoidable overhead for a bulk feed.

Page requests should not be responsible for importing warehouse data.

Manual updates are not practical at this scale or frequency.

Question 8: The team tested code in Staging and is ready to release it to Production. How is it normally moved?

AUpload it to Production directly from each developer sandbox

BReplicate it from Staging to Production

CRebuild the storefront by hand in Production

DCopy the files to Production over FTP

Correct answer: B. Replicate it from Staging to Production

The team prepares and tests changes in Staging, then uses replication to move them to Production.

Direct uploads from individual sandboxes bypass the standard release path.

Manually rebuilding Production is not the normal controlled deployment process.

FTP file copying is not the standard B2C Commerce deployment method.

Question 9: An external tax service sometimes stops responding and holds up checkout. What should the architect configure?

ARun the tax request only in an overnight job

BUse the service framework with a timeout and circuit breaker

CMake a plain HTTP request with no timeout

DCall the tax service directly from the shopper’s browser

Correct answer: B. Use the service framework with a timeout and circuit breaker

The service framework supports controls such as timeouts and circuit breakers so an unresponsive provider does not hold requests indefinitely.

Checkout needs a tax result during the shopper’s purchase, so an overnight job does not meet the need.

Without a timeout, a stalled provider can keep checkout waiting.

A browser-side call exposes integration details and does not provide the server-side controls needed here.

Question 10: A new site is being designed with a headless front end. Which API set should the team consider first?

BOCAPI for every new headless feature

CSCAPI and the Shopper APIs

DDirect database access

Correct answer: C. SCAPI and the Shopper APIs

SCAPI and the Shopper APIs are the current commerce APIs commonly used for new headless storefronts.

SOAP is not the default API choice for this new headless design.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Commerce Architect (Arch-303 – Retiring Feb 1, 2027) Archived Guide
chunks.content:
OCAPI remains in use, but SCAPI is the modern starting point for new headless work.

Direct database access is not an appropriate storefront integration pattern.

Question 11: Before Black Friday, load testing shows that some pages exceed platform quotas. What should the team do?

ATell shoppers to visit outside peak hours

BIgnore the findings because quotas apply only in sandboxes

DFind and fix the quota-heavy code before peak trading

Correct answer: D. Find and fix the quota-heavy code before peak trading

Quota issues can affect Production. The team should correct the code and retest before the expected traffic surge.

Changing shopper visit times does not correct the platform issue.

Production quotas also matter, so ignoring the test results is unsafe.

Disabling the eCDN does not fix the code that exceeds quotas and may hurt delivery performance.

Question 12: The merchandising team should manage promotions but must not change code or payment settings. How should access be limited?

ALeast-privilege Business Manager roles

BGive every merchandiser Administrator access

CRemove the promotions tools from Business Manager

DHave the whole team share one login

Correct answer: A. Least-privilege Business Manager roles

Business Manager roles can grant the promotion functions the team needs without granting unrelated permissions.

Administrator access is broader than the stated need.

Removing the promotions tools would prevent the team from doing its assigned work.

Shared accounts weaken accountability and do not enforce individual permissions.

Question 13: Shoppers in Asia report that product images load slowly, while the main site runs in Europe. What can help most?

ABundle all images inside the application cartridge

BServe the images and static files through eCDN

CTurn off page caching

DIncrease the image dimensions

Correct answer: B. Serve the images and static files through eCDN

The eCDN can serve static assets from locations closer to shoppers, reducing the distance those files travel.

Bundling images in the cartridge does not place them closer to shoppers and can complicate updates.

Page caching does not solve the geographic delivery of image files.

Larger images require more data and can make loading slower.

AWhen the site will not use any Salesforce APIs

CWhen the project values a fast launch and standard commerce features

Hard-coded templates require a code change and deployment to update banners.

B2C Commerce Developer exam: key concepts

SFRA Architecture: Cartridges & Overrides

SFRA is Salesforce B2C Commerce’s reference storefront architecture. It uses cartridges, which package controllers, templates, models, and static files. The cartridge path in Business Manager sets priority: a cartridge earlier in the path wins when files share a location. To customize the storefront, put changes in your own cartridge and leave the base cartridge intact. In controllers, `server.extend` adds behavior to a route, while `server.replace` replaces it. Understand how path order affects which version runs.

Controllers, Scripts & Server-Side Logic

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Commerce Developer (Comm-Dev-101 / CRT-500) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
SFRA controllers are JavaScript modules that use the `server` framework. Routes handle requests such as GET and POST, then render a template or return JSON. Middleware can add checks such as authentication, CSRF protection, or consent handling. Keep reusable business logic in models, helpers, or script modules instead of repeating it in controllers. The `dw.*` APIs provide access to server-side Commerce features. Custom scripts in `cartridge/scripts/` can hold logic shared by several routes. Be mindful of platform limits when a script queries or processes data.

Templates (ISML) & Client-Side Assets

ISML is the server-side language used to build storefront pages. `<isinclude>` inserts another template, `<isloop>` repeats content for a collection, `<isset>` assigns a value, and `<isif>` handles a condition. Resource bundles store text for different locales. Put static JavaScript, CSS, and images in `cartridge/static/` and reference them with `URLUtils.staticURL()`. SFRA uses build tools such as Webpack to prepare browser code and SASS to produce CSS. Controllers pass data to templates through `pdict`. Keep dynamic content and caching behavior in mind when extending a page.

Jobs, Feeds & Business Manager Configuration

Commerce Cloud jobs run scripts on a schedule or when started by an administrator. Teams use them for tasks such as importing product or inventory feeds and exporting orders. Configure job steps in Business Manager. IMPEX supports bulk import and export using formats such as XML and CSV. Site Preferences hold settings that administrators can change and code can read through `dw.system.Site.current.preferences`. Custom Attributes add fields to standard objects such as products, orders, or customers. Know where to configure a job and how a controller reads a site preference.

Testing, Debugging & Deployment

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Commerce Developer (Comm-Dev-101 / CRT-500) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Teams use build tools such as `sgmf-scripts` and deployment tools such as `sfcc-ci` to prepare and upload cartridges. Uploaded code is assigned to a code version, which is then activated. Use the Request Log and `dw.system.Logger` to investigate requests and application behavior. The Pipeline Profiler can help identify slow routes. Test controllers with dependencies that can be mocked, and use the project’s test tools and reports. For a release, understand the steps from uploading cartridges to activating the code version, and know where to look when errors appear in Business Manager.

A storefront request hits a Route (controller), which calls Models to fetch/shape data, renders an ISML template, and can be extended by a custom cartridge without ever modifying the base SFRA cartridge.

How to prepare for the B2C Commerce Developer exam

The exam checks whether you can build and troubleshoot B2C Commerce storefront features. Practice tracing a request through a controller, template, script, and any API or Business Manager settings it depends on.

Know how controllers, models, and ISML templates work together, and how the cartridge path chooses which implementation runs.

Practice creating and extending routes with `server.get`, `server.post`, `server.append`, `server.prepend`, and `server.replace`. Add middleware for the needed checks and return either JSON or a rendered template.

Review tags such as `<isset>`, `<isif>`, `<isloop>`, and `<isinclude>`. Learn how templates use locale, currency, and content assets, and how caching affects dynamic page content.

Scripts and Commerce APIs

Write reusable CommonJS modules and use the `dw.*` APIs for catalog, order, and customer tasks. Know how server-side scripts call external services through `dw.net.HTTPClient`.

Business Manager Settings

Practice setting up catalogs, price books, promotions, and site preferences. Know how Business Manager settings relate to the storefront and how to manage cartridges with the tools used by your team.

DSet the visual style for storefront pages

Correct answer: B. Handle a request and decide what response to return

A controller handles the request, runs server-side logic, and chooses a template or response such as JSON.

Product data belongs to the catalog and data layer, not in the controller itself.

Jobs are configured separately and are not the controller’s main role.

Visual styling is handled by client-side assets such as CSS.

Question 5: Two controllers need to use the same server-side logic. What is a good way to share it?

AA shared script module

BCreate a template fragment for each controller to render

CCopy the function into both controllers

DStore the logic text in a custom object

Correct answer: A. A shared script module

A shared script module keeps one implementation that both controllers can call.

A template fragment is for rendering page content, not sharing server-side business logic.

Copying the function creates two versions that can drift apart.

A custom object stores data, not executable shared code.

Question 6: Why should developers watch platform API and query quotas?

AThey limit how many products a catalog can contain

BThey control how often storefront cache can be cleared

CExceeding a limit can slow down or fail a request

DThey set the maximum number of cartridges on a site

Correct answer: C. Exceeding a limit can slow down or fail a request

The platform limits some operations within a request; exceeding those limits can produce warnings and cause failures.

Catalog size is not what these per-request limits describe.

Cache clearing frequency is controlled separately.

The limits do not determine how many cartridges a site can use.

Question 7: What do OCAPI and SCAPI provide in a B2C Commerce solution?

AA way to import a catalog from a retailer’s backend only

BThe rendering engine for shopper-facing pages

CThe screens merchants use in Business Manager

DCommerce APIs for external clients

Correct answer: D. Commerce APIs for external clients

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Commerce Developer (Comm-Dev-101 / CRT-500) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
These APIs let external applications, including headless storefronts and integrations, work with commerce data and operations.

Catalog imports can use other supported feed and job patterns; that is not the APIs’ only purpose.

Storefront page rendering is handled by the storefront architecture or a separate front end.

Business Manager provides merchant configuration screens.

Question 8: A loyalty program offers members a different product price. Which setup supports this?

ADuplicate all eligible products in another catalog

BAssign a separate price book to the member customer group

CRequire each member to enter a promotion code

DStore the member price in a custom product attribute

Correct answer: B. Assign a separate price book to the member customer group

A customer group can be associated with a price book so eligible shoppers receive the group’s prices.

Duplicating products is not needed to provide group-specific prices.

A promotion code is not the same as resolving prices through a customer group.

A custom attribute does not replace the platform’s price book behavior.

Question 9: A job must process the full product catalog. What should the developer plan for?

ATurn off the storefront for the whole run

BProcess the job in chunks

CHandle records one at a time in a single long operation

DRun the job during peak traffic to spot errors quickly

Correct answer: B. Process the job in chunks

Breaking large workloads into chunks helps the job stay within limits and recover if a step fails.

The storefront does not generally need to be disabled for a catalog job.

One long operation can consume too many resources and fail before completion.

Peak traffic is a poor time to run a resource-intensive job.

Question 10: Why does storefront caching matter?

AIt guarantees the catalog is always current

BIt lowers response time under load

CIt removes the need to consider API quotas

DIt guarantees every shopper sees personalized prices

Correct answer: B. It lowers response time under load

Caching suitable content lets the storefront serve pages faster under real traffic.

Caching can make content stale unless its rules and invalidation are managed.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Commerce Developer (Comm-Dev-101 / CRT-500) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Caching does not remove platform limits on API or query use.

Personalized pricing still needs correct shopper and cache handling.

Question 11: Personalized content for one shopper appears in another shopper’s cached page. What is the likely cause?

AA platform quota was exceeded while rendering the page

BA product is missing a custom attribute

CCache personalized output by shopper

DThe custom cartridge is in the wrong path position

Correct answer: C. Cache personalized output by shopper

If a cached response depends on the shopper but the cache does not distinguish shoppers, one person may receive another person’s content.

A quota issue may affect request behavior but does not explain sharing one shopper’s cached output.

A product field issue would not make personalized output cross between shoppers.

Cartridge order affects which code runs, not whether the cache varies by shopper.

Question 12: How does a storefront catalog differ from a master catalog?

AOne is for merchant edits and one is only for developer edits

BOne contains physical goods and the other only digital goods

COne is for a site and the other is for a locale

DMaster defines products; storefront organizes browsing

Correct answer: D. Master defines products; storefront organizes browsing

Products are defined in the master catalog and placed into storefront catalog structures that control site navigation.

Both catalog types can be managed through appropriate commerce tools and permissions.

The difference is not based on whether products are physical or digital.

A storefront catalog controls the assortment and navigation; it is not simply a locale setting.

Question 13: A retailer switches to a headless front end that calls B2C Commerce APIs. What changes for the developer?

AJobs can no longer run without a storefront

BThe cartridge path has no use anywhere in the solution

CSystem objects can no longer have custom attributes

DThe front end renders; Commerce serves API data

Correct answer: D. The front end renders; Commerce serves API data

In a headless design, a separate front end handles presentation and consumes platform data and operations through APIs.

Jobs can still run as platform processes in a headless implementation.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Commerce Developer (Comm-Dev-101 / CRT-500) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
The cartridge path can still matter for server-side code and other platform features.

Custom attributes can still extend system objects in a headless solution.

Question 14: A custom checkout needs to collect payment details. What is the safer approach?

ALet the payment provider collect the details directly

BSend card details through the controller and log them for later

CSave card details in a custom shopper attribute

DKeep card details in the session until the order is placed

Correct answer: A. Let the payment provider collect the details directly

Use the provider’s hosted fields or redirect so raw card data does not pass through the storefront application or its logs.

Logging card details exposes sensitive data and should be avoided.

Storing card details on the shopper profile would retain sensitive payment data in the application.

Session storage still puts card data in the application environment.

Question 15: Which work is a B2C Commerce developer mainly responsible for?

AChoosing the storefront’s visual design and brand style

BDeciding which products the merchandising team should promote

CStorefront behavior, integrations, and data extensions

DOperating the underlying hosting infrastructure

Correct answer: C. Storefront behavior, integrations, and data extensions

Developers implement and customize storefront behavior, extend the data model, and connect Commerce with other systems.

Visual design may be delivered with developers, but this does not describe the developer’s main platform responsibility.

Merchandising teams decide which products to feature.

Salesforce operates the underlying Commerce hosting infrastructure.

Is the B2C Solution Architect Exam Hard?

This exam page covers B2C solution design across commerce, customer engagement and service. Expect to reason about how the parts of a customer journey fit together.

60 scored questions in 120 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.

63% to pass, which is 38 correct answers out of 60.

B2C Solution Architect Exam Format Explained

The B2C Solution Architect exam is a timed Salesforce credential exam. Use the format below to plan pacing and practice-test strategy.

Multiple-choice & multiple-select

How Many Questions Are Scenario-Based?

Scenarios describe a retailer’s goal and ask which design best supports the customer journey, operations or non-functional needs.

Best Way to Pass on Your First Attempt

Trace the shopping journey: Map how a customer discovers products, checks out, and gets help after the sale. Note which cloud owns each step.

Design the commerce and order flow: Review catalogs, promotions, carts, order capture, fulfillment routing, returns, and refunds as one connected solution.

Plan for peak shopping periods: Use scale, caching, and recovery plans to support traffic spikes, global storefronts, and service uptime.

Coordinate releases across clouds: Plan changes to Commerce, Marketing Cloud, and Salesforce metadata together, and identify where testing or rollback is needed.

B2C Solution Architect: Key Concepts

Start with the customer journey and business goals. Map each step to the Salesforce product or service that supports it, and document the boundaries between systems.

Multi-Cloud Data Flow

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Solution Architect (Arch-302) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Decide which system owns each customer or order record and how updates move between products. Keep identity matching, consent and error handling in the design.

Shoppers may browse anonymously before creating an account. Plan how the solution recognizes a returning customer, handles duplicate profiles and respects consent.

Orders and Fulfillment

Commerce captures the purchase. Order-management and fulfillment processes handle what happens next, such as routing, delivery, returns and status updates.

Plan for busy shopping periods, response time, recovery and safe releases. Choose caching and scaling approaches that fit the actual traffic and service requirements.

B2C Commerce captures purchase behavior, syncs it to Marketing Cloud for personalized campaigns, and hands off post-purchase issues to Service Cloud: all three need a shared customer identity to stay in sync.

How to Pass the Salesforce B2C Solution Architect Exam

Map each requirement to the customer journey and the Salesforce products that support it.

Follow the customer journey

Identify what the shopper is doing, which system owns the step and what information the next step needs.

Check identity and data ownership

Look for duplicate profiles, consent rules and unclear ownership between connected clouds.

Design for order completion

Follow the order through fulfillment and customer support, including failure and return paths.

Use constraints to compare options

Choose a design that meets the stated scale, availability, mobile and release needs without adding unrelated components.

Question 1: A retailer wants one design that ties its consumer storefront to supporting Salesforce services. What should the architect lead?

ACross-cloud customer solution

BA list of storefront page changes only

CA service-desk process without commerce data

DA product catalogue migration with no customer journey

Correct answer: A. Cross-cloud customer solution

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Solution Architect (Arch-302) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:

A list of storefront page changes only does not fit because it addresses a different need than A customer-focused design across the relevant Salesforce clouds.

A service-desk process without commerce data does not fit because it addresses a different need than A customer-focused design across the relevant Salesforce clouds.

A product catalogue migration with no customer journey does not fit because it addresses a different need than A customer-focused design across the relevant Salesforce clouds.

Question 2: A team is planning a direct-to-consumer online store. What does B2C mean?

BBusiness-to-Consumer

Correct answer: B. Business-to-Consumer

B2C means Business-to-Consumer: a business sells products or services directly to consumers.

Business-to-Channel does not fit because it addresses a different need than Business-to-Consumer.

Brand-to-Customer does not fit because it addresses a different need than Business-to-Consumer.

Buyer-to-Commerce does not fit because it addresses a different need than Business-to-Consumer.

Question 3: A company needs a consumer storefront, campaign engagement and customer support. Which Salesforce capabilities best match those needs?

ASales Cloud, Tableau and Slack

BService Cloud and Heroku alone

CCommerce, Marketing and Service

DExperience Cloud and Revenue Cloud only

Correct answer: C. Commerce, Marketing and Service

Commerce supports the storefront, Marketing Cloud supports customer engagement, and Service Cloud supports service.

Sales Cloud, Tableau and Slack does not fit because it addresses a different need than B2C Commerce, Marketing Cloud and Service Cloud.

Service Cloud and Heroku alone does not fit because it addresses a different need than B2C Commerce, Marketing Cloud and Service Cloud.

Experience Cloud and Revenue Cloud only does not fit because it addresses a different need than B2C Commerce, Marketing Cloud and Service Cloud.

Question 4: A customer journey spans shopping, marketing messages and post-purchase support. What does a multi-cloud design require?

AKeeping each cloud isolated from the others

BUsing one product for every business process

CSending all customer data into a spreadsheet

DCoordinate data and interactions across clouds

Correct answer: D. Coordinate data and interactions across clouds

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Solution Architect (Arch-302) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
A multi-cloud solution coordinates the data and customer experience across the products used in the journey.

Keeping each cloud isolated from the others does not fit because it addresses a different need than Coordinating data and interactions across the products involved.

Using one product for every business process does not fit because it addresses a different need than Coordinating data and interactions across the products involved.

Sending all customer data into a spreadsheet does not fit because it addresses a different need than Coordinating data and interactions across the products involved.

CRetail store associates with no platform responsibilities

Campaign writers focused only on creative copy does not fit because it addresses a different need than Architects and senior consultants designing consumer commerce solutions.
