Product designers focused only on visual assets does not fit because it addresses a different need than Architects and senior consultants designing consumer commerce solutions.

AA partner-only account portal

BConsumer shopping storefront

CA field-service dispatch console

DA back-office finance ledger

The storefront is the consumer-facing channel where shoppers browse and purchase.

A partner-only account portal does not fit because it addresses a different need than A consumer-facing online shopping experience.

A field-service dispatch console does not fit because it addresses a different need than A consumer-facing online shopping experience.

A back-office finance ledger does not fit because it addresses a different need than A consumer-facing online shopping experience.

chunks.content:
AA Service Cloud case queue

CCommerce-to-Marketing integration

DA Tableau extract with no customer linkage

The Commerce and Marketing Cloud integration can share relevant commerce data for marketing use cases; the exact connector and design depend on the implementation.

AA fixed storefront theme with no external interface

BA single server-rendered page tied to the commerce UI

CA monolithic application with no commerce APIs

DHeadless commerce with APIs

Headless commerce separates the presentation layer from commerce services exposed through APIs.

A single server-rendered page tied to the commerce UI does not fit because it addresses a different need than Headless commerce using APIs and a separate front end.

A monolithic application with no commerce APIs does not fit because it addresses a different need than Headless commerce using APIs and a separate front end.

Question 9: A retailer wants recommendations on product pages based on shopper context. Which capability should it consider?

AProduct recommendations

BA static product list with no shopper signals

CA service case assignment rule

DA manual spreadsheet sent to shoppers

Personalization and recommendation capabilities can tailor product suggestions using available shopper context and configured rules.

A static product list with no shopper signals does not fit because it addresses a different need than Personalization and recommendation features.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Solution Architect (Arch-302) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
A service case assignment rule does not fit because it addresses a different need than Personalization and recommendation features.

A manual spreadsheet sent to shoppers does not fit because it addresses a different need than Personalization and recommendation features.

Question 10: After checkout, a retailer needs to coordinate fulfillment and keep order status visible. Which integration area matters?

AStorefront page analytics

BPost-purchase order fulfillment

CMarketing email templates

DProduct image storage

Correct answer: B. Post-purchase order fulfillment

Post-purchase order fulfillment supports post-purchase processing such as fulfillment and order status updates.

Storefront page analytics does not fit because it addresses a different need than Order Management integration.

Marketing email templates does not fit because it addresses a different need than Order Management integration.

Product image storage does not fit because it addresses a different need than Order Management integration.

Question 11: What should an architect check when several Salesforce clouds share customer data?

AWhether each cloud can use a different identity for the same person

BWhether the customer profile can be omitted from the design

CData flow, identity and consistency

DWhether all customer interactions can be moved to one report

Correct answer: C. Data flow, identity and consistency

A multi-cloud architecture needs clear data flows, identity matching and a consistent customer experience.

Whether each cloud can use a different identity for the same person does not fit because it addresses a different need than How data flows, identity is matched and experiences remain consistent.

Whether the customer profile can be omitted from the design does not fit because it addresses a different need than How data flows, identity is matched and experiences remain consistent.

Whether all customer interactions can be moved to one report does not fit because it addresses a different need than How data flows, identity is matched and experiences remain consistent.

Question 12: What is the architect’s role in a B2C Commerce program?

AWrite every storefront component alone

BManage only the campaign calendar

COwn only the service team’s case queue

DEnd-to-end B2C design

Correct answer: D. End-to-end B2C design

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Solution Architect (Arch-302) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
The architect aligns the solution across Commerce and the other products required to meet the customer and business needs.

Write every storefront component alone does not fit because it addresses a different need than Guide the end-to-end design across commerce and related services.

Manage only the campaign calendar does not fit because it addresses a different need than Guide the end-to-end design across commerce and related services.

Own only the service team’s case queue does not fit because it addresses a different need than Guide the end-to-end design across commerce and related services.

Question 13: A retailer expects seasonal traffic spikes and does not want to manage storefront servers. Which deployment model fits?

ACloud-hosted scalable service

BA single on-premises server sized for average traffic

CA fixed local instance with no scale plan

DA desktop application installed for each shopper

Correct answer: A. Cloud-hosted scalable service

A cloud-hosted service avoids customer-managed storefront servers and supports scale according to the service design and plan.

A single on-premises server sized for average traffic does not fit because it addresses a different need than A cloud-hosted commerce service sized for variable demand.

A fixed local instance with no scale plan does not fit because it addresses a different need than A cloud-hosted commerce service sized for variable demand.

A desktop application installed for each shopper does not fit because it addresses a different need than A cloud-hosted commerce service sized for variable demand.

Question 14: A shopper needs help with an order after purchase. Which Salesforce capability is most relevant?

AMarketing Cloud audience segmentation

BCustomer support and order cases

CCommerce product catalogue management

DTableau dashboard authoring

Correct answer: B. Customer support and order cases

Service Cloud supports customer service workflows, including cases and order-related support.

Marketing Cloud audience segmentation does not fit because it addresses a different need than Service Cloud case and customer support.

Commerce product catalogue management does not fit because it addresses a different need than Service Cloud case and customer support.

Tableau dashboard authoring does not fit because it addresses a different need than Service Cloud case and customer support.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified B2C Solution Architect (Arch-302) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Question 15: Which design principle should guide a consumer commerce solution?

AOptimize internal reporting before customer needs

BBuild desktop pages first and defer mobile behavior

CCustomer journey, performance and mobile

DTreat each cloud as a separate customer experience

Correct answer: C. Customer journey, performance and mobile

Business Analyst exam format

You can take the exam online with a proctor or at a test center. Here is what to expect:

Multiple-choice & multiple-select

How Many Questions Are Scenario-Based?

Most questions describe a project situation, such as stakeholders who disagree or a requirement that keeps changing. They ask what the analyst should do next.

Best Way to Pass on Your First Attempt

Choose the right discovery method: Interviews, workshops, observation, surveys, and document review each help with different needs.

Write clear user stories: Include a role, goal, and benefit. Add acceptance criteria a tester can check.

Map the process first: Document the current process, then the future process, and list the gaps.

Know what Salesforce can do: Learn enough to tell whether a requirement is simple to configure, costly, or not possible.

Business Analyst: Key Concepts

Discovery and Elicitation

You need to ask for requirements and learn how work is done. Interviews give you time to learn from one person, especially about sensitive topics. Workshops help a group discuss issues and agree on decisions. Observation means watching someone do the work; it can reveal steps they forget to mention. Surveys reach many people with simple questions, but you cannot ask follow-up questions. Document analysis and reviews of the current system show how work happens today. Choose the method based on whether you need detail, agreement, broad input, or evidence. Prepare questions, record decisions, and share your notes so people can correct anything you missed.

User Stories and Acceptance Criteria

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Business Analyst (BA-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
A user story states the user’s role, goal, and benefit. For example: “As a sales rep, I want to see a customer’s open cases on an opportunity so that I know about problems before a renewal call.” The benefit helps the team decide how important the story is. Acceptance criteria list what must be true for the story to be complete. They should be clear enough for a tester to check. Good stories are small enough for one work cycle and focus on the need, not a set design. A story about a screen layout may describe a solution before the team understands the need.

Stakeholders and Getting Decisions Made

Projects often stall because people disagree. Map stakeholders by their influence and interest, then plan how to involve each group. Choose who can make decisions before conflicts come up. When people want different things, return to the business goal and what you learned during discovery; do not decide based only on job title. Keep a RAID record of risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies. Write assumptions down because hidden assumptions can lead to late surprises.

Process Mapping and Gap Analysis

Map the current state before you design a solution. The real process often differs from how people describe it. Then map the future state. Compare the two to complete a gap analysis and identify work for the backlog. Keep process maps easy to read; swimlanes can show who does each step. Note when work moves from Salesforce to email or spreadsheets, where delays and errors can occur. A map also helps explain why a step was removed.

Requirements, Testing and Adoption

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Business Analyst (BA-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Separate functional requirements, which describe what a system must do, from non-functional requirements such as speed, security, accessibility, and capacity. These are easy to miss and can be costly to add later. Use traceability to connect each business need to a story and a test. Plan user acceptance testing with real users who check the solution against the acceptance criteria. Then plan training, communication, and a way to measure whether people use the solution. A solution only helps if people use it.

Every BA exam scenario maps to one of five stages. A Requirements Traceability Matrix ties each stage’s artifacts back to the original business requirement, so nothing is built, or tested, that wasn’t asked for.

How to pass the Salesforce Business Analyst exam

Most questions ask what the analyst should do next. The best answer usually helps the team understand the need or record an agreement before building a solution.

Choosing an Elicitation Technique

Use an interview for detail or sensitive topics, a workshop to help a group agree, observation to learn what people really do, and a survey to ask simple questions of many people.

Include the role, goal, benefit, and acceptance criteria a tester can check. If a story describes a screen instead of a need, it may jump to a solution too soon.

Map the current process first, then the future process, then identify the gap. Swimlanes show who does each step and where work leaves Salesforce.

Users run user acceptance testing against the acceptance criteria. A project team demo is not UAT.

Map stakeholder influence and interest, name decision-makers early, and use business goals and discovery evidence to resolve disagreements.

Performance measures are non-functional requirements, not the main purpose of acceptance criteria.

Communications Cloud AP: core exam concepts

Product Catalog & Offer Management

The Enterprise Product Catalog (EPC) stores the products and offers a provider sells. A product describes a service or device; its attributes capture choices such as speed or color. An offer is what a customer can buy and may combine several products into a bundle, such as broadband and TV. Promotions apply limited-time discounts, while price lists hold prices that may vary by market or channel. Reusable products let a change, such as replacing a router model, carry through to every offer that uses it.

chunks.title: Salesforce Accredited Agentforce Communications Professional (Communications Cloud AP) Guide

Industries CPQ for Telecom

Industries CPQ provides a cart where an agent or customer selects offers, chooses attributes, and sees the price. Rules keep choices valid. Eligibility rules decide whether a customer can buy an offer, perhaps based on service location. Compatibility rules prevent combinations that cannot work together, such as two broadband plans on one line. Context rules use customer or location information to change what appears. The cart can support agent workflows and Digital Commerce channels through APIs.

Order Management & Orchestration

When a customer submits an order, Industries Order Management uses decomposition to break the commercial request into the technical work needed to deliver it. An orchestration plan runs the work in the required sequence. For example, the plan may reserve a phone number, ship a router, and then activate a line, while communicating with external systems. If a task fails, the plan can retry, wait, or alert an operator. The customer sees one order even when several back-office tasks are required.

Contract & Subscription Lifecycle

After fulfillment, the customer’s services are recorded as assets on the account. Later service requests often use MACD: move, add, change, or disconnect. Upgrading a broadband speed changes an existing asset rather than starting an unrelated service. Contracts record terms such as commitment length and early termination fees, and may be renewed. Accurate assets give future service changes a reliable starting point.

Partner Ecosystem & Channel Management

Communications providers may sell through retail shops, partners, and online channels. An Experience Cloud site can give partners sales tools that use the same catalog and cart as internal agents, with channel-specific prices or offers. OmniStudio supports many guided experiences: OmniScripts guide users through steps, FlexCards summarize customer information, Integration Procedures gather data from systems, and Data Mappers read, transform, and save records.

Payment terms cover finance rather than merchandising layout.

Question 5: A representative takes a shelf photo and the system identifies visible products. What capability is being used?

AA manual count entered by the representative

BImage recognition for a shelf audit

CAn automatic replenishment order to the distribution center

DA retailer-provided planogram template

Correct answer: B. Image recognition for a shelf audit

Image recognition analyzes the photo to identify products or shelf conditions for the audit.

Manual counting relies on the rep to enter each observation rather than analyzing the image.

Replenishment may follow an audit but is not the image analysis itself.

A planogram describes the intended layout; it does not identify products in a photo.

chunks.content:
Question 6: Why might a consumer goods team measure its share of shelf?

ARetailers must publish the figure each quarter

BIt sets the supplier's payment terms

CIt determines the approved field headcount

DShelf space can influence what shoppers buy

Correct answer: D. Shelf space can influence what shoppers buy

The amount and placement of shelf space can affect product visibility and sales, so teams track it as an execution measure.

There is no general rule requiring retailers to publish this figure quarterly.

Payment terms are negotiated separately from shelf placement.

Staffing levels are an internal decision, not calculated from shelf share alone.

Question 7: A six-week promotion ran in 300 outlets. Which measure best estimates whether it increased sales?

AThe number of display units shipped to stores

BThe number of photos uploaded by representatives

CThe number of outlets visited during the promotion

DSales lift compared with a suitable baseline period

Correct answer: D. Sales lift compared with a suitable baseline period

Comparing sales with a comparable baseline helps estimate the change associated with the promotion.

Shipments measure product sent to stores, not the resulting sales lift.

Photo counts show data capture volume, not the promotion's sales effect.

Visit counts measure field activity rather than customer purchasing.

Question 8: What does trade promotion management help a company do?

ARecruit and schedule field representatives

BPlan and fund promotions with retail partners

CDesign product packaging artwork

DRoute delivery vehicles to stores

Correct answer: B. Plan and fund promotions with retail partners

Trade promotion management supports planning, funding, and tracking promotional activity with retailers.

Recruitment and staffing are workforce activities, not trade promotion planning.

Packaging design is separate from managing retailer promotions.

Vehicle routing is a logistics task rather than promotion management.

Question 9: A product is missing from the shelf, but the store has plenty of it in the back room. What problem should the visit record flag?

AA planogram design error

BAn in-store replenishment issue

CA pricing dispute with the retailer

DA shortage at the manufacturer's plant

Correct answer: B. An in-store replenishment issue

Because stock is already in the store, moving it from the back room to the shelf is an in-store replenishment issue.

The observation does not show that the intended shelf layout is wrong.

Price does not explain why available stock remains in the back room.

The stock is present at the outlet, so a factory shortage is not indicated.

Question 10: Why might a company schedule high-volume outlets more often than small stores?

ARepresentatives are contractually capped at one call per store

BAll stores in a chain must be visited on the same day

CThe mobile app limits the number of weekly calls

DOutlet size and sales potential vary

Correct answer: D. Outlet size and sales potential vary

Visit frequency can reflect outlet value and service needs, so a high-volume store may warrant more frequent attention.

This is not generally determined by a fixed contractual limit on calls.

A chain does not need every store visited on the same day.

App synchronization capacity is not the reason to vary call frequency.

Question 11: What is one benefit of recording competitor presence during a store visit?

AIt shows how the wider category is performing

BIt fulfills a universal retailer reporting requirement

CIt makes measuring the company's own shelf presence unnecessary

DIt lets the supplier set competitors' retail prices

Correct answer: A. It shows how the wider category is performing

Competitor observations help put a company's own shelf and sales results in the context of the wider category.

There is no universal requirement for suppliers to report every brand in a store.

Competitor information adds context but does not replace measuring the company's products.

A supplier cannot set another company's prices at a retailer.

Question 12: A manager wants to know whether representatives completed their scheduled calls. What should they review?

AVisit completion compared with the call plan

BProduct volume shipped into the region

CThe number of territory photos uploaded

DThe number of promotions agreed during the quarter

Correct answer: A. Visit completion compared with the call plan

Comparing completed visits with the plan directly shows whether scheduled calls took place.

chunks.title: Salesforce Accredited Agentforce Consumer Goods Professional (Consumer Goods Cloud AP) Guide
chunks.content:
Shipment volume measures product movement, not completion of store calls.

Photo counts can vary and do not establish whether planned calls happened.

Promotion count measures commercial agreements, not field-call completion.

Question 13: A representative captures visit information offline and later reconnects. What should happen to the saved data?

AIt waits for an administrator to approve each upload

BIt syncs to the org when connectivity returns

CIt is discarded because offline data cannot be trusted

DIt is emailed to a manager for manual entry

Correct answer: B. It syncs to the org when connectivity returns

Offline capture preserves the representative's work so it can synchronize to the org after connectivity returns.

Requiring manual approval for every upload is not the normal offline-sync process.

Offline capture is designed to retain valid work made without a connection.

Email and re-entry would defeat the purpose of capturing information in the app.

Question 14: Why might a field team record the price displayed on a store shelf?

ASuppliers are legally required to enforce each retailer's price

BIt is the only way to know what the retailer ordered

CShelf price can affect demand and how shoppers view the brand

DIt sets the representative's commission

Correct answer: C. Shelf price can affect demand and how shoppers view the brand

The displayed retail price can influence shopper choices and brand positioning, so observing it is useful context.

A supplier generally does not control the retailer's resale price.

Order records show what the retailer purchased; shelf price is a separate observation.

Representative commission is not normally set by the shelf price alone.

Question 15: Which statement best describes Consumer Goods Cloud?

AIt plans next year's product portfolio

BIt schedules factory production

CIt supports field execution at retail outlets

DIt manages field staff payroll and expenses

Correct answer: C. It supports field execution at retail outlets

Consumer Goods Cloud supports retail field work such as planning visits, recording store conditions, and managing execution.

Product portfolio planning is a separate business planning activity.

Factory scheduling belongs to manufacturing operations.

Payroll and expenses are handled through workforce or finance systems.

Consumer Goods TPM AP: Key Concepts

Trade Promotion Planning & Fund Management

Retailers and consumer goods companies use trade funds to pay for promotions. An account plan sets volume, revenue and spending goals. A fixed fund has a set budget; a variable fund can increase with sales. Track planned, committed and actual spending against the fund.

Promotion Execution & Tactics

A promotion defines the retailer, products and dates. Its tactics describe activities such as a price reduction, display or flyer placement. Each tactic has an expected cost and sales effect. Teams can use approval rules and templates to manage promotion spending.

Settlement & Claims Processing

A retailer may request payment through a claim or subtract an amount from an invoice as a deduction. Match the request to the promotion and tactic, check the amount, and investigate differences before approving payment. This helps prevent duplicate payment and inaccurate spend.

Forecasting & Baseline Analytics

Baseline volume is the estimated sales without a promotion. Incremental volume is the additional sales attributed to it. Compare incremental profit with promotion costs to assess return, then compare forecast and actual results after the event.

Integration with ERP & Retailer Data

TPM uses shipment and invoice data from ERP systems and point-of-sale data from retailers or providers. Product and account hierarchies support planning at the right level. Consistent customer and product IDs help connect transactions and send settlement information back to finance.

Salesforce Certified Consumer Goods Cloud Trade Promotion Management Accredited Professional Practice Questions (With Explanations)

Test your knowledge with these 15 sample questions.

Answered: 0 / 15Correct: 0

Question 1: A retailer sold 12,000 cases during a promotion. Sales without the promotion were expected to be 9,000. How many cases were incremental?

Correct answer: B. 3,000 cases

Incremental volume is the extra volume caused by the promotion: total minus baseline, so 12,000 minus 9,000.

12,000 is total volume, which includes sales that would have happened anyway.

Adding them together has no meaning here.

9,000 is the baseline.

chunks.title: Consumer Goods Cloud: Trade Promotion Management Accredited Professional Guide (Retiring Feb 2027)

Question 2: A brand sets aside five cents per shipped case for retailer promotions. Which fund type fits?

AA variable fund that grows as eligible shipment volume increases

BA deduction taken from the retailer invoice after a sale

CA fixed fund with a balance agreed before the period starts

DA retailer claim requesting payment for a promotion

Correct answer: A. A variable fund that grows as eligible shipment volume increases

The amount depends on how many cases are shipped, so the fund grows with volume.

A deduction is money the retailer takes off an invoice.

A fixed fund has a set amount decided in advance.

A claim is a retailer's request to be paid.

Question 3: A retailer uses both a temporary price cut and an in-store display during one two-week campaign. How should these be represented?

AAs separate promotions managed in different planning periods

CAs one activity split into two separate claim records

DAs two tactics in one promotion

Correct answer: D. As two tactics in one promotion

Tactics describe the activities within a promotion, each with its own cost and effect.

Account plans cover the whole year for a retailer.

Funds pay for tactics, they don't describe them.

Claims come after the promotion.

Question 4: After a promotion, a retailer reduces its next invoice by $8,000. What is this amount?

AA deduction linked to the promotion and taken off an invoice

BA tactic that describes one planned promotional activity

CA sales baseline used to estimate expected volume without promotion

DA fund that holds the budget available for promotional spending

Correct answer: A. A deduction linked to the promotion and taken off an invoice

Deductions are amounts the retailer takes off an invoice, which must be matched and checked against what was agreed.

A tactic is a planned activity.

Baseline is a volume measure.

Question 5: A retailer submits a claim that is $2,000 above the agreed tactic cost. What should the team do?

AAutomatically increase the fund budget

BReview the difference before approving payment

CDelete the promotion

DPay the entire claim immediately

chunks.title: Consumer Goods Cloud: Trade Promotion Management Accredited Professional Guide (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Correct answer: B. Review the difference before approving payment

Differences should be checked before paying, so the company doesn't overpay.

Raising the budget hides the problem.

Deleting the promotion loses the record.

Paying without checking risks paying for things that weren't agreed.

Question 6: Which measure best indicates whether a promotion delivered value for its cost?

ATotal units sold, including volume that may have occurred anyway

BThe number of tactics used to carry out the promotion

CROI comparing incremental profit with the cost of the promotion

DThe length of time the promotion remained active

Correct answer: C. ROI comparing incremental profit with the cost of the promotion

ROI looks at the extra profit the promotion created against what it cost.

Total volume includes sales that would have happened anyway.

More tactics doesn't mean better results.

Length doesn't measure value.

Question 7: Where does a company's shipment, or sell-in, data usually originate?

CThe retailer's promotional flyer

Correct answer: D. The company's ERP

Shipments and invoices are recorded in the ERP and loaded into TPM.

Account plans hold targets.

The flyer is a promotion activity.

Question 8: Planners need to compare a promotion's actual results with its forecast. Which analysis should they use?

Correct answer: B. Post-event analysis

Post-event analysis compares forecast with actual results, which improves future planning.

A fund transfer moves budget.

A claim is a payment request.

An account plan sets targets for the future.

Question 9: A key account manager needs to check whether planned promotions will meet a retailer's annual volume target. Which record should they review?

AThe retailer's account plan with its annual targets and planned activity

BThe product price used to calculate the retailer order value

CAn individual claim submitted after a promotion has ended

DThe ERP invoice list showing past shipments and customer charges

Correct answer: A. The retailer's account plan with its annual targets and planned activity

Account plans compare targets with planned promotions, showing gaps early.

Price alone doesn't show targets.

One claim shows one payment.

Invoices show past sales, not plans against targets.

AProceed without checking whether the planned spend fits the available budget

BDelete the fund record so the promotion can be approved without a limit

CSend the plan through approval rules before committing the promotion spend

DAutomatically approve the related claim before checking the fund balance

Correct answer: C. Send the plan through approval rules before committing the promotion spend

Approval rules can check spend against available funds before a promotion goes ahead.

Ignoring funds defeats budget control.

Deleting the fund loses budget tracking.

Automatic approval risks overspending.

Question 11: A data provider sends weekly retailer point-of-sale data. What does this data help TPM measure?

AThe tactics planned for the promotion and retailer account

BA replacement for the ERP

CWhat consumers actually purchased

DThe budget assigned to each fund

Correct answer: C. What consumers actually purchased

Sell-out data shows real consumer purchases, which helps measure promotion effect.

Tactics are planned by users.

The ERP still holds shipments and invoices.

Budgets are set separately.

Question 12: A team wants to plan retailer-group promotions at the brand level instead of for each item. What data structure supports this?

AA separate Salesforce org for each brand and retailer group

BManual spreadsheets used to plan each brand and customer group

CProduct and account hierarchies

DA separate fund for every item

Correct answer: C. Product and account hierarchies

Hierarchies let users plan at higher levels, like brand and retailer group, and roll numbers up and down.

A separate org isn't needed.

Spreadsheets bypass the system.

A fund per item is the opposite of planning at brand level.

Question 13: Teams repeatedly create the same promotion type from scratch. What can make setup faster and more consistent?

ALonger promotion periods

Correct answer: D. Promotion templates

Templates pre-fill common promotion types, so they are faster to create and set up the same way.

Length doesn't affect setup time.

Fewer tactics may not match the plan.

More funds don't speed up setup.

chunks.content:
Question 14: Why should product and customer identifiers align across TPM, the ERP, and retailer data?

ATo match shipment, sell-out, and claim records for the right products and customers

BTo lower the amount paid for promotional tactics across all retailers

CTo stop a fund from reaching its approved spending limit during the period

DTo improve the speed of pages on the company website for retail users

Correct answer: A. To match shipment, sell-out, and claim records for the right products and customers

Consistent IDs let the system tie each piece of data to the right product, customer and promotion.

Costs are set by the tactic, not the ID.

Matching IDs doesn't add money to funds.

Website speed is unrelated.

Question 15: A promotion increased sales volume, but its deep price cut reduced profit. What does this result show?

AAny promotion that raises sales is profitable

BA large volume lift does not guarantee a positive ROI

CBaselines are irrelevant

DThe fund balance was too small

Correct answer: B. A large volume lift does not guarantee a positive ROI

ROI depends on profit, not just volume. A deep discount can drive volume while losing money.

Lift and profit are not the same thing.

Baselines are needed to measure lift.

Fund size doesn't explain lost profit.

Contact Center AP: Key Concepts

Omni-Channel Routing & Queues

chunks.title: Contact Center Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Omni-Channel routes cases, chats, calls, and other work to available agents. Queue-based routing offers work to available members of a queue. Skills-based routing matches work to agents with the right skills, such as a language or product. Omni-Channel Flows can use logic, such as sending VIP customers to a specialist team. Routing configurations set priority and how much capacity each work item uses. Agents choose a presence status to show which types of work they can take.

Service Cloud Voice & CTI Integration

Service Cloud Voice brings phone calls into the Service Console alongside the customer record and transcript. It can use Amazon Connect or a partner telephony provider. Calls can be routed through Omni-Channel with other work. The IVR (phone menu) and contact flows are set up in the telephony system, which can look up Salesforce data. Real-time transcription can help supervisors follow calls and can support AI suggestions.

Einstein Bots & Digital Engagement

Customers can contact a business through messaging such as web chat, in-app messaging, SMS, and WhatsApp. Bots, including Einstein Bots and Agentforce agents, can answer common questions, collect details, and hand a conversation to a person. Pass the conversation and details to the agent so the customer does not have to repeat them. Omni-Channel can route messaging sessions as it routes cases and calls.

Knowledge Management & Deflection

Knowledge articles can support several contact-center channels: agents search for and attach answers to cases, help sites publish self-service content, and bots can suggest articles during chat. When the customer resolves an issue without agent help, the contact center records a deflected interaction. Keep article publishing and audience visibility in mind when planning which answers each channel can surface.

Reporting & Contact Center Analytics

Omni Supervisor lets supervisors monitor queues, agent status, and wait times in real time, and reassign work. Reports and dashboards can show average handle time, first contact resolution, wait time, abandonment rate, and customer satisfaction. Use these measures to review staffing, routing, and bot content.

CPQ Administrator: core exam concepts

Product Rules and Price Rules

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified CPQ Administrator (Sales-Admn-202 / CPQ-211) Historical Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Product rules control what users can select in a bundle or product search. Validation rules report conditions that must be fixed, selection rules add or change options, alert rules show a warning, and filter rules narrow search results. Price rules use conditions and actions to update quote or quote line fields. Evaluation events determine when a price rule runs, such as Before Calculate or After Calculate. When a scenario asks to control product choices, consider a product rule; when it asks to set a field value, consider a price rule.

Bundles, Features, and Options

A bundle is a parent product with configurable options, which can be grouped into features. Feature minimum and maximum values control how many options a user can select. An option can have its own quantity and pricing behavior; a bundled option contributes to the parent price instead of showing its own separate total. Configuration attributes let a user make a selection that rules can use to control other options. Nested bundles allow an option to contain another configurable group.

The Pricing Waterfall

CPQ calculates prices in stages: list price, special price, regular price, customer price, and net price. The price book supplies list price. Contracted prices and block pricing can affect special price; quantity adjustments feed into regular price; discount schedules and manual discounts contribute to customer price; partner or distributor discounts can affect net price. A discount schedule can use slab pricing, where each tier applies to units within that tier, or range pricing, where the reached tier applies to the full quantity.

Discounts, Contracted Prices, and Approvals

Discount schedules apply configured discounts by volume or term. A contracted price stores a negotiated price for a product and account. Sales users may enter manual discounts, subject to configured limits and approvals. Advanced Approvals supports approval chains and features such as smart approvals, which can skip an approver who already approved an equal or greater discount. Identify whether a question concerns calculating a price or routing a quote for approval.

Contracts, Subscriptions, Renewals, and Amendments

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified CPQ Administrator (Sales-Admn-202 / CPQ-211) Historical Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
When a quote is ordered and contracted, CPQ can create subscription records with start and end dates. Renewal forecasting and renewal quoting settings control automatic creation of renewal opportunities and quotes. Amendments change a contract during its active term. The amendment quote uses the contract and its subscriptions as the starting point, and CPQ prorates changes over the remaining term. Keep renewals, which start a new term, separate from amendments, which change the current term.

An Opportunity generates a Quote, where Product Rules, Price Rules, and Discount Schedules determine the final price. Advanced Approvals route discounts above threshold. Once Primary and Closed Won, CPQ can generate a Contract that drives future Renewals.

Question 1: A bundle should make Premium Support unavailable whenever a buyer selects the Basic tier. Which configuration fits?

AA selection rule that disables Premium Support

BA validation rule that blocks the quote after configuration

CA price rule that changes the quote line amount

DA discount schedule for the Basic tier

Correct answer: A. A selection rule that disables Premium Support

Selection rules can enable or disable bundle options based on another choice, which matches this requirement.

A validation rule reports or blocks an invalid configuration rather than disabling the option as the user chooses.

Price rules update field values and do not control whether a product option is available.

AA separate price book for the account

CA discount schedule for all accounts

DA manual discount on each quote

Correct answer: B. A contracted price

A contracted price stores the negotiated account and product price so CPQ can apply it to future quotes.

A separate price book is not the CPQ feature for maintaining a contracted product price.

A discount schedule varies by quantity or term rather than by a particular account price.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified CPQ Administrator (Sales-Admn-202 / CPQ-211) Historical Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Manual entry depends on the user and does not apply automatically.

Question 3: A schedule applies the tier reached at 100 units to all 100 units. Which schedule method is this?

Correct answer: C. Range pricing

Range pricing applies the reached tier to the full quantity, so all 100 units use that tier rate.

Slab pricing applies each tier rate only to the units within that tier.

Term pricing varies by subscription length, not quantity tiers.

Block pricing assigns a fixed price to a quantity block rather than applying a reached discount rate to all units.

Question 4: A customer wants 20 more licenses four months into a 12-month contract. What should the admin create?

AA new quote on a separate opportunity

BA renewal quote for the next term

CAn amendment quote from the contract

DAn edit to the original quote

Correct answer: C. An amendment quote from the contract

An amendment quote changes an active contract and can prorate the additional licenses over the remaining term.

A separate quote would not make the change against the active contract.

A renewal quote is for the next contract term, not a mid-term change.

The contracted sale should be changed through an amendment rather than by editing the original quote.

Question 5: At which pricing stage do discount schedules contribute their discount?

Correct answer: B. Customer price

Discount schedules contribute to the customer price stage of the CPQ pricing waterfall.

Special price is where mechanisms such as contracted prices and block pricing can apply.

Net price follows customer price and can include partner or distributor discounts.

List price comes from the price book before later pricing adjustments.

Question 6: A price rule must set a field before CPQ calculates prices. Which evaluation event should it use?

Correct answer: D. Before Calculate

Before Calculate runs before the pricing calculation, allowing the rule to set the field in time.

On Save is not a CPQ price rule evaluation event for this purpose.

On Initialization runs when the editor initializes, not immediately before a calculation.

After Calculate occurs after the pricing calculation has completed.

chunks.content:

Correct answer: C. Alert

An alert rule presents a message without blocking the user from continuing.

Validation rules are used to flag conditions that may prevent a quote from proceeding.

Selection rules change which options are selected or available.

Filter rules limit the products displayed in product search.

Question 8: What does CPQ create for subscription products when an ordered quote is contracted?

ADated subscription records

BRecords held until the renewal date

DOne-time product records

Correct answer: A. Dated subscription records

Contracting creates subscription records that represent the service term and support later renewals or amendments.

The subscriptions are created during contracting rather than waiting until renewal.

The quote remains as the record of what was sold; its lines are not simply deleted.

A subscription product remains a subscription rather than becoming a one-time product.

Question 9: An approver approved a 20% discount. On resubmission at 15%, the same approver should be skipped. Which feature supports this?

AA validation rule attached to the quote record

BA standard Salesforce approval process

CAn alert rule shown during product configuration

Correct answer: D. Smart approvals

Smart approvals can skip an approver who previously approved an equal or greater discount.

Validation rules address record conditions and do not determine whether an approver is repeated.

The requirement describes smart approval behavior rather than a basic approval process.

Product alert rules display messages during configuration and do not route approvals.

Question 10: A bundle feature must require at least one and no more than three options. Where should this be set?

AThe option quantity value on each individual product option

BThe price book entry linked to the parent bundle product

CA validation product rule that runs after selections are made

DFeature min/max option limits

Correct answer: D. Feature min/max option limits

Feature minimum and maximum values directly set how many options a user must or may select.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified CPQ Administrator (Sales-Admn-202 / CPQ-211) Historical Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Option quantity controls how many units of an option are added, not the number of choices in a feature.

Price book entries define price information rather than selection limits.

A validation rule could report an invalid count, but the feature fields define the selection limits.

Question 11: What does the bundled flag on a product option mean for its price?

AIncluded in the price of the parent product

BThe option must always be free

CThe admin must manually discount it to zero

DIt always has a separately priced quote line

Correct answer: A. Included in the price of the parent product

A bundled option contributes to the parent product price rather than adding a separate option price.

Bundled describes how the price is represented; it does not mean the option has no value.

The bundled setting handles the pricing relationship without a manual zero discount.

A separately priced option is the behavior of an unbundled option.

Question 12: Why add a configuration attribute at the top of a bundle configurator?

ATo remove the need for product rules

BTo store the final quote total

CA choice that drives dependent options

DTo set the contract end date

Correct answer: C. A choice that drives dependent options

A configuration attribute lets a user make a choice that selection rules can apply to options below it.

Attributes can provide inputs to product rules rather than replace the rules.

The quote calculation determines totals; a configuration attribute is not the total field.

Contract dates are set through the contract and subscription process.

Question 13: A renewal opportunity and quote should be created as a contract approaches its end date. What controls this?

AThe amendment process

BRenewal forecast and quote creation settings

CA custom scheduled Apex job

DA price rule with an After Calculate event

Correct answer: B. Renewal forecast and quote creation settings

The contract renewal forecasting and renewal quoting settings govern automatic renewal record creation.

Amendments handle changes during the current contract term.

Standard CPQ renewal settings can support this without a custom scheduled job.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified CPQ Administrator (Sales-Admn-202 / CPQ-211) Historical Guide & Practice Questions

Price rules update quote values and do not create renewal opportunities.

Question 14: Why might a user-entered manual discount not affect the net price as expected?

AThe net price stage does not include discounts entered on a quote

BAn earlier price stage may set the value before later adjustments

CCPQ does not support manual discounts on quoted products

DManual discounts apply only to subscription product lines

Correct answer: B. An earlier price stage may set the value before later adjustments

The pricing waterfall runs in order, and earlier values or settings can affect how later discounting is calculated.

Net price is calculated after discounts rather than excluding them all.

Manual discounts are a supported CPQ capability.

Discounts can apply to one-time products as well as subscriptions.

Question 15: What does a product filter rule do?

ALimits the products returned by search

BWrites a value into a target quote field

CBlocks a quote from being saved

DCalculates prorated charges for an amendment

Correct answer: A. Limits the products returned by search

A filter rule narrows the products returned during product selection based on its conditions.

Writing field values is handled by price rule actions.

A validation rule is used to flag or prevent an invalid quote condition.

Amendment proration is part of CPQ contract change calculations.

chunks.title: CPQ and Billing Consultant Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
CPQ and Billing AP: core concepts

Salesforce Billing extends a CPQ process into billing and payment activities. A quote can be ordered, producing order records that Billing uses to generate invoices. Billing policies can define invoice timing, payment terms, and consolidation behavior. Legal entities represent the billing entity involved in a transaction. Tax integrations can calculate tax on invoices. Be prepared to explain the record relationships and the setup needed for the process.

Invoice Generation and Billing Rules

Billing rules define when and how a charge should be invoiced. Bill Now can invoice immediately; Bill in Advance invoices at the beginning of a period; Bill in Arrears invoices after a period ends. Billing frequency can be monthly, quarterly, annual, or one-time, depending on the product setup. An invoice run processes eligible charges and creates invoices with invoice lines. Credit notes can record adjustments, while billing batches can support high-volume processing.

Usage billing supports variable charges based on consumption, such as API calls or data transfer. Usage records can be summarized for a billing period and rated using configured rates or tiers. The resulting rated usage can be included in invoicing. An overage charge applies when consumption exceeds an amount included in a subscription. Understand how usage data enters the process and how it becomes a billable charge.

Payments and Failed Charges

Payment configuration connects invoices to payment methods and processors. Payment terms describe when an invoice is due. Auto-pay can charge a stored payment method according to the configured process. Dunning manages follow-up for failed payments, such as retry attempts and customer notices. Payment allocations connect payments to invoices, while refunds and credit memos can reverse or adjust charges. Know how these records support collections and account servicing.

Revenue Recognition and Reporting

chunks.title: CPQ and Billing Consultant Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Revenue schedules spread revenue across periods when recognition follows a service term, or recognize it at a point in time when appropriate. Revenue recognition rules define the timing, and transactions record amounts for accounting periods. Finance period settings establish those period boundaries. Reports can help finance teams compare recognized and deferred revenue. Learn how changes to a contract can affect the schedule and its reporting.

Salesforce Certified CPQ and Billing Consultant Accredited Professional Practice Questions (With Explanations)

Test your knowledge with these 15 sample questions.

Answered: 0 / 15Correct: 0

Question 1: A contracted sale should produce monthly invoices. Which CPQ Billing record supports the planned invoice dates?

AA separate opportunity for each monthly charge

BA billing schedule associated with the order product

CA renewal contract for every monthly period

DA new quote created at the start of each month

Correct answer: B. A billing schedule associated with the order product

A billing schedule defines when eligible charges are due for invoicing across the subscription term.

Opportunities track sales work and are not created for each recurring invoice.

A billing schedule associated with the order product supports recurring invoice timing.

Renewal contracts cover later terms, not each billing period in the current term.

Question 2: How does an invoice differ from an invoice line?

AAn invoice is only for subscriptions; a line is only for one-time items

BThe invoice stores tax and each line stores the payment

CThe invoice is the document, and its lines list the individual charges

DThe invoice is a draft while its lines are final posted records

Correct answer: C. The invoice is the document, and its lines list the individual charges

The invoice is the overall billing record, while invoice lines represent the charges included on it.

Both subscriptions and one-time charges can appear on invoices depending on configuration.

Tax and payments are not divided between invoice and line in this way.

Invoice lines are part of the invoice rather than independently final records.

Question 3: A customer upgrades during a contract and should pay only for the remaining term. What supports the adjusted charge?

chunks.title: CPQ and Billing Consultant Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
AProration on the amendment

BA replacement contract starting at the original date

CA manual finance adjustment on a future invoice

DA credit note for the full original annual amount

Correct answer: A. Proration on the amendment

Proration on an amendment adjusts the charge to account for the remaining contract period.

A replacement contract is not needed to adjust a mid-term change.

A manual adjustment bypasses the amendment and proration process.

Crediting the full annual amount would not reflect the value of the upgrade.

Question 4: What does revenue recognition determine?

AThe maximum discount permitted on a quote line

BWhich payment method a customer may use

CWhen revenue is recorded relative to invoicing

DWhich currency is shown on an invoice

Correct answer: C. When revenue is recorded relative to invoicing

Revenue recognition determines when billed amounts are recognized as revenue for accounting purposes.

Discount limits affect quote pricing, not the timing of revenue recognition.

Payment methods control collection, not when revenue is recognized.

Invoice currency is separate from revenue timing.

Question 5: A posted invoice contains an error. What is the appropriate way to correct the billed amount?

AEdit the posted invoice and save it again

BIssue a credit note against the invoice

CLeave it unchanged and add a note to the account

DDelete it and create a replacement invoice

Correct answer: B. Issue a credit note against the invoice

A credit note records an adjustment against the posted invoice while preserving the billing history.

Posted invoices should not simply be edited to erase the original transaction.

An account note does not correct the invoiced amount or record the adjustment.

Deleting the posted invoice would remove the audit trail rather than make a traceable correction.

Question 6: What action typically triggers order creation in a CPQ and Billing flow?

ASaving a draft quote in the Quote Line Editor

BOrdering the accepted quote

CAdding the first subscription product to the quote

DSubmitting the quote for manager approval

Correct answer: B. Ordering the accepted quote

Ordering the accepted quote creates the order that can continue into Billing.

chunks.title: CPQ and Billing Consultant Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
A draft save preserves quote work but does not create the ordered transaction.

Adding a product configures the quote but does not order it.

Approval is a review step and is not itself the order trigger.

Question 7: A customer pays only part of an invoice balance. How should the payment be recorded?

AAs a contract amendment lowering the term value

BAs a new invoice for the unpaid amount

CAs a partial payment allocated to the invoice

DAs a credit note for the unpaid balance

Correct answer: C. As a partial payment allocated to the invoice

A partial payment is allocated against the invoice, leaving the remaining balance open.

An amendment changes contract terms rather than recording money received.

A second invoice would duplicate the charge instead of recording partial settlement.

A credit note reduces a charge; it does not represent a partial payment.

Question 8: What does a Billing rule control?

AWhich products a salesperson may add to a quote

BWhich approval chain a discounted quote follows

CThe order of quote lines in the editor

DHow and when charges are invoiced

Correct answer: D. How and when charges are invoiced

Billing rules define the timing and method used to invoice charges.

Product availability is controlled through product setup and rules.

Approval routing is managed by approval configuration.

Quote line display order is separate from billing rules.

Question 9: A January-to-December subscription is billed quarterly. How many billing periods are there?

ATwelve monthly periods

BOne period for the entire contract

CFour quarterly periods

DThree periods because the first is billed with the order

Correct answer: C. Four quarterly periods

A one-year term billed quarterly has four billing periods.

Monthly billing would produce twelve periods, but this subscription is quarterly.

A single period would represent one-time or annual billing, not quarterly billing.

The order does not remove a quarter from the billing schedule.

Question 10: What does a tax rule do in CPQ Billing?

ADetermines how tax is calculated for a charge

BBlocks invoice posting until a tax reference is entered

CReports annual tax collected by a legal entity

chunks.title: CPQ and Billing Consultant Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
DConverts tax to the company functional currency

Correct answer: A. Determines how tax is calculated for a charge

A tax rule determines how tax should be calculated for the charge under the configured tax setup.

A tax rule calculates tax; it does not necessarily impose that particular posting condition.

Reporting summarizes tax after calculation and does not define the calculation itself.

Currency conversion is a separate finance or tax integration behavior.

Question 11: Why use an evergreen subscription instead of a fixed-term subscription?

AThe purchase has no recurring service component

BThe service continues until it is canceled

CThe contract must be renegotiated at every term end

DThe customer wants annual rather than monthly invoices

Correct answer: B. The service continues until it is canceled

An evergreen subscription continues until a cancellation ends it rather than expiring on a fixed end date.

Evergreen describes a recurring service, not a one-time purchase.

It does not require renewal negotiations at a fixed term boundary.

Invoice frequency is independent of whether a subscription is evergreen.

Question 12: An order is active but no invoice has been generated. What is a likely reason?

AThe next billing date has not arrived yet

BThe quote was not approved before ordering

CThe customer is missing an industry value

DThe product is configured as a bundle

Correct answer: A. The next billing date has not arrived yet

If billing follows a schedule, no invoice may be due until the next scheduled billing date.

The order being active indicates it has already passed the relevant order process.

An industry value is not generally required to determine billing schedule timing.

Bundled products can still be billed according to their setup.

Question 13: What does an invoice run do?

AReprices open quotes with current price book values

BCloses the accounting period to further postings

CResends every unpaid invoice by email

DCreates invoices from charges whose schedules are due

Correct answer: D. Creates invoices from charges whose schedules are due

An invoice run processes due billable charges and generates their invoices.

Quote repricing is separate from invoice generation.

chunks.title: CPQ and Billing Consultant Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Closing an accounting period is a finance-period control, not an invoice run.

An invoice run generates invoices rather than simply resending existing ones.

Question 14: A customer cancels a prepaid annual subscription halfway through the term. What may be issued for the unused period?

AA renewal quote starting on the cancellation date

BAn amendment that increases the contract value

CA new invoice for months of service not delivered

DA credit for the unused portion of the term

Correct answer: D. A credit for the unused portion of the term

A credit can account for the unused prepaid service when the subscription is canceled, subject to the configured policy.

A renewal starts a later term and does not handle unused prepaid value.

Cancellation does not normally increase the contract value for undelivered service.

Billing the customer for undelivered months would not provide the described adjustment.

Question 15: Which statement describes the relationship between CPQ and Billing?

ACPQ creates the order, and Billing invoices the ordered charges

BBilling creates the quote, and CPQ collects customer payments

CThey are alternatives, so an org can use only one

DCPQ manages subscriptions while Billing handles only one-time charges

Correct answer: A. CPQ creates the order, and Billing invoices the ordered charges

CPQ supports product configuration and quoting through order creation; Billing processes the charges for invoicing.

Billing does not replace CPQ for quote creation, and payment collection is not CPQ’s role.

CPQ and Billing can work together as parts of a quote-to-cash process.

Billing can support recurring subscription charges as well as other configured charges.

The exam spans CRM Analytics data preparation and dashboards as well as Einstein Discovery models and predictions. Security design and model evaluation require careful study because they involve decisions beyond simply building a chart.

Evaluate models before deployment: Review model metrics, potential leakage, and bias checks.

CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant exam format

The exam is proctored online or at a test center. Questions cover data preparation, dashboard behavior, security, and predictive analytics.

Multiple-choice & multiple-select

How Many Questions Are Scenario-Based?

Many questions describe an analytics requirement and ask which feature best supports it. Compare solutions by their behavior and maintenance needs, such as using a recipe for data preparation or inherited sharing when the goal is to respect Salesforce sharing.

Best Way to Pass on Your First Attempt

Build a data preparation flow: Load, join, transform, and output data so you understand how recipes and dataflows differ.

Practice security design: Work through owner-based and role-based examples, and understand what each security approach can express.

Create and assess a Discovery story: Review model metrics and check for leakage and bias before deployment.

Learn dashboard interactions: Understand how selection and results bindings pass values between widgets, and when SAQL is needed.

CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery: core concepts

Datasets, Dataflows, and Recipes

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
CRM Analytics dashboards and lenses query datasets. A dataset is prepared data that is refreshed through a data preparation process rather than a live view of Salesforce records. Dataflows define preparation steps in a JSON-based format. Recipes provide a visual way to join and transform data, with previews along the way. Common dataflow operations include digesting Salesforce data, augmenting a dataset with related columns, flattening hierarchical data, and registering an output dataset. Choose the preparation tool that fits the requirement and the org’s established approach.

Lenses, Dashboards, and Bindings

A lens explores one dataset. A dashboard combines visualizations and other widgets. Bindings pass a value from one widget or query to another. A selection binding uses a user selection; a results binding uses query output. Pages can organize dashboard views. For performance and clarity, limit unnecessary queries and filter data close to where it is prepared or queried. Faceting can coordinate filters across related widgets.

Einstein Discovery Stories and Models

An Einstein Discovery story analyzes a dataset in relation to an outcome and highlights factors associated with that outcome. Review the model metrics that fit the outcome type: numeric predictions can be evaluated with measures such as R-squared and mean absolute error; classification models can be evaluated with a confusion matrix and related measures. Metrics are only part of the review. Check whether an input variable reveals information that would not be available when a prediction is made, and use bias checks to assess differences across relevant groups before deployment.

Deploying Predictions to Salesforce

A prediction definition connects a model to a Salesforce object so scores and related insights can be used in the business process. Deployment requires mapping model variables to fields available on the target object. Predictions may be evaluated as a user works with a record or applied to records in bulk, depending on the setup. A prediction can also be used in Flow to support an automated follow-up. Know how the model inputs map to the target data and how the score will be used.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
CRM Analytics datasets need an explicit access design. A security predicate filters dataset rows using dataset fields and user information. For example, an owner-based rule can compare the row owner with the current user. Hierarchy requirements may need a flattened hierarchy field or another representation suitable for the predicate. Inherited sharing can align dataset access with sharing on the source Salesforce object where supported. Choose based on the access requirement, source data, supported scale, and maintenance needs; do not assume that dataset access automatically mirrors Salesforce record access.

A Story trains a predictive model against a dataset, surfaces narrative insights and key predictors, and once deployed can be embedded via a prediction field or Prompt Template so Salesforce records get real-time predicted outcomes.

How to prepare for the CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant exam

For each scenario, identify whether it concerns data preparation, dashboard interaction, row access, model evaluation, or prediction deployment. Then choose the feature that meets the requirement and can be maintained.

Choose Recipes or Dataflows

Understand how both tools prepare data, and review the common dataflow operations. For a new preparation flow, know the capabilities of the visual recipe experience.

Write and Review Security Rules

Practice owner-based and hierarchy-based access examples. Be able to explain when an explicit predicate is needed and when inherited sharing may fit.

Assess the Model Before Deployment

Use appropriate metrics for the prediction type, check for leakage, and assess bias across relevant groups before publishing a model.

Know the Binding Types

Selection bindings use a user’s selection; results bindings use query results. Build a small example of each to learn how one widget can affect another.

Map and Use Predictions

When deploying a prediction, map the model variables to fields on the Salesforce object and decide whether users, bulk processing, or Flow will consume the score.

Exam format: 60 questions, 90 min, 65% passing score.

Salesforce Certified CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant Practice Questions (With Explanations)

Test your knowledge with these 20 sample questions.

Answered: 0 / 20Correct: 0

Question 1: A dataset should show each user only rows they own. Which approach directly filters the rows by the current user?

AA dashboard-level owner filter

BRemove the dataset from every app

CAn owner-based security predicate

DField-level security on the source object

Correct answer: C. An owner-based security predicate

A security predicate can compare the row owner value with the current user and restrict dataset rows accordingly.

A dashboard filter affects a particular view and is not a dataset-wide access rule.

Removing the dataset prevents use rather than providing owner-based row access.

Field-level security controls access to fields, not which dataset rows a user can see.

Question 2: The requirement is for dataset access to follow existing Salesforce object sharing, and the data volume is moderate. What should be considered first?

AInherited sharing on the dataset

BNo row restriction because app access is sufficient

CA separate dataset for every role

DA hand-written predicate that duplicates the sharing model

Correct answer: A. Inherited sharing on the dataset

Inherited sharing can use access from the underlying Salesforce object when the dataset setup supports it.

This directly matches the goal of respecting the source object sharing model.

App access alone does not necessarily restrict which rows a user can query.

Duplicating datasets by role increases maintenance and is not required by this scenario.

Question 3: A Discovery model has strong accuracy, but one input field is populated only after the outcome is known. What should the team do?

ADeploy because the accuracy score is high

BRemove the field and retrain

CConvert the field to text and keep it

DDeploy and document the limitation

Correct answer: B. Remove the field and retrain

A field that reveals information unavailable at prediction time can leak the outcome; remove it and retrain before judging the model again.

Strong metrics do not make a model valid if it uses information from after the outcome.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Changing the field type does not remove the information leakage.

Documentation does not correct a model that relies on an unavailable future value.

Question 4: Which dataflow operation adds matching columns from one dataset to another?

Correct answer: A. Augment

Augment joins related columns from another dataset based on matching key fields.

Digest extracts Salesforce object data into the data preparation flow.

Register writes the prepared output as a dataset.

Flatten changes hierarchical data into a form that can be queried.

Question 5: A dashboard widget should use the result of another query, rather than a value the user clicked. Which binding is appropriate?

BA security predicate

Correct answer: A. A results binding

A results binding passes output from one query to another widget or query.

A security predicate limits data access and does not connect query results between widgets.

A separate dataset is not necessary just to pass one query’s result.

A selection binding responds to user selections rather than query output.

Question 6: Which tool is a visual option for preparing and transforming data in CRM Analytics?

DA recipe in Data Prep

Correct answer: D. A recipe in Data Prep

Recipes provide a visual data preparation workflow with transformation steps and previews.

A report snapshot is not the CRM Analytics data preparation tool described here.

Apex can process data in custom code but is not the visual recipe interface.

Dataflows are JSON-defined; the question asks for the visual preparation tool.

Question 7: A deployed score should create a follow-up task when it falls below a chosen threshold. What can automate that response?

AAsk users to check the score and create tasks manually

BAdd a formula to the dashboard

CUse the prediction in a Flow

DRetrain the model with a different threshold

Correct answer: C. Use the prediction in a Flow

Flow can consume a prediction and create an action, such as a follow-up task, when conditions are met.

Manual review does not automate the requested follow-up.

A dashboard formula does not itself create Salesforce tasks.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Changing the model threshold is not the same as automating a task from the score.

Question 8: Which dataflow operation can make a role hierarchy usable as dataset columns for filtering?

Correct answer: A. Flatten

Flatten can turn hierarchical data into columns that can be queried or used in a predicate.

Augment joins related columns but does not itself convert a hierarchy to flat rows.

dim2mea changes a dimension into a measure; it does not represent a role hierarchy.

Slice is not the dataflow operation described for flattening hierarchical relationships.

Question 9: Which measures are suitable when evaluating a model that predicts a numeric value such as deal amount?

APrecision and recall

CR-squared and mean absolute error

DThe number of insights produced

Correct answer: C. R-squared and mean absolute error

R-squared and mean absolute error are examples of metrics used to evaluate numeric predictions.

Precision and recall are generally used for classification outcomes.

A confusion matrix summarizes classification results rather than numeric prediction error.

The count of insights does not measure the accuracy of numeric predictions.

Question 10: Why can adding many widgets make a CRM Analytics dashboard slower?

AThe server must render each widget in a strict sequence

BEach widget can add another dataset query

CA new dataset is created for every widget

DPredicates run only once for each user session

Correct answer: B. Each widget can add another dataset query

More widgets can mean more queries and requests, increasing the work needed to load the dashboard.

Widgets do not necessarily render in a strict sequence on the server.

Dataset count does not automatically increase with each dashboard widget.

Data 360 Consultant: core concepts

The Data 360 Workflow

A common workflow is to ingest source data, map it to the shared data model, resolve identities, create useful insights or segments, and activate results. Data streams connect to sources such as Salesforce, cloud storage, websites, or applications. Ingested data is stored in data lake objects (DLOs), then mapped to data model objects (DMOs) that represent concepts such as individuals or engagements. Identity resolution links records that refer to the same person. Segments select profiles that meet specified criteria, and activations send membership to a destination.

Ingestion and Data Modeling

Data streams bring data into Data 360 through configured connectors or other supported ingestion methods. Data lake objects retain ingested source data. Mapping aligns fields and records with data model objects, which provide a consistent structure for using data across sources. Keys and relationships matter because they determine how records connect. Learn which ingestion method and mapping approach fit the source and the freshness requirement.

Identity Resolution and Unified Profiles

Identity resolution applies match rules to determine which source records refer to the same individual. Reconciliation rules determine which source value is used for a field when records are unified. The resulting unified profile brings together information from linked records. Matching and reconciliation solve different problems: matching decides whether records belong together, while reconciliation selects the value displayed for a field.

Calculated Insights, Segments, and Activations

Calculated insights create derived measures from Data 360 data, such as purchase totals or days since a customer’s last activity. A segment selects profiles that meet criteria and can be refreshed according to its configuration. An activation publishes segment membership to a destination, such as a marketing platform or another connected system. Understand how source data, unified profiles, calculated insights, and segments support a downstream audience.

Consent, Governance, and Data Actions

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Data 360 Consultant (Data-Con-101 / Data Cloud) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Data 360 supports consent and privacy requirements through the configured consent data and privacy attributes. Implementations must use those controls to honor applicable preferences and requests. Data actions can respond to configured changes, such as segment membership, and initiate downstream work. Consider data governance, destination behavior, and refresh timing when designing an activation.

Records from multiple Data Streams pass through Match Rules (email, phone, custom logic). Matched records merge into a single Unified Individual, which powers Segments and Calculated Insights.

How to prepare for the Data 360 Consultant exam

For each scenario, identify the step involved: source connection, data mapping, identity resolution, segment creation, or activation. Then choose the feature that performs that step.

Know the Identity Resolution Steps

Match rules determine whether records belong to the same individual. Reconciliation rules choose the surviving field values. Practice both decisions with records from multiple sources.

Map a Source to the Data Model

Ingest sample records and map their fields to suitable data model objects. Check identifiers and relationships so records can be connected correctly.

Build and Activate an Audience

Create a segment from profile criteria, then select a destination and activation settings. Understand how segment refresh affects when the audience changes.

Compare Ingestion Options

Review batch and streaming options and the cases where data can be accessed without being copied. Choose based on source capability and freshness needs.

Apply Consent and Governance

Understand how consent and privacy attributes inform profile use and activation. Make sure downstream destinations respect the configured requirements.

AA live sales dashboard that streams current results

BA Marketing Cloud journey started by a segment

CAn Apex export job that sends data to a warehouse

DA source connection that brings data into Data 360

A data stream connects Data 360 to a source and brings that source data into the platform.

ARemote SOAP external objects

BCRM Analytics report types

CCustom Lead fields that store source system metadata

DMOs provide a standardized structure for representing data such as individuals and engagements.

AChecks privacy consent before ingestion

BAssigns Salesforce IDs to profiles

CMatch records into a unified profile

DAuthenticates source APIs with OAuth

AA Person Account that replaces duplicate Contacts

CA report type listing interactions for an Account

DA Marketing Cloud subscriber record enriched with CRM data

Question 6: What is a Data 360 segment?

AA Marketing Cloud list used only for subscription preferences

BA criteria-based audience of unified profiles

CA scheduled export to a business intelligence platform

DA permission set group for Data 360 users
