ARuns identity resolution rules on each newly ingested data stream

BGives users access to edit segments

CPublishes segment membership to a connected destination

DTurns on Data 360 in Salesforce Setup

Activation sends a segment and its membership to a configured destination for downstream use.

AA Salesforce metric updated by Apex

BA metric derived from Data 360 data

CAn Einstein score stored in a formula field

DA dashboard widget showing segment counts

AShield encryption keys that hide fields

BA daily synced Marketing Cloud opt-out

CConfigured consent and privacy attributes

AManage org sharing and Data 360 user permissions

BA single shared dataset for everyone

An unrestricted permission set controls access broadly, it doesn't create data isolation by business unit.

A Marketing Cloud business unit manages Marketing Cloud, not Data 360 data isolation.

Question 17: Two incoming records both have the email field populated, but with slightly different spellings of the customer's name. Which type of matching rule is designed to catch this as a likely match?

AA fuzzy match rule on name + address

BAn exact match rule on email only

CNo rule can catch this

DA rule based on record creation date

Correct answer: A. A fuzzy match rule on name + address

Fuzzy matching is designed to catch records that are likely the same person despite small variations, like a misspelled name, by matching on a combination of attributes rather than requiring an exact string match.

An exact match rule on email would actually work here too if emails matched exactly, but the question is about handling near-miss name spelling, which is what fuzzy matching is for.

Fuzzy matching exists specifically to catch cases like this.

Record creation date has nothing to do with identifying the same real-world person.

Question 18: A consultant needs to calculate each customer's total spend over the last 90 days from Data Model Object data. What's used to build that metric?

AA Calculated Insight, written as a SQL query against DMOs

BA Data Action triggered by a change in a Data Model Object

DAn Activation Target

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Data 360 Consultant (Data-Con-101 / Data Cloud) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Correct answer: A. A Calculated Insight, written as a SQL query against DMOs

Calculated Insights are SQL-based metrics computed over DMO data, exactly the kind of aggregation needed for a rolling spend total.

A Data Action triggers an event based on a condition, it doesn't compute an aggregated metric.

A Data Space isolates data, it doesn't calculate anything.

An Activation Target is a destination for a segment, not a calculation mechanism.

Question 19: A client asks whether they should use Data 360 or a narrower, already-existing Salesforce feature to solve a straightforward reporting need. What should the consultant do first?

AScope the actual business requirement and recommend the right-sized tool, not default to the newest platform

BRecommend Data 360 for every reporting need, because it is the newest and broadest Salesforce data platform

CTell the client it's impossible without more licenses

DBuild the solution before discussing requirements

Correct answer: A. Scope the actual business requirement and recommend the right-sized tool, not default to the newest platform

Solution Positioning is about matching the actual requirement to the right capability, sometimes that's Data 360, and sometimes an existing, simpler Salesforce feature already covers it.

Defaulting to Data 360 regardless of fit is the opposite of good solution positioning.

Jumping to "it's impossible" without scoping the requirement isn't a real assessment.

Building before understanding the requirement risks solving the wrong problem.

Question 20: A marketing user should be able to view Data 360 segments and insights, but not change ingestion or admin settings. Which permission set fits?

AData 360 Marketing Viewer

CA blank profile with no permission set

DSystem Administrator

Correct answer: A. Data 360 Marketing Viewer

A Marketing Viewer-style permission set gives read access to segments and insights without granting the broader admin and ingestion configuration rights that a Data 360 Admin permission set would include.

Data 360 Admin grants configuration access well beyond what this user needs.

A blank profile with no permission set would leave the user without even the viewing access required.

System Administrator is far broader access than the scenario calls for, and isn't the Data 360-specific answer.

Platform Data Architect: core concepts

Data Models, Relationships, and Big Objects

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Data Architect (Plat-Arch-201) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Choose standard or custom objects, external objects, and Big Objects based on the data and access pattern. Relationship types affect how records relate and how users access them. Big Objects support high-volume historical data, and queries are constrained by the configured index fields. Platform Events provide a schema-defined way to publish event messages. Evaluate each choice against the workload and published platform limits.

Master Data Management and Duplicate Control

Master data management defines how systems identify important entities, resolve duplicates, and maintain trusted values. A golden record can be assembled using survivorship rules that select values by source trust or recency. Salesforce Matching Rules find records that may be duplicates; Duplicate Rules control what happens when a match is found. External IDs can support upserts and cross-system references. Design for traceability so teams can understand where values came from.

Migration and Integration

Choose a migration method based on data volume, transformation needs, latency, and operations. Bulk API 2.0 supports asynchronous processing of large data loads and manages batches. External IDs support upsert and relationships across systems. Load parent records before dependent children when relationships require them. Plan validation, error handling, retries, and rollback or recovery before the migration begins.

Data Quality and Governance

Governance sets expectations for data ownership, quality, privacy, classification, and protection. Validation Rules can reject values that fail business checks. Matching and Duplicate Rules help manage duplicate records, while field history features can support audit needs when configured. Select the controls that meet the organization’s policies and make ongoing stewardship part of the design.

Large Data Volumes and Performance

At large scale, query selectivity, indexing, data growth, and archive strategy all affect performance. The query optimizer decides whether an available index is useful for a particular query. Custom indexes can support selective filters; skinny tables address certain query performance needs. Big Objects and external data options can support some historical or high-volume use cases. Follow current Salesforce guidance for the specific workload rather than assuming one tool fits every query.

Salesforce Certified Platform Data Architect Practice Questions (With Explanations)

Test your knowledge with these 15 sample questions.

Answered: 0 / 15Correct: 0

Question 1: A custom object with tens of millions of rows is timing out because its query filters on a non-indexed field. What should the architect evaluate first?

AIndex the filter field when the query is selective

BIncrease the API request limit so the query can run longer

CMove the object to a Big Object to remove query time limits

DEnable a skinny table because it indexes every filtered field

Correct answer: A. Index the filter field when the query is selective

A custom index may help the optimizer use a selective filter, provided the query and field meet platform requirements.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Data Architect (Plat-Arch-201) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
API request limits do not make an unselective database query faster.

Big Objects have query constraints and do not remove all time limits.

Skinny tables are not a general-purpose index for every filtered field.

Question 2: Which set of concerns matters when designing for large data volumes?

AOnly the number of fields on the object

BGovernor limits, indexing, and query selectivity

CPage layout complexity alone

DThe number of reports, without considering query patterns

Correct answer: B. Governor limits, indexing, and query selectivity

Large-volume designs must account for platform limits, indexes, and how selective the queries will be.

This combines key performance and scale considerations.

Field count alone does not determine whether a large-volume query will perform well.

Page layouts do not address query selectivity or data volume.

Question 3: A large Bulk API 2.0 load is causing row locks because many child records update the same parent. What should the team try?

AEnable PK Chunking so updates to the shared parent run in parallel

BDisable all validation rules for the whole migration

CGroup load rows by parent lookup

DReduce every batch to one record

Correct answer: C. Group load rows by parent lookup

Grouping records by parent can help organize processing and reduce concurrent updates to the same parent, subject to the load design.

PK Chunking splits work by record ranges and may not solve contention on a shared parent.

This helps keep related updates together and can reduce locking contention.

Disabling every validation rule may undermine data quality and does not directly resolve parent locks.

Question 4: A child record must always have a parent, and it should inherit key access and lifecycle behavior from that parent. Which relationship is appropriate?

Correct answer: D. Master-detail

A master-detail relationship requires a parent and ties key access and lifecycle behavior to that parent.

A lookup can allow a child record to exist without a parent.

This relationship type fits the required parent dependency.

External and indirect lookups link to external records rather than enforcing this standard parent relationship.

Question 5: What does an archiving strategy address?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Data Architect (Plat-Arch-201) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
AMove historical data off-platform and retain required access

BKeeping a second backup in the same object

CDeleting historical data immediately without review

DExporting records once without defining future retrieval

Correct answer: A. Move historical data off-platform and retain required access

Archiving moves older data from active storage while considering how it may need to be accessed later.

A backup alone does not reduce active data volume or define archive access.

Immediate deletion may violate retention or business needs.

A one-time export does not define ongoing retention or retrieval.

Question 6: What is a Salesforce Big Object designed to support?

AA standard CRM record with a large set of page layouts

BHigh-volume, append-oriented historical data

CA report type for joined dashboard data

DA dashboard with very many widgets

Correct answer: B. High-volume, append-oriented historical data

Big Objects support large volumes of data, commonly for historical or archival use cases.

Big Objects are not standard CRM objects configured with page layouts.

Report types are a separate reporting feature.

Dashboard size is unrelated to Big Objects.

Question 7: Which indexing approach can improve a selective SOQL query?

AAvoid indexes on fields used in filters

BUse suitable indexes to support selective filtered queries

CIndex filtered fields selectively

DIndex formula fields only

Correct answer: C. Index filtered fields selectively

Standard and custom indexes can help when the query filters are selective and the index is appropriate.

Avoiding indexes may leave a selective query without useful access paths.

This is the appropriate approach, subject to selectivity and platform guidance.

Indexing every field is not supported or useful as a general strategy.

Question 8: Two source systems contain the same customer but disagree on the phone number. How should an MDM design choose the golden record value?

AKeep the value from whichever system was loaded first

BStore both values permanently without selecting a trusted value

CDiscard both values and ask the customer to re-enter them

DApply a survivorship rule using source trust or recency

Correct answer: D. Apply a survivorship rule using source trust or recency

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Data Architect (Plat-Arch-201) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
A survivorship rule defines which source value wins, using criteria such as source trust or most recent update.

Load order is not a reliable business rule for choosing an attribute.

Keeping both values without a resolution policy does not establish a usable golden record.

Requiring re-entry discards available source data and does not define MDM behavior.

Question 9: Which relationship can allow a child record to exist without a parent record?

BA junction record may use two parent relationships

CA junction object commonly links two records through relationships

Correct answer: A. Lookup

A lookup relationship can be optional, allowing the child record to exist without a linked parent.

Master-detail requires a parent record.

A junction object commonly uses master-detail relationships and is not the general answer here.

Indirect lookup links external records and does not describe the standard optional parent relationship.

Question 10: What is the purpose of a soft-delete approach?

APermanently erase data immediately

BMark deleted but retain for recovery or compliance

CExport records without changing their status

DMove records to an archive and remove all references

Correct answer: B. Mark deleted but retain for recovery or compliance

Soft deletion marks records as deleted while retaining them for a defined recovery or retention period.

Permanent erasure is a hard delete, not a soft delete.

Exporting data does not change its deletion status.

Archiving may be part of retention but is not the definition of soft delete.

Question 11: Which synchronous SOQL query limit applies to Apex transactions?

AThere is no per-transaction SOQL query limit

BUnlimited queries when using Bulk API

C100 SOQL queries per transaction

D50 SOQL queries per transaction

Correct answer: C. 100 SOQL queries per transaction

A synchronous Apex transaction is subject to a limit of 100 SOQL queries.

Salesforce enforces a per-transaction query limit.

Bulk API does not remove Apex transaction governor limits.

The synchronous limit is not 50 queries.

Question 12: What problem does master data management address?

AReporting and dashboard layout

BArchiving old records only

CMigrating data without resolving duplicates

DDeduplicate and improve data quality

Correct answer: D. Deduplicate and improve data quality

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Data Architect (Plat-Arch-201) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
MDM establishes trusted data through practices such as deduplication, survivorship, and ongoing quality management.

Reporting layout is not the core purpose of MDM.

Archiving may support data management but does not establish trusted master records.

Migration alone does not resolve duplicate or conflicting data.

Question 13: Which Salesforce data store is suited to high-volume append-oriented historical data?

AA standard CRM object for ordinary transactional records

BA Big Object is intended for very high volumes of historical data

CA custom object with triggers on every insert

Correct answer: A. A standard CRM object for ordinary transactional records

Big Objects are designed for very large volumes of data, including append-oriented historical data.

Standard objects are not designed specifically for this high-volume archive pattern.

Custom triggers add processing and do not make a custom object a Big Object.

External objects expose data stored outside Salesforce rather than storing it in a Big Object.

Question 14: What is a benefit of using an external object?

AIt replaces all custom objects in the org

BQuery external records without copying them

CIt archives Salesforce records automatically

DIt creates reports without requiring a data source

Correct answer: B. Query external records without copying them

External objects let users work with data stored outside Salesforce without replicating it into the org.

External objects complement rather than replace custom objects.

Archiving Salesforce records requires a separate archive design.

Reports still require an underlying data source.

Question 15: Which design choice helps prepare for growth in data volume?

AIgnore platform limits until performance declines

BRely only on backups

CArchive data, add useful indexes, and keep queries selective

DExport all data without defining retrieval needs

Correct answer: C. Archive data, add useful indexes, and keep queries selective

Archiving and selective query design help manage growth while preserving the access the business needs.

Waiting until a problem appears can leave little time to correct architecture.

Backups do not reduce active data volume or improve query selectivity.

Exports without a retrieval plan do not form a complete data strategy.

Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect: core concepts

Choose an environment that fits the work. Developer sandboxes copy metadata and support individual development; Developer Pro provides more space for test data. Partial Copy sandboxes include metadata and a selected sample of data, which can support QA and training. Full sandboxes copy production data and metadata and are useful for realistic user acceptance and performance testing. Scratch orgs are temporary environments created from source and a definition file, typically for package development and automated testing. Review the current limits and refresh intervals for each type.

Version Control and Source-Driven Development

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect (Plat-Arch-202) Guide
chunks.content:
In a source-driven process, version control is the authoritative record of changes. Developers work in branches, commit changes, and merge reviewed work through a pull request. The team can then deploy the approved source to test and production environments. This preserves history and makes it easier to recreate an environment after a sandbox refresh. Salesforce CLI supports source synchronization and deployment as part of this workflow.

CI/CD, CLI, and Packages

A continuous integration pipeline can retrieve source, deploy it to a test org, run checks and tests, and report whether the change is ready. Salesforce CLI supports deployment and validation. A validated production deployment may be quick deployed later when it remains eligible. Unlocked packages group metadata into versioned components that can be installed and upgraded. DevOps Center offers a guided interface for Git-based change management. Change sets can still suit simple org-to-org releases but provide fewer controls and no source history.

Production deployments that include Apex must meet the platform’s overall code coverage requirement, and deployed code must have appropriate test coverage. Test levels determine which tests run: RunLocalTests, RunSpecifiedTests, or RunAllTestsInOrg. Under RunSpecifiedTests, each deployed class must meet the applicable coverage requirement from the tests run. Use independent test data so tests do not depend on records in a particular org. Plan integration, acceptance, and regression testing in suitable environments.

Release Order and Recovery

Deploy prerequisites before components that depend on them, such as fields before layouts or code that references those fields. Some metadata deletions require a destructive changes manifest and deployment tooling that supports it. Salesforce does not provide a universal rollback button for metadata deployments. Keep known-good source in version control and prepare a redeployment or mitigation plan. Feature flags can help disable a new capability while a fix is prepared. Test upcoming seasonal releases in a preview sandbox when appropriate.

Feature branches merge into a release branch, which is validated in a full/partial-copy sandbox, then promoted to production. Each merge triggers automated tests before advancing.

If work is lost during refreshes or the team cannot trace changes, establish a reviewed source-control workflow and deploy from versioned source.

Choose a Package Strategy

Unlocked packages can divide a large org into versioned components. Managed packages serve distribution use cases such as ISV products. Understand how scratch orgs and a Dev Hub support package development.

Build Automated Checks

A CI pipeline can deploy a pull request to a test org and run the required tests before merge. Validate production deployments ahead of the release window when possible.

A developer writes a trigger that runs a SOQL query inside a for loop. What governor limit risk does this create?

Platform Developer I: Key Concepts for the Exam

Apex Governor Limits & the Limits Class

Governor limits keep one transaction from using too many shared resources. Examples of synchronous limits include: 100 SOQL queries, 150 DML statements, 50,000 records returned from queries, 6 MB heap size, 10 seconds CPU time. Some limits differ in asynchronous transactions; check the limit for the specific context. Use Limits.getQueries() and Limits.getLimitQueries() from the Limits class to inspect usage while code runs. Practise choosing a fix for code that approaches a limit.

Bulkification: Never Put SOQL or DML Inside a Loop

A bulk-safe pattern is to query records before loops using SOQL with IN:triggerIdSet, collect changes in a List or Map inside loops, then perform DML after loops. Map<Id, SObject> can connect trigger records to related records by ID. Use Database.insert(records, false) for partial success (returns SaveResult array). Practise spotting queries or DML inside loops and moving the operations outside them.

Apex Triggers: Order of Execution & Handler Pattern

Before triggers fire before the record is saved. Use them to validate or modify field values before save (changes to Trigger.new persist without extra DML). After triggers run after the record is saved but before the transaction commits. Use them when you need the record Id or to update related records. Key context variables: Trigger.new, Trigger.old (not available on insert), Trigger.isInsert, Trigger.isUpdate. Best practice: one trigger per object, all logic delegated to a handler class. Review Salesforce’s Order of Execution: before-save flows and before triggers run before the record is saved, while after triggers and after-save flows run before commit.

SOQL: Relationships, Aggregates & SOSL

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I (Plat-Dev-201 / PD1) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
A child-to-parent query uses dot notation: SELECT Id, Account.Name FROM Contact . A parent-to-child query uses a subquery: SELECT Id, (SELECT Id FROM Contacts) FROM Account . Aggregate functions such as COUNT(), SUM(), and AVG() summarize records; use GROUP BY when results need groups. SOSL searches multiple objects simultaneously: FIND ’term’ IN ALL FIELDS RETURNING Account, Contact. Use SOSL for cross-object searches; use SOQL when you know the object.

Process Automation: Flow vs. Apex Triggers

Compare declarative automation with programmatic automation when choosing a solution. Use Flow for supported declarative processes, including record updates and guided screens. Consider Apex triggers for requirements that need programmatic behavior. Both can fire on the same record, the Order of Execution determines which runs first (before-save and after-save flows run at different points in the save sequence). Consider maintainability, platform limits, and the scenario’s constraints before choosing Flow or Apex.

Testing Framework: SeeAllData, Test.startTest & HttpCalloutMock

Minimum 75% code coverage required across all Apex to deploy to production. Test classes use @isTest. Test data is isolated by default (SeeAllData=false), create all test data explicitly using @TestSetup or within each test method. Test.startTest() resets governor limits and marks the start of the tested code; Test.stopTest() forces async operations (future methods, batch jobs) to complete synchronously. Mock HTTP callouts with Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, mockImpl). @TestVisible exposes private members to test classes without making them public.

Agentforce for Developers: Use Cases and Limits

The Developer Fundamentals section (27%) now includes an objective on the use cases and limitations of Agentforce for Developers, the AI assistant that suggests Apex and Lightning Web Component code and generates test classes inside your development tools. For the exam, know what it helps with (drafting code, explaining existing code, generating unit tests) and where it stops: generated code still has to be reviewed, bulkified, tested and deployed like any other code, and it does not relax governor limits or the 75% coverage rule. The User Interface section (25%) also expects you to know that Apex can be exposed to Agentforce, alongside Lightning components and Flow.

Lightning Web Components (LWC): Wire Service & @AuraEnabled

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I (Plat-Dev-201 / PD1) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
LWC is the modern Salesforce UI framework. Key decorators: @track (reactive private properties), @api (public properties exposed to parent), @wire (reactive Apex method calls). The @wire decorator connects an LWC to an Apex method marked @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true), the cacheable flag is required for @wire. Use lightning-record-form for standard record CRUD without writing Apex. Communication between components uses CustomEvent (child to parent) and LightningMessageService (unrelated components).

Core Apex Code Patterns for PD1

Practise reading and explaining these Apex patterns. For each example, trace the data, identify the execution context, and consider how it behaves with multiple records.

1. Bulk-Safe Trigger with Handler Class

This example delegates trigger logic to a handler. It queries once and updates the collected records outside the loop.

2. Database Class with Partial Success & Error Handling

Use Database.insert(records, false) to allow partial success. Check each SaveResult for errors.

3. Test Class with HttpCalloutMock

For a test that makes an HTTP callout, implement HttpCalloutMock and register it with Test.setMock().

All automation that fires on a single DML operation, before/after triggers, Record-Triggered Flows, and Process Builder, runs inside one execution context. Governor limits (SOQL queries, DML statements, CPU time) accumulate across all of them, not per-automation. This is why bulkification and avoiding recursive updates matters for PD1.

How to Pass the Platform Developer I (PD1) Exam

Practise applying Apex concepts to development scenarios. Read each requirement, identify the execution context and limits, and compare the proposed solutions.

Governor Limit Questions, the Pattern to Recognise

Check whether a loop runs a query or a DML statement for each record. Collect records in a list and perform DML outside the loop, such as insert contactList;. Query the data you need before the loop and use a map to find related records by ID.

Testing Questions, the Three Rules to Memorise

Review the 75% overall Apex coverage requirement and the separate rules for triggers. Create the data your tests need instead of depending on existing records. For an HTTP callout test, register a mock with Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, mockImpl), then assert the result.

Async Apex Selection: Which Method for Which Scenario

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I (Plat-Dev-201 / PD1) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Compare the needs of the job. Batch Apex can process large collections in chunks; Queueable Apex supports chaining and complex inputs. Scheduled Apex runs work at a specified time. Future methods also run asynchronously, but have their own input and execution restrictions.

Trigger Scenarios: Before vs After

Use a before trigger to update fields on Trigger.new without extra DML. An after trigger can use the saved record ID to create related records. Use addError() to reject invalid records, and design queries for multiple records.

Read the requirement and trace the code before comparing choices. Check whether an option fits the execution context, such as a queueable job or the order of DML and callouts. Question 1: A developer needs to create a trigger that fires after a record is inserted and updated. Which trigger events should be used?

Aafter insert, after update

Bbefore insert, before update

Cafter insert, before update

Correct answer: A. after insert, after update

The 'after insert' and 'after update' trigger events fire after the record is saved to the database, which is required when you need to access the record Id or related records.

'before insert, before update' fires prior to save, when the record doesn't yet have an Id, insufficient for logic needing the saved record or related records.

'after insert, before update' mixes timing incorrectly for this scenario's need to run after both operations.

'isInsert, isUpdate' are trigger context variables, not trigger event names, this option misidentifies the concept being asked about.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I (Plat-Dev-201 / PD1) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Question 2: What is the governor limit for the maximum number of SOQL queries in a single transaction?

Correct answer: B. 100 queries

The synchronous governor limit for SOQL queries is 100 per transaction. For asynchronous contexts, the limit is 200.

50 understates the actual synchronous SOQL limit of 100.

150 overstates the actual synchronous SOQL limit of 100.

200 is the asynchronous limit, not the synchronous limit this question asks about.

Question 3: Which annotation is used to expose an Apex method as a REST web service?

Correct answer: A. @RestResource

The @RestResource annotation is used at the class level to expose an Apex class as a REST resource. Individual methods use @HttpGet, @HttpPost, etc.

@HttpGet is a method-level annotation for REST verbs, not the class-level annotation that exposes the class itself as a REST resource.

@RemoteAction exposes Apex to Visualforce remoting, unrelated to REST web services.

@AuraEnabled exposes methods to Lightning components, not REST API consumers.

Question 4: A developer writes a SOQL query: SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Name LIKE '%tech%'. What will this query return?

AAccounts where Name starts with 'tech'

BAccounts where Name ends with 'tech'

CAccounts where Name contains 'tech'

DAccounts where Name equals 'tech'

Correct answer: C. Accounts where Name contains 'tech'

The % wildcard matches any number of characters. Using %tech% matches any Account where the Name contains 'tech' anywhere in the string.

'starts with' would require the pattern 'tech%' (no leading wildcard), not '%tech%'.

'ends with' would require the pattern '%tech' (no trailing wildcard), not '%tech%'.

'equals' would require no wildcards at all: LIKE with wildcards never means exact equality.

Question 5: Which method should be used to perform DML operations inside a for loop safely?

CCollect records in a list and perform DML outside the loop

Correct answer: C. Collect records in a list and perform DML outside the loop

To avoid hitting governor limits, you should always collect records in a list during the loop and perform DML operations outside the loop (bulk processing).

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I (Plat-Dev-201 / PD1) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Database.insert() alone doesn't address the loop-placement issue: DML inside a loop is the problem regardless of which insert method is used.

A plain insert statement inside a loop has the same governor-limit risk as any DML call inside a loop.

@future methods don't solve bulkification, they move work asynchronously but don't fix DML-in-a-loop patterns.

Question 6: What is the minimum code coverage required for Apex classes and triggers to be deployed to production?

Correct answer: B. 75%

Salesforce requires at least 75% code coverage for Apex classes and triggers to be deployed to production. This ensures code quality and reliability.

60% is below Salesforce's actual required threshold of 75%.

80% overstates the actual required minimum, though it's often recommended as a safety margin.

100% is not required by Salesforce, though desirable in some rigorous engineering practices.

Question 7: Which annotation is used to make an Apex method available to Lightning Web Components?

Correct answer: A. @AuraEnabled

The @AuraEnabled annotation makes an Apex method available to Lightning Web Components (LWC) and Aura components, allowing them to call server-side logic.

@RemoteAction exposes methods to Visualforce remoting, not modern LWC/Aura components.

@RestResource exposes a class as a REST API endpoint, unrelated to LWC method calls.

@InvocableMethod exposes Apex to Flow and Process Builder, not LWC.

Question 8: A developer wants to create a trigger that processes records in bulk. What is the best practice?

AProcess records one at a time in a for loop

BCollect records in a list and process outside the loop

CUse @future methods for all processing

DUse synchronous methods only

Correct answer: B. Collect records in a list and process outside the loop

Best practice is to collect records in a list during iteration and process them in bulk outside the loop to avoid hitting governor limits.

Processing one record at a time in a loop is the anti-pattern that causes governor limit issues, not the best practice.

@future methods don't solve bulkification, they simply defer execution asynchronously.

'Synchronous methods only' doesn't address the bulk-processing requirement at all.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I (Plat-Dev-201 / PD1) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Question 9: What is the governor limit for DML statements in a single transaction?

Correct answer: B. 150 DML statements

The synchronous governor limit for DML statements (insert, update, delete, upsert, etc.) is 150 per transaction.

100 DML statements understates the actual synchronous limit of 150.

200 DML statements overstates the actual synchronous limit of 150.

The DML statement limit is not unlimited: Salesforce enforces a specific cap to protect the multi-tenant platform.

Question 10: Which method is used to handle partial success in DML operations?

CDatabase.insert() with allOrNone parameter

Correct answer: A. Database.insert()

Database.insert() returns a Database.SaveResult array, allowing you to handle partial success. The insert statement throws an exception if any record fails.

A plain insert statement throws an exception on any failure, it doesn't support partial success handling.

'Database.insert() with allOrNone parameter' set to true behaves like the plain insert statement (all-or-nothing); it's the default false setting on Database.insert() that enables partial success.

'All of the above' is incorrect since the plain insert statement specifically does NOT support partial success.

Question 11: What is the purpose of Test.runAs() in Apex test classes?

ATo test with different user permissions

BTo test asynchronous code

CTo test batch classes

Correct answer: A. To test with different user permissions

Test.runAs() allows you to execute test code in the context of a specific user, enabling you to test with different user permissions and sharing rules.

Test.runAs() doesn't test asynchronous code, that's unrelated to its purpose of switching user context.

Test.runAs() isn't specific to batch class testing, it applies to any Apex test scenario needing a different user context.

Test.runAs() isn't specific to trigger testing, it's a general user-context testing mechanism usable anywhere.

Question 12: Which exception type should be thrown when validation fails in Apex?

CAuraHandledException

DCustom exception class

Correct answer: B. DmlException

DmlException is thrown when DML operations fail. For custom validation errors, you can throw DmlException with a custom message.

A generic Exception doesn't carry the DML-specific context that DmlException provides for failed database operations.

AuraHandledException is specifically for surfacing errors to Lightning components, not general DML failure handling.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I (Plat-Dev-201 / PD1) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
A custom exception class can be used, but DmlException is the standard, built-in type specifically for DML failures.

Question 13: A developer wants to query related records in a single SOQL query. Which clause should be used?

CRelationship query (dot notation)

Correct answer: C. Relationship query (dot notation)

SOQL uses relationship queries (dot notation) to query related records, such as 'SELECT Id, Account.Name FROM Contact' to get the Account name for each Contact.

JOIN is not valid SOQL syntax: SOQL uses relationship dot-notation instead of SQL-style joins.

INNER JOIN is SQL syntax, not valid SOQL: Salesforce's query language doesn't support this keyword.

A subquery (parent-to-child) is a different SOQL technique for retrieving child records, not the dot-notation syntax used for the parent-to-child scenario described here.

Question 14: What is the purpose of the @TestVisible annotation?

ATo make a method available to test classes

BTo make a private method or variable accessible to test classes

CTo mark a class as a test class

DTo enable test coverage

Correct answer: B. To make a private method or variable accessible to test classes

@TestVisible allows test classes to access private methods and variables, enabling better test coverage without making them public.

'To make a method available to test classes' is too broad; @TestVisible specifically exposes private members, not general method availability.

@TestVisible doesn't mark a class as a test class, that's unrelated to its actual purpose.

@TestVisible doesn't enable test coverage tracking, that's a platform-level, automatic measurement, not something this annotation controls.

Question 15: What is the maximum number of records a synchronous Apex transaction can process through DML statements?

Correct answer: A. 10,000 records

A synchronous Apex transaction can process up to 10,000 records through DML statements. Query-row and other limits are separate.

50,000 is a common SOQL query-row limit, not the DML row limit.

100,000 exceeds the synchronous DML row limit.

200,000 exceeds the synchronous DML row limit.

Question 16: A flow updates 200 records and an Apex trigger reads their parent accounts. How should the trigger retrieve the parents?

AQuery the parent inside each iteration

BRetrieve every account before filtering

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I (Plat-Dev-201 / PD1) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
CSchedule a separate query for each parent

DCollect parent IDs and query once

Correct answer: D. Collect parent IDs and query once

Reading the relevant parents in one query outside the loop keeps query use bounded for bulk updates.

One query per input risks exceeding the transaction limit.

Querying all accounts wastes query rows and heap space.

A job per parent adds overhead and can exceed enqueue limits.

Question 17: A child component lets users select a product. Its containing LWC needs to react to the selection. How should the child notify it?

ACall a controller on the parent page

BAssign the parent’s tracked property

CExpose the selected product as a DOM ID

DDispatch a custom event for selection

Correct answer: D. Dispatch a custom event for selection

The child dispatches an event, and the parent registers a listener to handle the selection.

A page controller is not the normal child-to-parent LWC interface.

The child does not own the parent’s reactive state.

A DOM ID does not notify the parent about the selection.

Question 18: A record-triggered flow must normalize a field on the triggering record before it is written. Which configuration fits?

AAn after-save flow with a related record update

BA schedule-triggered flow run each night

CA screen flow launched from a record action

DA before-save record-triggered flow

Correct answer: D. A before-save record-triggered flow

A before-save flow can set fields on the triggering record before persistence without an extra record update.

Updating after save adds an operation for a change that can occur earlier.

Scheduled processing delays normalization.

A screen flow depends on a user taking an action.

Question 19: A platform developer wants to test that a retry count stays unchanged when a validation error stops an operation. What should the test assert?

AThe executing user has an active profile

BThe class compiles without any warnings

CThe stored counter equals its original value

DThe overall test run meets a coverage goal

Correct answer: C. The stored counter equals its original value

Checking the counter after the failure verifies the business behavior at the transaction boundary.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I (Plat-Dev-201 / PD1) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
The user’s profile does not establish whether the retry count changed.

Compilation cannot establish the runtime outcome.

Coverage can increase without asserting the required behavior.

Question 20: A helper needs to find an Account through its unique external ID from an order system. How should the value enter a fixed SOQL query?

ABuild the field value into a SOQL fragment

BPass the identifier as the object API name

CQuery all accounts and filter in the UI

DUse a variable bound in the WHERE clause

Correct answer: D. Use a variable bound in the WHERE clause

A bind variable keeps the fixed SOQL statement separate from the incoming match value.

String assembly can mishandle input values and is unnecessary for a fixed query.

The external ID identifies a record, not the queried object.

Fetching every account wastes resources and exposes unnecessary data.

Salesforce Certified Platform Developer (PD1) Exam FAQs

What is covered on the Salesforce Certified Platform Developer (PD1) exam?

The Salesforce Certified Platform Developer (PD1) exam (formerly Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I) has 4 sections. Process Automation and Logic (28%) and Developer Fundamentals (27%) together make up 55% of the exam. The full section-by-section weightage is in the table on this page.

What programming languages do I need to know for Platform Developer I?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I (Plat-Dev-201 / PD1) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
You need to know Apex (Salesforce's Java-like language) and JavaScript for Lightning Web Components. Experience with Java, C#, or similar object-oriented languages is helpful, but you can learn Apex through Trailhead and hands-on practice.

How much coding experience do I need for Platform Developer I?

While some programming experience is helpful, you can learn Apex and Lightning Web Components through Trailhead. The exam focuses on understanding when to use code vs declarative tools, governor limits, testing, and basic Apex/LWC concepts rather than advanced programming.

What is the PD1 passing score and exam format in Summer '26?

The Platform Developer I (PD1) exam has 60 multiple-choice questions, 105 minutes, and a passing score of 68% (41 correct). Salesforce may include 5 unscored pilot questions. The exam costs $200 USD (retake $100 USD) and is available online-proctored or at a test center.

What are the most common reasons candidates fail PD1?

Common failure points: (1) not knowing governor limits (SOQL 100/transaction, DML 150/transaction) and when they trigger, (2) writing DML or SOQL inside a for loop, the exam's most common trap, (3) misunderstanding the 75% code coverage rule and how Test.startTest()/stopTest() affect limit resets, and (4) confusing @AuraEnabled, @RestResource, and @InvocableMethod annotations.

How to Approach PD1 Scenario Questions

Governor limit questions: Check whether SOQL or DML runs repeatedly inside a loop. Consider collecting IDs, querying once, and using a map to find results.

Async Apex questions: Match the work to the tool: consider asynchronous Apex for trigger callouts, Queueable for chaining or complex inputs, Batch for large datasets, and Scheduled Apex for timed work.

LWC questions: Use @api to expose a child component property or method. Use a custom event when a child needs to notify its parent. Review when to call Apex imperatively and when to use @wire.

Platform Developer II Exam Format Explained

You can take the exam online with a proctor or at a test centre. Many questions ask you to review code or select an approach for a development task.

Multiple-choice & multiple-select

How Many Questions Are Scenario-Based?

Many questions show a short code example or describe a requirement. One common pattern is code that works for one record but fails when it processes 200 records; you must identify a bulk-safe fix.

Best Way to Pass on Your First Attempt

Write bulk-safe code: Do not put queries or DML inside loops. Gather records in collections and perform each operation once.

Choose the right async tool: Learn the limits and uses of Future methods, Queueable, Batch, and Scheduled Apex. Queueable supports chaining and can carry state.

Use clear code patterns: Keep one trigger per object and put its logic in a handler class. Separate data access from business logic.

Practice writing tests: Create test data, mock callouts, and use Test.startTest and Test.stopTest to run asynchronous work.

Platform Developer II: Key Concepts

Write Apex That Handles Bulk Work

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer II (Plat-Dev-301 / PD2) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Your Apex should work for one record and for a batch of 200. Keep SOQL queries and DML operations outside loops. Query the needed records, store them in a map or collection, process them in memory, and save changes together. A common pattern is one trigger per object with the logic in a handler class. This keeps the trigger easier to follow and makes the logic easier to test. On large objects, use selective queries because filters on unindexed fields can perform poorly. Remember the synchronous limits listed here: 100 SOQL queries, 150 DML statements, 50,000 queried records, and 10,000 records per DML operation.

Choose the Right Asynchronous Tool

Future methods accept only primitive parameters, cannot be chained, and do not return a job ID. Queueable Apex accepts objects, returns a job ID, can be chained, and can keep state. Use Batch Apex to process large numbers of records in chunks; each chunk gets its own governor limits. Scheduled Apex starts work at a set time and is often used to launch a batch job. Asynchronous transactions have some higher limits, including 200 SOQL queries and more CPU time, which can make them useful when work should run outside the main transaction.

Integrations, Callouts, and Events

A trigger cannot make a callout directly. Run the callout asynchronously, using a future method marked for callouts or a Queueable. Put endpoints and authentication in Named Credentials instead of storing secrets in code. The limits shown here are 100 callouts per transaction and 120 seconds total. A Platform Event lets one part of a system publish information for subscribers to handle separately, reducing dependence between them. Change Data Capture sends record change information to subscribers. In tests, use Test.setMock because tests cannot call an external network.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer II (Plat-Dev-301 / PD2) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Create the records your tests need instead of depending on data already in an org. @TestSetup can create data shared by test methods. Avoid SeeAllData because it makes tests depend on the org’s contents. Put the code under test between Test.startTest and Test.stopTest; this resets governor limits and runs queued asynchronous work before you check the results. Use HttpCalloutMock for callouts, and use Test.isRunningTest sparingly. Deployment requires 75% Apex test coverage, but tests should also check expected results, bulk behavior, and failure cases.

Apply Security in Apex

Apex runs in system mode by default, so it may not follow the current user’s record access. With sharing respects record sharing; without sharing ignores it; inherited sharing follows the caller’s sharing context. Record sharing does not enforce field access. Use Security.stripInaccessible or WITH USER_MODE to prevent access to fields the user should not read or write. WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED is another option for SOQL when appropriate. Methods marked @AuraEnabled can be called from a front end, so validate inputs and check access inside the method.

Choose by data volume and chaining needs: @future for simple fire-and-forget calls with primitive parameters, Queueable when you need chaining or complex object parameters, and Batch when processing more records than fit in one transaction.

How to Pass the Salesforce Platform Developer II Exam

For each code sample or requirement, compare the choices against bulk behavior, governor limits, and how the code handles failures.

A query or DML operation inside a loop is a warning sign. Gather records in collections and perform the operation once.

Pick an Asynchronous Tool

Choose Queueable when you need object parameters, chaining, or a job ID. Use Batch for large volumes and Scheduled Apex for work that runs on a timetable.

Choose an Integration Pattern

Run callouts asynchronously instead of in a trigger. Store endpoint and authentication details in Named Credentials. Use Platform Events to separate a publisher from its subscribers.

Keep Trigger Logic Organized

Use one trigger per object and move the business logic into a handler class. Avoid designs that cause the trigger to run repeatedly.

Test Behavior, Not Just Coverage

Question 1: Which design pattern creates one class instance that can be reused throughout a transaction?

Correct answer: B. Singleton Pattern

The Singleton Pattern creates only one instance of a class and provides a shared way to access it.

Factory Pattern creates objects based on input; it does not ensure there is only one instance.

Decorator Pattern adds behavior to an object; it does not limit how many instances are created.

Strategy Pattern lets code switch between algorithms; it does not control how many instances exist.

Question 2: What does the @TestSetup annotation do?

AMocks external services

BBypasses governor limits for every test method in the class

CRuns tests in parallel

DCreates test data once for all test methods in the class

Correct answer: D. Creates test data once for all test methods in the class

@TestSetup creates data once before the test methods run. Each test method can use that data, which can make test setup more efficient.

@TestSetup creates records with DML; use HttpCalloutMock to mock an HTTP callout.

@TestSetup does not change governor limits. Each test method still has the standard limits.

@TestSetup does not control whether tests run in parallel. That is configured separately.

Question 3: How can a trigger start a callout?

ACall Database.executeBatch

BUse a @future(callout=true) method

CMake the callout directly in the trigger

Correct answer: B. Use a @future(callout=true) method

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer II (Plat-Dev-301 / PD2) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
A trigger cannot make a callout directly. Use @future(callout=true) or Queueable Apex with Database.AllowsCallouts to make the callout asynchronously.

Database.executeBatch starts a batch job; the batch code must still make the callout in its execute method.

A trigger cannot make a direct callout because it runs inside an active transaction.

Platform Events support publish-and-subscribe messaging; they do not remove the restriction on direct callouts from triggers.

Question 4: What is one benefit of using Platform Events for integrations instead of traditional triggers?

AThey support loosely coupled, asynchronous communication

BThey always run faster

CThey have lower governor limits

DThey handle every error automatically, with no retry logic needed

Correct answer: A. They support loosely coupled, asynchronous communication

Platform Events let systems communicate asynchronously without depending directly on each other. This can make integrations easier to scale and maintain.

Platform Events run asynchronously; they are not meant to provide faster real-time execution.

Platform Events do not lower governor limits. Apex transactions still have standard limits.

Each subscriber still needs its own retry and error-handling logic.

Question 5: How can a batch job start another batch job after it finishes?

AImplement Database.Stateful

BImplement Database.Batchable

CCall Database.executeBatch from the current job’s finish method

DImplement Database.AllowsCallouts and call the next job from the start method

Correct answer: C. Call Database.executeBatch from the current job’s finish method

Call Database.executeBatch from the current batch job’s finish method to start the next batch job.

Database.Stateful keeps instance variable values between batch execute calls; it does not chain jobs.

Database.Batchable is required for a batch class but does not chain jobs by itself.

Database.AllowsCallouts allows a batch job to make HTTP callouts; it does not chain jobs.

Question 6: What does the Database.Stateful interface do in batch Apex?

AKeeps instance variable values between batch runs

BMakes the batch run faster

CBypasses governor limits

DAllows the batch to make callouts to external services

Correct answer: A. Keeps instance variable values between batch runs

Database.Stateful keeps instance variable values between batch executions.

Database.Stateful does not improve speed; it preserves state.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer II (Plat-Dev-301 / PD2) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
It does not bypass governor limits. Each batch chunk still has standard limits.

Database.AllowsCallouts is the interface used to allow callouts from batch Apex.

Question 7: Which design pattern separates trigger code from business logic?

AFactory Pattern by itself

BDecorator Pattern applied to each trigger by itself

CTrigger Handler pattern with service classes

DSingleton Pattern by itself

Correct answer: C. Trigger Handler pattern with service classes

The Trigger Handler pattern keeps the trigger code separate from business logic, which makes the code easier to maintain.

Factory handles object creation; it does not separate trigger code from business logic by itself.

Decorator adds behavior to objects; it does not organize trigger logic by itself.

Singleton controls instance creation; it does not separate trigger code from business logic.

Question 8: What can Queueable Apex do that @future cannot?

CChain jobs, accept complex parameters, and return job IDs

DRun synchronously in the same transaction as the calling code

Correct answer: C. Chain jobs, accept complex parameters, and return job IDs

Queueable Apex supports job chaining, complex parameters, and job ID tracking.

Queueable Apex and @future have similar governor limits in most cases.

Queueable Apex is not inherently faster than @future; both run asynchronously.

Queueable Apex runs asynchronously, just like @future.

Question 9: What security checks should Apex exposed to an LWC apply?

BSharing checks, with no field-level security

CField-level security, with no sharing checks, and no @AuraEnabled annotation

DUse @AuraEnabled and enforce field-level security and sharing

Correct answer: D. Use @AuraEnabled and enforce field-level security and sharing

Apex methods exposed to an LWC must enforce field-level security and sharing.

User-facing Apex code still needs security checks.

Sharing checks alone do not protect fields a user cannot access.

Field-level security alone does not limit which records a user can access.

Question 10: What does the Strategy pattern let you do?

ACreate one shared instance

BSwap between algorithms in separate classes

DCreate objects without naming their concrete classes

Correct answer: B. Swap between algorithms in separate classes

The Strategy pattern lets code switch between algorithms at runtime.

A shared single instance describes the Singleton pattern.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer II (Plat-Dev-301 / PD2) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Event handling is often associated with the Observer pattern, not Strategy.

Object creation is handled by patterns such as Factory, not Strategy.

Question 11: Which heap-size limits apply to Apex?

B6 MB for synchronous Apex, with no separate asynchronous limit

CThere is no heap limit

DAbout 6 MB for synchronous and 12 MB for asynchronous Apex

Correct answer: D. About 6 MB for synchronous and 12 MB for asynchronous Apex

Apex has a heap limit of about 6 MB for synchronous code and 12 MB for asynchronous code.

1 MB is below the synchronous heap limit.

6 MB is the synchronous limit; asynchronous Apex has a higher limit.

Salesforce enforces heap limits to protect the shared platform.

Question 12: What does Test.isRunningTest() do?

AChecks whether code is running in a test so it can use conditional logic

CMakes code run faster

DBypasses governor limits for the code that runs inside the test method

Correct answer: A. Checks whether code is running in a test so it can use conditional logic

Test.isRunningTest() checks whether code is running in a test. Code can use this check for mock responses or other test-specific behavior.

It does not skip tests; it only detects the test context.

It does not improve execution speed.

Governor limits still apply in tests.

Question 13: How can Apex be made available to Flow or Process Builder?

Correct answer: C. Use InvocableMethod

An InvocableMethod makes an Apex method available to Flow and Process Builder.

@AuraEnabled exposes Apex methods to Lightning components, not Flow or Process Builder.

@RestResource exposes Apex as a REST service, not as a Flow action.

A trigger runs after record changes; Flow or Process Builder cannot invoke it directly.

Question 14: What is a common use for Platform Events?

ADecoupled integrations, logging, and messaging between orgs

BBatch processing of large record sets

DSynchronous triggers that must finish in the same transaction

Correct answer: A. Decoupled integrations, logging, and messaging between orgs

Platform Events support loosely coupled, event-driven systems.

Batch processing uses Batchable Apex, not Platform Events.

Scheduled jobs use the Schedulable interface, not Platform Events.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer II (Plat-Dev-301 / PD2) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Platform Events are asynchronous, not synchronous-only.

Question 15: How can you avoid creating the same test data in every Apex test method?

ACreate data separately in every test method

BUse @TestSetup to create shared test data

CWrite fewer assertions

Correct answer: B. Use @TestSetup to create shared test data

@TestSetup creates data once for the test class so each test method can use it.

Creating the same data in each method repeats work and can slow tests.

Fewer assertions do not make a test run faster, and they can reduce test quality.

SeeAllData=true ties tests to org data and can make them fragile and unpredictable.

Question 16: A batch job updates invoices with partial success enabled. How should support identify which input rows failed?

ACheck the batch job status after finish

BRead the last updated invoice timestamp

CQuery the rows using the batch job ID

DMatch each SaveResult to its input row

Correct answer: D. Match each SaveResult to its input row

SaveResult entries follow the input order. Inspect each failure’s errors and log its source row.

The job status summarizes execution without identifying every row.

A timestamp cannot explain which input rows failed.

The async job ID does not identify the affected invoice rows.

Question 17: An Apex service queries records for an LWC. It must enforce the caller’s object, field, and record access. Which query mode fits?

ARun a system-mode SOQL query

BCache the response in the browser

CMark the Apex method cacheable

DUse SOQL in USER_MODE

Correct answer: D. Use SOQL in USER_MODE

User-mode SOQL enforces object, field, and record access for the query operation.

System mode does not provide those user access checks by default.

A browser cache cannot enforce access on the server.

Cacheability changes how results are fetched and stored.

Question 18: A scheduled calculation must be tested without depending on the current date. How should the date be supplied?

AFetch the date from the running user

BRead the date from a global constant

CPass a date into the calculation

DRead the date in every helper method

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer II (Plat-Dev-301 / PD2) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Correct answer: A. Fetch the date from the running user

Passing the date lets production use its clock while tests exercise a fixed date and boundary cases.

The running user does not make time deterministic.

A global fixed date would affect production behavior.

Each helper still depends on a changing clock.

Question 19: A service uses an HTTP callout to retrieve exchange rates. What should the unit test use to simulate a timeout response?

AChange the endpoint to a test org

BSet an HttpCalloutMock response

CSupply a static test exchange rate

DRun the callout after Test.stopTest

Correct answer: B. Set an HttpCalloutMock response

Register an HttpCalloutMock to return a fixed HTTP response, such as 504, without calling the provider.

A test endpoint still makes the result depend on an external service.

A static rate skips the HTTP error handling path.

Test.stopTest runs async work but does not supply an HTTP response.

Question 20: An Apex team packages an implementation behind an interface. Two consumers need different implementations. What simplifies testing both paths?

ACreate one singleton implementation

BInject an interface implementation

CMake the interface methods static

DAdd a test flag to the implementation

Correct answer: C. Make the interface methods static

Inject either implementation through the interface and replace it with a test double when isolating callers.

Static methods do not give each consumer a configurable instance.

A singleton fixes the implementation choice for both consumers.

A test flag changes production behavior instead of isolating the dependency.

What is covered on the Salesforce Certified Platform Developer II (PD2) exam?

BAs a contact under a placeholder account

CAs a lead until the student accepts an offer

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Education Cloud Consultant: Archived Exam Notes & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Correct answer: D. As a person account

The study example represents an unaffiliated person as a person account. Confirm the model used by the institution before applying this pattern.

An applicant does not need an internal Salesforce user record merely to be represented as a person.

A placeholder account is not the model choice described in this example.

A lead may suit some processes, but it is not the answer in this specific study scenario.

Question 2: What does an affiliation record capture in an education data model?

AA connection between a person and an organization

BThe courses a student takes during one academic term

CThe advisor assigned to support a student

DThe financial aid package awarded to a student

Correct answer: A. A connection between a person and an organization

An affiliation represents a relationship between a person and an organization, such as an institution or employer.

This describes the relationship captured by an affiliation.

Course participation is represented through academic program and course records.

An advisor relationship is a separate assignment.

Question 3: A learner joins a degree program and takes six courses within it. Which structure best represents this?

AAn opportunity for the program with six product lines

BOne affiliation listing all courses in its description

CA program enrollment connected to the course records

DSix separate program enrollments, one for each course

Correct answer: C. A program enrollment connected to the course records

A program enrollment represents participation in the program and can relate to the courses taken, subject to the selected data model.

Opportunities represent sales processes and do not model academic participation in this example.

An affiliation links a person to an organization rather than listing course enrollment.

One enrollment per course would confuse course participation with program enrollment.

Question 4: Why might an education solution represent a household as well as an individual student?

AFamily members may participate in decisions and giving

BCourse connections require every student to belong to a household

CRegulations require each home address to use a separate object

DA person account cannot store more than one address

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Education Cloud Consultant: Archived Exam Notes & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Correct answer: A. Family members may participate in decisions and giving

Households can help represent family relationships that matter to education decisions and advancement activity.

Course relationships do not universally require a household record.

This is not a general regulatory requirement for modeling addresses.

Address handling depends on the chosen data model and does not by itself require a household.

Question 5: An admissions team needs to track an application through review, interview, and decision. Which record best fits the process in this example?

AA task for each stage

BA case for each application step

CA program enrollment for each stage

DAn application record with stages

Correct answer: D. An application record with stages

An application record can track the applicant’s progress through the defined admissions stages.

Tasks may support assigned work but do not replace the application lifecycle record.

Cases manage service issues and are not the application process record described here.

Program enrollment applies after admission when the student participates in a program.

Question 6: What does an advisor relationship record describe?

AThe advisor’s employment contract

BWhich advisor supports a student and how

CFees charged for advising

DThe courses the advisor teaches

Correct answer: B. Which advisor supports a student and how

The relationship identifies which advisor supports the student and the capacity of that support.

An advisor’s employment contract belongs in personnel records.

Fees are not the purpose of a student-advisor relationship record.

Teaching assignments are separate from identifying a student’s advisor.

Question 7: A student pauses study and returns the following year. How should the institution preserve the history?

ADelete the original enrollment and recreate it on return

BKeep the history and record the new enrollment period

CCreate a second person account for the returning student

DRemove the gap from the affiliation record

Correct answer: B. Keep the history and record the new enrollment period

Retaining the original history and recording the new period preserves the student’s timeline.

Deleting the original enrollment would erase useful academic history.

The returning learner is the same person, so a second person account would fragment their history.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Education Cloud Consultant: Archived Exam Notes & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Editing out the gap would hide a meaningful period in the student’s record.

Question 8: Why model the structure of colleges, faculties, and departments?

AIt can reflect how the institution’s units relate to each other

BIt determines which employees can log in

CIt sets the order in which applicants receive offers

DIt calculates tuition for every program

Correct answer: A. It can reflect how the institution’s units relate to each other

An organizational hierarchy can represent how institutional units are arranged and related.

Login access is controlled through user and permission settings.

Admissions offers are handled by the admissions process, not organizational nesting.

Tuition is determined by program and pricing rules, not by hierarchy alone.

Question 9: An institution wants to learn which recruitment events are associated with later enrollments. What data link helps answer this?

AAsk each enrolled student to remember every event

BCompare yearly event counts with total enrollment

CConnect event attendance with the application record

DCount attendance at each event

Correct answer: C. Connect event attendance with the application record

Linking attendance to the application allows the institution to analyze event participation alongside application outcomes.

Asking people to remember events may produce incomplete information.

Comparing aggregate event and enrollment totals cannot link an attendee to an outcome.

Attendance counts show event reach but not the later enrollment of each attendee.

Question 10: What is the difference between a course and a course offering?

AThe course is undergraduate; the offering is postgraduate

BThe course is in-person; the offering is online

CThe course defines the subject; the offering is a specific run of it

DFaculty create the course; admissions creates the offering

Correct answer: C. The course defines the subject; the offering is a specific run of it

A course defines the academic subject, while an offering represents a particular instance or run of that course.

The distinction does not depend on undergraduate or postgraduate level.

A course and its offering can have different delivery modes.

The difference is not based on which team creates each record.

BWhether the custom object can be renamed to the standard name

CWhether the data should be moved to another org

DWhether the standard model already meets the requirement

Correct answer: D. Whether the standard model already meets the requirement

Compare the requirement with the available standard data model before deciding whether custom storage is needed.

Capacity does not establish whether the data model fits the requirement.

Renaming a custom object does not give it standard object behavior.

A separate org is not the first step in assessing a data model.

AOpportunities cannot store start and end dates

BEnrollment represents ongoing study, not a sales deal

COnly program enrollment can link to a person account

DEducation records cannot be reported with opportunities

Correct answer: B. Enrollment represents ongoing study, not a sales deal

Program enrollment represents a learner’s participation in an academic program rather than a prospective sales transaction.

Opportunities can store dates; that is not the reason to use enrollment.

The relationship to a person depends on the chosen data model.

Education data can be reported; reporting is not the key distinction.

AA separate alumni database synced nightly

BA second person account created after graduation

CThe same person record can relate to both histories

DA rule that locks academic records at graduation

Correct answer: C. The same person record can relate to both histories

Keeping one person identity connected to academic and advancement information supports a broader relationship view, subject to access controls.

A separate database can fragment history and requires synchronization.

A second person account could split one individual’s records.

Locking records does not connect academic and giving data.

Email Specialist: core concepts

Email Authentication and Deliverability

SPF identifies which sending servers are authorized for a domain. DKIM adds a cryptographic signature that receiving systems can verify with the domain’s public key. DMARC tells receivers how to handle messages that fail SPF or DKIM checks, using a policy such as none, quarantine, or reject. The Sender Authentication Package bundles key domain and sending configuration. Understand what each mechanism verifies and how reputation, complaints, and bounce handling affect delivery.

Subscribers, Lists, and Data Extensions

All Subscribers holds subscriber status used across sends. Publication Lists manage preferences for particular content types. Suppression Lists exclude addresses from sends, and Auto-Suppression Lists can apply exclusions across sends. Data Extensions store structured records and custom fields for segmentation and personalization. Subscriber keys identify contacts consistently. Global unsubscribes take precedence over more specific audience selections.

Send Classifications and Message Type

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Marketing Cloud Engagement Specialist (MC-202 / CRT-550 / Email Specialist) Guide
chunks.content:
Send classifications combine sender and delivery settings with the commercial or transactional treatment of a send. Commercial messages require the relevant unsubscribe handling. Transactional messages must be genuinely tied to a transaction and should not be used to bypass marketing consent. Select the classification that matches the message purpose and the organization’s compliance requirements.

AMPscript for Personalization

Lookup retrieves a value from a Data Extension, while LookupRows returns matching rows. AttributeValue reads a subscriber or send-context attribute, and IIF provides a conditional expression. These functions can personalize content when used with the correct data and keys. Practice following short snippets and checking how missing values are handled.

Tracking and Email Metrics

Tracking reports include sends, deliveries, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, and complaints. Delivered messages are generally calculated after bounce handling. Open rate and click-to-open rate answer different questions; CTOR compares clicks with opens. Hard bounces are permanent failures and soft bounces are temporary failures. Match each metric to the business question and interpret tracking data with its known limitations.

Before an inbox provider accepts a message, it checks SPF (authorized senders), DKIM (signature integrity), and DMARC (policy on failure), the Sender Authentication Package bundles all three plus a dedicated IP and domain.

Question 1: AMPscript is a scripting language in Marketing Cloud. What is it useful for?

AScheduling a nightly automation to import subscriber files from FTP

BChanging content for each subscriber using stored data

CChoosing the sending domain and dedicated IP for a send

DSetting how long rows stay in a data extension

AMPscript runs when an email is sent. It can look up and check data, then change the content for each subscriber.

The sending and delivery profiles determine the sending domain and IP.

Question 2: A team’s emails go to spam at one email provider. The DNS has SPF but no DKIM record. What should they do first?

ARemove the unsubscribe link to reduce complaints

BPublish a DKIM record for the sending domain

CMark every send as transactional

DIncrease sending volume to build a stronger reputation

Correct answer: B. Publish a DKIM record for the sending domain

DKIM signs the message so the receiving provider can check that it came from an approved sender and was not changed in transit. Missing DKIM can cause filtering, even when SPF passes.

Removing the unsubscribe link breaks anti-spam rules and can lead to more complaints.

Marking commercial email as transactional is a compliance problem, not a solution.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Marketing Cloud Engagement Specialist (MC-202 / CRT-550 / Email Specialist) Guide

ACopy the best send time from a different brand’s audience

CUse send-time optimization right away for the entire list

DChoose a reasonable time and gather data first

Send-time optimization uses each subscriber’s engagement data. For a new list, the data is insufficient, so start with a reasonable default and gather real engagement first.

A different brand’s audience may behave differently.

Waiting months to send a campaign delays it without a good reason.
