Question 2: What is the purpose of the household account model?

AIt holds the grant applications the organisation has submitted this year

BIt records which volunteers are available for each of the upcoming events

CIt groups people who give and are addressed together

DIt stores the employer of each contact so that matching gifts can be claimed

Correct answer: C. It groups people who give and are addressed together

Households let an organisation address a couple or family once and see their combined giving, which is how most individual fundraising works.

Grants are modelled as their own kind of opportunity.

Volunteer availability is tracked separately.

Employer relationships are handled by affiliations.

Question 3: A supporter gives £20 every month by direct debit. How should this be set up?

AAs a single annual opportunity for £240 with a note describing the schedule

BAs a recurring donation that generates the instalments

CAs twelve separate opportunities created by hand at the start of each year

DAs a campaign with the supporter added as a member once every month

Correct answer: B. As a recurring donation that generates the instalments

Recurring donations hold the schedule and generate the individual gift records, so the commitment and the instalments are both visible.

One annual figure hides whether each instalment was actually received.

Manual creation is laborious and breaks when the gift changes.

Campaign membership does not record money received.

Question 4: What does a General Accounting Unit allocation do?

AIt stores the payment method the supporter used to make their gift

BIt records which member of the fundraising team secured the donation

CIt assigns part of a gift to a fund or purpose

DIt tracks the date on which the gift was acknowledged in writing

Correct answer: C. It assigns part of a gift to a fund or purpose

GAU allocations split a gift across funds or restricted purposes, which is what lets a nonprofit report on restricted income.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Nonprofit Success Pack (NPSP) Consultant (NP-Con-101) Historical Study Guide
chunks.content:
Payment method is a field on the payment record.

Credit to a fundraiser is handled by ownership and soft credits.

Acknowledgement is tracked by its own fields.

Question 5: A couple gives jointly but only one of them is named on the cheque. How is the other recognised?

ABy creating a second opportunity for the same gift under their own name

BThrough a soft credit

CBy splitting the gift amount equally across two separate opportunities

DBy adding them as the primary contact and removing the original donor

Correct answer: B. Through a soft credit

Soft credits recognise influence or shared responsibility for a gift without double counting the income.

A duplicate opportunity inflates the organisation's reported income.

Splitting the amount understates what each person is associated with.

Replacing the donor misstates who actually gave.

Question 6: Why does double counting matter so much in nonprofit reporting?

ADuplicate records prevent acknowledgement letters from being generated

BReported income has to reconcile with the accounts

CSoft credits are unable to be reported on alongside hard credit figures

DSalesforce imposes a limit on how many opportunities an account may hold

Correct answer: B. Reported income has to reconcile with the accounts

Fundraising totals are published and audited, so a gift recorded twice overstates income and undermines trust in the data.

Letters can still be generated from duplicated records, wrongly.

Both can be reported on, which is precisely why the distinction is kept.

There is no such record limit in play.

Question 7: An organisation receives a grant with reporting conditions attached. How is this usually handled?

AAs an opportunity with a record type for grants

BAs a recurring donation with the reporting dates set as its instalments

CAs a case raised against the funder so the conditions can be tracked

DAs a campaign with the funder added as the only member of that campaign

Correct answer: A. As an opportunity with a record type for grants

Grants are modelled as opportunities with their own record type and stages, which accommodates the application and reporting lifecycle.

A grant is not a regular recurring gift.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Nonprofit Success Pack (NPSP) Consultant (NP-Con-101) Historical Study Guide
chunks.content:
Cases are for service queries rather than income.

Campaigns group appeals and responses, not grant conditions.

AImporting the organisation's entire contact database from a legacy system

BGenerating the acknowledgement letters for gifts received in the period

CReconciling the organisation's bank statement against its accounting system

DEntering many gifts quickly and consistently

Correct answer: D. Entering many gifts quickly and consistently

Batch gift entry gives a fast, validated screen for keying in a pile of gifts, which is what a post opening or event produces.

Bulk contact loading uses data import tools.

Acknowledgement is a separate downstream process.

Bank reconciliation happens in the finance system.

Merging two people destroys one person's record entirely.

OmniStudio Consultant Exam Format Explained

This proctored exam checks how you design OmniStudio solutions for real business processes. Use the 105-minute limit to work through the requirement, identify the component responsibilities, and trace the data flow.

Multiple-choice & multiple-select

How Many Questions Are Scenario-Based?

Questions describe a user journey or data-processing task. Decide whether the solution needs a guided script, a data display, a data operation, or server-side orchestration.

Best Way to Pass on Your First Attempt

Map the component roles: Match user input to OmniScript, a compact record view to FlexCard, data access to Data Mapper, and server-side orchestration to Integration Procedure.

Trace the JSON: Follow one value from an Extract through an OmniScript or procedure and into a Load or response.

Compare server-side choices: Know when a single Data Mapper is enough and when several calls belong in an Integration Procedure.

Debug a real build: Use preview output to find missing keys, incorrect mappings, and errors between components.

OmniStudio Consultant: Key Concepts

FlexCards: Displaying Data Contextually

FlexCards show contextual data from Salesforce records or connected sources within Experience Cloud, Lightning pages, or other OmniStudio experiences. Child cards can surface related records. A custom action can launch an OmniScript, open a Lightning component, or navigate to a record. Data can come from a DataRaptor Extract, Integration Procedure, or Apex. Use a card to give users relevant details where they need them.

OmniScripts: Guided User Experiences

OmniScripts guide a user through a multi-step process. Steps and groups organize inputs such as text, dates, selections, checkboxes, and lookups. Conditional display rules can reveal elements based on earlier responses; data sources can populate choices or prefill fields. Validation checks business rules before the user continues. Common uses include onboarding, service requests, and claims.

Integration Procedures: Backend Orchestration

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified OmniStudio Consultant (Plat-Con-201) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Integration Procedures coordinate backend work without requiring user interaction. OmniScripts and FlexCards can call them, as can other processes. An IP can query or write Salesforce data through DataRaptor actions, call an external REST service through HTTP Action, invoke Apex, set values, and branch or loop. It can combine and transform results from multiple sources before returning them to the caller.

DataRaptors: Data Access and Transformation

DataRaptors handle reading, writing, or reshaping data. Extract reads Salesforce data into structured JSON; Load creates or updates records; Transform maps between structures without writing to Salesforce; Turbo Extract performs a simpler, optimized read using SOQL. Choose the type to match the operation. A Load can create related parent and child records in one operation.

OmniStudio Architecture in Industry Clouds

Industry Clouds include Health, Financial Services, Communications, and Energy and Utilities. Their packages can provide industry-specific OmniScripts and FlexCards, which teams configure or extend. These components work with standard Salesforce objects and industry data models. Business Rules Engine offers declarative if-then logic that can guide OmniScript branches without hard-coding those decisions.

Well-designed OmniScripts keep each step focused, use conditional views to skip irrelevant questions, and call reusable sub-OmniScripts for shared sequences instead of duplicating steps across scripts.

How to Pass the Salesforce OmniStudio Consultant Exam

Start with the business requirement, then choose the OmniStudio components and data flow that fit it.

Tool Selection Framework

Match each task to its tool. FlexCards display contextual information, OmniScripts guide users through steps, DataRaptors handle Salesforce data, and Integration Procedures coordinate server-side work.

Business Process to OmniScript Mapping

Break the business process into guided steps and map the data each step needs. Consider a sub-OmniScript when the same process can be reused.

Data Integration Architecture

Compare DataRaptor Extract with an Integration Procedure when retrieving data. Review transformation needs and whether the procedure must call an external API.

Use FlexCards to present information such as account details or case summaries. Plan states for loading, empty, error, and populated results.

Performance & Scalability

OmniStudio Developer: Key Concepts

The Four Main OmniStudio Tools

OmniScript guides a user through steps, collects information, and shows results. It can support tasks such as opening an account or changing a plan. FlexCard displays a compact summary of a record and can offer actions, such as opening an OmniScript. A Data Mapper (formerly DataRaptor) reads, transforms, or writes data. Integration Procedure runs server-side logic, calls other services, and combines results. Many exam questions ask which of these tools best fits a task.

Data Mapper: Extract, Load, and Transform

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified OmniStudio Developer (Plat-Dev-210) Practice Exam & Study Guide
chunks.content:
A Data Mapper Extract reads Salesforce data and returns it in a format such as JSON. Data Mapper Load writes input data to Salesforce records. Data Mapper Transform changes data from one shape to another without reading or writing Salesforce records. Turbo Extract is a faster option for simpler reads from one Salesforce object and related records, but it has fewer configuration options. Use Data Mappers for reusable, declarative data work that admins can update without Apex.

Integration Procedures and Performance

An Integration Procedure runs on the server and can combine several operations in one request. It can call Data Mappers, external services through HTTP actions, and Apex through Remote Actions. A Chainable procedure can continue work in another transaction when more processing is needed. Parallel elements can run independent calls at the same time. Use an Integration Procedure for server-side work rather than making an OmniScript call out repeatedly.

OmniScript Structure and Custom Components

An OmniScript contains steps and elements. Input elements collect data, display elements show it, and action elements read or save data. Conditional views show or hide elements based on the user’s answers. The script stores information in JSON, and each element reads from or writes to named keys. When standard elements do not meet a need, a custom Lightning Web Component can be placed in the script and exchange data with it. OmniStudio components can also appear on Lightning pages or Experience Cloud sites.

Debugging, Deployment, and Versions

OmniStudio components use versions. Activate the version users need; create a new version to make changes. Preview and the debug panel show the JSON at each step, which helps find missing or unexpected data. Teams can move components between orgs as datapacks and include them in a release process. Record IDs differ across orgs, so hard-coded IDs can cause a component to work in one environment but fail in another.

Use a FlexCard to display compact record data at a glance. Use an OmniScript to guide a user through a multi-step process. Both can call the same Integration Procedures and DataRaptors underneath.

chunks.title: Order Management Administrator Accredited Professional Study Guide (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
An order usually arrives from a commerce store or another system as an Order. Order Management creates an Order Summary, the main record for later fulfillment, changes, and returns. Order Item Summaries represent the products in the order. Order Delivery Group Summaries group items by delivery address and method. The original Order records what was submitted. Later changes are tracked against the Order Summary so teams can compare the original order with its current state.

Fulfillment and Inventory

Order Management creates Fulfillment Orders for the locations that will ship items. A Location may be a warehouse or store. Routing logic, often in a flow, decides which location should fulfill each item, such as the closest location with stock. One Order Summary can be split across several Fulfillment Orders. Warehouse staff or another system updates each Fulfillment Order as items are picked, packed, and shipped. An invoice can be created and payment captured when items ship.

Cancellations, Returns, and Refunds

Before an item ships, a customer can cancel it. Order Management creates a Change Order and updates the Order Summary totals. After an item ships, the customer can return it through a Return Order with Return Order Line Items. When the return is received, the item is marked as returned and a refund can be issued through a credit memo. Service agents can use built-in actions from the Order Summary. The system records the reason for the return for reporting.

Prices, Discounts, Taxes, and Payments

The original order provides prices, discounts, and taxes. Order Management stores these values on the Order Summary and its item summaries. When an item is cancelled or returned, the system calculates the refund, including the item’s share of order-level discounts and tax. A goodwill discount is recorded as a price adjustment so totals stay correct. Payment Summaries show what was authorized, captured, or refunded.

Commerce Integration and Omnichannel Inventory

chunks.title: Order Management Administrator Accredited Professional Study Guide (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Omnichannel Inventory tracks stock at different locations. Location groups let a store show availability across a set of locations, such as warehouses in one country. When a customer places an order, inventory is reserved so the same stock is not sold twice. The reservation moves to the location that fulfills the order. Order Management can connect to B2C or B2B Commerce and to warehouse or ERP systems through APIs and events. Failed automated steps can create process exceptions for agents to review.

DThe shopping Cart record.

Correct answer: C. The Order Summary record.

The Order Summary becomes the main record for tracking what happens to an order after it is submitted.

The original Order records what was submitted; later activity is tracked on the Order Summary.

An Account represents the customer, not the lifecycle of one order.

This record tracks the order’s later fulfillment, changes, and returns.

Question 2: Items in one order will ship from two warehouses. How should this be represented?

ACreate two separate Account records for the customer.

BCreate a Fulfillment Order for each warehouse.

CCreate one Return Order for the two shipments.

DCreate two Order Summaries for the original order.

Correct answer: B. Create a Fulfillment Order for each warehouse.

Order Management can split fulfillment across two Fulfillment Orders, one for each warehouse.

The same customer can have an order fulfilled from more than one location.

This represents separate fulfillment work at each location.

A Return Order tracks returned items, not outbound shipments.

Question 3: A customer cancels an item before it ships. What does Order Management create?

AA new Order for the remaining items.

BA Case on the customer’s Account.

CA Return Order for the unshipped item.

Correct answer: D. A Change Order.

chunks.title: Order Management Administrator Accredited Professional Study Guide (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
A Change Order records the cancellation and updates the Order Summary amount.

A new Order is not needed to cancel one line.

A Case is for customer service work, not the order change itself.

A Return Order handles items that have shipped and are being sent back.

Question 4: A customer wants a refund for an item that has already shipped. What should the agent use?

AA Return Order with its line items.

BDelete the Order Item Summary from the order.

CEdit the original Order record.

DCreate a Change Order to cancel the shipped item.

Correct answer: A. A Return Order with its line items.

A Return Order and its line items record items being sent back after shipment.

This is the process for a return after shipment.

Deleting the summary removes history instead of recording a return.

The original Order records what was submitted and should not be edited to handle a return.

Question 5: The company wants to route orders to the closest warehouse that has stock. Where is this logic usually configured?

AUse the order-routing flow.

BIn the product description field on the record.

CIn a report used to list the warehouses.

DIn the Account page layout settings.

Correct answer: A. Use the order-routing flow.

A routing flow can choose the fulfillment location and create Fulfillment Orders.

This is where order routing logic is commonly configured.

A product description does not decide which location ships an order.

A report displays data but does not route fulfillment work.

Question 6: The online store should show available stock across warehouses in Germany. What should be configured?

AA different storefront for every warehouse.

BA custom field on each product record.

CA daily email from each warehouse with its stock.

DA location group for the German warehouses.

Correct answer: D. A location group for the German warehouses.

A location group can combine locations so the store can show their availability together.

Separate storefronts are not needed to group stock locations.

A product field does not calculate availability across warehouses.

A daily email would be delayed and would not provide current availability.

chunks.title: Order Management Administrator Accredited Professional Study Guide (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Question 7: Why does Order Management reserve inventory when a customer places an order?

AIncrease the price of each item on the order.

BPrevent the same stock from being sold twice.

CCreate an invoice before the items ship.

DHide the item from storefront search while shipping.

Correct answer: B. Prevent the same stock from being sold twice.

A reservation holds stock for the order so another order cannot claim the same inventory.

Reservations do not change the item price.

An invoice is a separate step in the order lifecycle.

A reservation affects available stock, not whether the product appears in search.

Question 8: An order flow fails because a payment service does not respond. Where can agents find the failed process for review?

AWait for the customer to report the problem.

BSearch email messages for a failure notice.

CDelete the order and ask the customer to order again.

DReview the process exception raised by the failed step.

Correct answer: D. Review the process exception raised by the failed step.

A process exception records a failed automated step so an agent can review and resolve it.

Waiting for a complaint does not help staff identify failures early.

Email may not contain a complete or searchable record of the exception.

Deleting the order removes history and may create more problems.

Question 9: An agent gives a customer a goodwill discount after the order is placed. How should the discount be recorded?

AAdd a note to the customer’s Account only.

BEdit the original Order total.

CRecord a price adjustment on the Order Summary.

DDelete one of the ordered items.

Correct answer: C. Record a price adjustment on the Order Summary.

A price adjustment records the discount on the Order Summary while preserving the original Order.

A note does not update the order totals.

The original Order records what was submitted and should remain unchanged.

Deleting a product changes the order contents; it does not record a goodwill discount.

Question 10: An order had a 10% order-level discount. The customer returns one of three items. What should the refund include?

chunks.title: Order Management Administrator Accredited Professional Study Guide (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
AThe full original order amount.

BRefund price minus its discount share, plus tax.

CThe full item price without any discount.

DNo refund, because discounted items cannot be returned.

Correct answer: B. Refund price minus its discount share, plus tax.

The refund should include the returned item’s price after its share of the order discount, plus applicable tax.

The customer returned one item, not the entire order.

This accounts for the item’s discount share and tax.

A discount does not prevent a refund for a valid return.

Question 11: When is payment usually captured for items in an order?

AWhen the items ship and an invoice is created.

BWhen the customer first creates an account.

CWhen the customer adds items to a cart.

DOnly after the customer returns an item.

Correct answer: A. When the items ship and an invoice is created.

Payment can usually be captured when items ship and an invoice exists.

This is the usual point for capturing payment on shipped items.

Creating a customer account does not capture order payment.

A cart is not a submitted order ready for payment capture.

Question 12: Which record tracks one product line in an Order Summary, including its ordered, cancelled, and returned quantities?

Correct answer: C. Order Item Summary

An Order Item Summary tracks details for a product line in the Order Summary.

A Fulfillment Order tracks work sent to a location.

A Location is a warehouse, store, or other fulfillment point.

A Payment Summary tracks payment activity.

Question 13: Customers can choose different delivery addresses for products in one order. Which record groups items by delivery address and method?

AA Return Order Summary for items that were sent back.

BAn Order Delivery Group Summary for address and method.

CA Change Order for a cancellation or adjustment.

DA Credit Memo for a customer refund.

Correct answer: B. An Order Delivery Group Summary for address and method.

An Order Delivery Group Summary groups items by delivery address and shipping method.

A Return Order Summary is for returned items.

This record groups items by delivery details.

chunks.title: Order Management Administrator Accredited Professional Study Guide (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
A Change Order records changes to the order.

Question 14: A warehouse system needs to tell Salesforce that a Fulfillment Order shipped. What is the best approach?

AUpdate the Fulfillment Order by API.

BCreate a new Order record.

CEdit the customer’s Account record.

DEmail the customer service team.

Correct answer: A. Update the Fulfillment Order by API.

The warehouse system can update the Fulfillment Order through an API integration.

This updates the fulfillment status in Salesforce.

A new Order would incorrectly create another customer order.

The Account record does not track the shipment status.

Question 15: Where do service agents usually handle order cancellations and returns?

AOpen Developer Console to inspect the Salesforce data.

BUse Setup to change the company’s order settings.

CUse built-in actions on the Order Summary.

DUse Data Loader to update the order record manually.

Correct answer: C. Use built-in actions on the Order Summary.

Agents usually use the Order Summary and its built-in actions to manage cancellations and returns.

Developer Console is for development work.

Setup is for configuring Salesforce, not routine service work.

This is where agents can use the order actions.

Order Management Developer AP: Key Concepts

chunks.title: Order Management Developer Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Order Management uses related records to represent an order and its later activity. Learn how order data is imported, converted, queried, and updated. Salesforce APIs can create records in real time. Choose an API that fits the data and integration need, and handle errors so failed requests can be investigated or safely retried.

Automation and platform development

Use Flow for supported low-code automation and Apex when the requirement needs custom code. Apex actions can be called from Flow and other Salesforce features. Keep automation bulk-safe, and test both successful work and failures.

Integrations and order management design

An Order Management project may connect Commerce, payment, invoicing, warehouse, or other systems. Map what each system does and when it sends or receives data. Use platform features such as triggers, events, and notifications where they fit the integration.

Reference frameworks and historical data

The exam guide included Salesforce reference implementations and frameworks for importing historical orders and resolving customer records. Learn what each framework supports before recommending it; a framework does not replace the need to map the customer’s data and process.

Omnichannel Inventory and advanced cases

Omnichannel Inventory helps coordinate availability across locations and channels. Consider how it connects with Order Management and Commerce. The guide also covered more involved requirements such as bulk orders, fraud detection, and remorse periods.

Salesforce Certified Order Management Developer Accredited Professional Practice Questions (With Explanations)

Test your knowledge with these 15 sample questions.

Answered: 0 / 15Correct: 0

Question 1: A customer places one order for items stored at different warehouses. Which feature decides where each item should go?

AThe account record’s preferred warehouse for the customer

BA product setting that assigns every unit to one warehouse

CA manual order split created by a support agent

DOrder routing that allocates items to fulfillment locations

Correct answer: D. Order routing that allocates items to fulfillment locations

Order routing can allocate items to locations based on the order and available fulfillment choices.

The account’s preferred warehouse does not make item-level allocation decisions.

A fixed product location cannot respond to each order’s fulfillment needs.

chunks.title: Order Management Developer Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Manual splits do not provide scalable order routing.

Question 2: What does a fulfillment order represent in Salesforce Order Management?

AA customer invoice for goods that have arrived

BA payment authorization created when the order is submitted

CA request to return goods after delivery

DThe items that one fulfillment location must process

Correct answer: D. The items that one fulfillment location must process

A fulfillment order groups the items that a location is responsible for fulfilling.

An invoice is a separate financial document.

Payment authorization is a payment step, not a fulfillment record.

A return uses return-related records and processes.

Question 3: A buyer cancels one item from an order with three items, before shipping. What should the system do?

ACancel the full order and ask the buyer to place it again

BUpdate the order summary to reflect the cancelled item

CShip the item and wait for the buyer to return it

DIssue a credit but leave the order data unchanged

Correct answer: B. Update the order summary to reflect the cancelled item

The order can be amended to remove the cancelled item while the other items continue.

Cancelling the full order also affects items the buyer still wants.

Shipping the cancelled item ignores the buyer’s request.

A credit alone leaves the order records out of sync.

Question 4: Which description best fits an order summary?

AA record of the order’s current state and later changes

BA permanent copy of the order exactly as first submitted

CA shipping label for each package leaving a warehouse

DA list containing only payments captured for the order

Correct answer: A. A record of the order’s current state and later changes

The order summary reflects the order as it moves through changes and fulfillment.

The original order record preserves the initial submission.

A shipping label is used to ship a package.

Payment records track payment activity separately.

Question 5: A developer must run logic as soon as an order changes to a certain status. Which approach fits?

ARun a scheduled job that checks every open order each night

chunks.title: Order Management Developer Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
BUse a validation rule to prevent the status change

CUse a record-triggered Flow or Apex for the status change

DAsk a support agent to review each status update

Correct answer: C. Use a record-triggered Flow or Apex for the status change

A record-triggered Flow or Apex can respond when the order status changes.

A nightly job delays the response and checks records that may not have changed.

A validation rule blocks a change instead of responding to it.

Manual review is not an automated response.

Question 6: An integration retries a payment request after a network timeout. Why should it use an idempotency key?

AAn order is limited to one payment record for its entire life

BThe retry should not charge the customer a second time

CThe payment service requires requests in one fixed sequence

DApex cannot make a callout more than once

Correct answer: B. The retry should not charge the customer a second time

An idempotency key helps the payment service recognize a retry and avoid processing the same payment twice.

An order can have more than one payment-related record.

Request ordering is a separate integration concern.

Callouts can be retried; the retry must be safe.

Question 7: A customer returns one discounted item from an order. What should the refund amount be based on?

AThe full order total, including every shipping charge

BThe item’s current list price on the day of the return

CA fixed percentage of the original order total

DThe amount paid for that returned item

Correct answer: D. The amount paid for that returned item

The refund should reflect the amount paid for the returned item, including any applicable discount.

Refunding the entire order would include items the customer kept.

The current list price may differ from the amount originally paid.

A fixed percentage may not match the item’s paid price.

Question 8: What information does an order delivery group provide?

AItems that will be delivered together to one address

BCarriers approved for a particular sales region

CWarehouses that hold stock for each product

DThe required processing order for fulfillment records

chunks.title: Order Management Developer Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Correct answer: A. Items that will be delivered together to one address

A delivery group associates items with a delivery destination and method.

Carrier approval is configuration, not the group’s purpose.

Inventory records track stock by location.

A delivery group does not set the processing sequence.

Question 9: A promotion causes many orders to arrive at once. What should a developer check in custom Apex?

AWhether the org has enough fulfillment locations configured

BWhether each order can be processed in its own transaction

CWhether the code handles records in bulk

DWhether automation should be disabled during the sale

Correct answer: C. Whether the code handles records in bulk

Bulk-safe code can process groups of records while respecting Apex limits.

More locations do not fix code that processes records inefficiently.

Separate processing for each record can exceed limits at high volume.

Disabling automation can leave orders incomplete.

Question 10: In Order Management, what does order capture mean?

ACharging a payment method after the goods have shipped

BRecording delivery confirmation from the carrier

CCreating an order from a customer purchase

DAssigning ordered items to fulfillment locations

Correct answer: C. Creating an order from a customer purchase

Order capture creates the order in Salesforce from the customer’s purchase.

Charging a payment method is a separate payment action.

Delivery confirmation happens after shipment.

Allocation follows capture as part of fulfillment.

Question 11: A location cannot fulfill an item because it has no stock. What is a suitable next step?

ACancel every item on the order and notify the customer

BReallocate the item to another location that can fulfill it

CShip the other items and omit the unavailable item without notice

DKeep the order on hold without a status update

Correct answer: B. Reallocate the item to another location that can fulfill it

If another location can fulfill the item, reallocation can keep the order moving.

Cancelling every item may be unnecessary if only one is unavailable.

Omitting the item without telling the customer creates a service problem.

An unexplained hold leaves the customer and staff without useful status.

chunks.title: Order Management Developer Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Question 12: Why might a developer publish a platform event when an order changes?

ATo let other systems react without coupling them to the order process

BTo calculate the refund due for each returned item

CTo enforce validation rules on order summary records

DTo store order history for external systems to query later

Correct answer: A. To let other systems react without coupling them to the order process

A platform event lets subscribers react to a change without the publishing process needing to know each subscriber.

Refund calculation is business logic, not the purpose of an event.

Validation rules govern record changes directly.

An event is a message, not a queryable history store.

Question 13: Which statement explains the difference between an order and its order summary?

AA user creates the summary manually, while Salesforce creates the order

BThe order summary is maintained as the captured order moves through its lifecycle

COnly customers can see the summary, while only staff can see the order

DThe summary is for subscriptions, while orders are for physical goods

Correct answer: B. The order summary is maintained as the captured order moves through its lifecycle

The order summary is the managed record used to represent order activity after capture.

Both records are created as part of the order process.

Who can see a record depends on access settings.

The distinction does not depend on whether goods are physical.

Question 14: An order has shipped and is with the carrier. The customer asks to change the delivery address. What is the realistic response?

AContact the carrier because editing Salesforce will not redirect the parcel

BEdit the summary and assume the carrier receives the new address

CCancel the shipped fulfillment order to recall the parcel

DAdd a delivery group to redirect the parcel already in transit

Correct answer: A. Contact the carrier because editing Salesforce will not redirect the parcel

Once the parcel is with the carrier, changing a Salesforce record does not redirect it.

Editing a record does not automatically change the carrier’s shipment.

Cancelling a shipped fulfillment order does not recall the parcel.

chunks.title: Order Management Developer Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
A new delivery group would not redirect a parcel already in transit.

Question 15: Which task is Salesforce Order Management designed to support?

ARunning the online storefront where buyers browse products

BPreparing financial statements for recognized revenue

CManaging orders from capture through fulfillment and returns

DOperating warehouse equipment inside a distribution center

Correct answer: C. Managing orders from capture through fulfillment and returns

Order Management supports the order lifecycle, including capture, fulfillment, changes, returns, and refunds.

A storefront is provided by Commerce or another sales channel.

Financial statements are prepared by finance systems and processes.

Warehouse equipment is handled by warehouse systems.

Account Engagement Consultant: Key Exam Concepts

Plan the implementation

Start with the client’s marketing goals, teams, Salesforce setup, and data. Then decide how Account Engagement business units, user access, connector settings, and campaigns should be organized. Match the design to the client’s structure instead of adding complexity without a need.

Choose the right automation

Engagement Studio is for nurturing prospects through a planned series of steps. Automation Rules evaluate criteria and can take ongoing actions. Segmentation Rules create a list based on criteria at a point in time. Choose the tool that fits the job and the timing the client needs.

Align marketing and sales campaigns

Account Engagement campaigns commonly show a prospect’s first marketing touch. Salesforce campaigns and campaign influence support broader campaign tracking and opportunity reporting. Plan campaign hierarchy and member statuses so the teams can interpret the results consistently.

Design scoring, grading, and segments

Scoring reflects a prospect’s activity, such as visits and email engagement. Grading reflects how well the prospect matches the client’s target profile. Scoring categories can separate interest in different products. Segmentation Rules create a list at a point in time, while Dynamic Lists keep matching records up to date.

Report on business results

Choose reports that answer the client’s questions. Teams may need to see prospect activity, campaign performance, or how marketing relates to pipeline and revenue. Agree on the measures and data definitions before building dashboards.

Scoring rises with engagement activity (opens, clicks, form fills), it measures interest. Grading is set from profile attributes (title, industry, company size), it measures fit. Sales should prioritize prospects that are high on both axes.

BWhether sales users have completed a product navigation course

CWhether the client needs more nurture-program licenses

DHow often the connector checks for new prospect activity

AThe client’s expected number of new prospects per month

BThe order in which the client opened its sales regions

CThe traits shared by its strongest existing customers

DThe number of questions on its lead capture form

Correct answer: C. The traits shared by its strongest existing customers

Grading measures fit, so use attributes that describe the client’s target customers.

Monthly prospect volume does not describe who is a good fit.

Region launch dates do not define the target profile.

The form’s field count does not determine which traits matter.

Question 3: Marketing wants qualified prospects assigned to sales once they meet agreed score and grade thresholds. What should the consultant use?

AA weekly meeting where staff select prospects by hand

BAutomation rule using score and grade thresholds

CA static segmentation list that is rebuilt each morning

DA completion action added to every form in the account

Correct answer: B. Automation rule using score and grade thresholds

An automation rule can keep evaluating prospects and assign those who meet the agreed criteria.

Manual review adds delay and does not automate the handoff.

A static list is a point-in-time group, not ongoing threshold evaluation.

A form completion action runs on a form event, not when a prospect later qualifies.

AThe connector will automatically turn off after a field limit is reached

CAccount Engagement will stop calculating prospect scores

DSalesforce will reject every record with marketing fields

A field count does not by itself mean the connector will turn off.

Field sync does not stop the scoring feature.

Salesforce can store custom fields; the concern is whether the data is useful.

Question 5: A company has three brands with separate audiences and marketing teams. What should the consultant evaluate?

AGiving each brand a separate Salesforce org by default

BWhether enough custom fields exist for each brand

CUse business units to separate brand teams and prospect data

DSharing one tracking domain across every brand

Correct answer: C. Use business units to separate brand teams and prospect data

Business units can separate marketing assets, prospects, and access when the organization needs that structure.

Separate Salesforce orgs are not automatically required for separate brands.

Custom-field count does not answer how to organize brands and access.

A shared tracking domain may not suit every brand’s needs.

ARequiring every profile field on the first visit

BProgressive profiling on later visits

CRemoving the consent language from the form

DTurning off scoring for people who submit the form

Correct answer: B. Progressive profiling on later visits

Progressive profiling asks for a few new details on later visits, keeping the first form shorter.

Requiring every field at once can make the first form longer.

Progressive profiling does not remove consent requirements.

Scoring is separate from how a form gathers profile details.

Question 7: Prospects are being assigned to sales users who have left the company. What should the consultant inspect?

AThe score needed before a prospect can be assigned

BThe tracking domain used on the company’s landing pages

CReview assignment rules and the users they assign prospects to

DHow often the connector syncs records

Correct answer: C. Review assignment rules and the users they assign prospects to

Assignment rules may still point to inactive users or outdated queues.

The threshold does not explain why assignments go to former employees.

Tracking domains do not choose the assignment owner.

Sync timing is separate from the owner selected by assignment rules.

Question 8: Before building a nurture program, what should the consultant clarify with the client?

AThe planned email volume for each calendar month

BThe total size of the prospect database

CThe approved colors for email templates

DThe next decision the program should help prospects reach

Correct answer: D. The next decision the program should help prospects reach

The program should support a clear prospect goal; that goal guides the messages and branches.

Email volume alone does not explain what the program should achieve.

Database size does not define the journey or decision.

Brand colors do not determine the nurture path.

Question 9: A new nurture program causes a sharp rise in unsubscribes. What should the consultant investigate first?

AEmails sent too often or without relevant content

BWhether the tracking domain is verified for email sending

CWhether the program includes a wait step between every email

DWhether prospects had a grade before entering the program

Correct answer: A. Emails sent too often or without relevant content

Too many messages or irrelevant content can lead prospects to unsubscribe.

A tracking domain can matter for tracking, but it does not explain message relevance or frequency.

Wait steps alone do not ensure that the program suits its audience.

Having a grade is not required for every nurture program.

Question 10: A marketer needs to keep certain prospects out of one email send. What is a suppression list for?

ATo store prospects who have not yet been assigned to sales

BTo collect the highest-scoring prospects for a special send

CTo exclude selected prospects from that send

DTo track which prospects opened an earlier email

Correct answer: C. To exclude selected prospects from that send

A suppression list excludes its members from an email send.

Assignment status is a separate prospect attribute.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Marketing Cloud Account Engagement Consultant (CRT-302 / Pardot) Historical Guide
chunks.content:
A suppression list does not select recipients for priority.

Opens are tracked as email activity, not by a suppression list.

AUse a form handler with the existing external form

BA native form that replaces the external form

CA segmentation rule that collects the submitted fields

DA completion action added to the existing web page

Correct answer: A. Use a form handler with the existing external form

A form handler can receive submissions while the client keeps the external form markup.

A native form would replace the form the client needs to keep.

A segmentation rule groups records; it does not accept form submissions.

A completion action runs after an Account Engagement action and does not receive the external form data by itself.

Question 12: Why configure an Account Engagement tracking domain with the client’s own domain?

AIt sets the number of landing pages the account can publish

BIt is required to record any prospect activity at all

CIt removes the need to follow consent rules

DUse a tracking domain branded for the client

Correct answer: D. Use a tracking domain branded for the client

A branded tracking domain lets tracked links and pages use the client’s domain.

The domain does not set the landing-page limit.

Tracking can work with other configured domains as well.

A branded domain does not replace consent obligations.

Question 13: A client has many inactive prospects and wants to protect email deliverability. What is a sensible plan?

ASend the same large campaign to all prospects to find active people

BIncrease send frequency across the full database

CDelete all prospects who have not engaged recently

DRe-engage inactive prospects, then suppress nonresponders

Correct answer: D. Re-engage inactive prospects, then suppress nonresponders

Give inactive prospects a clear chance to re-engage, then reduce sends to those who do not respond.

A large blast to everyone may harm deliverability.

More frequent messages can worsen engagement and deliverability.

Immediate deletion may discard records before the client confirms its retention needs.

Scoring estimates interest based on actions such as form submissions, email clicks, and page visits. Grading measures fit with a target profile, using details such as role, industry, or company size. Segmentation Rules create a list from criteria at the time the rule runs; Dynamic Lists update as prospects meet or stop meeting criteria.

Visitors and prospects

AAccount Engagement creates a prospect record using the submitted identifying details

A sales rep does not need to create the prospect manually after an identified form submission.

Account Engagement records the prospect as well as the form activity.

Question 2: Which action usually adds to a prospect’s score?

AWorking for a company in the target industry

BHolding a job title listed in the ideal customer profile

CWorking at a company of the preferred size

DOpening a marketing email and clicking a link

Correct answer: D. Opening a marketing email and clicking a link

Scoring reflects engagement activities such as email opens and link clicks. Grading uses profile attributes to measure fit.

Industry is a profile detail used to assess fit.

Job title is a profile detail used to assess fit.

Company size is a profile detail used to assess fit.

Question 3: A prospect downloads several guides but works at a company outside the target market. How should the record reflect this?

ALow score and high grade

BHigh score and high grade

CHigh score and low grade

DLow score and low grade

Correct answer: C. High score and low grade

Scoring measures how interested a prospect is, and the downloads show interest. Grading measures fit, so this prospect should have a lower grade.

The downloads show activity, so the score should not be low.

A poor fit should not receive a high grade simply for being active.

The prospect is engaged, so the score should be high.

Automation Rules continually check updated prospects against criteria and can run again when Repeat Rule is enabled. This lets the rule apply actions when prospects meet the criteria again.

A Segmentation Rule creates a list at the time it runs.

A one-time export does not continue to evaluate changing criteria.

Salesforce Platform Foundations: Key Concepts for the Exam

How the Salesforce Platform Works

Salesforce is a cloud platform used by many customers. This shared model is called multi-tenant. Each customer works in a separate org, where their data is kept apart. Salesforce releases platform updates three times a year, in Spring, Summer, and Winter. Most changes are made in Setup without writing code. A sandbox is a copy of an org for building and testing changes. After testing, teams can move those changes to the live org, called production.

Objects, Records, and Fields

Salesforce stores information in objects, much like tables in a database. A record is one item in an object, and a field stores one piece of information about that item. Common standard objects include Lead for a potential customer who is not yet qualified, Account for a company or person you work with, Contact for a person linked to an account, Opportunity for a potential sale, and Case for a customer issue. You can create custom objects for information that standard objects do not cover. Relationships connect records: a lookup is a flexible link, while with master-detail the child record depends on its parent and inherits its record access. Converting a Lead creates an Account and Contact, and can also create an Opportunity.

How Access Is Controlled

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Foundations (Plat-101 / Associate) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Salesforce access has several layers. Login settings decide whether and when someone can sign in. A profile and any permission sets control which objects and fields they can use and what actions they can take. Record access is managed separately: the org-wide default sets the starting access for each object, and the role hierarchy and sharing rules can give users access to more records. In short, profiles and permission sets control what users can do, while record sharing controls which records they can do it to.

Automation and Reports

Flow Builder automates work such as updating records, sending emails, and guiding users through a process. Validation rules prevent records with invalid data from being saved. Approval processes send records to people for review. A report lists or summarizes records using a report type, and a dashboard displays report information as charts and metrics. List views show a filtered set of records on an object tab. For this exam, focus on which tool fits each need.

The Salesforce Ecosystem

AppExchange is Salesforce's marketplace for apps and components. Some are free and some are paid, and they can be installed in an org. Trailhead is Salesforce's free learning site, with lessons, trails, badges, and hands-on Superbadges. The Trailblazer Community is a place to ask questions and share solutions. Learn the main product families and their general purpose: Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Experience Cloud, Tableau, MuleSoft, Slack, and Data 360.

Salesforce is a cloud CRM platform: your data lives in Objects (Accounts, Contacts, Opportunities), organized by Apps, viewed through Lightning Experience, and extended by clouds like Sales, Service, and Marketing on the same underlying platform.

Favorites (the star icon) are shortcuts to pages a user visits often. Users change their own time zone, locale, and language in personal settings, while org customization happens in Setup, where Quick Find locates a setting.

Know how Lead, Account, Contact, Opportunity, and Case relate, and that converting a Lead creates an Account and a Contact and can create an Opportunity. Custom objects and fields carry a __c suffix in their API names. A lookup is a loose link; with master-detail, deleting the parent deletes its children and the parent can hold roll-up summary fields. Schema Builder shows objects and relationships on one canvas. For data integrity, compare required fields, picklists, validation rules, and duplicate and matching rules. For data visibility, review org-wide defaults, roles, and sharing. The Data Import Wizard handles up to 50,000 records; Data Loader handles larger jobs.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Foundations (Plat-101 / Associate) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
A report type decides which objects and fields a report can use. The four formats are tabular (a plain list), summary (grouped rows with subtotals), matrix (grouped by rows and columns), and joined (several blocks). Reports live in folders, which control who can see them, and users can subscribe to a report to receive results on a schedule. Each dashboard component is driven by one source report. A dashboard shows data as its running user sees it, unless it is a dynamic dashboard, which shows each viewer their own data.

4-Week Salesforce Platform Foundations Study Plan

Use this four-week plan as a starting point and adjust it to your experience. A free Trailhead Playground is enough to follow along.

Week 1 — Salesforce Ecosystem (32%): Complete the Trailhead “Salesforce Platform Basics” and “CRM for Lightning Experience” modules. Learn Customer 360, the main product clouds, AppExchange, and Trailhead itself.

Week 2 — Navigation (28%) and Data Model (25%): Practise the App Launcher, global search, list views, and the Salesforce mobile app. Study standard versus custom objects, field types, and lookup versus master-detail relationships, and build an object in a Trailhead Playground.

Week 3 — Reports & Dashboards (15%) plus review: Learn what reports and dashboards do and how a list view differs from both. Revisit anything shaky from Weeks 1 and 2.

Week 4 — Mock exams and review: Take full timed practice exams and target 75%+ before booking. Review any weak areas the practice results turned up.

Decision Rules for Platform Foundations Scenario Questions

About a third of the questions use short scenarios. Focus on standard Salesforce features, not custom development that would be out of scope for a foundations exam.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform Foundations (Plat-101 / Associate) Study Guide & Practice Questions
chunks.content:
Field type questions: text fields store alphanumeric data, number fields store numeric values, lookup fields create a relationship to another object, and master-detail fields create a tighter parent-child relationship where the child cannot exist without the parent. Formula fields calculate values from other fields and are read-only.

Security questions: profiles control which objects and fields a user can access, and permission sets add access on top of a profile; they cannot restrict what a profile already grants. Org-wide defaults set the baseline sharing level, and sharing rules open up access beyond that baseline.

Automation questions: validation rules prevent saving invalid data, formula fields calculate read-only values, and Flow automates processes, a screen flow for guided users and an auto-launched flow for background logic. “When a record is saved, automatically update a field” points to an auto-launched flow on record save, not a manual process.

3 Concepts That Fail Most Platform Foundations Candidates

These are not the hardest topics; they are the ones where candidates are most confidently wrong. Learn the distinction early.

1. Standard Objects vs. Custom Objects: What You Can and Cannot Modify

Standard objects (Account, Contact, Opportunity, Case) are provided by Salesforce and cannot be deleted; you can add fields, page layouts, and validation rules, but you cannot remove their core fields. Custom objects are fully user-defined and can be deleted if no records exist.

2. Profiles vs. Permission Sets: Baseline vs. Extension

Profiles define the baseline permissions for a group of users: what objects they can access, what apps they see, and their login hours. Permission sets add permissions on top of a profile, never used to restrict what a profile already grants.

3. App Launcher vs. Navigation Bar vs. Home Page: Three Separate Areas

The App Launcher shows all apps available to a user, customised through profiles and permission sets. The navigation bar, inside a Lightning app, defines which tabs are visible in that app. The Home page displays components relevant to the user's role. These are three separate customisation surfaces, not one.

CAssign new records to users based on a set of routing criteria

DPrevent records from saving when a field fails a set condition

What is covered on the Salesforce Certified Platform Foundations (Plat-101) exam?

Process Automation AP: Key Concepts

Flow Types and When They Run

chunks.title: Process Automation Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Record-triggered flows run when a record is created, updated, or deleted. A before-save flow can quickly change fields on the record that started it. An after-save flow can update related records, send emails, and run actions. Scheduled paths run later, such as three days after a Case opens. Screen flows guide a user through steps. Schedule-triggered flows process groups of records at set times. Autolaunched flows start from another flow, Apex, or a button. Platform event-triggered flows run when an event occurs.

Reusable and Advanced Flow Patterns

Use subflows to reuse logic in multiple flows. Use collections to work with many records: collect records in a loop, then update them together after the loop. Decision elements send a flow down different paths. An asynchronous path moves slow work, such as an external call, outside the main transaction. Flow Orchestration coordinates a process with several steps and people, such as onboarding. Use clear entry conditions so a flow runs only when needed.

Approvals and Service Targets

Approval processes route records such as discounts or expenses to people who can approve or reject them. Newer Flow approvals can support more flexible routing. In Service Cloud, entitlements and milestones track service targets, such as responding within four hours. Milestone actions can notify or escalate as a deadline approaches. Choose the tool that fits the process instead of putting every task into one flow.

Flow handles many automation needs. Apex may be a better choice for very complex logic, heavy processing across large data sets, or tasks Flow cannot do. When an object has both Apex triggers and flows, learn the order of execution. Before-save flows run before before triggers; after-save flows run after after triggers. Too many automations on one object can be hard to maintain. Organize them by trigger type and use clear entry conditions.

Testing, Debugging, and Deployment

chunks.title: Process Automation Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Use Debug in Flow Builder to step through a flow and inspect values. Flow tests check how record-triggered flows behave and can run before deployment. Add fault paths to elements that may fail, so the flow can log an error or notify someone. Deploy flows with change sets, Salesforce CLI, or DevOps Center, then activate the right version. Older workflow rules and Process Builder processes can be moved to Flow with the Migrate to Flow tool where it helps.

Question 1: A saved Opportunity needs its Region field set from the owner’s country. No other action is needed. Which flow fits?

AA screen flow that asks a user to set Region.

BA before-save record-triggered flow on Opportunity.

CAn after-save flow that updates the same Opportunity.

DA schedule-triggered flow that runs later.

Correct answer: B. A before-save record-triggered flow on Opportunity.

A before-save flow can update the triggering record before it is saved, which fits this requirement.

Screen flows guide users through steps and are not needed for this automatic field update.

This is the best fit for updating a field on the record being saved.

An after-save flow is not needed when only the triggering record must change.

Question 2: When a Case closes, the system must create a Task on the related Account. Which flow should run?

AAn after-save record-triggered flow on Case.

BA before-save flow on Case that edits its fields.

CA schedule-triggered flow that processes Cases later.

DA platform event-triggered flow unrelated to the Case save.

Correct answer: A. An after-save record-triggered flow on Case.

An after-save flow can create a related Task after the Case is saved.

This is the right flow type for creating a related record after the Case closes.

A before-save flow is designed for changes to the Case itself, not creating a related Task.

A schedule-triggered flow is not needed for an action that should happen when the Case closes.

chunks.title: Process Automation Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Question 3: If a Case is still open three days after creation, its owner should get a reminder email. What should the team use?

AA scheduled path in a record-triggered flow.

BA screen flow that the owner must open.

CA manual reminder added to the owner’s calendar.

DA before-save flow that runs only when the Case is created.

Correct answer: A. A scheduled path in a record-triggered flow.

A scheduled path can run three days after the Case is created and send the reminder if it is still open.

This is the automatic option that can run after a set delay.

The team wants an automatic reminder, not a user-run screen flow.

A manual calendar reminder could be missed and does not check Case status.

Question 4: A flow updates 300 Contacts inside a loop and fails during a data load. How should it be changed?

ACollect the Contacts and update them after the loop.

BCreate 300 separate flows, one for each Contact.

CRemove the loop without replacing its processing.

DAdd a Pause element inside the loop.

Correct answer: A. Collect the Contacts and update them after the loop.

Collect records during the loop and update them together afterward to avoid repeated operations.

This bulk-safe pattern handles many records more efficiently.

Hundreds of separate flows would be hard to maintain and do not solve the bulk design issue.

Removing the loop would stop the flow from processing the Contact records.

Question 5: A Create Records step sometimes fails, and users see only a generic error. What should the builder add?

AA fault path to log the error or notify an administrator.

BA Pause element after the Create Records step.

CA Decision element with no outcomes.

DA second Create Records step that repeats the same action.

Correct answer: A. A fault path to log the error or notify an administrator.

A fault path can capture the error and log it or notify someone who can investigate.

This provides a useful response when the Create Records step fails.

A Pause element does not handle or explain the error.

chunks.title: Process Automation Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
A Decision with no outcomes does not provide error handling.

Question 6: Four flows need the same address-checking logic. What is the best design?

ACopy the same logic into all four flows.

BBuild the logic once as a subflow and call it from each flow.

CAsk each user to check every address by hand.

DMove the logic into a validation rule, even if it must return data.

Correct answer: B. Build the logic once as a subflow and call it from each flow.

A subflow lets the team reuse the same address-checking logic in multiple flows.

Copying logic makes updates harder because each copy must be maintained.

This is the reusable design that keeps the logic in one place.

Manual checks are less consistent and do not reuse automation.

Question 7: A flow must call an external system after a record is saved, without making the user wait. What should it use?

AA screen flow started by the user.

BA validation rule on the record.

CA before-save flow that runs before the record is saved.

DAn asynchronous path in the record-triggered flow.

Correct answer: D. An asynchronous path in the record-triggered flow.

An asynchronous path can run the external call after the record save without delaying the user.

A screen flow would require a user to start the action.

Validation Rules check data; they do not call external systems.

A before-save flow runs in the save transaction and is not the right place for this call.

Question 8: Every night at 1 a.m., all overdue open Opportunities should be marked Closed Lost. Which flow fits?

AA screen flow for a sales rep to run.

BA platform event-triggered flow that waits for an event.

CA schedule-triggered flow that checks the Opportunities nightly.

DA before-save flow that runs only when a record changes.

Correct answer: C. A schedule-triggered flow that checks the Opportunities nightly.

A schedule-triggered flow can run at a set time and process records that meet the criteria.

A screen flow requires a user to start it.

No platform event is described as triggering this work.

chunks.title: Process Automation Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
A before-save flow runs when a record is saved, not every night on a schedule.

Question 9: Discounts above 20% need approval from a sales manager and then Finance. Which tool is designed for this?

AA report that lists high-discount deals.

BAn approval process or Flow approval with the required steps.

CA validation rule that blocks all discounts over 20%.

DA before-save flow that changes the discount amount.

Correct answer: B. An approval process or Flow approval with the required steps.

An approval process or Flow approval can route a discount through the required approvers.

A report shows records but does not request approval.

This can send the discount to the sales manager and then Finance.

The company wants review and approval, not a rule that blocks every discount.

Question 10: IT, HR, and a manager each complete onboarding steps over several days. What should coordinate the process?

AA dashboard showing all new hires.

BOne before-save flow that runs when a record is created.

CFlow Orchestration for the steps and people involved.

DA validation rule on the new hire record.

Correct answer: C. Flow Orchestration for the steps and people involved.

Flow Orchestration coordinates multi-step work assigned to different people over time.

A dashboard reports progress but does not coordinate the steps.

A before-save flow is not designed for a long process involving several people.

A Validation Rule checks data but does not coordinate a multi-person process.

Question 11: A support team must respond to Premium customers within four hours and warn managers when time is nearly up. What should it use?

AA Campaign to identify Premium customers.

BA screen flow for agents to track time manually.

CEntitlements with milestone actions.

DA Lead assignment rule for Cases.

Correct answer: C. Entitlements with milestone actions.

Entitlements and milestone actions can track the response target and send a warning as the deadline approaches.

Campaigns are for marketing, not service-level timing.

A manual screen flow does not reliably track elapsed time.

Lead assignment rules route Leads, not Case service deadlines.

chunks.title: Process Automation Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Question 12: A business process requires complex logic across millions of records. What should the architect consider?

AA before-save flow that starts separately for every record.

BBatch Apex for large-volume processing and complex logic.

CA screen flow that asks an admin to approve each record.

DAdding more fields without changing the automation.

Correct answer: B. Batch Apex for large-volume processing and complex logic.

Batch Apex can process large data volumes and handle complex logic that may not fit Flow well.

A record-triggered flow for every record may not be the best design for this volume and logic.

A screen flow requires manual work and is not suitable for millions of records.

Adding fields does not address the processing volume or complex logic.

Question 13: An org still uses old workflow rules and Process Builder processes. What should the team do?

ADelete them all without replacing the automation they provide.

BLeave them unchanged forever, even when they need updates.

CRebuild them as Validation Rules, even if they take actions.

DMove them to Flow, using Migrate to Flow where it helps.

Correct answer: D. Move them to Flow, using Migrate to Flow where it helps.

Salesforce recommends Flow for new automation; the migration tool can help move older processes.

Deleting them without replacement could break business processes.

Leaving them forever may make future changes harder.

Validation Rules check data; they do not replace all automation actions.

Question 14: Before deployment, the team wants to check a record-triggered flow with example records. What should it use?

AA page layout to preview the record.

BA standard email template.

CA dashboard showing flow activity.

DFlow tests and Debug in Flow Builder.

Correct answer: D. Flow tests and Debug in Flow Builder.

Flow tests and Debug help the team check how the flow behaves before deployment.

A page layout changes record display; it does not test flow behavior.

An email template stores message content and does not test a flow.

A dashboard can report data but does not run the flow test.

chunks.title: Process Automation Accredited Professional Study Guide & Practice Questions (Retiring Feb 2027)
chunks.content:
Question 15: A flow should run only when an Account’s Industry changes, but it currently runs on every update. What should be changed?

AAdd more Decision elements later in the flow.

BChange the record-triggered flow into a screen flow.

CSet entry conditions so it runs only when Industry changes.

DAdd a Pause element to delay the flow.

Correct answer: C. Set entry conditions so it runs only when Industry changes.

Tight entry conditions prevent the flow from running when the Industry value has not changed.

Later Decision elements do not prevent the flow from starting on every update.

A screen flow would require a user to start it and would not meet the automatic requirement.

A Pause element delays work but does not check whether Industry changed.

chunks.title: Salesforce Accredited Agentforce 360 for Public Sector Professional (Public Sector AP) Guide
chunks.content:
People and businesses apply for licences and permits, such as food service approval or a building permit. A regulatory authorization type defines a licence or permit and its rules. An application is submitted, often through a public portal, and then reviewed for checks, fees, and approvals. Once approved, the licence record includes an expiry date. Applicants can view the application status online, and renewals can use a similar process.

Grant programs use funding opportunities to describe available funds and eligibility. Organizations submit applications for review and scoring. If approved, an application becomes an award with a budget and conditions. Disbursements record payments, which may depend on milestones or grantee reports. These records help agencies track how public funds are awarded and spent.

Inspections and compliance

Inspectors visit locations to check requirements, such as restaurant hygiene or building safety. A planned visit can include assessment tasks for the inspector to complete, including on a mobile device. The result may pass, fail, or require follow-up. A failed check can create a violation and enforcement action, with another inspection scheduled as needed. The inspection connects to the business and its licence.

Digital service for constituents

People expect to apply, pay, and check progress online. Experience Cloud portals allow constituents to submit applications, provide documents, and follow status. OmniStudio can power the forms: OmniScripts guide users through steps, while Integration Procedures and Data Mappers retrieve and save information. Forms should be accessible and usable on phones. Government Cloud is designed for public sector security standards.

How to prepare for the Public Sector Solutions AP exam

First identify the agency process in the question: licensing, inspection, grants, benefits, or cases. Then select the record or feature that supports that process.

Know the public sector records

Licensing uses authorization types and applications; grants use opportunities, applications, and awards; inspections use visits and assessments.

Follow the grant lifecycle

A funding opportunity leads to an application, review, and award. Disbursements record payments, which may depend on milestones.

Regulatory authorization types define licence rules. Applications pass through review before an issued licence receives an expiry date.

Support constituent self-service

Question 1: A city wants local businesses to apply for food licences online and follow their applications. What should the agency configure?

AA licence application process with an online public form

BA visit for inspectors only

CA funding opportunity for grants

DA separate marketing campaign and landing page for each business

Correct answer: A. A licence application process with an online public form

Licensing and permitting manages applications, review, and issuing licences. A portal lets applicants submit requests and check progress.

Inspection visits are used to check compliance, often after a licence is issued.

Grant opportunities support funding, not licence applications.

Campaigns are marketing records, not a licensing process.

Question 2: Where should an agency define the rules for a particular licence, such as a liquor licence?

BA regulatory authorization type

DA grant funding opportunity record

Correct answer: B. A regulatory authorization type

A regulatory authorization type defines a licence or permit category and its rules.

Dashboards display data but do not define licence rules.

Queues route work to users; they do not define a licence type.

Funding opportunities describe grants.

Question 3: An inspector needs to visit a restaurant and complete a hygiene checklist on a tablet. What should the agency use?

AAn inspection visit with assessment tasks

CA grant application with an attached document checklist

Correct answer: A. An inspection visit with assessment tasks

An inspection visit can include assessment tasks that an inspector completes in the field.

A renewal extends an existing licence.

Grant applications request funding.

Question 4: A restaurant does not pass its hygiene inspection. What is an appropriate next step?

AClose the business account

BRecord a violation and plan a follow-up inspection

CDelete the inspection record and schedule nothing further

DIssue another licence

Correct answer: B. Record a violation and plan a follow-up inspection

A failed assessment can result in a violation and a repeat inspection, linked to the business and its licence.

Closing an account is not how an inspection failure is recorded.

A failed visit should remain in the record for history.

A failed inspection does not justify issuing another licence.

Question 5: A state agency is offering $2 million in community grants. Where should it describe the program and eligibility?

AA funding opportunity

BA benefits enrollment

DA regulatory authorization type

Correct answer: A. A funding opportunity

A funding opportunity describes a grant program, including what is offered and who may apply.

Benefit enrollment is for people receiving benefits.

Inspection visits record compliance checks.

Authorization types define licences and permits.

Question 6: A grant award should be paid in three installments as the recipient meets milestones. Which record supports these payments?

AOne payment made before any milestones

CDisbursements connected to milestones

Correct answer: C. Disbursements connected to milestones

Disbursements record grant payments and can be tied to milestones or reports.

A single advance payment would not represent the requested staged payments.

Violations track failed compliance checks.

Licence renewals are unrelated to grant payments.

Question 7: A review panel must score grant applications before deciding which to fund. What should the agency use?

AA dashboard of applications that each reviewer reads on their own

BA structured application review with reviewers and scores

Correct answer: B. A structured application review with reviewers and scores

The grants process supports application reviews in which assigned reviewers can score submissions.

A dashboard presents information but does not conduct a review.

An inbox does not provide a structured scoring process.

Licence types support licensing, not grant review.

OmniScripts guide a person through steps. Integration Procedures can retrieve data from another system.

Campaigns are used for marketing.

Reports show existing data rather than guiding an intake flow.

A text field cannot guide a multi-step form or retrieve external data.

Question 9: A complaint investigation requires interviews with several people. Which Public Sector Solutions area supports this work?
