chunks.content:
Practice connecting to data, choosing a view, adding filters, creating a simple calculation, and arranging sheets on a dashboard. Use the official exam outline to find any skills you still need to practice.

Tableau Desktop Foundations Exam Format Explained

The exam is proctored online or at a test center. Salesforce lists 40 scored questions, up to five unscored questions, and 70 minutes.

Multiple-choice & multiple-select

How Many Questions Are Scenario-Based?

Questions may describe a small analysis task, such as comparing sales across regions or showing the top products, and ask which Tableau feature fits.

Best Way to Pass on Your First Attempt

Know dimensions and measures: Dimensions describe categories or dates. Measures contain values that Tableau can summarize.

Learn the Marks card: Colour, Size, Label, Detail, and Tooltip control how a view displays its data.

Practice filters and sorting: Filter categories or values, sort by a measure, and choose whether a filter applies to one sheet or several.

Build a small dashboard: Combine sheets, add a filter, and test how a selection in one view affects the others.

Tableau Desktop Foundations: Key Concepts

Connect and prepare data

Tableau Desktop can connect to files, databases, and published data sources. A join combines columns from related tables; a union stacks rows from tables with a similar structure. A live connection queries the source as you work. An extract stores a copy in Tableau’s format and can support faster analysis or offline work. Tableau classifies fields as dimensions, which describe categories, and measures, which contain values to summarize.

Place fields on Rows and Columns to build a view. Show Me suggests charts that fit the selected fields. The Marks card controls how the data appears: use Colour, Size, Label, Detail, or Tooltip to change the marks. Measures are summarized by default, often as a sum, but you can choose another aggregation when needed.

Filter, sort, and group data

chunks.title: Tableau Desktop Foundations (Analytics-101) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Dimension filters keep or remove categories; measure filters keep values that meet a numeric condition. A Top N filter can show the leading products by sales. You can display a filter for viewers and set which sheets it affects. Sort data by a field or value. Groups combine field members, sets save selected members, and hierarchies let viewers move from a broader level to a more detailed one.

A calculated field combines existing fields or values. You can use arithmetic, text and date functions, or IF and CASE logic. Aggregate functions such as SUM and AVG summarize rows for a mark. Table calculations, such as running total or percent of total, work with the values already shown in the view.

Create dashboards and stories

A dashboard places multiple sheets on one canvas. Tiled objects fit into the layout; floating objects can be positioned freely. Dashboard actions make views interactive, for example by filtering one sheet from a selection in another. A story arranges sheets or dashboards into a sequence with captions. You can share finished work by publishing it to Tableau Cloud or Tableau Server.

Foundations exam questions frequently ask which chart best fits a scenario, matching data shape to chart type is the core skill tested.

How to Pass the Tableau Desktop Foundations Exam

These questions focus on everyday Tableau Desktop tasks. Identify what should change in the view or data, then select the feature designed for that task.

Connect and combine data

Joins add related columns; unions add rows from similarly structured tables. Choose a live connection for current source data or an extract when a stored copy better fits the task.

Build and refine views

Use Show Me to explore chart options. Put fields on the Marks card to change how data appears, and choose the right aggregation for a measure.

Use Top N filters for ranked results. Groups combine field members, sets save a selection, and hierarchies support drill-down.

Use calculated fields for new values such as profit margin. Use table calculations for summaries based on marks already in the view.

Tableau Desktop Foundations Practice Questions (With Explanations)

Test your knowledge with these 15 sample questions.

Answered: 0 / 15Correct: 0

Question 1: A sales table and a returns table share an Order ID. You want return details beside each matching sale. Which data operation fits?

AA dashboard action that filters the sales view

BA calculated field that combines the two IDs

CA join that matches the tables on Order ID

DA union that adds the return rows below sales

Correct answer: C. A join that matches the tables on Order ID

A join matches rows on a shared field and brings columns from both tables into the data model.

A dashboard action filters views; it does not combine source tables.

A calculated field creates a value from fields but does not combine tables.

A union stacks rows rather than matching related records.

Question 2: You have several monthly files with the same columns and want their records in one table. What should you use?

AA group to combine category labels

BA set to save selected records

CA union to stack the rows

DA join to match records by a shared field

Correct answer: C. A union to stack the rows

A union stacks rows from similarly structured tables, which fits monthly files with the same columns.

A group combines members of a field, not table rows.

A set saves a selection of members.

A join matches rows across tables and adds columns.

Question 3: How do dimensions and measures usually differ in a Tableau view?

ADimensions are always dates, while measures are always text

BDimensions break data into categories; measures are summarized values

CMeasures create categories, while dimensions are summed

chunks.title: Tableau Desktop Foundations (Analytics-101) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
DBoth types are interchangeable and behave the same way

Correct answer: B. Dimensions break data into categories; measures are summarized values

Dimensions describe categories to compare; measures hold values that Tableau can aggregate.

Dimensions can be text, dates, geographic fields, or other categories.

This reverses the usual roles of dimensions and measures.

The two field types are used differently in views.

Question 4: A scatter plot shows one mark for each region. You want one mark per customer but want to keep the same colours. Where should you place Customer?

AOn the Filters shelf

BOn Detail in the Marks card

COn Colour in the Marks card

DOn Columns beside the region field

Correct answer: B. On Detail in the Marks card

Detail adds information that can split marks without changing their visual colour.

A filter limits which records appear; it does not define the mark detail.

Colour would change the colour encoding.

Columns changes the view structure and may create a different layout.

Question 5: A manager wants to show only the five products with the highest sales. What is the simplest approach?

AUse a Top N filter on Product, ranked by Sales

BHide the other products manually after sorting

CSort the products and leave every product in the view

DFilter Sales above a guessed value

Correct answer: A. Use a Top N filter on Product, ranked by Sales

A Top N filter keeps the leading members based on the selected measure.

Manual hiding must be repeated and may not update as data changes.

Sorting changes order but does not remove the other products.

A guessed threshold may return more or fewer than five products.

Question 6: Dashboard viewers need to choose which Region appears in the view. What should you add?

AA calculated field for every region

BA visible filter control for Region

CA group that contains all regions

DA separate dashboard for each region

Correct answer: B. A visible filter control for Region

A visible filter lets viewers choose the region themselves.

A calculated field is unnecessary for choosing a region.

chunks.title: Tableau Desktop Foundations (Analytics-101) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
A group combines values but does not provide the required viewer control.

Separate dashboards are harder to maintain when a filter can do the job.

Question 7: A Region filter should affect every worksheet that uses the same data source. What should you set?

AApply the filter to all worksheets that use that data source

BCopy the filter to each sheet as a separate field

CPlace the filter on Detail in the Marks card

DConvert the filter into a set

Correct answer: A. Apply the filter to all worksheets that use that data source

A filter can be configured to apply to all worksheets that use the same data source.

Duplicating the filter is harder to maintain and may lead to inconsistent settings.

Detail changes mark granularity; it does not set filter scope.

A set is a saved group of members, not a setting for filter scope.

Question 8: Which calculation returns profit as a share of sales at the level shown in the view?

AUse a Top N filter to rank products by profit and keep the leaders

BUnion a second source table that stores each product’s precomputed profit-to-sales ratio

CGroup the profit values into categories such as low, medium, and high

DDivide aggregated profit by aggregated sales in a calculated field

Correct answer: D. Divide aggregated profit by aggregated sales in a calculated field

The calculation SUM(Profit) / SUM(Sales) returns the ratio using the aggregation level of the current view.

A Top N filter selects ranked members; it does not compute a ratio.

A union stacks rows and does not calculate a ratio for the current view.

A group combines field members instead of calculating a ratio.

Question 9: Several low-volume product categories should appear as one “Other” category. Which feature should you use?

AA set that saves a selection for analysis

BA hierarchy that adds drill-down levels

CA group that combines category members

DAn extract that stores a data copy

Correct answer: C. A group that combines category members

A group combines selected members of a field into one category.

chunks.title: Tableau Desktop Foundations (Analytics-101) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
A set saves a selection but does not merge members into one label.

A hierarchy supports drill-down between levels.

An extract stores data; it does not regroup categories.

Question 10: A source database is slow, and analysts need to work offline while travelling. Which connection type fits?

AAn extract stored in Tableau

BA live connection to the database

CA story made from the current worksheet

DA union of the database tables

Correct answer: A. An extract stored in Tableau

An extract stores a copy of the data in Tableau’s format and can be used offline.

A live connection queries the source and requires access to it.

A story presents views; it does not store the source data.

A union combines rows from tables but does not provide offline access.

Question 11: A user selects a mark in one dashboard sheet, and another sheet should show only related records. What should you configure?

AA data source filter that permanently removes records

BA filter action between the sheets

CA publish command for Tableau Cloud

DA calculated field based on the selected mark

Correct answer: B. A filter action between the sheets

A filter action uses a selection in one view to filter another view.

A dashboard selection should not permanently remove source records.

Publishing shares the workbook but does not create the interaction.

A calculated field is not the dashboard interaction mechanism.

Question 12: You want to guide viewers through a finding in a sequence, with a caption for each step. What should you create?

DA dashboard with floating objects

Correct answer: A. A story

A story presents sheets or dashboards in sequence and can include captions.

A set saves selected field members.

A hierarchy organizes levels for drilling into data.

A dashboard combines views but does not provide the same narrative sequence.

Question 13: Viewers need to drill from Country to State and then City within one view. What should you create?

AThree unrelated worksheets

BA group that combines the countries

CA hierarchy of the geographic fields

DA measure filter on sales

Correct answer: C. A hierarchy of the geographic fields

chunks.title: Tableau Desktop Foundations (Analytics-101) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
A hierarchy lets viewers move through related fields from broad to detailed levels.

Separate sheets do not provide drill-down in one view.

A group combines members instead of creating levels.

A measure filter limits values; it does not create geographic levels.

Question 14: A view shows total sales, but the user needs the average sales value for each order. Which setting should change?

AChange the mark type from bars to lines

BChange the field’s data type to a different kind of value

CRearrange the objects on the dashboard

DChange the measure aggregation from SUM to AVG

Correct answer: D. Change the measure aggregation from SUM to AVG

Switching the measure aggregation from SUM to AVG changes the displayed value from a total to an average.

Mark type changes how data is drawn, not how it is summarized.

The data type defines the kind of value, not the aggregation.

Dashboard layout affects placement, not the value calculation.

Question 15: You select several fields and want Tableau to suggest chart types that fit them. Which feature should you open?

AThe data source page to create an extract

BThe publish dialog to share the workbook

CThe calculation editor to write a formula

DShow Me to review suitable chart types

Correct answer: D. Show Me to review suitable chart types

Show Me suggests chart types based on the selected fields.

The data source page manages connections and data preparation.

The publish dialog shares the workbook.

The calculation editor is for creating fields, not suggesting chart types.

Tableau Server Administrator: concepts to review

Server architecture and processes

Tableau Server uses processes that can run on one or more nodes. VizQL renders views; Application Server handles web requests and API calls; Data Server manages data connections and caching; Backgrounder runs tasks such as refreshes and subscriptions; Data Engine stores and queries Hyper extracts; and Repository (PostgreSQL) stores users, content, and workgroup metadata. A single-node installation runs processes on one machine; a multi-node cluster distributes them for scale and resilience.

Installation, configuration, and TSM

Tableau Services Manager (TSM) provides command-line and web-based administration for Tableau Server. TSM commands change configuration and manage backups and restores. The web interface supports common administrative tasks. Installation requires a supported server, an administrator account, and a product key. Initial setup includes an administrator, authentication mode, and SSL/TLS certificates as needed. Identity stores can be local, Active Directory, or LDAP.

chunks.title: Tableau Server Administrator (Analytics-SA-201) Practice Questions & Study Guide
chunks.content:
Site roles define user capabilities: Creator users can create and publish; Explorers can interact and have limited editing; Viewers can view content. License limits depend on the license agreement. Active Directory group synchronization can automate user provisioning and map groups to site roles. Users may belong to multiple sites with different roles. Monitor licence use and reports to stay within the organization’s entitlements.

Projects, content, and permissions

Projects organize workbooks, data sources, and flows in a hierarchy. Permission capabilities include View, Download, Edit, Publish, Connect, Move, and Delete. Permissions may be allowed, denied, or inherited from a project. Child projects normally inherit from their parent unless configured otherwise. Locked permissions enforce the project’s permission model and prevent content owners from changing permissions on individual items. Design the project structure around governance and business needs.

Monitoring and troubleshooting

Admin Views show server activity such as background tasks, user activity, traffic to views, and disk use. TSM jobs commands help manage background work. Tableau Server logs provide detail about process activity and can help investigate refresh, rendering, and authentication issues. The repository can support advanced usage analysis. Monitor refresh outcomes and investigate common causes such as credentials, network problems, and query timeouts.

TSM is the command-line/API layer for installing, configuring, and managing the Tableau Server topology, it controls which processes (VizQL, Backgrounder, Repository) run on which node.

For the review board, you receive an enterprise scenario, design a solution, and present it to a panel of CTAs. The panel asks detailed questions about the design. What the judges assess

The same skills appear across both stages: cover every stated requirement; explain important choices and alternatives; recognize trade-offs; identify risks and mitigations; and communicate clearly to a business audience. Deep platform knowledge is expected. The assessment focuses on the reasoning built on that knowledge.

Prepare through practice

Use complete scenarios, create a design within a time limit, and present it to people who will interrupt with questions. Follow a consistent outline covering data, security, integration, delivery lifecycle, and licensing. Record yourself and notice where you avoid a clear decision. Mock boards with practising CTAs help prepare for the actual format.

The CTA board is a structured design-and-defend exercise: you receive a complex scenario, prepare an architecture, present it, then defend your decisions under direct questioning from a panel of architects.

How to prepare for the Salesforce Technical Architect assessment

Preparation is about applying architecture knowledge and explaining decisions under pressure. Practise these skills with full scenarios.

Explain each decision

For every component, state the requirement it serves and the alternative you considered.

Name the cost or limitation of each design choice and why you accepted it.

Consider data volume, integration outages, adoption, and governance, then explain how you would mitigate issues.

Connect to business outcomes

Start with what the solution achieves, then explain the design in language stakeholders can follow.

Practise mock boards with people who interrupt and challenge your reasoning; reading alone cannot build this skill.

Technical Architect Evaluation: concepts to prepare

Purpose of the evaluation

The evaluation is a smaller readiness stage before the full review board. It uses a hypothetical company, its goals, systems, and constraints, and one evaluator rather than a panel. Passing lets you book the board. Take it seriously: the ability to understand requirements and defend architecture decisions is tested again at the board.

Read the scenario closely

Separate requirements and constraints—such as residency rules, existing systems, or budget—from background details. A common mistake is designing for an expected problem rather than the one described. List each requirement and check it against your design before presenting so you can show how it is covered.

Build a complete design

A strong design covers the data model, record access, integrations, release approach, and required licences. Prefer standard platform features when they fit. Explain and defend decisions

Technical Architect Review Board: preparation guide

You receive a scenario about a company, including its goals, systems, constraints, and problems. You prepare an architecture, present it to a panel, and answer extended questions. The judges test whether the solution meets the requirements, holds together, and can be defended under pressure. They are evaluating the required areas, not calculating a percentage score.

Design for the stated needs

Address the scenario in front of you. Cover the data model and expected volume, record access for internal and external users, integrations and data direction, release practices, and licences. Prefer standard features where they fit and explain any custom work. Keep the design proportionate: every unnecessary component adds cost and creates another decision to defend.

Present for a mixed audience

Explain the business outcome and solution outline first, then work through a consistent structure. Use diagrams that are readable and easy to discuss. Manage time so you reach each required area, including licensing and release management. Present in terms a business sponsor can follow; communication is part of the assessment.

Expect questions that challenge choices or introduce new complications. For each important decision, know the requirement it supports, the alternative you rejected, and the trade-off you accepted. Common failure patterns

Candidates can miss stated requirements, include components they cannot justify, ignore trade-offs, or run out of time before covering every area. These problems reflect judgement and presentation as much as technical knowledge. A repeatable structure and full mock-board practice help expose them before the assessment.

For each item in the architecture, identify the requirement it serves and the alternative you considered.

Raise risks and mitigations

Explain trade-offs yourself. Acknowledging limits shows that you assessed the design.

Listen to the question and address it directly instead of repeating a prepared answer.

Ask experienced architects to interrupt and question your decisions during rehearsal.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform User Experience Designer (Plat-UX-101 / UX Designer) Practice & Guide
chunks.content:
Is the UX Designer Exam Hard?

The UX Designer exam combines design practice with Salesforce configuration. Prepare for research methods, design thinking, and WCAG alongside SLDS, Lightning App Builder, and Dynamic Forms. Designers may need more platform practice; administrators may need to review research and accessibility.

60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.

65% to pass, which is 39 correct answers out of 60.

Know the five design thinking phases and the work products associated with each one.

Review WCAG 2.1 AA, POUR, and contrast requirements: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

Practice matching a research question to a method and describing what its findings can establish. Also review when Lightning App Builder, Dynamic Forms, or a compact layout addresses a page requirement.

UX Designer Exam Format Explained

The exam is proctored online or at a test center. It combines UX methods with Salesforce design features.

Multiple-choice & multiple-select

How Many Questions Are Scenario-Based?

Many questions present a situation and ask you to choose a research approach, identify an accessibility issue, or select a Salesforce feature that meets a page requirement.

Best Way to Pass on Your First Attempt

Connect each design thinking phase to its output: research informs Empathise, a problem statement supports Define, sketches support Ideate, a model supports Prototype, and user feedback supports Test.

Memorize the WCAG details that appear in practical questions, including contrast, text alternatives, keyboard access, and visible focus.

Use Lightning App Builder to practice placing Dynamic Forms fields, configuring visibility, and editing compact layouts.

Separate methods that explain user behavior, such as interviews and usability tests, from surveys and analytics that measure patterns across a larger group.

UX Designer: Key Concepts

The Five Phases of Design Thinking

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform User Experience Designer (Plat-UX-101 / UX Designer) Practice & Guide
chunks.content:
The five phases are Empathise, Define, Ideate, Prototype, and Test. Empathise gathers evidence through interviews, observation, personas, and journey maps. Define turns that evidence into a focused problem statement or how-might-we question. Ideate generates possible solutions, often with sketches or affinity diagrams. Prototype makes an idea tangible for feedback; Test evaluates it with users and produces findings for the next iteration. The process can move between phases as new evidence appears.

Choosing a Research Method

Choose a research method based on the question. Interviews explore motivations, contextual inquiry observes real tasks, and usability tests uncover where an interface causes difficulty. These qualitative methods help explain why. Surveys and analytics can measure how common a behavior or opinion is. Card sorting helps users group content and informs a proposed information structure; tree testing evaluates whether users can find items in an existing structure.

Wireframes, Prototypes and Handoff

Choose fidelity to match the decision being made. Low-fidelity sketches and wireframes help teams agree on layout before investing in detail. High-fidelity designs communicate final visual treatment. Interactive prototypes help evaluate flows and task completion. Handoff should also describe component states, empty and error cases, validation, and responsive behavior so implementation covers more than the ideal path.

Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 and SLDS

WCAG uses four principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust (POUR). Provide text alternatives, captions, and adequate contrast: at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Make interactions available from a keyboard with visible focus. Use predictable navigation, clear labels, and actionable errors. Valid markup and suitable ARIA names and roles support assistive technology. SLDS components provide an accessible baseline when their intended markup and behavior are preserved.

Lightning App Builder, Dynamic Forms and the Tooling

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform User Experience Designer (Plat-UX-101 / UX Designer) Practice & Guide
chunks.content:
Lightning App Builder arranges components on record pages and can show or hide components based on rules. Dynamic Forms lets admins place individual fields and set field visibility conditions. Dynamic Actions applies similar context rules to actions. Compact layouts determine the highlights panel and mobile preview content. Path guides users through a process with stage-specific fields and guidance. Match the requirement to the feature that controls that part of the page.

SLDS design tokens set base colors/spacing platform-wide. Styling hooks let you override specific CSS custom properties at the component level, without touching or forking the core SLDS stylesheet.

How to Pass the Salesforce UX Designer Exam

This exam asks you to apply design practice inside a platform with fixed components. The design content is mostly recall; the Salesforce content needs an hour in App Builder.

Phases by Their Artefacts

Use the artifact named in a question to identify the relevant phase, and remember that design thinking can loop back when testing reveals a new need.

Review 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text, along with keyboard access, visible focus, and text alternatives.

Qualitative or Quantitative

Use interviews and usability studies to learn why; use surveys and analytics to estimate how many people show a pattern.

Card Sorting Versus Tree Testing

Card sorting helps develop a content structure. Tree testing checks whether people can navigate a structure that already exists.

Dynamic Forms and Visibility Rules

Practice a field visibility rule in Lightning App Builder so you can recognize when Dynamic Forms is the right tool.

Salesforce Certified Platform User Experience Designer Practice Questions (With Explanations)

Test your knowledge with these 15 sample questions.

Answered: 0 / 15Correct: 0

Question 1: A team interviewed users for three weeks and then wrote a problem statement. Which design thinking phase did it finish?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform User Experience Designer (Plat-UX-101 / UX Designer) Practice & Guide
chunks.content:
Correct answer: D. Define

Define turns research findings into a clear problem statement.

Ideate creates possible solutions after the problem is defined.

Test checks a prototype, which has not been made yet.

Empathise is the research phase that came before the problem statement.

Question 2: A designer wants to know whether users can find a policy in the current navigation. Which method should they use?

Correct answer: C. Tree testing

Tree testing checks whether people can find information in an existing structure.

A/B testing compares two versions of something.

A survey asks people what they think; it does not show whether they can navigate.

Card sorting shows how people would group information when designing a structure.

Question 3: Text on a custom component has a contrast ratio of 3.2:1 against its background. Which WCAG 2.1 AA rule does it fail for normal text?

AUnderstandable, because grey is unclear

BPerceivable, because normal text needs at least 4.5:1

CRobust, because grey is not a valid color

DOperable, because the text cannot be clicked

Correct answer: B. Perceivable, because normal text needs at least 4.5:1

Contrast is part of Perceivable. Normal-size text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.

Understandable is about clear, predictable content and behavior.

The stated contrast ratio is below the minimum for normal text.

Robust is about working with assistive technology; Operable is about input and controls.

Question 4: A record page should show the Reason for Discount field only when Discount is above zero. What should the team use?

ADynamic Forms with a field visibility rule

BA compact layout for the record highlights panel

CA new record type for discount requests

DA validation rule on the object

Correct answer: A. Dynamic Forms with a field visibility rule

Dynamic Forms can show or hide a field based on a field value.

Compact layouts control the highlights panel, not field visibility on the form.

A new record type is more than this requirement needs.

Validation Rules check data; they do not hide fields.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform User Experience Designer (Plat-UX-101 / UX Designer) Practice & Guide
chunks.content:
Question 5: A product owner wants to know why users abandon a multi-step form. Which research method can answer this?

AModerated usability testing with a small group

BReviewing page-view analytics

CCounting support tickets

DSending a satisfaction survey to every user

Correct answer: A. Moderated usability testing with a small group

Watching users try the task can show where they stop and why.

Analytics can show that users leave, but usually not why.

Support tickets only include people who report a problem and may not reveal where the form fails.

A survey can collect opinions but may not show the exact point where users get stuck.

Question 6: A dropdown can only be opened with a mouse. Which WCAG principle does this violate?

Correct answer: C. Operable

Operable includes being able to use controls with a keyboard, not just a mouse.

Understandable concerns clear content and predictable behavior.

Perceivable concerns whether people can sense content, such as through text alternatives and contrast.

Robust concerns compatibility with assistive technology.

Question 7: Why are Lightning Design System components usually a good choice for accessibility?

AThey improve performance by reducing every page load time

BThey cannot be customized or extended

CThey remove the need to follow WCAG

DThey include accessible markup, focus handling, and ARIA support

Correct answer: D. They include accessible markup, focus handling, and ARIA support

SLDS components include accessibility features such as suitable markup and focus handling, reducing the work needed to meet accessibility requirements.

Page speed is a separate concern from accessibility.

SLDS components can be themed and extended.

Teams still need to meet WCAG; SLDS helps with that work.

Question 8: A stakeholder wants to agree on the page layout and information order before visual design begins. What should the designer create?

AA written specification only

BLow-fidelity wireframes

CA clickable prototype with final content

DA fully styled high-fidelity mock

Correct answer: B. Low-fidelity wireframes

Low-fidelity wireframes focus the discussion on layout and hierarchy before color and detailed styling.

A written document alone can make it hard to review layout.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform User Experience Designer (Plat-UX-101 / UX Designer) Practice & Guide
chunks.content:
An interactive prototype helps test a flow, which is a later step.

A detailed mock may shift the discussion to color and styling too early.

Question 9: What can card sorting tell a designer?

AWhether a prototype is usable

BHow many users prefer a certain color

CHow users group and label content

DWhether a page meets contrast rules

Correct answer: C. How users group and label content

Card sorting shows how users expect related information to be grouped and labeled.

Usability testing checks whether people can use a prototype.

A survey can measure preferences across many people.

Contrast is checked against accessibility standards, not with card sorting.

Question 10: A long record page overwhelms users, and different teams need different fields. What should the team try?

AUse Dynamic Forms with field visibility rules

BCreate separate custom objects for each team’s fields

CTrain users to scroll through the long page

DRemove fields that some users do not need

Correct answer: A. Use Dynamic Forms with field visibility rules

Dynamic Forms lets the team organize fields and show them only when relevant.

Separate objects would split the data to solve a page-layout problem.

Training does not fix a page that is hard to use.

Removing fields could prevent other teams from doing their work.

Question 11: Which design handoff detail is often missed and can cause implementation problems?

AThe designer’s rationale document

CA list of competitors

DEmpty, loading, and error states

Correct answer: D. Empty, loading, and error states

If a design only shows the normal, completed state, developers may have to guess what to build for empty, loading, or error situations.

The rationale is useful, but missing interface states can directly change what gets built.

Fonts should be specified, but the question asks for a common gap in interface behavior.

Competitor research provides background, not build details.

Question 12: How many participants are often enough for a usability test to find recurring problems?

Correct answer: C. Five to eight

A small group of about five to eight participants can reveal recurring usability problems.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certified Platform User Experience Designer (Plat-UX-101 / UX Designer) Practice & Guide
chunks.content:
One participant may reveal a problem, but cannot show whether it recurs.

A group of 30 to 50 is more typical of a quantitative study.

Hundreds of participants are usually used for surveys or analytics, not a usability test.

Question 13: What do Dynamic Actions control on a Salesforce record page?

ARecord sharing rules

BWhich buttons appear based on the record context

CWhich fields are required

DThe highlights panel at the top of the page

Correct answer: B. Which buttons appear based on the record context

Dynamic Actions show the actions that fit the current record context.

Sharing Rules control access to records.

Field requirements are controlled by field settings or validation logic.

Compact layouts control the highlights panel.

Question 14: A designer wants to measure how many of 4,000 users have the same navigation complaint. Which method fits?

Correct answer: B. A survey

A survey can measure how widespread an opinion or complaint is across a large group.

Usability tests show how a small group behaves and where they struggle.

Contextual inquiry closely observes a small number of people in their work setting.

Card sorting helps design or review how information is grouped.

Question 15: Which statement best describes the design thinking phases?

AThey are iterative, and teams can return to an earlier phase

BThey can happen in any order and all mean the same thing

CThey are optional after the first release

DThey follow a strict order, with each phase completed only once

Correct answer: A. They are iterative, and teams can return to an earlier phase

Design thinking is iterative. Testing can show that a team should redefine the problem or create new ideas.

The phases have different purposes, even though teams may return to earlier phases.

Teams can keep learning and improving after release.

The phases are revisited; they are not a one-way process.

chunks.title: Salesforce Consultant Cert Path (Summer '26): Which Order?
chunks.content:
Download as PNGSave or share this roadmap.

Step 1: Build a Foundation with Administrator (ADM-201)

Consultant exams assume that you understand the Salesforce platform at the ADM-201 level. Before you pursue one, make sure you know objects, fields, automation, security, and reports. Consultant exams build on these topics.

Step 2: Choose a Cloud Specialization

Choose a Salesforce cloud that matches your current work or the area you want to enter. Many consultants focus on the products their employer implements most often. ADM-201 is the foundation for the core cloud exams below, with one exception: Marketing Cloud Engagement Consultant requires Marketing Cloud Engagement Administrator instead.

Sales Cloud Consultant

Covers opportunities, forecasting, territories, and CPQ basics. It is a common consultant certification.

Service Cloud Consultant

Covers cases, entitlements, omnichannel routing, Knowledge, and service contracts.

Experience Cloud Consultant

Covers customer and partner portals, license types, external-user sharing, and Experience Builder.

Field Service Consultant

Covers work orders, service territories, scheduling, and mobile workforce management.

Marketing Cloud Engagement Consultant

Covers discovery, solution design, account setup, business unit strategy, and data design.

Prerequisite exception: this exam requires Marketing Cloud Engagement Administrator, not ADM-201.

Education Cloud Consultant

Covers the EDA data model, student lifecycle, higher education, and FERPA.

Additional Consultant Specialisations

Pardot Specialist / Pardot Consultant: These certifications cover Account Engagement marketing automation. Take Specialist before Consultant. Pardot exam tips

Revenue Cloud Consultant: Covers CPQ, billing, and revenue recognition. CPQ knowledge helps before you take the exam.

Business Analyst: Covers discovery, user stories, and stakeholder management. Its 72% passing score is higher than standard certifications. BA exam tips

Nonprofit Cloud Consultant: Covers the NPSP data model, donor management, and grant tracking for nonprofits.

Health Cloud Consultant: Covers patient and member management, care coordination, and healthcare compliance such as HIPAA.

Common Consultant Certification Pairings

ADM-201 + Sales Cloud + Service Cloud

Email Specialist + Marketing Cloud Consultant + Pardot Specialist

ADM-201 + Sales/Service Cloud + Experience Cloud

Which should you take first?

Take CPQ Administrator if:

You configure Salesforce CPQ, products, pricing rules, quote templates

You implement quote-to-cash processes for clients

You are earlier in your CPQ journey and need the foundational credential

You want the more widely recognised CPQ certification

Take CPQ Billing Accredited Professional if:

You already hold CPQ Administrator and want a specialist extension

Your clients use Salesforce Billing for invoicing and revenue recognition

You work on full Revenue Cloud implementations including billing workflows

You want to differentiate as a Revenue Cloud specialist

Our Recommendation: Start with CPQ Administrator

Start with CPQ Administrator to build your CPQ foundation. CPQ & Billing AP adds Billing topics. After gaining CPQ project experience, consider the AP if your work also involves billing.

Side-by-Side Comparison

How Both Exams Cover the CPQ Pricing Waterfall

List Price → base price from price book, set at product level

Customer / Partner Price → customer-specific or channel partner pricing

Regular Price → after Discount Schedules (volume-based automatic discounts)

Special / Net Price → after manual rep discount and additional discount; final price paid

CPQ Administrator covers scenarios where discount types interact. CPQ & Billing AP tests pricing concepts alongside billing and invoice generation.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between CPQ Administrator and CPQ & Billing AP?

CPQ Administrator is a full certification: $200, 60 questions, 105 minutes, and a 65% pass mark. It tests advanced CPQ setup, including product rules, pricing, quote templates, and contracts. CPQ & Billing AP is an Accredited Professional credential: $150, 40 questions, 60 minutes, and a Pass/Fail result. It covers CPQ plus Salesforce Billing, invoices, payments, and billing amendments. The AP exam is shorter; CPQ Administrator goes deeper into CPQ.

Should I take CPQ Administrator or CPQ & Billing AP first?

The AP has 40 questions and takes 60 minutes, so it may be a quicker starting point if you are new to CPQ or need billing knowledge too. CPQ Administrator tests CPQ in greater depth and may suit a CPQ specialist. Some people take the AP first, then prepare for the full Administrator exam.

chunks.title: CPQ Admin vs CPQ & Billing AP: Which Cert to Take?
chunks.content:
Does CPQ & Billing AP cover the same material as CPQ Administrator?

Both cover CPQ topics such as pricing, product bundles, quotes, and contracts. CPQ Administrator goes further into complex product rules, discount schedules, SBQQ custom actions, and quote template styling. CPQ & Billing AP also covers Billing topics such as invoices and payments.

Which CPQ certification is better for a Revenue Cloud consultant?

CPQ & Billing AP includes both CPQ and Billing, while CPQ Administrator focuses on CPQ. For work that spans the full quote-to-cash process, the broader AP scope may be a closer fit. Both credentials have some exposure to the Revenue Cloud Advanced transition described for 2025–2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between CPQ Administrator and Revenue Cloud Consultant?

CPQ Administrator covers product setup and quoting in Salesforce CPQ, including bundles, pricing rules, discount schedules, quote templates, and contracts. Revenue Cloud Consultant covers more of the quote-to-cash process: CPQ, billing and payment terms, revenue recognition (ASC 606), subscriptions, and the link between CPQ and Salesforce Billing.

Which certification should I take first: CPQ Admin or Revenue Cloud Consultant?

The recommendation here is to take CPQ Administrator first. Revenue Cloud Consultant assumes strong CPQ knowledge, and about 30–40% of its exam overlaps with CPQ product and pricing topics. Candidates often hold CPQ Administrator or have similar project experience. If you work only with quoting, pricing, and contracts, CPQ Admin may be enough. If your work includes billing and revenue recognition, consider Revenue Cloud Consultant next.

What does Salesforce Billing add to CPQ?

Salesforce Billing handles steps after a CPQ order, including invoice creation, payments, billing schedules (annual, monthly, or usage-based), revenue recognition under ASC 606, and financial reports. In this process, CPQ covers the quote and contract; Billing continues from the order through invoicing and payment.

How much overlap is there between CPQ Admin and Revenue Cloud Consultant exams?

chunks.title: CPQ Administrator vs Revenue Cloud Consultant (Summer '26)

The exams overlap by about 30–40%. Both cover CPQ product setup, pricing, bundles, quote templates, and contracts. Revenue Cloud Consultant adds billing schedules, invoices, payments, revenue recognition, billing amendments and renewals, and the Salesforce Billing data model. CPQ knowledge carries over to those shared topics.

What experience is recommended for Revenue Cloud Consultant?

Salesforce recommends at least two years of CPQ implementation experience and exposure to Salesforce Billing projects. You should understand the quote-to-cash process and have configured a CPQ implementation. The exam uses scenarios to test consulting decisions about billing and revenue recognition.

chunks.title: Data Cloud vs CRM Analytics Consultant: Which Cert to Take?
chunks.content:
Which should you take first?

Take Data Cloud Consultant if:

Your projects bring customer data together from several systems

You work with Salesforce CDP, Data Cloud, or real-time activation

You want to build skills in a growing area of Salesforce in 2026

You understand data pipelines and identity resolution concepts

Take CRM Analytics Consultant if:

You build dashboards, query data with SAQL, or create Einstein Discovery models

Your work focuses on Salesforce analytics and reporting

You regularly use Tableau CRM or Einstein Analytics

You work as a BI or data analyst in a Salesforce organization

Our Recommendation: Start with Data Cloud Consultant

Choose Data Cloud if your projects center on joining and activating customer data or supporting AI use cases. Choose CRM Analytics if your work is to build dashboards, reports, and predictions from Salesforce data. The product you use at work is a strong guide to which exam to take first.

Side-by-Side Comparison

Which Should You Take?

Choose Data Cloud Consultant when your projects connect customer data across systems or activate it for Marketing Cloud, AI, or Agentforce.

Choose CRM Analytics Consultant when you build dashboards, bring business intelligence into sales workflows, or use Einstein Discovery for predictions.

If you are unsure, compare the projects available to you. Data Cloud has a stronger role in 2026 AI and personalization work; CRM Analytics fits reporting and analytics work.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between Data Cloud and CRM Analytics in Salesforce?

Salesforce Data Cloud (formerly Customer Data Platform) brings customer data from different sources together in a unified profile. It focuses on data ingestion, identity resolution, segmentation, and activation. CRM Analytics (formerly Einstein Analytics / Tableau CRM) helps teams explore Salesforce data with dashboards, reports, and AI predictions. Data Cloud prepares and activates data; CRM Analytics analyzes and presents it.

Which is more valuable: Data Cloud Consultant or CRM Analytics Consultant?

chunks.title: Data Cloud vs CRM Analytics Consultant: Which Cert to Take?
chunks.content:
Data Cloud Consultant has higher demand in 2026 as companies focus on AI and unified customer data. Data Cloud supports Agentforce, Einstein AI, and Marketing Cloud Personalisation, so it is part of many enterprise Salesforce strategies. CRM Analytics Consultant is useful in analytics-focused roles and industries with strong business intelligence needs. If you work on data strategy or AI activation, consider Data Cloud first.

Do Data Cloud and CRM Analytics overlap?

Both certifications involve data, and Data Cloud data can feed CRM Analytics dashboards. Their exam topics differ. Data Cloud Consultant covers data streams, identity resolution, segmentation, calculated insights, and unified data models. CRM Analytics Consultant covers datasets, recipes, dashboards, lenses, SAQL queries, and Einstein Discovery predictions.

Is Data Cloud Consultant harder than CRM Analytics Consultant?

Both exams have 60 questions, 105 minutes, a 65% passing score, and a $200 fee. Some candidates find Data Cloud more conceptually challenging because its technology is newer and its architecture topics, such as identity resolution, streaming ingestion, and calculated insights, may be unfamiliar. CRM Analytics can be challenging because it requires hands-on work with SAQL queries and recipe-level data transformations.

chunks.title: Salesforce Developer Cert Path (Summer '26): Which First?
chunks.content:
Download as PNGSave or share this roadmap.

Start Here: Which Cert Based on Your Experience

Salesforce Platform Developer I (PD1)

PD1 is the starting point for Salesforce developer certifications. It covers Apex fundamentals, SOQL and DML, governor limits, trigger best practices, and basic LWC skills. You need PD1 before taking PD2, and many senior developer roles require it.

Salesforce JavaScript Developer I

JavaScript Developer I covers modern JavaScript skills, including ES6+, asynchronous patterns, Jest testing, and debugging. It may be useful if you build LWC-heavy apps or want a senior UI developer role. Take it alongside or after PD1; JavaScript knowledge supports LWC study.

Salesforce Platform Developer II (PD2)

PD2 is a respected developer credential and a prerequisite for the architect track. It covers advanced Apex patterns, REST and SOAP integrations, performance, and enterprise design patterns such as trigger frameworks and selector, domain, and service layers. Most candidates need project experience as well as study before this exam.

Integration Architect

Integration Architect demonstrates advanced integration skills and is part of the path toward Certified Technical Architect (CTA). It covers integration patterns, security protocols, performance, and MuleSoft and middleware decisions. It may suit developers moving into technical lead or architect roles.

Our editorial standards

Use official Salesforce certification pages and exam guides as the primary source for exam names, costs, durations, question counts, and section weightage.

Flag older certification names and aliases such as ADM-201 or Pardot while also using the current official Salesforce naming where relevant.

Write original practice questions from public objectives and common implementation scenarios, not from leaked or memorized exam content.

Add visible official-source references on certification pages so readers can verify the latest exam guide before booking.

Review every certification page each release cycle, and re-check exam facts against the issuer’s current exam guide before republishing.

Primary sources: We use Salesforce certification pages, exam guides, pricing pages, and release documentation as primary sources.

Secondary context: For context, we may use candidate feedback, implementation experience, public Trailhead learning paths, and Search Console query data.

Not accepted: We do not use braindumps, leaked exams, memory-based real exam questions, or copied copyrighted question banks.

Corrections and update process

Exam details can change when Salesforce updates guides, retires or renames credentials, or changes prices. When we find a mismatch, we check the official source and update the related page details, FAQ, schema, and internal cards.

To report an issue, use the contact form with the Trailblaze Prep URL and the official source you used.

chunks.title: How to Become a Salesforce Administrator (Summer '26 Guide)
chunks.content:
Avg Entry Salary (US)

Prerequisites Required

Step-by-Step: From Zero to Salesforce Admin

Create a Free Salesforce Developer Edition Org

Visit developer.salesforce.com/signup and create a free Developer Edition org. Use this Salesforce environment to try the tasks you study for the ADM-201 exam. Practice configuring the platform as you learn; reading about a feature alone may not prepare you to recognize how it works in a scenario.

Complete Salesforce Trailhead Admin Trails (Free)

Trailhead (trailhead.salesforce.com) is Salesforce’s free learning platform. Start with the “Admin Beginner” trail, continue to “Admin Intermediate,” then complete “Prepare for Your Salesforce Administrator Credential.” The modules cover ADM-201 topics and include exercises in a Trailhead Playground org.

Study the 7 ADM-201 Exam Sections by Weight

The ADM-201 exam has 8 sections. Use their weights to plan your study time. Data and Analytics Management is 17%; Configuration and Setup, Object Manager and Lightning App Builder, and Automation are 15% each. Together, those four sections make up 62% of the exam. Sales and Marketing, Service and Support, and Productivity and Collaboration are 10% each; Agentforce is 8%.

Practice With Scenario-Based Mock Questions

ADM-201 asks you to apply Salesforce knowledge to business situations, such as choosing what an administrator should do to meet a company’s needs. Practice answering scenario questions with a time limit. Use practice tests to find gaps, then review those topics in Trailhead or your org. Aim for 75%+ on 3 full mock exams before booking. Try the free ADM-201 practice test to check your readiness.

Book and Pass the ADM-201 Exam

Register through Trailhead Academy (trailheadacademy.salesforce.com). Choose an online proctored exam at home, delivered via Pearson VUE (OnVUE) and requiring a webcam, quiet room, and verified ID, or book at a test center. The exam has 60 scored questions plus up to five unscored questions, lasts 105 minutes, and requires a 68% passing score. You see the result after submitting. If you do not pass, you can retake after 1 day for $100.

Build a Portfolio and Apply for Roles

chunks.title: How to Become a Salesforce Administrator (Summer '26 Guide)
chunks.content:
After passing ADM-201, create a portfolio in a Developer Edition org with examples such as custom objects, flows, and reports. Meet other professionals through the Trailblazer Community, local user groups, and LinkedIn groups. Add your certification badge to LinkedIn and apply for “Junior Salesforce Administrator” and “Salesforce Administrator” roles. “Salesforce Support Analyst” can also be an entry role. Choose a next certification, such as App Builder or Service Cloud Consultant, when it supports your goals.

Who Becomes a Salesforce Administrator?

People move into Salesforce administration from many fields, including work outside IT. These backgrounds can provide useful experience:

Use this free official platform to complete the “Admin Beginner” and “Admin Intermediate” trails. The lessons include hands-on challenges and cover exam topics. It is a good place to begin.

Developer Edition Org

Create a free Salesforce environment at developer.salesforce.com/signup. Try each feature as you study so you can see how it works in practice.

Salesforce Help Documentation

Salesforce Help is free. When Trailhead introduces a topic, use the related Help article to learn more. This is useful for the sharing model (OWD and sharing rules) and Flow Builder.

Free Practice Questions

Use scenario-based tests to find topics that need more study. Try our free Salesforce Administrator practice questions, aligned with the Summer '26 exam weights.

Salesforce Trailblazer Community

Visit trailblazers.salesforce.com to ask questions, find a study group, and meet other candidates. The “Certification” group includes discussions about ADM-201 preparation.

Career Path After ADM-201

After ADM-201, choose a next step that matches the work you want to do:

Advanced Administrator

Sales Cloud Consultant

Service Cloud Consultant

Experience Cloud Consultant

Platform Developer I (PD1)

Platform Developer II (PD2)

Common Mistakes That Cause First-Time Failures

Studying theory without practice. Read about OWD settings, then configure them and check access with a second user. Try the features in your org as part of your study routine.

Skipping the security model. Review OWD settings, role hierarchy, profiles, permission sets, and sharing rules. Remember the difference: roles control record visibility, while profiles control object access. Both are tested.

chunks.title: How to Become a Salesforce Administrator (Summer '26 Guide)
chunks.content:
Booking before you are ready. Aim for 75%+ on 3 full mock exams. The 68% passing score may seem manageable, but exam scenarios can be challenging. Some candidates score 65–67%, just below passing, when they book too early.

Skipping lower-weight sections. Productivity and Collaboration is 10%, or about six questions. Review every section, then use the final week for a broad recap.

When Are You Ready to Book?

80%+ on 3 timed full mocks (60 scored questions / 105 min) on separate days

Once you meet this benchmark consistently, book the exam for 3–5 days later so the material is still fresh. If you are below the benchmark, use your mock results to identify the weakest sections and spend another week reviewing those topics.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take to become a Salesforce Administrator?

Plan for 8–12 weeks of part-time study (10–15 hours per week) if you are new to Salesforce. Prior CRM or database experience may shorten preparation to 4–6 weeks. The exam takes 105 minutes. After certification, many candidates spend 1–3 months looking for their first Salesforce Admin role.

What qualifications do I need to become a Salesforce Administrator?

There are no formal education prerequisites for the Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201) exam. You do not need a computer science degree, Salesforce experience, or another certification. You need to pass the exam (68% score), find study resources, and use a Salesforce Developer Edition org for hands-on practice. Admins come from business, sales, marketing, and other non-technical fields.

Is Salesforce administration a good career in 2026?

Salesforce Administrator can be an entry point to a technology career in 2026. Salesforce has over 150,000 customers globally and reports more demand for certified professionals than available supply. Entry-level Salesforce admins typically earn $60,000–$80,000 USD, while experienced admins with multiple certifications earn $90,000–$130,000. Admin experience can also lead toward consulting, architecture, or development.

Can I learn Salesforce for free?

chunks.title: How to Become a Salesforce Administrator (Summer '26 Guide)
chunks.content:
Yes. Trailhead (trailhead.salesforce.com), Salesforce’s official learning platform, offers free modules and guided projects. A Salesforce Developer Edition org is also free and gives you a place to practice. The ADM-201 exam costs $200, and retakes cost $100.

What comes after Salesforce Administrator?

After ADM-201, you could pursue Platform App Builder to build custom apps, Advanced Administrator for deeper admin skills, or Salesforce Business Analyst. Sales Cloud Consultant and Service Cloud Consultant are options for admins moving into consulting. Platform Developer I (PD1) suits people interested in development. The architect track starts with Application Architect.

The Architect Path: Stage by Stage

Study cannot replace implementation experience. Application Architect (4 Certs, Auto-Awarded)

Complete the four Application Architect components, either one at a time or in parallel: Platform App Builder, Platform Developer I (covered in the Foundation stage), Data Architect, and Sharing and Visibility Architect. Salesforce awards the credential after you pass all four; there is no separate Application Architect exam.

Platform App Builder (already completed)

Platform Developer I (already completed)

Sharing and Visibility Architect

System Architect (4 Component Certs, No Exam of Its Own)

System Architect covers infrastructure and integration topics, including API design, identity and access management (SSO, OAuth, SAML), and release management. Platform Developer I is the only component shared with Application Architect. The other three components are Integration Architect, IAM Architect, and Dev Lifecycle Architect. Salesforce grants the credential once you hold all four; there is no additional System Architect exam.

chunks.title: How to Become a Salesforce Architect (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Once you hold both Application and System Architect credentials, you can attempt the CTA evaluation. Prepare by studying architecture decision frameworks, practicing whiteboard diagrams, and taking part in mock board reviews. At the CTA Board Review, you will need to design an enterprise Salesforce architecture and explain it to senior architects.

CTA Board Review (live presentation to architect panel)

Salesforce Architect Salary (Summer '26)

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take to become a Salesforce Architect?

After PD1, earning the Application Architect credential (4 individual architect certs) often takes 2–4 years. The full CTA path, including Application Architect, System Architect, and CTA evaluation, takes 4–8 years for many candidates. The CTA Board Review is one of the most demanding credential processes in enterprise software. Successful candidates often have 8–12 years of Salesforce experience and have led several large enterprise implementations.

What certifications are required for Salesforce Application Architect?

Pass all four component certifications: Platform App Builder, Platform Developer I, Data Architect, and Sharing and Visibility Architect. Salesforce awards the Application Architect credential when you hold all four. There is no separate Application Architect exam.

What certifications are required for Salesforce System Architect?

You need Platform Developer I, Integration Architect, Identity and Access Management Architect, and Dev Lifecycle and Deployment Architect. There is no separate System Architect exam; Salesforce grants the credential when you hold all four. Platform Developer I is the only exam shared with Application Architect.

What is the CTA Board Review?

The Certified Technical Architect (CTA) Board Review is a live presentation, in person or virtual, to a panel of senior Salesforce architects. Candidates receive a complex business scenario and present an architecture solution. They use whiteboard diagrams, explain their design choices, and answer questions from the panel. The result is pass or fail, and many candidates attempt the review more than once.

What is the Salesforce architect salary in 2026?

chunks.title: How to Become a Salesforce Architect (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Application Architects typically earn $130,000–$160,000 USD. System Architects and CTAs earn $160,000–$200,000+. CTAs are among the highest-paid Salesforce professionals, and there are fewer than 1,000 worldwide as of 2026. Contract architects typically earn $150–$250 per hour, depending on specialization and location.

Earn Your ADM-201 First

It covers objects, fields, the data model, security (profiles, roles, and sharing rules), automation (Flow; Process Builder reached end of support in December 2025 and is replaced by Flow), reports, dashboards, and data management. Experience Cloud, Data Cloud, and Field Service can support higher-value projects. Marketing Cloud, which requires Email Specialist as a prerequisite, can lead to marketing technology work.

Sales Cloud Consultant, highest demand, broadest job market

Service Cloud Consultant, contact centre and support operations focus

Experience Cloud Consultant, digital portals and communities focus

How long does it take to become a Salesforce Consultant?

Plan for 6–12 months to move from no Salesforce experience to your first consultant role. The path includes ADM-201 (8–12 weeks) and a first consultant specialization (8–12 weeks). Finding a role may take another 1–3 months after certification. Prior experience in CRM, sales operations, or service operations can help you prepare faster.

What is the difference between a Salesforce Administrator and a Salesforce Consultant?

An Administrator manages and configures Salesforce within their own organization. A Consultant works with clients to gather requirements, design and configure solutions, train users, and manage launch. Consultants often work for implementation partners or consulting firms, and their roles are usually client-facing and project-based.

Which consultant certification should I take first: Sales Cloud or Service Cloud?

Choose based on your experience. Sales operations, CRM, or revenue operations experience may fit Sales Cloud Consultant. Customer support, contact centre, or service operations experience may fit Service Cloud Consultant. Both exams have 60 questions, take 105 minutes, and cost $200. The passing scores are 73% for Sales Cloud and 78% for Service Cloud. Both assume ADM-201 knowledge, and many consultants eventually earn both credentials.

Do I need project experience before the consultant exam?

Only a few consultant certifications have formal prerequisites, but hands-on project experience can help you on the exam. Consultant exams use scenarios that describe a business need and ask how to configure Salesforce to meet it. Candidates who have worked on a Sales Cloud or Service Cloud implementation may find these questions easier to understand than those who have only studied the theory.

Step-by-Step Developer Path

Learn Salesforce Platform Basics

Learn how the Salesforce platform works before you write Apex. Start with Trailhead and the Salesforce Fundamentals trail, which covers objects, fields, the data model, security (profiles, roles, and sharing), and basic automation. Create a free Salesforce Developer Edition org to practice along the way.

Salesforce Platform Basics (Trailhead)

Data Modeling trail (Trailhead)

Free Salesforce Developer Edition org

Learn Apex Fundamentals

Apex is Salesforce's Java-like programming language. Learn its syntax, data types, collections (List, Set, Map), SOQL and SOSL, triggers (before/after, insert/update/delete), classes, exception handling, and governor limits. Also study the 75% code coverage requirement for deployment. Practice writing triggers and classes in your Developer Edition org.

Apex Basics & Database trail (Trailhead)

Apex Developer Guide (Salesforce docs)

Trigger Fundamentals trail

Learn Lightning Web Components (LWC)

Lightning Web Components (LWC) is Salesforce's front-end framework built on web standards. Build your JavaScript (ES6+) skills first. Then learn component structure (HTML template, JS controller, CSS), data binding, event handling (@api, @track, and @wire decorators), calling Apex from LWC, and deploying components with SFDX. JavaScript Developer I can complement this study.

JavaScript Skills for Salesforce Developers (Trailhead)

Lightning Web Components Basics (Trailhead)

LWC Dev Guide (developer.salesforce.com)

Study Platform Developer I (PD1) Exam

Once you know Apex and LWC, prepare for the PD1 exam sections: Developer Fundamentals (27%), Process Automation and Logic (28%), User Interface (25%), and Testing, Debugging, and Deployment (20%). Use practice questions to find weak areas and aim for at least 75% on mock exams before scheduling.

Trailblaze Prep PD1 practice questions (free)

Get Project Experience

Certification can help you get noticed, but project experience also matters. Gain experience through pro bono work with Salesforce.org Nonprofit, open-source projects, or Salesforce implementations at your current employer. Document your work in a GitHub portfolio; employers may review code samples along with certifications.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take to become a Salesforce Developer?

Plan for 6–12 months to go from no Salesforce experience to PD1 certification and job readiness. The technical path is steeper than the admin path: Apex is similar to Java, and Lightning Web Components requires JavaScript skills. People with experience in Java, C#, Python, or JavaScript may prepare for PD1 in 12–16 weeks of focused study. Beginners may need 6–9 months.

Do I need to know programming before becoming a Salesforce Developer?

Programming experience helps, but it is not required. Salesforce recommends taking ADM-201 before PD1 so you understand the platform, data model, and security before writing Apex. If you are new to programming, allow extra time to learn Apex basics. JavaScript is also important for Lightning Web Components.

What is the Salesforce Platform Developer I (PD1) certification?

PD1 (Platform Developer I, exam DEV-450) is the core Salesforce developer certification. It covers Apex triggers and classes, SOQL and SOSL, governor limits, Lightning Web Components (LWC), Visualforce basics, testing (Test.startTest/stopTest and assert methods), and deployment (change sets and SFDX). The exam has 60 questions, lasts 105 minutes, has a 68% passing score, and costs $200.

What is the Salesforce developer salary in 2026?

Entry-level Salesforce Developers with PD1 and 0–2 years of experience typically earn $75,000–$100,000 USD. Mid-level developers with PD1 and PD2 and 2–5 years of experience earn $100,000–$140,000. Senior developers and architects earn $140,000–$180,000+. Contract developers typically earn $85–$130 per hour. Pay varies by location; US tech hubs pay 20–40% above national averages.

What comes after Platform Developer I?

After PD1, common next steps include Platform Developer II (PD2), which covers advanced Apex, integration architecture, and performance; JavaScript Developer I, which focuses on JavaScript and LWC skills; or the architect path, starting with Integration Architect or Data Architect. The architect path assumes strong PD1 knowledge. Many developers also earn admin-track credentials such as App Builder or Advanced Administrator.

chunks.title: How to Register for a Salesforce Certification Exam (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 14 November 2026

A complete step-by-step guide to booking your Salesforce exam: Trailhead Academy registration, exam format selection, identity requirements, and exam day preparation.

Step-by-Step Registration Guide

Sign in to Trailhead Academy

Go to trailheadacademy.salesforce.com and sign in with your Trailhead account, or create a free one if you don't have it yet. Make sure your name matches your government-issued photo ID exactly, to avoid problems on exam day, and use an email address you check often for confirmations and reminders.

Find your target exam

From your Trailhead Academy dashboard, search for your certification, such as Administrator or Platform Developer I. Check that you choose the right exam; some certifications have similarly named options, such as maintenance and initial certification.

Choose an exam format

Choose Online Proctored to take the exam at home or a Testing Centre to take it in person. Online exams require a webcam and a quiet room. Both formats use the same exam content, passing score, and result rules.

Select your date and time

Choose an available appointment that leaves enough time to study. Testing-centre availability depends on location. Book early if you want a wider choice of slots.

Pay by credit or debit card. If you have a voucher code, such as a retake discount or event voucher, enter it at checkout to adjust the fee. Keep your payment and exam confirmation emails.

For an online exam, run Pearson VUE’s OnVUE system check and prepare a quiet, private room. Have a valid government-issued photo ID that matches your booking. At a testing centre, arrive early and follow the confirmation instructions. Personal items are not allowed in the exam room.

Online Proctored Exam

✓ Take it at home or at work

✓ More flexible scheduling

✗ You need a webcam and microphone

✗ You need a private room without other people or pets

✗ Technical problems may interrupt the exam

✓ The centre provides the equipment

✓ The exam room is controlled and quiet

✓ Your own equipment cannot cause technical issues

✗ You must travel to the centre

chunks.title: How to Register for a Salesforce Certification Exam (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
✗ Appointment times may be less flexible

✗ A centre may not be available nearby

Common Registration Mistakes to Avoid

⚠ Name mismatch: Your Trailhead Academy account name must exactly match your ID. A difference in your middle name may cause a problem.

⚠ Registering through a third-party site: Book only through trailheadacademy.salesforce.com. Third-party "registration help" sites are not official.

⚠ Skipping the system check: Run Pearson VUE's OnVUE system check at least 24 hours before an online exam.

⚠ Assuming every retake is discounted: Check the current retake price for your credential. Foundations retakes are free, while Accredited Professional retakes cost the same as the first attempt.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where do I register for a Salesforce certification exam?

Register through Trailhead Academy (trailheadacademy.salesforce.com). Sign in with your Trailblazer account, find your exam, and book either an online-proctored session through Pearson VUE OnVUE or an onsite appointment at a Pearson VUE testing centre.

Can I take a Salesforce exam online from home?

Yes. Salesforce offers online-proctored exams through Pearson VUE OnVUE, booked via Trailhead Academy. You take the exam on your computer with a webcam while the system checks your identity and exam environment. You need a quiet, private room, a working webcam and microphone, a stable internet connection, and government-issued photo ID. Check Trailhead Academy for available appointment times.

What ID do I need for a Salesforce exam?

Bring a valid, government-issued photo ID with a name that exactly matches your Trailhead Academy account. Accepted IDs include a passport, national ID card, or driving licence. A mismatch may prevent you from taking the exam. For an online proctored exam, you will show your ID to the webcam during identity checks.

How far in advance should I book my Salesforce exam?

Book early if you want a broader choice of date, time, and format. Appointment availability varies by location and delivery type. Review Salesforce’s reschedule and cancellation rules before booking: online appointments require at least 24 hours’ notice, and onsite appointments require at least 48 hours’ notice for free changes.

Can I reschedule or cancel my Salesforce exam?

chunks.title: How to Register for a Salesforce Certification Exam (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Yes. Salesforce requires at least 24 hours’ notice for online-proctored exams and 48 hours’ notice for testing-centre exams. Changes made within those windows may result in the loss of your exam fee. See the current Salesforce reschedule and cancellation policy for exceptions and CTA-specific rules.

chunks.title: How to Study for a Salesforce Certification (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 6 November 2026

Build a study plan for your Salesforce exam. Learn how to combine Trailhead, hands-on practice, and mock exams, and how to avoid common study mistakes.

The Three-Pillar Study Method

1. Read and review concepts

Use Trailhead trails, the official exam guide, and release notes to learn how the features work.

Configure features in a Developer Edition org or Trailhead Playground instead of only reading about them.

3. Answer practice questions

Try scenario-based questions under exam conditions. Read explanations for correct and incorrect answers.

Step-by-Step Study Process

Get the official exam guide

Salesforce provides a free exam guide for each certification. It lists topic areas, their weighting, and recommended experience. Use it to plan what to study.

Match Trailhead content to exam topics

Find a Trailhead trail or module for each exam section. Many certifications have a "Prepare for Certification" section. Start with the topics that carry the most weight.

Practice each feature in a sandbox

Try the tasks you read about in a free Trailhead Playground or Developer Edition org. For example, if the exam covers validation rules, create some yourself.

Use practice questions while you study

After reviewing a section, answer untimed questions about it and read every explanation. Review both the answers you got right and those you missed.

Take full timed mock exams

In the final 1–2 weeks, take full mock exams with the same number of questions and time limit as the real test. Aim for 75% or higher on several mock exams before booking.

Set a date that gives you time to prepare. A scheduled exam can help you stay on track, but leave enough time for review.

The 5 Most Common Study Mistakes

⚠ Using only Trailhead: Reading helps you learn features, but practice questions also help you apply what you know.

⚠ Skipping sandbox practice: Try the features yourself instead of only reading about them.

⚠ Cramming the day before: Spread your study across several weeks so you can practice applying the material.

chunks.title: How to Study for a Salesforce Certification (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
⚠ Booking before you are ready: If you score below 65% on practice tests, spend more time studying. Aim for 75% or higher consistently before booking.

⚠ Ignoring low-weight topics: A 10% exam section may still contribute 5–6 questions. Review every section.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take to study for the Salesforce Administrator exam?

Most candidates prepare for the Administrator exam over 2–4 months, studying 8–15 hours a week. Your timeline depends on your experience: people who use Salesforce every day may need 4–6 weeks, while beginners may need 3–4 months. The exam covers many platform topics, so include hands-on practice in your plan.

Is Trailhead enough to pass a Salesforce certification exam?

Trailhead is useful for learning concepts, but it may not give you enough practice applying them to exam scenarios. Combine Trailhead (30–40% of study time), hands-on sandbox practice (30–40%), and practice questions (20–30%). Candidates who only read Trailhead material may know the features but struggle with scenario questions.

What is the most effective study method for Salesforce certifications?

Combine three methods: read Trailhead material and the official exam guide, practice tasks in a sandbox, and answer scenario-based questions. Hands-on work helps you apply what you read. A regular 60–90 minute study session each day is more useful than cramming.

How should I use practice questions effectively?

Use practice questions in two ways. First, work untimed and read the explanation for every answer. Then take full-length timed mock exams. For each wrong answer, learn why the right option is correct and why the other options are not. Aim for at least 75% on several full mock exams before booking.

Should I buy a paid study course for Salesforce certification?

Paid courses from providers such as Focus on Force, Udemy, and Salesforce Trailhead Academy can provide structure, but they are not required. Many candidates study with free Trailhead content, a free Developer Edition or Trailhead Playground, and practice questions. A paid course may help if you prefer a guided plan. Choose one with scenario-based practice similar to the exam.
