chunks.title: Integration vs System Architect: Salesforce Cert Comparison
chunks.content:
Which should you take first?

Take Integration Architect if:

Your projects involve API design, middleware, or enterprise integrations

You want to focus on integration before deciding on the full CTA path

You want a specialist credential for integration work

Your clients connect Salesforce with several other systems

Take System Architect if:

You plan to pursue the full Certified Technical Architect path

You already hold two or more domain architect credentials

You have 8+ years of Salesforce experience across multiple orgs

You are ready to complete the System Architect track

Our Recommendation: Start with Integration Architect

Integration Architect is a standalone exam for professionals who design system connections. System Architect represents completion of a broader group of exams in the CTA path. Start with Integration Architect if integration work is your goal; pursue System Architect when you are progressing through the full track.

Side-by-Side Comparison

Integration Architect: Core Topics to Master

Integration patterns: Request/reply, fire-and-forget, batch sync, and publish/subscribe with Platform Events or Change Data Capture. Be able to choose between synchronous and asynchronous designs.

API management: MuleSoft API-led connectivity (System, Process, and Experience API layers), Salesforce Connect for external objects, concurrent and daily API limits, and API versioning.

Data migration: Select Apex Data Loader, Data Import Wizard, or an ETL tool for the data volume. Plan the order for related objects, prevent duplicates, and validate the results after migration.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between Salesforce Integration Architect and System Architect?

Integration Architect is a specialist exam about enterprise integrations. It covers synchronous and asynchronous patterns, API management with MuleSoft, middleware choices, data migration, and Salesforce governor limits in integration scenarios. System Architect is a milestone in the CTA path. It recognizes completion of Integration Architect, Identity & Access Management Architect, and Dev Lifecycle & Deployment Architect.

Do I need Integration Architect before System Architect?

chunks.title: Integration vs System Architect: Salesforce Cert Comparison
chunks.content:
Yes, Integration Architect is one of three component exams for System Architect, along with Identity & Access Management Architect and Dev Lifecycle & Deployment Architect. Pass all three to earn the System Architect credential. Integration Architect can also be pursued on its own and counts toward the System Architect and CTA path.

Which is harder: Integration Architect or the other System Architect track exams?

Integration Architect is often considered the hardest of the three System Architect exams. It requires knowledge of enterprise integration patterns, API design, middleware and ESB selection, MuleSoft Anypoint Platform, and Salesforce integration limits such as concurrent API calls, streaming API limits, and batch size constraints. Identity & Access Management Architect is also challenging; Dev Lifecycle & Deployment Architect is generally considered more approachable.

How many architect exams are in the full CTA path?

The CTA pathway includes 6 architect-level exams across two tracks. Application Architect track (4 exams): Data Architect, Sharing & Visibility Architect, Platform App Builder, and the Application Architect credential exam. System Architect track (4 exams): Integration Architect, Identity & Access Management Architect, Dev Lifecycle & Deployment Architect, and the System Architect credential exam. After both tracks, you sit the CTA Evaluation Exam ($400) and, if successful, the CTA Review Board ($3,000).

Decision Matrix: Integration Architect or System Architect?

A practical look at the time and cost involved, the potential career benefits, and who may benefit most from certification.

Short answer: Yes, for most people

A certification can help show employers what you know, but its value depends on your experience, target role, and ability to apply the skills. A $200 exam fee and 8–12 weeks of study may support a $15,000–$30,000 salary increase. Salesforce has 150,000+ customers globally and reports more job openings than certified professionals to fill them.

The Numbers: Salary Impact by Role

Salary ranges are US national averages (Summer '26). Varies by location, company size, and experience.

Certification IS worth it if…

You are entering the Salesforce ecosystem or changing careers

You use Salesforce at work and want to demonstrate your skills

You want to move from an internal admin role into consulting

Your employer reimburses exam fees (common at Salesforce partners)

You are moving from a developer role toward architecture

You want to explore a career in a high-demand technology field

Certification is LESS worth it if…

✗You have 10+ years of Salesforce experience and need to strengthen your project portfolio

✗You are adding certifications without gaining hands-on project experience

✗You are pursuing 8+ certifications without a clear career progression plan

✗Your target role (such as CTA) values architecture experience over certification count

✗You only use Salesforce for one narrow task at your company

Real Cost vs Real Benefit

Exam fee: $75–$400 (most certs $200)

Study time: 40–120 hours (8–12 weeks part-time)

Retake fee: $100–$200 after a failed first attempt

Maintenance: 3 free Trailhead modules per release

Optional study courses: $50–$300

chunks.title: Is Salesforce Certification Worth It? (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
ROI example: ADM-201 costs $200 (exam) and takes about 60 hours of study. If it leads to a $15,000 salary increase, the exam fee equals less than 1 week of that additional salary. Include study time and any retake in your own calculation.

Job Market Demand (Summer '26)

Salesforce has over 150,000 customers globally. Agentforce AI features are driving new implementation work in 2025–2026.

IDC research projects that the Salesforce ecosystem will create 9.3 million jobs by 2026. The number of certified professionals has not kept pace with demand, which supports higher salaries.

ADM-201 can provide an entry point to admin roles. Developer and consultant roles tend to pay more and ask for more experience. Architect roles offer higher compensation, and some top firms have 5–10 year wait lists.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Salesforce certification increase salary?

Certification can support salary growth, though it does not guarantee a raise. Salesforce research and third-party surveys report that certified professionals earn 20–30% more than peers in similar roles. Entry-level ADM-201 certified admins earn $60,000–$80,000 vs $45,000–$60,000 without certification. Senior developers and architects with multiple certifications earn $130,000–$180,000+. Compare the $200 exam fee with a possible $15,000–$30,000 salary increase when considering the return.

How many Salesforce certifications do you need?

For many people, 2–4 certifications chosen for a clear career goal are enough. Start with a credential for your role, such as ADM-201, PD1, or Sales Cloud Consultant. A complementary credential, such as ADM-201 + App Builder or PD1 + Service Cloud Consultant, can broaden your skills. After 4–5 certifications, hands-on project experience may matter more than adding another credential.

How long does it take to get Salesforce certified?

Study time depends on your experience. A common estimate for ADM-201 is 8–12 weeks for beginners and 4–6 weeks for people with CRM experience. Platform Developer I may take 12–16 weeks if you already know programming. Consultant certifications such as Sales Cloud and Service Cloud may take 8–12 weeks after ADM-201. Your results will depend on your preparation and job opportunities.

Is Salesforce certification hard?

chunks.title: Is Salesforce Certification Worth It? (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Difficulty depends on the certification and what you already know. A beginner may prepare for ADM-201 in 8–12 weeks without prior tech experience. PD1 and consultant exams require deeper knowledge and scenario-based reasoning. Integration Architect and Data Architect typically call for 2–4 years of project experience. The CTA Board Review is one of the most demanding certification processes in enterprise software. Candidates who study 10–15 hours per week and use practice questions may pass on their first or second attempt.

Is Salesforce certification worth it for career changers?

A certification can help career changers show what they have learned about Salesforce. ADM-201 does not require a computer science degree or years of coding experience, and people from fields such as teaching, healthcare, accounting, and sales have moved into Salesforce roles. The exam costs $200, and a typical study plan may take 8–12 weeks. A $70,000–$100,000+ career is possible, but a credential alone cannot guarantee a job or salary.

You have built integrations using REST callouts, Platform Events, or external systems.

What Salesforce Admin Certification 201 Actually Tests

“Salesforce Admin Certification 201” usually refers to the Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator exam. The exam tests whether you can choose the right Salesforce feature for a business need, including when several options seem similar.

Learn how profiles, permission sets, roles, org-wide defaults, sharing rules, teams, queues, and field-level security work. Be clear on which settings control record access and which control object or field permissions.

Object model and app configuration

Practice working with standard and custom objects, lookup and master-detail relationships, record types, page layouts, Lightning record pages, business processes, and compact layouts in a dev org.

Flow is a common automation tool. Check whether a scenario specifically calls for an approval process, assignment rule, escalation rule, or another feature before choosing a solution.

Reports, dashboards, and data quality

Review report formats, dashboard running users, dynamic dashboards, import tools, duplicate management, and validation rules. Know when to use Data Loader and when to use Data Import Wizard.

When Are You Ready to Book ADM-201?

You can explain the difference between a profile, permission set, role, sharing rule, and field-level security without notes.

You can build a record-triggered Flow, validation rule, report, and dashboard in a Salesforce dev org.

You score at least 75% on three timed practice sets and understand each answer you missed.

You can complete a 60-question practice exam in under 95 minutes and still have time to review flagged questions.

If you are still unsure about security or Flow scenarios, continue practicing before you pay the exam fee. If your remaining gaps are in lower-weight productivity or collaboration topics, you may be close to ready.

chunks.title: Salesforce Admin vs Developer Career Paths (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 9 November 2026

Salesforce admins and developers solve different problems on the same platform. Compare their daily work, technical requirements, and likely progression to see which path better fits your interests.

Which should you take first?

Take Salesforce Administrator if:

You prefer configuring Salesforce and improving business processes

You want to start with a credential used for many admin roles

Your background is in operations, project management, or another non-technical field

You want to explore a common entry point into the Salesforce job market

Take Platform Developer I if:

You enjoy writing code and want to build Apex and LWC features

You have experience in software development or computer science

You want to pursue technical roles on the Salesforce platform

You can spend 3–6 months preparing for the technical exam

Our Recommendation: Start with Salesforce Administrator

Administrator helps you learn the platform and is useful in both admin and development roles. Start there if you are new to Salesforce. If you already have a programming background and want to build features in code, Platform Developer I may be a closer match.

⚙️ Salesforce Administrator

Day-to-day: Configuration, flows, reports, user support, change requests

Tools: Salesforce Setup, Flow Builder, Report Builder, Excel

Salary range: $70K–$120K (US, varies by location)

Progression: Junior Admin → Admin → Senior Admin → Admin Lead or Consultant

Best for: People who enjoy process design, business analysis, and working with stakeholders

💻 Salesforce Developer

Day-to-day: Apex, LWC, integrations, deployments, code reviews

Tools: VS Code, Developer Console, Git, Salesforce CLI

Salary range: $85K–$140K (US, varies by location)

Progression: Junior Dev → Developer → Senior Dev → Tech Lead or Architect

Best for: People with programming interest who enjoy solving technical challenges

Some roles combine configuration and development. Consultancies and mid-size firms may hire Salesforce Consultants, Technical Consultants, or Platform Developers who can work across both areas. These positions often ask for Administrator and Platform Developer I, making an admin foundation followed by PD1 one possible route into hybrid work.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it better to be a Salesforce Admin or Developer?

chunks.title: Salesforce Admin vs Developer Career Paths (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
The right path depends on the work you enjoy. Admins configure Salesforce, shape processes, and support users. Developers build with Apex and LWC, connect systems, and handle complex automation. Developers typically earn 10–20% more at equivalent experience levels, while admin roles are more common and may be easier to enter without programming experience.

What does a Salesforce Administrator do day to day?

A Salesforce Administrator manages access, customizes objects and page layouts, builds automation with tools such as flows, creates reports, troubleshoots user issues, and responds to business requests. The work includes configuring Salesforce, training users, and documenting processes. Most time is spent in the Salesforce interface rather than writing code.

What does a Salesforce Developer do day to day?

A Salesforce Developer writes and maintains Apex, builds Lightning Web Components (LWC), connects Salesforce to other systems through APIs, reviews code, and investigates technical issues. Developers work with tools such as VS Code, Developer Console, sandboxes, and version control. They typically spend 60–70% of their time coding or reviewing code.

Can I switch from Salesforce Admin to Developer?

Yes. Many developers begin as admins. Earn Platform Developer I after Administrator, build Apex and LWC projects in a sandbox, and look for roles that combine configuration and development, such as Salesforce Consultant or Platform Developer at a smaller firm. Admin experience can help you understand the business needs behind the code.

Which certifications do I need for Admin vs Developer careers?

For an admin career, start with Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201), then consider Advanced Administrator or a specialization such as CPQ or Service Cloud. For development, build on Administrator with Platform Developer I (PD1), then Platform Developer II (PD2). Admin knowledge is useful for developers because it covers the platform they build on.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certification Difficulty Ranking (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 9 November 2026

Compare major Salesforce certifications by difficulty, exam format, and the experience and study each may require.

These exams cover core concepts and require little or no Salesforce experience. They can be good starting points.

These foundational certifications may take 8–12 weeks of study if you have no prior experience.

These certifications build on foundational knowledge and benefit from hands-on project experience.

These advanced certifications usually require several years of Salesforce experience.

These are the most demanding Salesforce credentials and suit highly experienced professionals.

What Makes a Salesforce Exam Difficult?

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the easiest Salesforce certification?

Platform Foundations is currently the easiest Salesforce certification to take. It requires no prior Salesforce experience and covers the platform at a high level. The exam has 40 questions, a 62% passing score, and a $75 fee. AI Associate was once a common answer, but it retired in February 2026 and can no longer be booked. Its page on this site remains as a historical reference.

What is the hardest Salesforce certification?

The Salesforce Certified Technical Architect (CTA) Board Review is widely regarded as the hardest Salesforce credential. Candidates must hold both Application Architect and System Architect credentials (eight individual certifications in total), then give a live, two-hour presentation to a panel of senior Salesforce architects. There are fewer than 1,000 CTAs worldwide. Candidates typically have 8–12 years of Salesforce experience and may take the board more than once.

Is Platform Developer I (PD1) hard?

PD1 is moderately difficult. It covers Apex, SOQL, governor limits, Lightning Web Components, testing, and deployment. People with programming experience in languages such as Java, C#, or Python may need 8–12 weeks of focused study. Those new to programming may need 4–6 months. Salesforce does not publish a pass rate; community estimates put the first-attempt rate at 50–65%.

Is the Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201) exam hard?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certification Difficulty Ranking (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
ADM-201 can be challenging for complete beginners because it covers many topics: Salesforce features and objects, security, automation, reports, dashboards, and data management. The passing score is 68%. Many candidates without Salesforce experience study part time for 8–12 weeks. The main challenge is covering the full range of topics, even though no one section goes very deep.

Do Salesforce consultant exams have a higher fail rate than admin exams?

Consultant exams often feel harder than ADM-201 because they ask you to apply Salesforce features to business scenarios. A question may describe a business problem and ask which configuration would solve it. This tests product knowledge and consulting judgment, not just recall.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certification Maintenance Guide (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Summer ’26 maintenance modules are now live on Trailhead, released August 2026.

Deadline to complete: April 16, 2027. Log in to Trailhead and check your Credentials tab to see which modules are pending for your certifications.

Last updated: 9 November 2026

Learn when to complete maintenance, where to find Trailhead modules, and what happens if you miss a deadline. See the certification validity guide for more details.

How Salesforce Certification Maintenance Works

Salesforce releases three major platform updates each year: Spring (January/February), Summer (May/June), and Winter (September/October). Each release brings new features and changes.

Salesforce publishes maintenance modules on Trailhead for each release, but each credential only needs one badge per year, in the release cycle Salesforce assigns to it. The window is generous: roughly eight to twelve months from publication. The Summer ’26 modules published in August 2026 and are due April 16, 2027. Complete yours before its stated deadline to keep the certification Active.

Certifications in the same role category usually share one maintenance module. For example, someone with both ADM-201 and Advanced Administrator usually completes one Administrator-category module, not two.

How to Complete Maintenance: Step by Step

Watch for Salesforce release announcements

Salesforce announces releases on its blog and Trust.salesforce.com. Sign up for release email updates to hear when maintenance modules are available.

Go to trailhead.salesforce.com and sign in with the Salesforce account linked to your certification. Open your profile and select "Credentials."

Check for pending maintenance

Certifications with outstanding maintenance show an alert. Select a certification to see the required module and its deadline.

Complete the maintenance module

Open the Trailhead module, read each unit, and complete its challenge quiz. Modules usually take 20–60 minutes. You can pause and return later.

After you finish the module, check your certification status. Your Trailhead badge should show Active for the new release and the updated maintenance date.

What If You Miss the Maintenance Deadline?

Your certification becomes Inactive. It is not permanently revoked, but the status appears on your Trailhead credential profile.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certification Maintenance Guide (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
To reactivate it, complete every overdue maintenance module. Your status returns to Active after you finish them.

While it is Inactive, do not describe the certification as currently active on your resume, LinkedIn profile, or to clients. The status is visible in Trailhead verification.

Reactivation is free. Complete the overdue modules; Salesforce does not charge a reactivation fee.

Salesforce Release Schedule (Summer '26)

Each credential needs one badge per year, in the single release cycle Salesforce assigns to it — not one per release. Exact dates vary; check your Trailhead credential page for the deadline tied to your own certification.

Frequently Asked Questions

How often do Salesforce certifications need to be maintained?

Salesforce has three major releases each year: Spring, Summer, and Winter. Maintenance itself is annual: each credential has one badge per year, released in the cycle Salesforce assigns to it. You get roughly eight to twelve months to complete it, not 30 days. The Summer ’26 modules went live in August 2026 and are due April 16, 2027. Certifications in the same role category usually share a module, so you do not need one for each certification.

What happens if I miss the Salesforce certification maintenance deadline?

If you miss a maintenance deadline, your Trailhead credential status changes from Active to Inactive. The certification is not permanently revoked. Complete all overdue maintenance modules to reactivate it. While it is Inactive, do not describe it on your resume or LinkedIn profile as currently active.

Where do I find the Salesforce certification maintenance modules?

Salesforce publishes maintenance modules on Trailhead (trailhead.salesforce.com). Sign in, open your profile, and check Credentials for alerts about pending maintenance. You can also search the Trailhead module catalogue for "maintenance." Salesforce may also send reminders to your registered email address.

Do maintenance modules cost anything?

No. Salesforce maintenance modules are free. These short Trailhead modules usually take 20–60 minutes and cover platform changes related to your certification. Salesforce does not charge a maintenance fee.

Do all Salesforce certifications require maintenance?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certification Maintenance Guide (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Most role-based Salesforce certifications, including Administrator, Developer, Consultant, and Architect, require maintenance. Accredited Professional (AP) and some associate-level certifications may follow different rules. Check your certification at trailhead.salesforce.com/credentials for its schedule and any exceptions.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certification Passing Score by Tier (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 9 November 2026

Salesforce lists exact passing scores in official exam guides. This page shows verified scores where a guide is available. Scores range from 48% to 78%. Salesforce does not publish numerical cut scores for Accredited Professional and board-reviewed exams.

Note: figures below come from official Salesforce exam guides rather than estimates. Salesforce does not publish a numerical passing score for Accredited Professional and board-reviewed exams. On practice tests, aim about ten points above the score required for your exam.

Passing Scores by Certification Tier

How to Use This When Studying

Aim for 75% or higher. This gives you a margin above the exam threshold, which ranges from about 60% to 78%.

Do not aim only to scrape a pass. A score of 66% on a practice test may not translate to a pass on exam day.

Take several full practice exams. Scoring 75% or higher on two or three full tests can help you judge if you are ready.

Review each wrong answer. Learn why an answer was wrong instead of focusing only on your score.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the passing score for Salesforce Administrator exam?

Platform Administrator (ADM-201) requires a score of 68%, or 41 of the 60 scored questions. This figure comes from the official Salesforce exam guide.

Do all Salesforce exams have the same passing score?

No. Associate exams ($75) typically require about 62–70%. Specialist, Professional, and Consultant exams ($200) span 62–73%: Platform App Builder needs 73% and Agentforce Specialist needs 72%, while others sit nearer 62–68%. Architect exams ($400) range from 58% to about 70%. Always check the official exam guide for your specific exam.

How is the Salesforce exam score calculated?

Salesforce calculates your score as the percentage of scored questions you answered correctly and compares it with the passing score in the official exam guide. Unscored pilot questions do not count. You receive a pass or fail result and a breakdown by exam section.

What score should I aim for on practice exams?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certification Passing Score by Tier (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Aim for at least 75% on several full-length, timed practice exams before booking. This gives you a margin above the passing score, which ranges from about 60% to 78% depending on the exam. If you consistently score below 70%, spend more time studying before you book.

Does the Technical Architect (CTA) exam have a passing score?

The CTA is not a multiple-choice exam. In the live Board Review, you present a hypothetical architecture to a panel of CTAs. There is no numerical passing score. The board evaluates six criteria, including architecture, design, security, and scalability, then decides pass or fail. Prepare to explain your architecture clearly, not to reach a percentage threshold.

How to study for certification

Practice Until You Hit 75%+

Practice with questions for every Salesforce certification and track your score.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certification Validity & Expiry (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 9 November 2026

Salesforce certifications do not expire, but they require maintenance. Here’s exactly how certification validity works and how to keep yours Active.

Short answer: Certifications have no fixed expiry date

Salesforce certifications stay Active when you complete the required maintenance badge each year. The badge is released in the Spring, Summer, or Winter cycle assigned to that credential and is due one year after it becomes available.

How Certification Validity Works

After you pass a Salesforce certification exam, your Trailhead profile shows the credential as Active. The certification itself has no expiry date.

Salesforce releases three major platform updates each year: Spring (Jan/Feb), Summer (May/Jun), and Winter (Sep/Oct). Trailhead maintenance modules cover changes related to each certification area, but a given credential is tied to one of those cycles, so you complete one badge per year, not three.

The window is wide: roughly eight to twelve months from the day the badge publishes. The Summer ’26 modules went live in August 2026 and are due April 16, 2027. Meet the deadline and your status stays Active with an updated certification date. Miss it and your status changes to Inactive.

Certifications in the same role category, such as Administrator credentials, usually share one maintenance module. You do not need a separate module for every certification you hold.

Active vs Inactive: What It Means

✓ Required maintenance modules are complete for the current release

✓ Certification appears on the public Trailhead verification page

✓ You can list it as active on your resume and LinkedIn

✓ It counts toward Salesforce partner certification requirements

✓ Trailhead displays the certification badge on your profile

⚠ One or more maintenance modules are overdue

⚠ Public Trailhead verification shows it as Inactive

⚠ Do not list it as currently active on your resume

⚠ It does not count toward partner certification requirements

✓ You can reactivate it for free at any time

How Salesforce Compares to Other Certifications

Salesforce maintenance does not require a full exam retake.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do Salesforce certifications expire?

chunks.title: Salesforce Certification Validity & Expiry (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Salesforce certifications do not have a permanent expiry date, but they can become Inactive if you miss required maintenance. Salesforce releases platform updates three times a year (Spring, Summer, and Winter) and publishes related Trailhead maintenance modules. If you miss a deadline, your status changes from Active to Inactive. Complete the overdue modules to reactivate your certification.

How long is a Salesforce certification valid?

Salesforce certifications have no fixed expiry date. They remain valid as long as you complete the required maintenance modules. Modules are free and usually take 20–60 minutes each. Your certification date on Trailhead updates when you complete maintenance for a release.

What is the difference between Active and Inactive certification status?

Active means you have completed the required maintenance for your certification. Inactive means one or more modules are overdue. While your certification is Inactive, do not describe it as currently active on your resume, LinkedIn profile, or to clients. Employers and clients can see the status on the public Trailhead credential verification page.

How do I reactivate an Inactive Salesforce certification?

Sign in to Trailhead (trailhead.salesforce.com), open your profile, and select Credentials. Inactive certifications show the outstanding maintenance modules. Complete all overdue modules, which usually take 20–60 minutes each, to restore Active status. Reactivation is free. If maintenance is overdue for several releases, complete every outstanding module.

Do I need to retake the full exam to maintain my certification?

No. You do not need to retake the full exam. Maintenance means completing short Trailhead modules with quizzes about new features in the latest release. Plan for about 1–3 hours of maintenance per year for each certification category.

chunks.content:
Last updated: 13 November 2026

Find ways to lower Salesforce exam costs through event offers, partner benefits, Trailhead promotions, and retake discounts.

1. Salesforce Events (Most Reliable)

Dreamforce (San Francisco, September)

Salesforce's main annual conference has offered free associate-level exam vouchers to registered attendees, including Platform Foundations. AI Associate was also offered before it retired. In-person attendance has been required for voucher access.

World Tour Events (Global, throughout year)

Salesforce World Tour events in cities such as London, Sydney, and New York sometimes offer free or discounted exams. Check each event's agenda for current details.

TrailblazerDX (San Francisco, March)

This developer-focused conference has offered certification promotions for developer exams such as PD1, PD2, and JavaScript Developer I.

2. The 50% Retake Voucher (Guaranteed)

After you fail a Salesforce certification exam, a discounted retake voucher appears in your Trailhead Academy account. The discount is about 50% of the original fee.

A $200 exam retake costs about $100. A $400 architect exam retake costs about $200. A $75 associate exam retake costs about $38.

Retake vouchers do not have a short expiry, so you can use one when you are ready. Check current scheduling rules before booking another attempt.

3. Salesforce Partner Employee Benefits

Consulting partner (SI) employees

Some large Salesforce system integrators, such as Accenture, Deloitte, Cognizant, and Slalom, cover all certification exam fees for employees. Check your employer's learning and development policy or HR portal.

ISV partner employees

Independent software vendors that build on Salesforce may subsidize relevant certifications, such as Platform Developer I or App Builder, for their developers.

Salesforce employees receive free access to certification exams as an employee benefit.

4. Trailhead Promotions (Periodic)

Salesforce has offered free exam vouchers for completing selected Trailhead trails or earning superbadges. These campaigns run for a limited time.

Certification bundle promotions

Trailhead Academy sometimes offers a lower price for a bundle of certifications, such as ADM-201 and App Builder. Check its website for current prices.

How to find current promos

Follow @Trailhead and @SalesforceAdmns on social media, check the Salesforce blog, and join Trailblazer Community groups for promotion announcements.

chunks.title: Salesforce Certification Voucher & Discount Guide (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
What About Third-Party Voucher Sites?

Be cautious with third-party sites that advertise steeply discounted Salesforce exam vouchers. Exams are booked through Trailhead Academy and delivered via Pearson VUE (OnVUE), and voucher codes must be valid Salesforce-issued codes. Use the discount sources listed above.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are there legitimate Salesforce certification discounts?

Yes. Salesforce offers several legitimate discounts and vouchers. These may come through events such as Dreamforce, World Tour, and TrailblazerDX; employee benefits at Salesforce partners; Trailhead Academy promotions; or the discounted retake available after a failed attempt. Offers and eligibility vary.

Does Salesforce offer a 50% retake discount?

Yes. After a failed exam, Salesforce offers a discounted retake at about 50% of the original fee. For example, a $200 exam retake costs about $100, and a $400 architect exam retake costs about $200. The discount appears in your Trailhead Academy account after a failed attempt. It has no time limit.

Can I get a free Salesforce certification at Dreamforce?

Salesforce has offered free or discounted associate-level exams at Dreamforce in the past. Offers have included Platform Foundations and MuleSoft Integration Foundations. AI Associate retired in February 2026 and can no longer be booked. Availability changes each year and is announced closer to the event. In-person attendance may require paid Dreamforce registration. Check the Salesforce Trailhead blog for current offers.

Do Salesforce partner employees get exam discounts?

Employees of registered Salesforce partners, including ISVs, system integrators, and resellers, may receive exam subsidies. Benefits depend on the partner tier and agreement. Some large partners cover the full exam fee for relevant certifications. Ask your HR or learning team about your employer's policy.

Are there Trailhead vouchers for free certifications?

Salesforce has run limited-time Trailhead promotions that award exam vouchers for completing specific trails or superbadges. These offers are temporary. Follow @Trailhead and check the Salesforce Trailhead blog for announcements. Past promotions have typically lasted 30–90 days.

chunks.title: Salesforce Exam Retake Policy (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 14 November 2026

Find retake costs, waiting periods, attempt rules, and advice for preparing after a failed exam.

2026–2027 free-retake promotion

Salesforce and Pearson are offering one free retake for eligible $200 and $400 exams when candidates opted in and completed their paid first attempt by November 17, 2026. Eligible retakes can be taken January 4–April 7, 2027. Accredited Professional and Technical Architect exams are excluded. See Salesforce’s promotion terms.

✓ You can take the same exam 3 times per release cycle. Attempts reset when the next cycle starts.

✓ Wait 24 hours after your first failure and 14 days after your second. After your third, wait the next release cycle.

✓ Retakes cost 50% of the original exam price. Foundations exams carry no retake fee.

✓ Failed attempts do not appear on your public Trailhead profile

✓ Use your section score report to find areas that need more study.

Retake Costs by Exam Type

What to Do After Failing

Review your score report by section

Open your score report in Trailhead Academy after the exam. Note the sections that need more study and focus your review there.

Give yourself time to study

Avoid booking another attempt right away. The page recommends waiting 2–4 weeks to address the gaps in your score report before retaking the exam.

Vary your study approach

If you mainly read Trailhead material, add hands-on sandbox practice. If you already did hands-on work, try scenario-based practice questions. Use more than one study method.

Focus on weaker sections

Spend about 70% of your study time on sections where you scored below the passing threshold. Review stronger sections as needed.

Practice under exam conditions

Take full-length timed practice exams to build stamina and manage your time. Practice answering 60 questions in 90–105 minutes.

CTA Board Review: Different Policy

The Salesforce Certified Technical Architect Architect Evaluation and Review Board have separate pricing and scheduling rules. Confirm the current requirements with Salesforce before applying again.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Salesforce exam retake policy?

chunks.title: Salesforce Exam Retake Policy (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Within each release cycle, Salesforce allows 3 attempts at the same exam. After a first failure, wait 24 hours; after a second, wait 14 days; after a third, wait until the next release cycle. Attempts reset at the next release cycle.

How much does a Salesforce exam retake cost?

Most retakes cost 50% of the original exam fee. Accredited Professional exams cost $150 to retake, the same as the first attempt; Foundations exams have no retake fee. Pearson VUE applies the retake price when you book through Trailhead Academy.

How many times can I retake a Salesforce certification exam?

You can attempt the same exam 3 times in one release cycle. After a third failure, wait until the next release cycle begins; your attempt count then resets. The Technical Architect Review Board has separate policies, so check its current programme guidance.

What score report do I receive after failing?

Salesforce provides a section-level score report after the exam. Use the breakdown to identify topics that need more study; the report is available in Trailhead Academy.

Does failing a Salesforce exam affect my record permanently?

The public credential view is for earned certifications. For details about your exam history and score report, sign in to Trailhead Academy.

chunks.title: How to Get a Free Salesforce Certification (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 13 November 2026

Find ways to earn a Salesforce certification for free, plus lower-cost options when no free exam voucher is available.

Free certification exams are offered through limited-time promotions, not year-round. When no free voucher is available, the $75 associate-level exams are the lowest-cost option. This guide covers free and discounted routes.

Route 1: Salesforce Events (Most Reliable Free Opportunity)

Salesforce has offered free associate-level exam vouchers at major events. Dreamforce in San Francisco, held in September, is one opportunity; the company has offered Platform Foundations exams to registered attendees. World Tour events have also run offers for attendees. Announcements may appear 4–8 weeks before an event on the Salesforce blog and Trailhead social channels. Follow @Trailhead and @Salesforce for updates.

Route 2: Employer Sponsorship (Most Common Free Route)

If you work for or are joining a Salesforce consulting partner or ISV, your employer may pay for your exam. Partner companies have a financial reason to support employee certifications because they count toward partner tier requirements. Large system integrators such as Accenture, Deloitte, Capgemini, and Wipro, as well as smaller Salesforce partners, may have learning budgets for exams. Ask your manager or HR team before paying yourself.

Route 3: Trailhead Promotional Campaigns (Periodic)

Salesforce has run campaigns that award a free exam voucher after you complete a specific Trailhead trail or Superbadge challenge. These offers are temporary, often running for 30–90 days around a product launch or milestone. To find them, set Google Alerts for "Salesforce free certification" and "Trailhead exam voucher," follow Salesforce Trailhead, Salesforce Admins, and Salesforce Developers, and join Trailblazer Community groups.

Route 4: $75 Associate Certifications (Lowest Cost Entry)

When no free exam is available, associate-level exams cost $75 each. Options listed here include AI Associate, Platform Foundations, and MuleSoft Integration Foundations. AI Associate retired in February 2026 and can no longer be booked. Platform Foundations gives beginners a broad Salesforce overview, while MuleSoft Integration Foundations covers APIs and integration concepts. A $75 exam can be a low-cost way to start learning Salesforce.

Trailhead vs Certifications: What’s Free?

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.title: How to Get a Free Salesforce Certification (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Can I get a Salesforce certification for free?

Sometimes. Salesforce has offered free exam vouchers at events such as Dreamforce and World Tour. These offers have included associate-level exams that normally cost $75, such as Platform Foundations and MuleSoft Integration Foundations. AI Associate retired in February 2026. Employees of Salesforce consulting partners may also receive exam fee support from their employer.

Does Salesforce offer free certifications through Trailhead?

Yes. Trailhead modules, trails, superbadges, and other learning content are free. They are not Salesforce certifications, which require a separate proctored exam booked through Trailhead Academy. Salesforce sometimes runs limited-time promotions that award an exam voucher for completing a Trailhead trail.

What is the cheapest Salesforce certification?

The associate-level exams cost $75 each, the lowest standard fee in the Salesforce portfolio. Current options include Platform Foundations and MuleSoft Integration Foundations; AI Associate retired in February 2026. These exams offer a lower-cost entry point for beginners. Platform Foundations is a common first certification.

Can my employer pay for my Salesforce certification?

Some employers cover Salesforce exam fees, especially consulting partners whose partner tier depends on employee certifications. Other employers may reimburse exam fees through a learning and development budget. Ask your manager or HR team before paying yourself.

Are Trailhead Superbadges the same as certifications?

No. A Trailhead Superbadge and a Salesforce certification are different credentials. Superbadges are awarded for completing hands-on challenges and appear on your Trailhead profile, but they are not formal certifications. You earn a certification by passing a proctored exam booked through Trailhead Academy and delivered via Pearson VUE. Employers can check it on a separate public credential page. Both can be useful, though certifications may carry more weight in job applications.

Is certification worth it?

Platform Foundations study guide

Start with Platform Foundations: $75

Start with a lower-cost exam that does not require prior Salesforce experience. Free practice questions are available.

chunks.title: System Architect vs Application Architect (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 9 November 2026

Both credentials are part of the CTA path, but they cover different architecture domains and have different component exams. Compare their focus, cost, and shared requirement to decide where to begin.

Application Architect

Required exams (auto-awarded, no separate exam):

Platform App Builder ($200)

Platform Developer I ($200) ← shared

Data Architect ($400)

Sharing & Visibility Architect ($400)

Platform Developer I ($200) ← shared

Integration Architect ($400)

Dev Lifecycle & Deployment Architect ($400)

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between System Architect and Application Architect?

Salesforce awards Application Architect after you pass Platform App Builder, Platform Developer I, Data Architect, and Sharing and Visibility Architect. There is no separate exam. System Architect requires Platform Developer I, Integration Architect, Identity and Access Management Architect, and Dev Lifecycle and Deployment Architect, and is also awarded automatically. Application Architect focuses on application design and declarative tools; System Architect focuses on infrastructure, integration, and the platform.

Which should I pursue first: System Architect or Application Architect?

Many candidates start with Application Architect because its App Builder, Data Architect, and Sharing & Visibility exams cost $200–$400 each and may be a more accessible entry point than the infrastructure-heavy System Architect exams. This path also introduces application architecture before deeper work in integration and identity. If you already work in integration or security, you may prefer to begin with System Architect components.

How much does it cost to earn both credentials?

Application Architect costs: App Builder $200 + PD1 $200 + Data Architect $400 + Sharing & Visibility Architect $400 = $1,200. For System Architect, add Integration Architect $400 + IAM Architect $400 + Dev Lifecycle Architect $400 = $1,200 (PD1 is already counted under Application Architect). The stated combined estimate is approximately $2,600 for both credentials.

Are both credentials required for the CTA?

Yes. You must hold both System Architect and Application Architect before applying for the Salesforce Certified Technical Architect (CTA) Board Review. One credential alone is not enough, and both must be in Active status when you apply.

Do overlapping exams count toward both credentials?

chunks.title: System Architect vs Application Architect (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Platform Developer I is the only shared exam. Passing it once counts toward both credentials. Data Architect and Sharing and Visibility Architect count only toward Application Architect, while Integration Architect, IAM Architect, and Dev Lifecycle Architect count only toward System Architect. This reduces the number of unique exams from nine to eight for candidates pursuing both credentials and CTA.

Salesforce exam score questions

Why does Salesforce not show my overall exam score?

Salesforce reports a percentage for each section of the exam but not a single overall figure, on either the result screen or the confirmation email. The overall result is given only as pass or fail. This calculator reconstructs the overall percentage by weighting each section by its published share of the exam.

How is the weighted score calculated?

Each section percentage is multiplied by that section’s share of the exam, and the results are added together. A section worth 20% of the exam contributes four times as much as one worth 5%. If you fill in only some sections, the calculator normalises by the weight you supplied and tells you how much of the exam that covers.

Is the calculated score exact?

It is close, not exact. Salesforce does not publish how it rounds section percentages, nor how unscored trial questions are handled, so small differences are expected. Use it to see roughly how far above or below the pass mark you landed and which section cost you the most.

chunks.title: UX Designer vs Strategy Designer (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 9 November 2026

Both certifications are in the Salesforce Designer track, but one centers on user experience and the other on business strategy. Compare their work and exam focus to choose what fits your role.

Which should you take first?

You design Salesforce interfaces, flows, or Lightning page layouts

You want to show your knowledge of UX fundamentals and accessibility

You collaborate with developers on components and pages

You are entering the designer certification track

Take Strategy Designer if:

You lead discovery workshops, journey mapping, or design sprints

You turn broad business problems into Salesforce solutions

You work with stakeholders on strategy as well as interface decisions

You want to focus on strategy and design thinking

Our Recommendation: Start with UX Designer

Choose UX Designer if you want to apply research and interface design in Salesforce. Choose Strategy Designer if your work starts earlier, with discovery, business goals, and product direction. The order depends on whether your current work is hands-on design or strategic planning.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which should I take first: UX Designer or Strategy Designer?

Start with UX Designer if you have a design or UX background. It applies familiar skills such as research, wireframing, prototyping, and usability testing to Salesforce. If your background is business analysis, consulting, or product strategy, consider Strategy Designer, which focuses on design thinking and framing business problems. The certifications cover different parts of the design process, so some people earn both.

Are UX Designer and Strategy Designer useful for non-designers?

Yes. Admins who design user flows, business analysts who map processes, consultants who present solutions, and project managers who guide implementations can all use designer-track skills. UX and design thinking can help teams improve how people use Salesforce.

Which certification is harder: UX Designer or Strategy Designer?

chunks.title: UX Designer vs Strategy Designer (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Candidates may find Strategy Designer more challenging because it asks them to apply abstract design frameworks to complex business situations. The passing scores are 70% for Strategy Designer and 65% for UX Designer. UX Designer focuses on practical skills such as research methods, wireframing, and SLDS, which some candidates find easier to prepare for.

What jobs require UX Designer vs Strategy Designer?

UX Designer aligns with roles such as Salesforce UX Designer, Lightning Experience Designer, CRM Adoption Specialist, and Solution Designer. Strategy Designer aligns with Design Strategist, Digital Transformation Consultant, Product Manager, and Customer Experience Architect roles. Both can be relevant to senior consultant and architect roles that use design thinking.

Can I take both UX Designer and Strategy Designer exams?

Yes. The certifications cover different stages of design work. UX Designer focuses on execution: research, prototyping, and testing. Strategy Designer focuses on framing the business context, setting product direction, and measuring outcomes. Together, they cover work from strategic planning through detailed design.

chunks.title: Which Salesforce Certification Should I Get First? (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Last updated: 9 November 2026

Choose a first certification based on your experience and career goal. Use these paths to compare where to start and what to take next.

If you are new to Salesforce, start with Platform Foundations ($75) to learn the basics. Then consider Administrator ($200) as your main professional credential. If you already know Salesforce is the right path, you can start with Administrator.

I want to be a Salesforce Admin

Start with: Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201)

Study time: 2–4 months

Administrator covers core skills for admin work and can support applications for junior admin, CRM analyst, and business analyst roles. Many Salesforce admin tasks build on these skills.

Then: Advanced Administrator, then specialist certs (CPQ, Field Service, Experience Cloud)

I want to be a Salesforce Developer

Start with: Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201)

Study time: 2–4 months

Administrator teaches declarative Salesforce features that developers also use. Learning the platform first can make it easier to prepare for Platform Developer I and Apex work.

Then: Platform Developer I, then Platform Developer II

I want to be a Salesforce Consultant

Start with: Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201)

Study time: 2–4 months

Consultants need a solid understanding of the platform and its administration tools. Start with Administrator, then pursue a specialist certification in an area such as Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, or CPQ.

Then: Sales Cloud Consultant or Service Cloud Consultant, based on specialisation

I want to test the waters (not sure yet)

Start with: Platform Foundations

Study time: 2–4 weeks

Platform Foundations is a lower-cost introduction that does not require prior platform experience. It can help you decide whether you want to continue with Salesforce.

Then: Administrator (ADM-201) after confirming Salesforce is your direction

I work in marketing (Salesforce context)

Start with: Marketing Cloud Email Specialist

Study time: 4–8 weeks (with MC experience)

For people who use Marketing Cloud Engagement, Email Specialist is an accessible marketing-track option. B2B marketers who use Pardot, also called Account Engagement, can start with Pardot Specialist.

Then: Marketing Cloud Consultant or Pardot Consultant

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the most popular first Salesforce certification?

chunks.title: Which Salesforce Certification Should I Get First? (Summer '26)
chunks.content:
Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201) is the most common first certification. It is a core professional credential, and many admin, consultant, and business analyst roles require or prefer it. If you are new to Salesforce and want a lower-cost introduction, start with Platform Foundations ($75) before taking on the full Administrator study plan.

Can I get a Salesforce certification with no experience?

Yes. The associate-level certifications cost $75 each and are designed for beginners. Salesforce Platform Foundations and MuleSoft Integration Foundations are available; AI Associate retired in February 2026 and can no longer be booked. Platform Foundations is a common first choice. You can also take Administrator ($200) without Salesforce work experience, but plan for 3–4 months of study and hands-on sandbox practice.

Is the Salesforce Administrator certification the best first cert?

Administrator is a strong first certification for most people pursuing a Salesforce career. Many admin, junior consultant, business analyst, and CRM analyst roles require or prefer it. If you are unsure whether Salesforce is right for you, Platform Foundations ($75) offers a lower-cost introduction.

Should a developer start with Administrator or Platform Developer I?

Developers with software engineering experience can still benefit from starting with Administrator (ADM-201). It teaches declarative Salesforce features and how the platform works before you write Apex. Platform Developer I (PD1) is harder without that platform knowledge. A common path is Administrator, then PD1.

How long does it take to get the first Salesforce certification?

As a rough guide, allow 2–4 weeks of part-time Trailhead study for Platform Foundations ($75), 2–4 months (40–80 hours) for Administrator ($200), and 3–5 months for Platform Developer I ($200) if you already know how to program. Your starting knowledge matters: people new to Salesforce usually need more time than those who use it at work.
